papers.title_zh: A Totally Laparoscopic Transhiatal Approach for Esophageal Cancer During Mediastinoscopic Esophagectomy.
papers.title_en: A Totally Laparoscopic Transhiatal Approach for Esophageal Cancer During Mediastinoscopic Esophagectomy.
papers.authors: Konishi H, Sumiyoshi S, Inoue H, Nishibeppu K, Kosuga T, Yamamoto Y, Morimura R, Fujiwara H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Digestive Surgery, Department of Surgery, Kyoto Prefectural University of Medicine, Kajii-cho 465, Kamigyo-k…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Mediastinoscopic esophagectomy is a minimally invasive approach that avoids thoracotomy and single-lung ventilation. We previously performed this procedure using hand-assisted laparoscopic surgery (HALS) and recently established a totally laparoscopic transhiatal approach. This retrospective, non-randomized study reported laparoscopic technique and compared the feasibility and surgical outcomes of these approaches. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 262 patients who underwent radical mediastinoscopic esophagectomy using left cervical and transhiatal approaches at the Kyoto Prefectural University of Medicine between January 2020 and June 2026. HALS was performed in 202 patients and laparoscopy in 60 patients. Surgical procedures and perioperative outcomes were compared between the groups. RESULTS: Blood loss and total operative time did not differ significantly between the groups, although the transhiatal procedure tended to require a longer operative time with laparoscopy (p = 0.09). The approach used for middle mediastinal lymphadenectomy was similar between the two groups (43% vs. 35%, p = 0.28), and the overall number of dissected lymph nodes, excluding the upper mediastinal and cervical nodes, was comparable. However, significantly more abdominal lymph nodes were dissected with laparoscopy than with HALS (17.9 vs. 15.7, p = 0.04). Laparoscopic gastric mobilization and lymph node dissection were safely performed, with no significant differences in the rate of postoperative complications or curability. CONCLUSIONS: The totally laparoscopic transhiatal technique is a feasible and safe approach for mediastinoscopic esophagectomy, with surgical outcomes comparable to those of HALS and not inferior abdominal lymph node dissection. It may be particularly advantageous for cases requiring meticulous abdominal lymphadenectomy.

papers.title_zh: From Thoracotomy to Robotic Platforms in Thoracic Surgery: Technical Evolution, Simulation-Based Training, and Surgical Outcomes.
papers.title_en: From Thoracotomy to Robotic Platforms in Thoracic Surgery: Technical Evolution, Simulation-Based Training, and Surgical Outcomes.
papers.authors: Piazzolla M, Sampietro D, Delcuratolo MD, Girotti PNC, Muscarella LA, Parente P
papers.affiliation_highlight: Unit of Thoracic Surgery, Fondazione IRCCS Casa Sollievo Della Sofferenza, 71013 San Giovanni Rotondo, Italy.
papers.abstract_en: Thoracic surgery has progressively moved from open thoracotomy to video-assisted and robot-assisted approaches, reducing access-related trauma while changing the technical environment in which pulmonary resections are performed and taught. This narrative review examines the clinical evolution of open, video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS), and robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS), with particular attention to the evidence supporting their perioperative and oncological outcomes, the learning curves associated with minimally invasive surgery, and the role of simulation-based training. Randomized trials now provide robust evidence that VATS improve postoperative recovery compared with thoracotomy in appropriately selected patients with predominantly early-stage non-small cell lung cancer, without compromising long-term oncological outcomes. Randomized comparisons between RATS and VATS support RATS as an oncologically acceptable minimally invasive alternative and suggest advantages in selected technical endpoints, particularly blood loss and lymph node retrieval, but do not demonstrate consistent superiority in major clinical or survival outcomes. Learning curves vary according to previous experience, case complexity, supervision, institutional volume, and the endpoint used to define competence, making fixed case-number thresholds an incomplete measure of proficiency. Simulation can improve selected technical skills and provide objective performance assessment, although evidence becomes progressively less robust when moving from simulator performance to operating room transfer and patient-level outcomes. Surgical approach, therefore, should be interpreted within a broader framework that includes patient and tumour characteristics, oncological quality, surgical expertise, institutional resources, and structured training.

papers.title_zh: Systemic, Pleural, and Alveolar Cytokine Responses After Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Versus Open Lobectomy for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Prospective Observational Study.
papers.title_en: Systemic, Pleural, and Alveolar Cytokine Responses After Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Versus Open Lobectomy for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Prospective Observational Study.
papers.authors: Ancın B, Özercan MM, Yılmaz Y, Uysal S, Kumbasar U, Dikmen E, Sarıbaş Z, Doğan R et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Faculty of Medicine, Hacettepe University, Ankara 06100, Türkiye.
papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Surgical access and one-lung ventilation (OLV) may generate distinct systemic and local inflammatory responses after lung resection. We compared perioperative cytokine profiles in serum, pleural fluid, and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and open thoracotomy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods: This prospective, single-center, non-randomized observational study included 40 adults undergoing anatomical lobectomy with mediastinal lymph-node dissection (VATS, n = 20; open thoracotomy, n = 20). Surgical access was selected according to patient preference. TNF-α, IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10 were measured in serial serum and pleural-fluid samples and in BAL from both lungs before OLV and after resection. Results: Serum and pleural-fluid cytokines peaked at 4 h in both groups. Exploratory pointwise comparisons showed that at 24 h, serum TNF-α (4.89 [IQR, 4.43-5.92] vs. 4.01 [IQR, 3.75-5.12] pg/mL; p = 0.010), IL-6 (150.22 [IQR, 136.90-194.66] vs. 108.00 [IQR, 100.46-125.88] pg/mL; p < 0.001), and IL-8 (66.83 [IQR, 57.70-82.82] vs. 43.62 [IQR, 32.89-50.59] pg/mL; p = 0.001) were higher after thoracotomy than after VATS; differences at 48 h persisted for TNF-α (2.48 [IQR, 1.86-3.04] vs. 1.99 [IQR, 1.19-2.23] pg/mL; p = 0.010) and IL-8 (16.92 [IQR, 15.09-23.99] vs. 7.42 [IQR, 6.44-11.30] pg/mL; p < 0.001). Pleural-fluid IL-6 at 24 h and IL-8 at 48 h were also higher after thoracotomy, whereas BAL cytokines did not differ significantly by approach. Longitudinal GEE analyses showed significant approach-by-time interactions for serum TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-8 and for pleural-fluid IL-8, but not for pleural-fluid IL-6. Conclusions: VATS was associated with a lower systemic proinflammatory response than open thoracotomy, while differences in the pleural compartment were more limited and no detectable difference was observed in early alveolar cytokine responses. These findings highlight compartment-specific differences in perioperative inflammatory responses between VATS and open thoracotomy.

papers.title_zh: Aerosolized prostaglandin E1 improves oxygenation during one-lung ventilation: A dose-finding randomized controlled trial.
papers.title_en: Aerosolized prostaglandin E1 improves oxygenation during one-lung ventilation: A dose-finding randomized controlled trial.
papers.authors: Li P, Hu X, Li P, Xing L, Wang Q, Gu L, Wu C
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Anesthesiology, Jiangsu Cancer Hospital & Jiangsu Institute of Cancer Research & The Affiliated Cancer Hos…
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the effects of varying doses of aerosolized Prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) on oxygenation and intrapulmonary shunt fraction (Qs/Qt) during One-Lung Ventilation (OLV) under 60% Fraction of Inspired Oxygen (FiO2). Secondary objectives included evaluating the impact on intraoperative hypoxemia, postoperative Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS), and Postoperative Pulmonary Complications (PPCs). DESIGN: A prospective, single center, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial. SETTING: The study was conducted at a single academic medical center. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 160 patients aged 65‒84 years, with American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status II or III and Body Mass Index (BMI) < 30 kg/m2, undergoing elective esophageal cancer surgery were enrolled. Patients with certain comorbidities, respiratory diseases, or contraindications to PGE1 were excluded. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned to one of four groups: Group L ‒ Received 0.1 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group M ‒ Received 0.2 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group H ‒ Received 0.3 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group C (control) ‒ Received normal saline nebulization. Nebulization was performed for 10-minutes via a modified breathing circuit into the ventilated lung before initiating OLV. MEASUREMENTS: Arterial blood gas parameters (arterial partial pressure of oxygen, PaO2; arterial oxygen saturation, SaO2; arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide, PaCO2), hemodynamic variables (Mean Arterial Pressure [MAP]; Heart Rate [HR]), respiratory mechanics (Peak airway pressure [Ppeak]; dynamic lung compliance [Cdyn]), PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and Qs/Qt were recorded at multiple time points during OLV. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia and hypotension, PPCs within 7-days, and CPIS on postoperative day-2 were also assessed. MAIN RESULTS: All PGE1 groups showed significantly improved PaO2, SaO2, and PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and reduced Qs/Qt during the first 30-minutes of OLV compared to the control group. The High-dose group (H) demonstrated the greatest improvement in oxygenation. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia [Group L: 0/40 (0%), Group M: 0/40 (0%), Group H: 0/40 (0%), Group C: 3/40 (7.5%)] and hypotension did not differ significantly among groups; however, the hypoxemia finding was exploratory as the study was not powered for this endpoint. No significant differences were observed in PPCs incidence among groups, but group H was associated with a lower CPIS on postoperative day-2 compared to group C. Hemodynamic changes were transient and clinically manageable. CONCLUSIONS: Nebulized PGE1 at doses of 0.1-0.3 μg/kg improves oxygenation and reduces Qs/Qt during OLV under 60% oxygen, with the 0.3 μg/kg dose being most effective. It did not significantly reduce the incidence of PPCs within 7-days. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia was lower in the PGE1 groups (0/120) compared with the control group (3/40), but this was an exploratory finding as the study was not powered for this endpoint. The higher dose (0.3 μg/kg) was associated with a lower CPIS on postoperative day-2 (3.3 vs. 4.1), but CPIS is a surrogate marker, and this finding should be interpreted as exploratory. The clinical significance of this small difference is uncertain, as changes of this magnitude are below the typically recognized thresholds for meaningful clinical improvement. Hemodynamic monitoring is recommended when using higher doses of PGE1.

papers.title_zh: Effectiveness of Pharmaceutical Care in Reducing the Incidence of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-related Pneumonitis in Patients with NSCLC: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.title_en: Effectiveness of Pharmaceutical Care in Reducing the Incidence of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-related Pneumonitis in Patients with NSCLC: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Luo C, Lai Y, Zhang W, Lu H, Luo H, Wei L, Lin X, Zhou C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pharmacy, The First Affiliated Hospital, Guangzhou Medical University, Guangzhou, China; Guangzhou Medical…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pneumonitis (CIP) remains a potentially life-threatening adverse event that may be mitigated through structured pharmaceutical care interventions. OBJECTIVE: To assess the effectiveness of pharmacy services in reducing the occurrence of CIP among patients with NSCLC receiving ICIs. METHODS: Patients who underwent immunotherapy at our hospital between November, 2023 to September, 2024 were selected and randomized into the control and intervention groups (105 patients each). Intervention group received 6 months of pharmacy services, and CIP occurrence, clinical efficacy, medication adherence, and quality of life at 3, 6, and 9 months were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the intervention group had a significantly lower CIP incidence and immunotherapy suspension rate due to CIP (2.9% vs. 9.5%, P = 0.043), as well as significantly improved medication adherence at all time points (P < 0.05). The intervention group also had lower CIP severity and longer onset time (8.6 months vs. 6.2 months), along with numerically higher ORR (40.6% vs. 30.3%) and DCR (81.2% vs. 71.7%), and a favorable trend in emotional function scores; however, these differences did not reach statistical significance. CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacy care can reduce the incidence and severity, and increase the onset time of CIP, thus enhancing drug safety.

papers.title_zh: Thoracoscopic versus endoscopic resection for esophageal leiomyoma: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
papers.title_en: Thoracoscopic versus endoscopic resection for esophageal leiomyoma: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Zhang S, Geng Z, Hu Y, Yang X, Jiang D, Yin J, Lin M, Wang H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, No 180, Fenglin Road, Xuhui District, Shanghai, 20…
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Esophageal leiomyoma is the most common benign mesenchymal tumor of the esophagus. Minimally invasive management is performed by thoracoscopic surgery or endoscopic resection, but comparative evidence remains limited. This study evaluated perioperative outcomes and treatment-selection patterns for thoracic and endoscopic resection. METHODS: Patients with pathologically confirmed leiomyoma who underwent resection between January 2015 and September 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients with malignant components, biopsy/fine-needle aspiration only, or incomplete data were excluded. A 1:1 propensity score matching analysis was performed using nearest-neighbor matching with a caliper of 0.1, matching age, sex, tumor location, and maximal tumor diameter. RESULTS: A total of 1,348 patients were included in the primary analysis: 132 underwent minimally invasive thoracic surgery and 1,216 underwent endoscopic resection. In the endoscopic group, 54.5% underwent endoscopic submucosal dissection and 45.5% underwent submucosal tunneling endoscopic resection. In the MIS group, 62 patients (47.0%) received intraoperative endoscopic assistance. Endoscopic resection was associated with shorter operative duration (41.9 ± 39.9 vs 114.8 ± 71.0 min, p < 0.001) and shorter postoperative hospital stay (median 2.0 vs 5.0 days, p < 0.001), whereas minimally invasive thoracic surgery was used for larger tumors (median 5.0 vs 1.3 cm, p < 0.001). After matching, 113 pairs were analyzed. Endoscopic resection remained associated with shorter operative duration (73.7 ± 62.9 vs 111.6 ± 61.5 min, p = 0.009) and shorter postoperative hospital stay (median 3.0 vs 5.0 days, p < 0.001). In the matched cohort, nasogastric tube placement and delayed stay of 5 days or longer were less common after endoscopic resection. CONCLUSIONS: Endoscopic resection was associated with faster postoperative recovery in patients with esophageal leiomyoma, whereas thoracic surgery remained important for larger tumors and complex lesions. These findings support a size- and location-oriented treatment strategy rather than a universal preference for either approach.

papers.title_zh: Rethinking Age Limits for Robotic Lung Cancer Resection: Contemporary Short-Term Outcomes in Octogenarians.
papers.title_en: Rethinking Age Limits for Robotic Lung Cancer Resection: Contemporary Short-Term Outcomes in Octogenarians.
papers.authors: Bagrodia N, Djabri D, Boualoy T, Lopez K, Baiu I, D'souza DM, Merritt RE, Kneuertz PJ et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Thoracic Surgery, Department of Surgery, The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, 410 W 10th Ave., C…
papers.abstract_en: Objective: We sought to assess the outcomes of octogenarians compared to a reference group of younger patients undergoing robotic anatomic lung resection for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to better understand the postoperative expectations of this elderly patient population. Methods: A prospectively maintained Institutional General Thoracic Surgery Database was queried for patients aged 80 years and above (octogenarians) and 65-75 years (reference group) undergoing robotic lobectomy or segmentectomy for NSCLC between 2015 and 2026. Clinical data and postoperative outcomes were collected and compared using both unadjusted and 1:1 propensity-score matching. Results: In total, 822 patients were identified: 101 in the octogenarian group (mean age 82.4 years [standard deviation 2.2]) and 721 in the reference group (69.7 [3.1], p < 0.001). Postoperative complications that were more frequent in octogenarians included pneumothorax requiring chest tube insertion (5.9% vs. 2.2%, p = 0.043), atrial arrhythmias (18.8% vs. 9.2%, p = 0.005), and urinary tract infections (6.9% vs. 1.7%, p = 0.005). Air leak, atelectasis, pneumonia, respiratory failure, pleural effusion, empyema, and delirium did not differ between the groups. After propensity matching, there were no significant differences in the aforementioned postoperative outcomes. While the unadjusted length of stay was longer in octogenarians (4 days [interquartile range 3-5] vs. 3 [2-5], p = 0.012), this was no longer significant after matching (4 [3-5] vs. 3 [2-5], p = 0.369). There were no statistically significant differences in 30-day readmission rates (p = 0.197) or 30-day mortality (p = 0.781) after propensity-score matching. Conclusions: Among carefully selected octogenarians undergoing robotic anatomic lung resection for NSCLC, no statistically significant differences in short-term postoperative outcomes were detected compared with patients aged 65-75 years after adjustment for baseline differences. These findings support individualized surgical selection beyond chronologic age alone.

papers.title_zh: Metastasis Extraction From Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Clinical Notes Using Large Language Model-Based Classification: Retrospective Comparative Study.
papers.title_en: Metastasis Extraction From Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Clinical Notes Using Large Language Model-Based Classification: Retrospective Comparative Study.
papers.authors: Balaji S, Campbell K, Chen RZ, Smith D, Reyna MA, Sarker A, Wallach JD, Parikh RB et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Biomedical Informatics, School of Medicine, Emory University, Atlanta, GA, United States.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Identification of metastasis status in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a critical part of understanding disease prognosis, treatment courses, trial eligibility, and population-level cancer surveillance. However, metastasis status is inconsistently recorded in structured cancer registry fields, since manual abstraction of clinical notes is often an error-prone process. This challenge highlights an opportunity for leveraging large language models (LLMs) to conduct high-scale metastasis extraction from real-world clinical documentation. OBJECTIVE: We conducted a retrospective, multicohort comparative evaluation of 3 distinct LLMs for 2 independent classification tasks: overall metastasis presence at any site and brain/central nervous system (CNS) metastasis presence. We evaluated model performance on 2 independent NSCLC cohorts: one with registry labels and another with manual annotations. We further explored whether our methods could analyze clinical documentation and recover missing information in structured registry fields. METHODS: Patient cohorts were derived from the Winship Cancer Institute. Cohort 1 (n=579 patients; 24,887 notes across 69 note types; 2023-2025) used registry-linked metastasis fields as the reference standard. Cohort 2 (n=22 patients; 644 radiology notes; 2010-2021) was drawn from 2 completed randomized trials and used dual-annotated labels (Cohen κ: 0.93 overall metastasis; 0.88 CNS metastasis) as the reference standard. We fine-tuned the GatorTron-base encoder model for each independent binary classification task. We evaluated MedGemma-27B-text and Llama 3.1-70B using zero-shot prompting. A separate cohort of 675 patients with missing registry labels was used for an exploratory missingness-recovery analysis, validated against annotations of a random subsample. Our best-performing model was used to conduct further site-specific metastasis classification, based on available registry data. RESULTS: More than half (675/1260, 54%) of initially identified cohort 1 patients had missing or unknown registry metastasis labels. MedGemma demonstrated the best performance in overall metastasis classification (cohort 1: F1-score=0.80; cohort 2 patient-level: F1-score=1.0; cohort 2 note-level: F1-score=0.93). For brain/CNS metastasis, Llama3 performed best in both cohorts (cohort 1: F1-score=0.79; cohort 2 patient-level: F1-score=0.93; cohort 2 note-level: F1-score=0.86). The fine-tuned GatorTron model showed strong performance for classification of overall metastasis in cohort 1 (F1-score=0.72). Error analysis indicated that several model errors reflected incomplete registry labels, ambiguous clinical language, or missing documentation. In the exploratory recovery analysis, model predictions agreed with manual annotations at an accuracy of 0.90 and F1-score of 0.89. Additional site-specific metastasis classification by MedGemma demonstrated high performance for liver metastasis (F1-score=0.82) and bone metastasis (F1-score=0.79). CONCLUSIONS: All models demonstrated relatively high performance. The zero-shot generative models were more robust to nuanced documentation and context-dependent brain/CNS metastasis extraction. The fine-tuned encoder model demonstrated strong classification performance but may have been limited by potential inaccuracies in the registry reference standards during model training. This study further demonstrated the potential of LLMs in recovering plausible structured labels from narrative text, complementing cancer registries for metastasis ascertainment.

papers.title_zh: Durvalumab Plus High-Dose Radiation in NSCLC III: Long-Term Results from the Austrian Radio-Oncological Lung Cancer Study Association Registry (ALLSTAR).
papers.title_en: Durvalumab Plus High-Dose Radiation in NSCLC III: Long-Term Results from the Austrian Radio-Oncological Lung Cancer Study Association Registry (ALLSTAR).
papers.authors: Hörmandinger K, Ruznic E, Klebermass M, Grambozov B, Feurstein P, Karner J, Gruber G, Heilmann M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Comprehensive Cancer Centre, Department of Radiation Oncology, Medical University Innsbruck, A-6020 Innsbruck, Austria.
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Chemoradioimmunotherapy (CRIT) with 60-66 Gy is the standard of care (SoC) for non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) UICC stage III. The aim of this real-world data (RWD) study was to report the long-term impact of Durvalumab and radiation dose escalation on clinical outcomes. MATERIAL AND METHODS: ALLSTAR is a nationwide prospective multicentre registry for NSCLC UICC stage III, in which 12/14 Austrian centres participated (ethics approval number: 1002/2019). The basis for the current analysis is the third data extraction, which was completed on 2 June 2025. Apart from the SoC, alternative dose-fractionation and sequential CRT concepts >66 Gy were also permitted. Durvalumab maintenance treatment for one year was administered at the discretion of the tumour board at each centre. RESULTS: Compared to prior analyses by our group, 40 individuals who completed follow-up (FUP) were added to this final analysis, leading to a total patient population of 228 (156 CRT plus Durvalumab; 72 CRT). In 156 patients, Durvalumab was added to CRT, while 72 received CRT only. The median FUP periods were 41.0 (95%-CI: 36.7-45.4) and 37.8 months (95%-CI: 31.4-44.1) for the Durvalumab and CRT cohort, respectively. Radiation dose escalation combined with Durvalumab treatment was associated with a nominally higher ITC of 37 months (95%-CI: 24.5-not reached) compared with 17.7 months (95%-CI: 14.9-not reached) in patients receiving neither dose escalation nor Durvalumab (N = 135; HR = 0.61; 95%-CI: 0.37-1.006; p-value 0.051). With Durvalumab maintenance, a median PFS of 22.8 months (95%-CI: 19.4-38.3) was observed compared to 16.5 months (95%-CI: 12.6-24.5) without (N = 228; HR = 0.61; 95%-CI: 0.42-0.88; p-value 0.0071). Median OS was 52.6 months (95%-CI: 39.5-not reached) with Durvalumab compared to 27.4 months (95%-CI: 18.7-not reached) without (N = 228; HR = 0.52; 95%-CI: 0.34-0.78; log-rank p-value < 0.002). Median time to death or distant metastasis (TTDM) was 33.3 months (95%-CI: 23.5-45) in the Durvalumab cohort compared to 18.7 months (95%-CI: 14.8-not reached) in the CRT cohort (N = 228; HR = 0.60; 95%-CI: 0.42-0.89; log-rank p-value 0.01). Median time to death or local relapse (TDLR) with Durvalumab was 30.4 months (95%-CI: 23.5-51.1) compared to 17.2 months (95%-CI: 14.8-25.7) without (N = 226; HR = 0.58; 95%-CI: 0.40-0.83; log-rank p-value < 0.003). CONCLUSION: This final RWD analysis implies both a beneficial effect of high-dose irradiation combined with Durvalumab on ITC and the long-lasting impact of Durvalumab on PFS, OS, TTDM, and TDLR.

papers.title_zh: Prognostic Value of Pretreatment Modified Glasgow Prognostic Score in Nivolumab-Treated Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.title_en: Prognostic Value of Pretreatment Modified Glasgow Prognostic Score in Nivolumab-Treated Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Biter S, Kıdı MM, Aydınalp Camadan Y, İpek ŞA, Asarkaya E, Asoğlu H, Bayram E, Köşeci T et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Oncology, Çukurova University Faculty of Medicine, Adana 01330, Turkey.
papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have become a standard treatment option for advanced/metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, considerable heterogeneity exists among patients regarding treatment response and survival. This study aimed to determine whether the pretreatment modified Glasgow Prognostic Score (mGPS), a marker of systemic inflammation and nutritional status, is prognostically associated with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced/metastatic NSCLC treated with nivolumab at a single tertiary oncology center. Methods: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 130 adult patients with histologically confirmed advanced/metastatic NSCLC who received nivolumab at the Department of Medical Oncology, Çukurova University Faculty of Medicine. The pretreatment mGPS (0, 1, or 2), derived from baseline serum C-reactive protein (CRP) and albumin levels, was analyzed in relation to PFS and OS using the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression. The prognostic value of mGPS was tested in multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, histology, brain metastasis, liver metastasis, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR); the proportional hazards assumption was formally tested, and the incremental discriminative contribution of mGPS was assessed using bootstrap resampling. Results: Among 130 patients, 83.8% received nivolumab as second-line therapy. Pretreatment mGPS was 0, 1, and 2 in 40 (30.8%), 55 (42.3%), and 35 (26.9%) patients, respectively. Median OS was not reached, 9.7 months, and 3.0 months across mGPS 0, 1, and 2, respectively; corresponding median PFS values were 10.2, 4.8, and 3.0 months (log-rank p < 0.001 for both endpoints). After adjustment for age, sex, ECOG performance status, histology, brain metastasis, liver metastasis, and NLR, each one-point increase in mGPS remained associated with worse OS (adjusted HR 2.38; 95% CI 1.64-3.46; p < 0.001) and PFS (adjusted HR 1.81; 95% CI 1.32-2.48; p < 0.001), independent of the covariates included in the model. The proportional hazards assumption held for mGPS in both models. Addition of mGPS to the clinical-variables-only model was associated with higher model discrimination (Harrell's C-index: 0.676 to 0.737 for OS and 0.620 to 0.666 for PFS), a difference confirmed as statistically significant by bootstrap resampling (2000 iterations; 95% CI for the difference excluding zero, p < 0.001 for both endpoints). Conclusions: Pretreatment mGPS is a simple, readily available marker that shows a robust prognostic-rather than treatment-predictive-association with both OS and PFS in patients with advanced/metastatic NSCLC treated predominantly as second-line nivolumab monotherapy. Its addition to established clinical variables was associated with a statistically significant, though modest, improvement in prognostic discrimination. These findings require prospective, multicenter validation, including in first-line immunotherapy settings, before mGPS can be recommended for routine clinical risk stratification.

papers.title_zh: Preoperative CRP-Albumin-Lymphocyte (CALLY) Index Is Associated with Survival but Does Not Predict Anastomotic Leak or Major Morbidity After Minimally Invasive Esophagectomy.
papers.title_en: Preoperative CRP-Albumin-Lymphocyte (CALLY) Index Is Associated with Survival but Does Not Predict Anastomotic Leak or Major Morbidity After Minimally Invasive Esophagectomy.
papers.authors: Çağlıyan Ö, Düzköylü Y, Karaköse E, Kılavuz H, Şevik HO, Tekin O, Yoran ED, Topgül OH et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Gastroenterological Surgery, Başakşehir Çam and Sakura City Hospital, 34480 Istanbul, Turkey.
papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: The CRP-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index is promoted both as a marker of postoperative morbidity and as a prognostic factor for survival. These claims are rarely tested together, thresholds usually come from the dataset in which they are then tested, and the index is seldom compared against its components. We examined both in one minimally invasive esophagectomy cohort. Methods: Consecutive esophagectomies with a thoracoscopic or robotic thoracic phase at one centre were reviewed. The index was derived from the preoperative albumin, C-reactive protein, and lymphocyte count. Short-term endpoints were major morbidity (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ 3) and anastomotic leak; survival was analysed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox methods, with internal cut-points stress-tested by bootstrapping. Results: Of 154 esophagectomies screened, 22 open or transhiatal procedures and one exploration without resection were excluded, leaving 131 patients. Major morbidity occurred in 39 (29.8%), and leak in 21 (16.0%). The index discriminated neither: area under the curve 0.556 (95% CI: 0.450-0.663) and 0.481 (95% CI: 0.339-0.623). Over a median follow-up of 31.0 months, there were 39 deaths, and median survival was 62.1 months. Here, the index behaved differently: each unit of log-CALLY carried a hazard ratio of 0.776 (95% CI: 0.643-0.936, p = 0.008), and three-year survival rose from 48.5% in the lowest tertile to 77.1% in the highest (trend p = 0.020). The association held after adjustment for stage and nodal status (0.749, 95% CI: 0.609-0.922, p = 0.006), lifting the concordance index of a stage-based model from 0.699 to 0.741. However, entered with CRP, the index lost significance. Conclusions: The index said nothing useful about early surgical morbidity yet was independently associated with survival, although that signal did not survive adjustment for CRP alone. It belongs with prognostic markers rather than perioperative risk scores.

papers.title_zh: Pulmonary Resection for Bronchiectasis: Perioperative and Follow-Up Outcomes in a VATS-Dominant Cohort.
papers.title_en: Pulmonary Resection for Bronchiectasis: Perioperative and Follow-Up Outcomes in a VATS-Dominant Cohort.
papers.authors: Can A, Yıldıran H
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Faculty of Medicine, Selcuk University, Selçuklu, Konya 42131, Türkiye.
papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Surgical resection remains an important treatment option for selected patients with bronchiectasis who have persistent symptoms, recurrent pulmonary infections, or hemoptysis despite medical therapy. This study evaluated perioperative and follow-up outcomes after pulmonary resection for bronchiectasis in a predominantly video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS)-treated cohort. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort included patients who underwent pulmonary resection for bronchiectasis between January 2009 and January 2026. Baseline and follow-up data were analyzed at the patient level, whereas operative and perioperative outcomes were assessed at the procedure level. Follow-up duration was calculated from the most recent resection to the last available clinical assessment. Results: Thirty-four patients underwent 37 pulmonary resections. Multilobar disease was present in 14 procedures (37.8%). VATS was used in 30 procedures (81.1%) and thoracotomy in 7 (18.9%). Median hospital stay was 11 days (range, 4-41). Postoperative complications occurred after 6 procedures (16.2%), with no 30-day mortality. Complete or partial symptomatic improvement occurred after 31 procedures (83.8%). Median follow-up was 20.8 months (interquartile range, 5.9-58.8; range, 0.4-144.2). At the last available clinical assessment, 23 patients (67.6%) had no recorded symptoms; recurrent hemoptysis occurred in 1 (2.9%) and recurrent pulmonary infection in 2 (5.9%). Conclusions: Pulmonary resection for bronchiectasis was associated with acceptable morbidity, no 30-day mortality, and a high rate of postoperative clinical improvement in this VATS-dominant cohort. Most patients had no recorded symptoms at their last available clinical assessment, while recurrent hemoptysis and pulmonary infection were uncommon.

papers.title_zh: Routine pulmonary wound closure after thoracoscopic sublobar resection for congenital lung malformations in children: impact on early recovery, one-year CT-based lung expansion, and the learning curve.
papers.title_en: Routine pulmonary wound closure after thoracoscopic sublobar resection for congenital lung malformations in children: impact on early recovery, one-year CT-based lung expansion, and the learning curve.
papers.authors: Huang JX, Hong SM, Hong JJ, Liu JF, Qiu L, Zeng RJ, Chen Q, Wang ZC et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery, College of Clinical Medicine for Obstetrics & Gynecology and Pediatrics, Fujian Ch…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The necessity of routine pulmonary parenchymal wound closure following thoracoscopic sublobar resection for congenital lung malformations (CLMs) in children remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the association of routine wound closure with drainage-related recovery, perioperative outcomes, one-year computed tomography (CT)-based lung re-expansion, and the procedural learning curve. METHODS: Consecutive children who underwent thoracoscopic sublobar resection for CLMs between January 2021 and March 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. The cohort was divided into a non-closure group and a routine-closure group according to wound management strategy. Pulmonary wound closure was performed using an absorbable barbed suture, generally proceeding from the peripheral or lower-tension side toward the central or higher-tension region. Irregular wounds were managed by initiating closure from multiple peripheral points converging centrally while preserving the natural axis of residual bronchi and vasculature. Outcomes included chest tube duration, drainage volume, prolonged air leak, chest tube reinsertion, postoperative hospital stay, perioperative complications, one-year CT-based volumetric indices, and closure-time learning curve metrics. RESULTS: A total of 285 children were included, comprising 75 in the non-closure group and 210 in the closure group. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Compared with the non-closure group, the closure group exhibited significantly shorter chest tube duration (0.87 ± 0.74 vs. 2.81 ± 1.99 days, P < 0.001), lower postoperative drainage volume (2.12 ± 0.70 vs. 7.21 ± 2.58 mL/kg/day, P < 0.001), reduced rates of prolonged air leak and drainage failure, and shorter postoperative hospital stay (5.63 ± 0.83 vs. 7.68 ± 2.10 days, P < 0.001). At one-year follow-up, CT-based volumetric assessment revealed no evidence that wound closure restricted residual lung re-expansion. Closure time decreased from approximately 22 min in the early phase to 11 min in the late phase, with learning curve inflection points identified at cases 47 and 135. CONCLUSIONS: Routine pulmonary wound closure following thoracoscopic sublobar resection for pediatric CLMs was associated with improved drainage-related recovery and shorter hospitalization, without compromising one-year lung re-expansion on CT. Although closure adds a procedural step, efficiency improved substantially with experience, demonstrating a quantifiable learning curve.

papers.title_zh: Lazertinib plus pemetrexed and carboplatin in patients with EGFR-mutant advanced non-small cell lung cancer after progression on lazertinib.
papers.title_en: Lazertinib plus pemetrexed and carboplatin in patients with EGFR-mutant advanced non-small cell lung cancer after progression on lazertinib.
papers.authors: Hong MH, Shim BY, Kim CG, Kim YS, Lee S, Lee Y, Ahn BC, Ahn MJ et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Medical Oncology, Yonsei Cancer Center, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul, Korea.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Therapeutic strategies after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) remain suboptimal in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We investigated whether continuing EGFR inhibition with lazertinib combined with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy could extend clinical benefit after progression on prior lazertinib. METHODS: In the multicenter, single-arm, phase II LUCAS study (NCT05786430), patients with advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC who had progressed on lazertinib received lazertinib 240 mg daily plus pemetrexed-carboplatin for four cycles, followed by maintenance lazertinib and pemetrexed. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), intracranial PFS, safety, and exploratory ctDNA analyses. RESULTS: Of 86 patients, 46.5% had a history of brain metastases. Among 81 response-evaluable patients, median PFS was 9.5 months (95% CI: 6.3-9.6; one-sided p = 0.017 against a null median of 6.0 months). In the safety population, median OS was 15.9 months (95% CI: 12.4-20.0) and ORR was 36.0% (95% CI: 26.0-47.1). Outcomes were similar irrespective of prior lazertinib line or EGFR subtype. Baseline ctDNA-detected EGFR amplification was associated with inferior survival. Among 36 patients with radiologically evident baseline brain metastases, median intracranial PFS was 9.9 months (95% CI: 7.8-16.4) with infrequent isolated intracranial progression. Grade ≥ 3 adverse events occurred in 69.8%, predominantly hematologic, without new safety signals. CONCLUSIONS: Continuation of lazertinib with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy after progression on prior lazertinib was associated with meaningful systemic and intracranial activity and manageable toxicity. Randomized evaluation is required to establish the incremental benefit of lazertinib continuation.

papers.title_zh: Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic McKeown oesophagectomy using i-gel™ and continuous pressure support ventilation: A case report.
papers.title_en: Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic McKeown oesophagectomy using i-gel™ and continuous pressure support ventilation: A case report.
papers.authors: Ranjan M, Sirohiya P, Maurya P, Kumar N
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Onco-Anaesthesia and Palliative Medicine, Dr.
papers.abstract_en: Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (NIVATS) minimises airway trauma and ventilator-induced lung injury, yet its application in complex, multi-phase McKeown oesophagectomy is seldom reported. A 32-year-old female (40 kg, 140 cm and body mass index: 20.4 kg/m 2 ) presented for McKeown minimally invasive oesophagectomy following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. We employed a 'less invasive anaesthesia' strategy combining T9-T10 thoracic epidural analgesia with Bispectral Index-guided target-controlled propofol infusion. Continuous pressure support ventilation (16 cmH 2 O above a positive end-expiratory pressure of 5 cmH 2 O) with preserved spontaneous breathing was maintained via a size 3 i-gel™ throughout surgery; neuromuscular blockade and controlled mechanical ventilation were not used at any stage. Surgical exposure was optimised via right-sided capnothorax. The resulting permissive hypercapnia was haemodynamically well-tolerated. Recovery was uneventful, and the airway device was removed after protective airway reflexes had returned. She was discharged from the hospital on post-operative day 6 without any complications. NIVATS for McKeown oesophagectomy may be feasible in carefully selected patients.

papers.title_zh: Multimodal Transformer Integrating CT and Pathology for Postoperative Risk Stratification in Stage I Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.title_en: Multimodal Transformer Integrating CT and Pathology for Postoperative Risk Stratification in Stage I Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Wang L, Zong Y, Li X, Tang H, Yao J, Cao Y, Luo Y, Li J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiology, Jinling Hospital, The First School of Clinical Medicine, Southern Medical University, 305 Zhong…
papers.abstract_en: Purpose To develop and evaluate an interpretable, multimodal deep learning model to improve postoperative risk stratification and predict adjuvant therapy benefit in stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Materials and Methods In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with stage I NSCLC, a multimodal model called the Deep Learning-Radiomic-Text Transformer (DLRTransformer) was developed by integrating multiview 2.5-dimensional deep learning features from CT scans, radiomics, clinical variables, and prognostic embeddings extracted from pathology reports using a large language model. A central transformer architecture fuses these features to predict disease-free survival. Model performance was evaluated on independent external datasets and compared with guideline-based risk stratification. Associations between model-derived risk scores and tumor microenvironment features were analyzed to assess biologic interpretability. Results A total of 1073 patients (mean age ± SD, 60.8 years ± 9.8; 550 male) were enrolled from five centers. On external datasets, DLRTransformer demonstrated robust prognostic performance (concordance index, 0.77-0.78), outperforming the guideline-based risk stratification (concordance index, 0.60-0.65). Risk scores were associated with tumor microenvironment phenotypes, including increased neoplastic cellularity and reduced tertiary lymphoid structures. A treatment-by-risk interaction was observed (interaction hazard ratio [HR], 0.14; 95% CI: 0.06, 0.32; P < .01). In propensity score-matched subcohorts, adjuvant therapy improved disease-free survival in high-risk patients (HR, 0.30; 95% CI: 0.11, 0.84; P = .02) but not in low-risk patients (HR, 1.70; 95% CI: 0.97, 2.99; P = .06). Conclusion The DLRTransformer improved postoperative risk stratification compared with guideline-based risk stratification and identified patients with stage I NSCLC who benefited from adjuvant therapy. Keywords: Deep Learning, Large Language Models LLMs, CT, Prognosis & Prediction, Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC), Multimodal Deep Learning, Risk Stratification, Adjuvant Therapy, Tumor Microenvironment (TME) Supplemental material is available for this article. © The Author(s) 2026. papers.title_zh: Nodule Dye-Localization Using Interventional Fluoroscopy for Image-Guided Sublobar Lung Resection.
papers.title_en: Nodule Dye-Localization Using Interventional Fluoroscopy for Image-Guided Sublobar Lung Resection.
papers.authors: Wu YL, Kam KH, Liang CY, Lai YT, Jeng TH, Lee CC, Wu YF, Yang YC et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Thoracic Surgery, Department of Surgery, Ditmanson Medical Foundation Chia-Yi Christian Hospital, Chia-Yi, T…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Precise localization is critical for sublobar resection of small pulmonary nodules. We evaluated the safety, technical efficiency, and clinical outcomes of preoperative percutaneous dye-localization using a cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-enabled flat-panel detector interventional fluoroscopy system in a hybrid operating room (HOR). METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 74 consecutive patients (137 lesions) who underwent image-guided localization followed by video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) sublobar resection (wedge resection or segmentectomy) between 2022 and 2023 at Chia-Yi Christian Hospital. Procedural workflow, localization success, surgical margins, and perioperative outcomes were systematically analyzed. RESULTS: Technical localization success was achieved in 100% of lesions (mean nodule diameter: 8.59 ± 4.85 mm). The procedure required a mean of 1.31 ± 0.67 puncture attempts per lesion at a mean depth of 5.22 ± 1.86 cm. Procedure-related pneumothorax occurred in 29.7% (22/74) of patients, with 14.9% (11/74) requiring pigtail catheter drainage; pneumothorax occurrence was significantly associated with multiple puncture attempts (p < 0.001) and lower-lobe lesions (p = 0.001). Lower-lobe location was significantly associated with requiring more puncture attempts (p = 0.028). For malignant lesions, the mean pathological resection margin was 17.16 ± 8.73 mm, with 92.31% achieving a margin-to-tumor ratio (MTR) ≥ 1. The mean postoperative hospital stay was 3.04 ± 1.16 days. CONCLUSIONS: Single-stage image-guided dye-localization and VATS sublobar lung resection in an HOR using a biplane CBCT-enabled platform is safe, feasible, and effective. This streamlined workflow ensures high technical success and adequate surgical margins with manageable complications. Further studies are warranted to evaluate long-term oncological outcomes.

papers.title_zh: The Dynamic Role of Liquid Biopsy in Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: Emerging Opportunities and Clinical Challenges.
papers.title_en: The Dynamic Role of Liquid Biopsy in Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: Emerging Opportunities and Clinical Challenges.
papers.authors: Bazan Russo TD, Gristina V, Pepe F, Scimone C, Busuito G, Cozzolino D, Sarracino C, Ratto G et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Precision Medicine in Medical, Surgical and Critical Care (Me.Pre.C.C.), University of Palermo, 90127 Pale…
papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet predicting durable benefit and detecting resistance remain major challenges. As immunotherapy expands across disease stages, minimally invasive tools are increasingly needed to monitor response and inform treatment personalization. Liquid biopsy enables serial assessment of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and other blood-based biomarkers, complementing tissue analysis and imaging. This review critically synthesizes evidence across resectable, locally advanced, and metastatic NSCLC, integrating ctDNA dynamics with emerging multi-omics approaches. Its contribution is to distinguish the prognostic value of circulating biomarkers from evidence that using them to guide treatment improves patient outcomes, while identifying priorities for clinical translation. Across the reviewed studies, ctDNA clearance is associated with favorable outcomes, whereas persistent or rising ctDNA signals an increased risk of recurrence or progression, sometimes before radiological detection. Methylation, fragmentomics, plasma proteomics, and immune-cell profiling may provide complementary information on tumor-immune interactions. However, low tumor shedding, clonal hematopoiesis, assay variability, and unvalidated intervention thresholds limit routine use. The expansion of perioperative immunotherapy and emerging interest in biomarker-guided treatment adaptation make this synthesis timely. Prospective interventional trials are needed to determine whether liquid biopsy can safely guide treatment escalation, de-escalation, or discontinuation. By clarifying both the promise and the limitations of longitudinal monitoring, this review informs research aimed at detecting ineffective treatment earlier and reducing unnecessary treatment exposure while preserving cancer control.

papers.title_zh: A Chronobiological Prognostic Model for Resected Stage I Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.title_en: A Chronobiological Prognostic Model for Resected Stage I Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Leuzzi G, Minicozzi P, Verderio P, Ciniselli CM, Ferrari M, Pardolesi A, Stanzi A, Brandolini J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Thoracic Surgery, Fondazione IRCCS Istituto Nazionale dei Tumori, 20133 Milan, Italy.
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Chronobiology may influence outcomes in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but its prognostic role in early-stage disease remains unclear. We evaluated the association between perioperative chronobiological variables, systemic inflammation, and long-term outcomes after complete resection for stage I NSCLC. METHODS: 587 patients who underwent curative-intent resection for pathological stage I NSCLC between 2009 and 2018 were retrospectively reviewed. Chronobiological and inflammatory variables included season of surgery (spring/summer [21st March-22nd September], autumn/winter [23rd September-20th March]), time of day, day of week, and preoperative (CRP0 levels: low ≤ 3 mg/L, high > 3 mg/L) and postoperative day-3 (CRP3 levels: low ≤ 126 mg/L, high > 126 mg/L) C-reactive protein levels. The cohort was randomly divided into training (70%) and testing (30%) sets to develop and validate a prognostic model for overall survival (OS), taking into consideration the follow-up time. Disease-free survival (DFS) was analyzed as a secondary endpoint. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 6.7 years, with 80 deaths and 108 recurrences recorded. In the training set, older age (p = 0.0049), stage IB disease (p = 0.0301), high CRP0 (p = 0.0049), and high CRP3 (p = 0.0280) were associated with worse OS, while surgery performed during autumn/winter was associated with improved OS (p = 0.0312). The multivariate Cox model including age, stage, and season of surgery showed the best prognostic performance (C-index 0.67, 95% Bonferroni-adjusted CI 0.50-0.83) and was internally validated in the testing cohort (C-index 0.69, 95%CI 0.52-0.86). The resulting linear predictor remained associated with both OS and DFS in the overall population. CONCLUSIONS: A simple model integrating age, pathological stage, and season of surgery was associated with long-term outcomes after surgery in stage I NSCLC. This model provides an exploratory framework integrating host-, tumor-, and chronobiological dimensions of prognosis. These findings require external validation and further investigation of the biological mechanisms underlying seasonal variation.

papers.title_zh: AI-Driven Multi-Omics Approaches for Deciphering Small-Cell Lung Cancer Heterogeneity Using Nucleic-Acid-Based Features.
papers.title_en: AI-Driven Multi-Omics Approaches for Deciphering Small-Cell Lung Cancer Heterogeneity Using Nucleic-Acid-Based Features.
papers.authors: Zeeshan S, McVey C, Majeed S, Ahmed Z, Nichols M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Biomedical and Health Informatics, School of Medicine, The University of Missouri-Kansas City, Kansas City…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a rare but highly aggressive malignancy defined by rapid progression, early metastasis, and profound therapeutic resistance. Its extensive heterogeneity across genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and microenvironmental levels continues to undermine precision medicine. Emerging evidence highlights the complex role of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) alterations, histologic transformation from EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to SCLC, and the influence of distinct transcriptional subtypes on clinical behavior. METHODS: This review synthesizes current literature encompassing nucleic-acid-based determinants of resistance, SCLC molecular architecture, transformation biology, and subtype evolution, integrating findings from genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, imaging, and clinical studies. We additionally evaluated artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies with potential to unify multi-omics, radiomics, and clinical variables to model subtype plasticity, clonal evolution, and therapy-induced rewiring. RESULTS: The evidence demonstrates that traditional single-layer analyses are insufficient to capture the multiscale architecture of SCLC biology or the nonlinear interactions driving resistance, whereas AI-enabled multi-omics approaches offer advantages in enhancing subtype classification, supporting early detection, and improving prediction of therapeutic response. Key barriers such as tissue scarcity, limited biomarker availability, and extreme intratumoral heterogeneity remain significant challenges, though increasingly addressable through integrative computational frameworks. CONCLUSION: AI-driven systems-level integration reframes SCLC as a dynamically evolving, multilayered disease process, where nucleic-acid alterations are central to subtype evolution and treatment resistance, providing a conceptual model to guide biomarker discovery and therapeutic development. By leveraging AI-enabled multi-omics and radiomics, this framework has the potential to advance personalized clinical management and overcome longstanding diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in SCLC.

papers.title_zh: Refining Lung Cancer Care: The Emerging Role of Liquid Biopsy in Screening, Diagnosis, and Precision Oncology.
papers.title_en: Refining Lung Cancer Care: The Emerging Role of Liquid Biopsy in Screening, Diagnosis, and Precision Oncology.
papers.authors: Mansour H, Mazouji O, El Hammouti A, Alloubi I, Incitti R, El Kazzouli S, Ouhajjou A, Nejjari C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Euromed Research Center, Euromed University of Fes (UEMF), Fes 30000, Morocco.
papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer (LC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, representing a major public health challenge. Although low-dose computed tomography is currently the standard screening method for high-risk individuals to reduce mortality, its clinical performance is limited by false-positive findings and restricted accessibility. Emerging biomarker-based liquid biopsy offers a promising non-invasive approach for cancer detection. This narrative review provides a critical overview and evaluation of clinically endorsed liquid biopsy applications for guiding treatment in advanced-stage lung cancer, as well as investigational advances in liquid biopsy for early cancer detection. We also address challenges of current liquid biopsy technologies, the integration of artificial intelligence, implementation improvements, and future perspectives for their adoption into routine clinical practice. To complement this narrative review, a structured search of the ClinicalTrials.gov registry was performed to identify clinical trials evaluating liquid biopsy in lung cancer. Current evidence supports the clinical use of liquid biopsy for molecular profiling and treatment selection in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), whereas its application in early detection, screening, and minimal residual disease (MRD)-guided management remains investigational and requires further prospective validation. Overall, liquid biopsy represents a promising complementary approach to advance precision oncology and improve lung cancer management.

papers.title_zh: Longitudinal Assessment of EGFR and MET Transcriptional Activity Using Cell-Free Chromatin Immunoprecipitation in Two Patients with EGFR-Mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.title_en: Longitudinal Assessment of EGFR and MET Transcriptional Activity Using Cell-Free Chromatin Immunoprecipitation in Two Patients with EGFR-Mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Pedersen E, Maansson CT, Meldgaard P, Sorensen BS
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Clinical Biochemistry, Aarhus University Hospital, 8200 Aarhus, Denmark.
papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives:MET amplification represents the most common bypass resistance mechanism to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) treatment in EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Combination therapy with the EGFR-TKI, osimertinib, and the MET-TKI, crizotinib, has demonstrated clinical efficacy in overcoming this resistance. However, assessing MET transcriptional activity during treatment remains challenging. Methods: Cell-free chromatin immunoprecipitation (cfChIP) targeting H3 lysine 36 trimethylation (H3K36me3) was employed to investigate the transcriptional activity of the EGFR and MET genes in serial liquid biopsies obtained from two patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC. Droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) was used to quantify circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and cfChIP enrichment levels. Results: In PT1, H3K36me3 mEGFR and MET cfChIP enrichment increased during disease progression, with MET enrichment increasing further following the initiation of crizotinib/osimertinib combination therapy, during which the patient experienced a partial response. In PT2, MET amplification was detected in a liquid biopsy, but MET cfChIP enrichment remained low throughout the treatment course, and the patient did not respond to crizotinib. Conclusions: This two-patient feasibility study illustrates the potential of cfChIP-ddPCR for the longitudinal assessment of EGFR and MET transcriptional activity in liquid biopsies. These observations warrant further investigation of cfChIP as an approach for monitoring transcriptional activity during osimertinib/crizotinib treatment.

papers.title_zh: Biomarker Integration in the Perioperative Management of Early-Stage Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.title_en: Biomarker Integration in the Perioperative Management of Early-Stage Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Rabinovich EP, Martin LW
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Surgery, University of Virginia Health System, Charlottesville, VA 22903, USA.
papers.abstract_en: The concept of personalized medicine has tremendous appeal-tailoring diagnosis and treatment to an individual, rather than a "one-size-fits-all" approach. The management of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has rapidly evolved toward strategies increasingly guided by tumor biology and precision oncology. The safety and significant efficacy of biomarker-directed therapies in metastatic disease have fueled interest in applying precision oncology to early-stage, operable NSCLC. Advances in molecular profiling have revealed that a substantial proportion of resected NSCLC harbor actionable driver mutations, enabling the integration of targeted therapies into the perioperative setting. The success of adjuvant epidermal growth factor receptor and anaplastic lymphoma kinase inhibition established a framework for biomarker-driven therapy and highlights the importance of comprehensive molecular testing at diagnosis. In parallel, perioperative immune checkpoint inhibitor-based strategies have expanded treatment options for appropriately selected patients, further emphasizing the importance of molecular profiling. Significant implementation gaps remain, including incomplete molecular testing, delayed results, inadequate tissue sampling, fragmented workflows, and disparities in access. Beyond clinically actionable driver mutations, emerging research highlights radiogenomics and advances in the use of circulating tumor DNA for minimal residual disease detection, with important implications for early recurrence detection and patient prognostication, although these technologies differ in clinical maturity. Collectively, these developments emphasize the molecular heterogeneity underlying early-stage NSCLC and the expanding role of biomarkers in guiding clinical decision-making. Integrating genomic, radiographic, and biologic markers into clinical workflows will be essential to refine risk stratification, personalize perioperative treatment strategies, and ultimately improve long-term oncologic outcomes.

papers.title_zh: Clinicopathological and Perioperative Factors Associated with Overall Survival and 90-Day Mortality Following Esophagectomy for Esophageal Cancer.
papers.title_en: Clinicopathological and Perioperative Factors Associated with Overall Survival and 90-Day Mortality Following Esophagectomy for Esophageal Cancer.
papers.authors: Esin H, Güner M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of General Surgery, Izmir City Hospital, University of Health Sciences, 35540 Izmir, Türkiye.
papers.abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Esophageal cancer (EC) is an aggressive malignancy, and outcomes following esophagectomy are influenced by both oncological and perioperative factors. This study aimed to identify clinicopathological and perioperative factors associated with overall survival (OS) after esophagectomy for EC and, secondarily, to evaluate factors associated with 90-day mortality. Methods: A total of 101 patients who underwent radical esophagectomy with two-field lymphadenectomy between April 2016 and April 2023 were retrospectively evaluated. The primary outcome was OS, defined as the time from esophagectomy to death from any cause or the date of last follow-up. The secondary outcome was 90-day postoperative mortality. OS was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses, whereas 90-day mortality was assessed using Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression because of the limited number of events. Results: During follow-up, 74 patients (73.3%) died, including 11 deaths within 90 days after esophagectomy. The estimated 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS rates were 80.1%, 44.8%, and 38.0%, respectively. In the whole-cohort multivariable Cox model, stratified by surgical approach, lymph node positivity was associated with poorer OS (HR 10.57, 95% CI 4.78-23.38; p < 0.001). Among patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy (n = 76), lymph node positivity (HR 6.34, 95% CI 2.60-15.45; p < 0.001) and pathological non-response (HR 2.96, 95% CI 1.13-7.73; p = 0.027) were associated with poorer OS. In exploratory Firth regression analysis, lymph node positivity (OR 103.11, 95% CI 7.40 -> 1000; p < 0.001) and intraoperative complications (OR 75.58, 95% CI 7.42 -> 1000; p < 0.001) were strongly associated with 90-day mortality. Conclusions: Lymph node positivity was consistently associated with poorer OS both in the entire cohort and among patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Pathological non-response was additionally associated with poorer OS in the neoadjuvant chemotherapy subgroup, while lymph node positivity and intraoperative complications were strongly associated with 90-day mortality.

papers.title_zh: Cost-Effectiveness of Telisotuzumab Vedotin-tllv for Previously Treated High c-Met Protein-Overexpressing Nonsquamous Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer in the United States.
papers.title_en: Cost-Effectiveness of Telisotuzumab Vedotin-tllv for Previously Treated High c-Met Protein-Overexpressing Nonsquamous Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer in the United States.
papers.authors: Weiss GJ
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medicine, UMass Chan Medical School, Worcester, Massachusetts, USA.
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To estimate the incremental cost-effectiveness of telisotuzumab vedotin-tllv (teliso-V) versus docetaxel in previously treated high c-Met protein-overexpressing (≥50% of tumor cells with 3+ staining) advanced nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer. METHODS: A partitioned survival model with monthly cycles and a five-year horizon was built from the US healthcare sector perspective. Individual time-to-event data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves of the c-Met High subgroup (N=78) of LUMINOSITY and the CONTACT-01 docetaxel arm (N=180). Because individual covariate data were unavailable, a naive (unadjusted) indirect comparison was conducted. Seven parametric distributions were fit independently by arm; their median and range were the primary summary. The analysis was preregistered. RESULTS: The unadjusted overall survival hazard ratio favored teliso-V but was not statistically significant (HR 0.690; 95% CI 0.471-1.010). The median incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was approximately $2.0 million per QALY (range, $1.7-$2.2 million). Across 70,000 probabilistic iterations, cost-effectiveness was not achieved in any iteration at $50,000, $100,000, $150,000, or $200,000 per QALY. The threshold payment limit at $150,000 per QALY was approximately $1,209 per 100 mg (92% reduction). CONCLUSIONS: At the current Medicare Part B payment limit, telisotuzumab vedotin-tllv is unlikely to be cost-effective versus docetaxel in the US high c-Met protein-overexpressing population at conventional willingness-to-pay thresholds. The conclusion was robust to modeled survival extrapolation and parameter uncertainty. Because the comparison is unadjusted, comparative effectiveness remains uncertain pending randomized results.

papers.title_zh: Uniportal versus Multiportal Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery for Minimally Invasive Esophagectomy in Esophageal Cancer: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.title_en: Uniportal versus Multiportal Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery for Minimally Invasive Esophagectomy in Esophageal Cancer: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.authors: Amin F, Fatima R, Iqbal S, Bilal M, Sajid H, Raza A, Ahmed N, Shah S et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: King Edward Medical University, Lahore, Pakistan.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive esophagectomy has become the preferred surgical approach for esophageal cancer, with uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (uVATS) emerging as a potential refinement over conventional multiportal VATS (mVATS). However, comparative evidence remains limited to small single-centre studies. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively evaluate perioperative and safety outcomes of uVATS versus mVATS in patients undergoing minimally invasive esophagectomy. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and CNKI from inception through April 2026. Studies directly comparing uVATS with mVATS in adults undergoing minimally invasive esophagectomy were eligible. Binary outcomes were pooled as odds ratios and continuous outcomes as mean differences under REML random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using I² statistics. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework. RESULTS: Nine studies comparing uVATS and mVATS were included. uVATS was associated with significantly lower postoperative pain on day one (MD - 2.10, 95% CI - 3.63 to - 0.57; I² = 99.3%), reduced postoperative pneumonia (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.22-0.76; I² = 43.5%), and shorter length of hospital stay (MD - 2.13 days, 95% CI - 3.64 to - 0.63; I² = 96.8%). No significant differences were observed between approaches for anastomotic leakage (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.61-2.09), overall complications (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.47-1.32), recurrent laryngeal nerve injury (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.43-1.85), perioperative mortality (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.16-1.81), intraoperative blood loss, or total operative time. CONCLUSION: UVATS esophagectomy appears to be a feasible and safe alternative to mVATS, with potential advantages in postoperative pain, pulmonary morbidity, and hospital stay while maintaining comparable perioperative safety. The evidence base remains limited by high heterogeneity and predominance of observational studies. Multicenter randomized trials with standardized protocols and long-term oncologic follow-up are needed to consolidate these findings.

papers.title_zh: Carboplatin, Etoposide, and Durvalumab for Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer in a Patient Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis: A Case Report.
papers.title_en: Carboplatin, Etoposide, and Durvalumab for Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer in a Patient Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Fujita M, Matsunaga N, Tsuji H, Tamura Y, Tsuruoka K, Nakamura T, Ikeda S, Fujisaka Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Respiratory Medicine and Thoracic Oncology, Osaka Medical and Pharmaceutical University Hospital, Takatsuki City, Japan.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis exhibit a unique immunological state characterized by chronic inflammation and T-cell dysfunction. Evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of combination chemoimmunotherapy in dialysis patients remains extremely limited. CASE REPORT: We report a case of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (performance status 1, cT1cN2M1c, stage IVB) in a patient undergoing maintenance hemodialysis who received 4 cycles of carboplatin (300 mg/m2, day 1), etoposide (50 mg/m2, days 1 and 3), and durvalumab (1,500 mg/body, day 1). Treatment was safely continued after adjusting the dosing schedule and dose levels in accordance with the dialysis schedule. Although new brain metastases developed during treatment and whole-brain radiotherapy was administered, computed tomography after 4 cycles demonstrated a partial response, and durvalumab maintenance therapy was subsequently continued. Grade 4 thrombocytopenia and grade 3 anemia and neutropenia were observed as adverse events; however, these were manageable with transfusion support and dose reduction. Disease progression was subsequently observed. CONCLUSION: Carboplatin, etoposide, and durvalumab can provide meaningful therapeutic benefit even in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis when adverse events are appropriately managed.

papers.title_zh: Tumor DNA methylation subtypes and expression levels of CFISH predict response and overall survival to immunochemotherapy.
papers.title_en: Tumor DNA methylation subtypes and expression levels of CFISH predict response and overall survival to immunochemotherapy.
papers.authors: Fuchs HS, Xie P, James SA, Cao Z, Carroll TM, Inoue M, Siejka-Zielińska P, Kim S et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research, University of Oxford, Oxford, UK.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Predicting patient response to immunochemotherapy is vital but challenging and poorly studied in the (neo)adjuvant setting. We showed that tumor monocyte content (TMC) predicts overall survival of advanced esophageal cancer (OC) in response to immunochemotherapy. We report clinical outcomes of 35 operable OC patients receiving ICI-based therapy and molecular profiling of the unique phase-2 LUD2015-005 trial treating 73 OC patients (38 advanced/inoperable and 35 operable) in the (neo)adjuvant setting. METHODS: LUD2015-005 trial patients were treated with 4-week immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-only before combination with standard of care. Paired and longitudinally collected biopsies of tumor and multiple adjacent normal sites were bi-dissected to extract DNA and RNA. Whole-genome, methylome, single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data generated from the entire LUD2015-005 cohort were used for cell-deconvolution and data integration analysis. FINDINGS: Neoadjuvant ICI-based combination therapy of operable OC in the LUD2015-005 trial revealed improved overall outcomes. Tumor monocytes contribute to tumor immune microenvironment (TiME) remodeling and associate with tumor reactive CD8+ T cells upon ICI+ chemotherapy/chemoradiotherapy. We identified five DNA-methylation subtypes with distinct TiME and a TMC-related five-gene signature CFISH (CXCL8, FCN1, IFI30, SLC11A1, and HLA-DRA) as highly predictive biomarkers of overall survival in OC and beyond. CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the importance of the myeloid compartment in ICI response and the potential of CFISH and tumor DNA methylation in patient stratification for immunochemotherapy. FUNDING: This work is mainly funded by Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research, CRUK Grants A21998 and C30423/A2541, and NIHR Oxford Biomedical Research Center. AstraZeneca UK Limited provided durvalumab and tremelimumab for LUD2015-005.

papers.title_zh: Real-World Experience With Multimodal Treatment of Resectable Stage II-III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Single Institutional Analysis.
papers.title_en: Real-World Experience With Multimodal Treatment of Resectable Stage II-III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Single Institutional Analysis.
papers.authors: Griffo R, Niedermaier B, Klotz LV, Schneider M, Allgäuer M, Kriegsmann M, Roesch RM, Brendel L et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Thoraxklinik, University of Heidelberg, Heidelberg, Germany.
papers.abstract_en: Neoadjuvant therapy has recently become an integral component of multimodal treatment for resectable lung cancer. However, real-world data on perioperative morbidity and treatment adherence remain limited. This study aimed to assess the feasibility and safety of different neoadjuvant treatment approaches applied within daily clinical routine. We retrospectively analyzed patients with resectable stage II-III non-small cell lung cancer undergoing either neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy or chemotherapy/chemoradiotherapy followed by curative surgical resection. Treatment groups were compared with respect to perioperative outcomes, radiologic and pathologic downstaging, and pathologic response. A total of 143 patients met the inclusion criteria, of whom 46 (32.2%) received chemoimmunotherapy and 97 (67.8%) were treated with chemotherapy prior to surgery. Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation occurred in only two patients in the chemoimmunotherapy group and four patients in the chemotherapy group. Chemoimmunotherapy was associated with significantly higher rates of pathologic complete response (37.0% vs. 4.1%) and more pronounced nodal downstaging, with a higher proportion of patients achieving ypN0 status (76.1% vs. 34.0%). High tumoral PD-L1 expression (≥ 50%) and squamous cell carcinoma histology were independently associated with pathologic complete response. Real-world treatment with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy was feasible and resulted in improved response rates compared with chemotherapy, without increasing perioperative morbidity. Histology and high PD-L1 expression may serve as predictors for complete pathologic response, although the predictive value of PD-L1 requires confirmation in larger cohorts with more complete biomarker data.

papers.title_zh: The association between cirrhosis and outcomes among patients with lung cancer in Ontario between 2007 and 2017: A population-based study.
papers.title_en: The association between cirrhosis and outcomes among patients with lung cancer in Ontario between 2007 and 2017: A population-based study.
papers.authors: Ho AK, Djerboua M, Chung W, Robinson A, Flemming JA
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Public Health Sciences, Queen's University, Kingston, Ontario, Canada.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: We describe the association between cirrhosis and outcomes among patients treated for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: NSCLC cases in 2007-2017 in Ontario, Canada, were reviewed. Cirrhosis was identified using validated coding. The association between cirrhosis and outcomes was evaluated using logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier curves, and adjusted survival models. RESULTS: Among patients with stage 1-3 NSCLC receiving lung resection (n = 59,226), 3% had cirrhosis with higher 30-day (5% versus 2%, p < 0.001) and 90-day (8% versus 3%, p < 0.001) mortality. After multivariable logistic regression, cirrhosis was associated with higher mortality odds at 30 days (OR 2.35, 95% CI 1.39-3.99, p < 0.001) and 90 days (OR 2.10, 95% CI 1.38-3.21, p < 0.001); higher 90-day post-operative complications odds (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.14-1.81, p = 0.002); and higher hospital readmission odds at 30 days (OR 1.90, 95% CI 1.41-2.56, p < 0.001) and 90 days (OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.27-2.10, p = 0.001). Among those with stage 4 NSCLC (n = 27,357), adjusted Cox regression showed cirrhosis was associated with higher mortality (HR 1.10, 95% CI 1.02-1.18, p = 0.016). However, when liver-related mortality was a competing event, association between cirrhosis and cancer-specific mortality was absent (sHR 1.04, 95% CI 0.95-1.13, p = 0.395). A lower proportion of patients with cirrhosis received systemic treatments (31% versus 40%, p < 0.001), and a greater proportion experienced post-treatment complications: electrolyte disturbances (10% versus 5%, p < 0.001), kidney injury (5% versus 2%, p = 0.012), and thrombocytopenia (7% versus 2%, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Cirrhosis is associated with increased morbidity and mortality in stage 1-3 NSCLC patients undergoing curative surgery. Stage 4 NSCLC patients with cirrhosis are less likely to receive palliative treatment and may experience more post-treatment complications.
