papers.authors: Han X, Zhang T, Meng M, Wang J, Huang G, Dai J, Zhao Z, Yang X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Oncology, Shandong Provincial Hospital Affiliated to Shandong First Medical University, Jinan, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: MWA计划系统预测的PTZ大小与形态与术后24小时实测值基本一致；但至1个月时，长径、短径及SI的预测值均显著高于实测值。PTZ与病灶大小及消融功率正相关，不同病理类型也可影响消融区。
papers.ai_note: 全文无任何一致性统计量（偏差、 limits of agreement、Dice、相关系数）与置信区间，主要比较仅以“基本一致”“显著更大”定性表述，缺乏可复核的精度证据；关键临床终点实为1个月（消融疗效判定时点），而结论与标题口径偏向24小时的“一致”，存在选择性强调；1个月缩小可能反映组织收缩而非预测失准，两种机制未区分；病理亚型（浸润性腺癌 vs 不典型腺瘤样增生）比较样本量与多重性未交代。信息不足：多因素模型变量、效应值、并发症率均未报告。
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To validate the accuracy and reliability of the microwave ablation (MWA) planning system in predicting the postablation target zone (PTZ) in lung tumors after computed tomography (CT)-guided MWA and analyze its potential influencing factors. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 118 patients with 134 lung tumors, who underwent CT-guided MWA from May 2020 to September 2021, was conducted. CT images were collected at 24 hours and 1 month after MWA to evaluate the local effect and complications. The differences between the size and shape of the actual PTZ and predicted ones were compared, and the factors affecting PTZ were also analyzed. RESULTS: The predicted long diameters, short diameters, and spherical index (SI) of PTZ detected at 24 hours after MWA were basically consistent with the actual ones, but significantly larger than those detected at 1 month after MWA, and the difference was more pronounced in the short diameter than in the long diameter. The lesion diameter and ablation power had an independent effect on the ablation index (AI) at 24 hours after MWA ( P < 0.05), and there was a significant difference in AI between invasive adenocarcinoma and atypical adenomatoid hyperplasia at 24 hours after MWA ( P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: The size and shape of the PTZ predicted by MWA planning system were basically consistent with the actual ones detected at 24 hours after MWA. However, by 1 month, the predicted values of the long diameter, short diameter, and SIs were all significantly higher than the actual ones. PTZ is positively correlated with lesion size and ablation power, and different pathological types can also affect the ablation zone.

papers.study_type: 临床前动物实验 · 机制研究（SARS-CoV-2感染模型与实验性肿瘤模型）
papers.title_zh: SARS-CoV-2感染通过缺氧和炎症诱导的VEGF依赖性血管生成促进动物模型肺部肿瘤生长
papers.title_en: COVID-19 triggers pulmonary tumor outgrowth through hypoxia- and inflammation-induced VEGF-dependent angiogenesis.
papers.authors: Jing X, Ma M, Bai Y, Wu Y, Sun X, Wu J, Holgersson K, Wang X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Microbiology, Tumor and Cell Biology, Karolinska Institute, Stockholm, Sweden.
papers.authors_conclusion: Our data show that the COVID-19-induced hypoxia-VEGF-angiogenesis axis serves as one of the mechanisms for initiating tumor outgrowth in pulmonary tissues.
papers.ai_note: 仅为动物模型机制证据，摘要未报告样本量、效应量、置信区间或P值，无法定量评估；将SARS-CoV-2感染加速动物肿瘤生长的结果外推至人类休眠肺结节风险需谨慎；VEGF阻断的挽救实验支持通路依赖性，但不能证明COVID-19会促使人类结节进展。
papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary nodules are highly prevalent in adult human populations, with a substantial proportion representing dormant cancerous lesions. We hypothesized that these pulmonary dormant cancers debilitate in growth owing to the lack of an angiogenic switch in tumors. In this study, we comprehensively investigated the hypothesis that specific pathological triggers can activate this angiogenic switch utilizing severe acute respiratory coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection-induced hypoxia as a primary physiological stimulus. Our findings provide compelling experimental evidence demonstrating that SARS-CoV-2 infection induces profound pulmonary hypoxia and severe tissue inflammation in animal models. This microenvironmental disruption markedly upregulates the expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2) within lung tissues. The resulting hyperactivation of the downstream VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling pathway effectively drives robust pulmonary neovascularization, a phenomenon frequently documented in clinical observations of COVID-19 patients. Furthermore, employing an established experimental tumor model, we demonstrated that SARS-CoV-2 infection directly accelerates tumor outgrowth via this specific VEGF angiogenesis-dependent cascade. Crucially, the targeted administration of a neutralizing antibody to block VEGF significantly suppressed tumor progression and outgrowth in SARS-CoV-2-infected, tumor-bearing animals. Our data show that the COVID-19-induced hypoxia-VEGF-angiogenesis axis serves as one of the mechanisms for initiating tumor outgrowth in pulmonary tissues.

papers.title_zh: Not all major pathological responses are equal: prognostic heterogeneity and risk stratification after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in resectable NSCLC.
papers.title_en: Not all major pathological responses are equal: prognostic heterogeneity and risk stratification after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in resectable NSCLC.
papers.authors: Lin J, Xu H, Tang J, He C, Li P, Lin X, Wu J, Huang Z et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital of Shantou University Medical College, Shantou, China.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Major pathological response (MPR) is a widely used efficacy endpoint for neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT) in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, whether MPR without pathological complete response (pCR) represents a prognostically homogeneous population remains unclear, and optimal postoperative management strategies require further exploration. This study evaluated the prognostic heterogeneity, risk stratification, and recurrence patterns of patients achieving MPR. METHODS: This dual-center, retrospective cohort study included 588 patients with resectable NSCLC who received NCIT followed by radical surgery. The primary endpoint was recurrence-free survival (RFS). Patients were categorized into mutually exclusive pCR (n=200), non-pCR MPR (≤10% residual viable tumor without pCR; n = 111), and Non-MPR (n=277) groups. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression were used to evaluate prognostic factors and develop a risk-stratification system within the MPR subgroup. Additionally, the effect of postoperative adjuvant therapy was evaluated via exploratory subgroup analyses, and anatomical recurrence patterns were systematically compared across response groups. RESULTS: Recurrence-free survival (RFS) differed among the three groups, with MPR representing an intermediate-risk state. Within the MPR subgroup, baseline cT3-4 stage, postoperative ypN positivity, and lower harvested lymph node count were independently associated with RFS. A simplified system effectively divided MPR patients into low-risk (RFS comparable to pCR) and high-risk groups (RFS approaching Non-MPR). Adjuvant therapy showed no statistically significant RFS benefit in pathological response subgroups. Furthermore, recurrence patterns did not significantly differ among response groups, with brain and bone remaining the predominant distant metastatic sites. CONCLUSIONS: Non-pCR MPR after NCIT is a prognostically heterogeneous state in NSCLC. Stratifying these patients using baseline cT stage, ypN status, and lymph node count refines postoperative risk assessment, highlighting the continued necessity of thorough lymph node dissection. Although adjuvant therapy did not show a definitive RFS benefit in our cohort, its potential value, especially in high-risk MPR patients, warrants prospective validation and should not be interpreted as evidence of lack of benefit. Furthermore, the observed recurrence patterns across response groups, with brain and bone being frequently observed metastatic sites, provide preliminary insights into metastatic distribution after NCIT and may serve as a reference for future surveillance studies.

papers.title_zh: Neoadjuvant serplulimab combined with chemotherapy in locally advanced driver gene-negative squamous NSCLC: a multicenter observational study.
papers.title_en: Neoadjuvant serplulimab combined with chemotherapy in locally advanced driver gene-negative squamous NSCLC: a multicenter observational study.
papers.authors: Lin N, Yang Z, Yu F, Lin J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University, Fuzhou, China.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Previous evidence demonstrated that neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy provides significant prognostic benefits for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). While the efficacy of serplulimab, an anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody, has been well established in advanced driver gene-negative NSCLC in the ASTRUM-004 trial, its efficacy in the neoadjuvant setting remains unclear. This real-world study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of neoadjuvant serplulimab plus chemotherapy in patients with locally advanced squamous NSCLC, with a particular focus on pathological response outcomes. METHODS: This was a multicenter, retrospective-prospective, real-world observational study. Electronic medical records were retrospectively reviewed to identify eligible patients with locally advanced squamous NSCLC who received at least 1 cycle of neoadjuvant serplulimab (300 mg, Q3W) combined with platinum-taxane chemotherapy. Prospective follow-up was conducted to complete courses and outcomes. The primary endpoint was major pathologic response (MPR), and the secondary endpoints included pathological complete response (pCR), objective response rate (ORR), event-free survival (EFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. RESULTS: Thirty patients were included (median age 64 years; 96.7% male; 86.7% stage III). Most patients received two cycles of neoadjuvant therapy (46.67%), and 80% achieved a radiologic ORR (95% CI, 61.4-92.3%). Surgery was performed on 28 patients (93.33%), with MPR and pCR achieved in 57.1% (95% CI, 39.1-73.5%) and 28.6% (95% CI, 15.3-47.1%), respectively, and an R0 resection rate of 92.9%. Compared with the historical chemotherapy group, the observed MPR was significantly higher (57.1% vs 8.9% and 11.0%; P < 0.001). The median EFS reached 29.97 months, and the 12-month EFS rate was 91.8% (95% CI, 81.4-100%). The OS data were immature. Grade 3 adverse events occurred in 6.7% of patients, and no grade 4-5 events or perioperative immune-related complications were reported. Exploratory analyses revealed that a lower post-treatment neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR< 3) was positively correlated with MPR, whereas advanced T stage (T3-T4) was negatively associated. CONCLUSION: Neoadjuvant serplulimab-chemotherapy demonstrated promising efficacy and manageable toxicity in real-world locally advanced NSCLC. Survival outcomes require longer follow-up to assess clinical benefit.

papers.title_en: Pretreatment CT radiomics for prediction of pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in NSCLC: a multicenter study incorporating habitat analysis.
papers.authors: Zheng S, Huang S, Zhang J, Yang X, Ye P, Wang W, Li W, Liu H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiology, Medical Artificial General Intelligence for Computation (MAGIC) Lab, National Clinical Research…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) varies among patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study aimed to quantify intratumoral heterogeneity using habitat analysis and to develop a pretreatment model for predicting pCR. METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, 287 patients with NSCLC who received NACI followed by surgery were included. Patients were randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 147) and an internal validation cohort (n = 63), with an independent external test cohort (n = 77). K-means clustering was used to partition tumors into three habitat subregions based on entropy. Radiomics features were extracted from pretreatment CT images at the whole-tumor and habitat levels. Whole-tumor, habitat-based, and combined models were developed to predict pCR. Model performance was evaluated using area under the curve (AUC) analysis, and model interpretability was assessed using Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). RESULTS: The habitat-based model showed acceptable predictive performance across the training, internal validation, and external test cohorts, with AUCs of 0.74, 0.71, and 0.67, respectively, and showed higher AUCs compared with the whole-tumor radiomics model, which achieved AUCs of 0.72, 0.68, and 0.65. The combined model achieved performance comparable to the habitat-based model. SHAP analysis suggested that, among the habitat-derived features, the most influential predictive features were primarily associated with the high-entropy habitat subregion. CONCLUSION: The habitat-based model shows potential performance for predicting pCR, and features from a high-entropy habitat subregion may provide complementary imaging information for preoperative assessment of treatment response.

papers.title_zh: Bridging radiomics and histopathology: cross-modality consistency of radiomic features from CT to micro-CT in NSCLC.
papers.title_en: Bridging radiomics and histopathology: cross-modality consistency of radiomic features from CT to micro-CT in NSCLC.
papers.authors: Brizzi L, Bortolotto C, Cabini RF, Brero F, Megalizzi S, D'Ambrosio G, Filibian M, Gioia R et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiology, IRCCS Policlinico San Matteo, Pavia, Italy.
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Radiomics extracts quantitative features from medical images that may provide non-invasive biomarkers of tumor biology and heterogeneity. However, few studies have explored radiomics on micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) or its transferability to clinical CT. This study investigates the reproducibility and the potential biological correlation of radiomic features across in vivo CT, ex vivo CT, and ex vivo micro-CT in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 60 NSCLC patients with preoperative CT scans and surgical specimens was analyzed. Ex vivo CT and micro-CT images were acquired and compared with in vivo CT using standardized preprocessing, including normalization, resampling, and registration. Tumor regions of interest (ROIs) were semi-automatically segmented, and 93 radiomic features were extracted with Pyradiomics. Cross-modality reproducibility and associations with histotype were evaluated using Spearman correlation, intraclass correlation coefficient, Bland-Altman analysis, and Mann-Whitney U test. RESULTS: Normalization and volume matching improved feature repeatability, with the highest agreement observed in normalized datasets using subsampled ROIs. Four texture-based features consistently showed high reproducibility and potential biological correlation, likely reflecting intratumoral heterogeneity and variation in cell density: DependenceNonUniformity, GrayLevelNonUniformity (GLDM and GLRLM), and Coarseness (NGTDM). These features reliably distinguished adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma across modalities, confirming their stability and potential as candidate features for transferable biomarkers. CONCLUSION: Harmonization and volume standardization are essential for cross-modality radiomic analyses. Stable texture features provide a potential transferable signature bridging micro-CT and clinical CT imaging in NSCLC, supporting their role as candidate features for further investigation in biologically oriented studies. KEY POINTS: Question Micro-CT serves as an intermediate imaging scale enabling radiomic feature extraction from ex vivo NSCLC tumors, allowing direct comparison with in vivo and ex vivo CT. Findings Intensity normalization and volume-matched subsampling between in vivo CT, ex vivo CT, and micro-CT reduced cross-modality feature variability, improving feature reproducibility. Relevance statement Normalization, volume matching, and cross-modality analysis support the identification of candidate texture features with consistent cross-scale behavior and exploratory associations with NSCLC histotype.

papers.title_en: Exploratory analysis of extracellular vesicle Profile changes during pembrolizumab treatment in NSCLC.
papers.authors: Hirano Y, Yagishita S, Shinno Y, Goto Y, Araya J, Yamamoto Y, Fujita Y
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Respiratory Diseases, Department of Internal Medicine, The Jikei University School of Medicine, Tokyo, Japan…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Predictive biomarkers for pembrolizumab resistance and durable clinical benefit in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain insufficient. METHODS: Serum extracellular vesicles (EVs) were isolated from 98 patients with advanced NSCLC treated with pembrolizumab monotherapy. Isolation was performed using CD9/CD63 antibodies, and EV proteins were identified using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Patients were classified into primary resistance and clinical benefit groups; patients with clinical benefit were further divided into acquired resistance and long-term responder groups. Differential protein abundance, pathway enrichment, progression-free survival (PFS), and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed. RESULTS: The cohort included 40 patients with primary resistance and 58 with clinical benefit. Proteomic analysis identified 305 differentially abundant EV proteins between these groups. Proteins enriched in primary resistance were associated with extracellular matrix organization, adhesion, complement activation, and chemotaxis, whereas response-enriched proteins were related to mitochondrial metabolism, fatty acid oxidation, and vesicle/lysosome-associated transport. TNXB and SMIM1 showed moderate discriminatory performance for primary resistance, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.712 and 0.706, respectively. A four-protein panel comprising TNXB, KRT12, TFPI2, and HLA-E improved discrimination between primary resistance and clinical benefit, achieving an AUC of 0.788. Among patients with clinical benefit, ITLN1, ABCG5, NPC1L1, MME, and NOP2 distinguished acquired resistance from long-term response, and a four-protein panel comprising ITLN1, ABCG5, NPC1L1, and NOP2 achieved an AUC of 0.808. CONCLUSION: Circulating EV proteomic analysis identified candidate biomarkers for pembrolizumab resistance and durable clinical benefit in advanced NSCLC.

papers.title_zh: Second-line therapy in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer: an unmet need highlighted by real-world evidence from the LALUCA registry.
papers.title_en: Second-line therapy in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer: an unmet need highlighted by real-world evidence from the LALUCA registry.
papers.authors: Moser D, Lang-Stöberl A, Fabikan H, Krainer-Jacobs J, Illini O, Ay L, Müser N, Weinlinger C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Karl Landsteiner Institute of Lung Research and Pulmonary Oncology, Vienna, Austria; Department of Respiratory and Criti…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) has a dismal prognosis as patients progress within months after first-line systemic treatment. Until recently, topotecan was the only approved second-line treatment in Europe. However, due to its limited efficacy, various treatment strategies are being employed. This study aimed to depict the therapeutic landscape of second-line treatment in ES-SCLC and to evaluate survival outcomes in a real-world setting. METHODS: Data from the Austrian LALUCA registry, a prospective, multicenter clinical lung cancer registry, were reviewed for all patients diagnosed with ES-SCLC between November 2020 and October 2025. Clinical and treatment characteristics were assessed with special emphasis to second-line treatment. The primary outcomes were overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and time to next treatment (TTNT). RESULTS: Among 203 patients with histologically confirmed ES-SCLC included in this study, 75 patients (36.9%) received second-line therapy. The main reason for no second-line treatment (n = 128) at data cut-off was death in 49.2% and switch to best supportive care in 18.8%. Second-line treatment consisted of anthracycline-based treatment regimens in 57.3%, topotecan in 26.7% and re-challenge of platinum-based chemo- or chemoimmunotherapy in 16.0% of patients. The median duration of second-line treatment was 2 months (range: 0.0-8.2) with a median PFS of 4.7 months (95% CI: 3.9, 5.8), and median OS of 7.1 months (95% CI: 5.1, 9.3). The median TTNT between first- and second-line treatment was 6.4 months (range: 0.3 - 38.7). The main reasons for treatment discontinuation were disease progression in 30.7%, followed by completed regimen in 24.0% and death in 13.3%. CONCLUSION: This real-world analysis shows poor outcomes in patients with progressing ES-SCLC, reflected by both short median PFS and duration of second-line treatment, along with high rates of treatment discontinuation due to progression, highlighting the urgent need for more effective and tolerable treatment options.

papers.title_zh: Decoding Treatment Response and Prognosis in Unresectable Locally Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer by Integrating Spatiotemporal Heterogeneity From 18F-FDG Positron Emission Tomography-Computed Tomography: A Multicenter Study.
papers.title_en: Decoding Treatment Response and Prognosis in Unresectable Locally Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer by Integrating Spatiotemporal Heterogeneity From 18F-FDG Positron Emission Tomography-Computed Tomography: A Multicenter Study.
papers.authors: Ji Y, Wang J, Zhou M, Wang Y, Dai Z, Zheng J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiology, The Second Qilu Hospital of Shandong University, Jinan, Shandong, China.
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Treatment response in unresectable locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (LA-NSCLC) is highly variable due to marked intratumoral heterogeneity, while existing predictive biomarkers lack accuracy. We aimed to develop and validate a pretreatment 18F-FDG positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT)-derived spatiotemporal heterogeneity model to predict treatment response and prognosis in unresectable LA-NSCLC, and to explore its biological underpinnings. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In a multicenter cohort of 434 patients with unresectable LA-NSCLC (training: n = 215; internal validation: n = 93; external validation: n = 126), treatment response was classified as responsive or nonresponsive based on initial assessment. Four distinct habitats (PEThigh-CThigh, PETlow-CTlow, PETlow-CThigh, and PEThigh-CTlow) were generated via the Otsu algorithm. Temporal heterogeneity was quantified using metabolic hotspot displacement (normalized distance from the hotspot to the tumor centroid and normalized distance from the hotspot to the tumor periphery) and integrated with spatial radiomics to build a multidimensional spatiotemporal model. Model performance was evaluated against conventional metrics, with interpretability enhanced via nomogram and SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier curves, and public transcriptomic data were analyzed to characterize underlying pathways. RESULTS: The spatiotemporal model accurately predicted treatment response with AUCs of 0.822 (training), 0.821 (internal validation), and 0.810 (external validation), significantly outperforming conventional whole-tumor PET-CT models. It maintained robust generalizability across treatment subgroups and effectively stratified patients by progression-free survival and overall survival (P < .01). PEThigh-CThigh habitat volume fraction correlated with treatment resistance, whereas PETlow-CTlow habitat correlated with better response. Exploratory pathway analysis highlighted key pathways involving drug metabolism, glycolytic reprogramming, and immune microenvironment remodeling. CONCLUSION: This study establishes a noninvasive spatiotemporal heterogeneity biomarker based on 18F-FDG PET-CT that reliably predicts treatment response and prognostic outcomes in unresectable LA-NSCLC. It offers valuable insights for personalized clinical decision making and supports precision oncology.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Oncology, The First People's Hospital of Chenzhou, The First School of Clinical Medicine, Xiangnan Univers…
papers.authors_conclusion: 作者结论：EGFR突变NSCLC的预后受更广泛的基因组背景强烈影响，尤其是TP53突变和总体共突变负荷；EGFR亚型特异的生存差异及TP53/ATM定义的DDR相关发现应谨慎解读，原因包括研究来源异质性、临床注释不完整及DDR基因定义有限。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未报告任何效应量、95%CI或P值，关键阳性/阴性结论（TP53独立预后、PIK3CA相关、共突变负荷梯度）均无法量化核验。研究基于cBioPortal多来源公共队列，研究来源异质性是核心混杂，作者亦承认仅能用校正模型部分处理，残余混杂与批次效应难以排除；肿瘤分期信息不完整（“available tumor stage”），生存终点定义、随访完整性与治疗背景（TKI时代、治疗线数）未描述，可能严重影响OS解释。生存分析从844例中排除24例，排除原因未说明，存在选择偏倚可能。TP53/ATM的DDR定义事后构建且ATM事件稀少，阳性结论主要由TP53驱动，DDR这一概念标签有过度概括之嫌。整体属探索性假设生成，不宜作为独立预后分层依据。
papers.abstract_en: METHODS: Clinical and genomic data of patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC were collected from publicly available cBioPortal cohorts. Cohort composition, stage availability, recurrent co-mutations, and study-origin heterogeneity were evaluated. Patients harboring EGFR Del19 or L858R mutations and available survival information were included for survival analyses. Genomic landscapes were analyzed using a standardized Del19/L858R survival cohort. Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression models, including sensitivity analyses adjusted for study origin and available tumor stage. Co-mutation burden and TP53/ATM-defined DDR-related alterations were further assessed as exploratory prognostic features. RESULTS: A total of 1,024 EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients were identified. Among them, 844 patients harbored Del19 or L858R mutations. Among the 844 patients with EGFR Del19 or L858R mutations, 820 had complete survival information and were included in survival analyses (Del19, n = 429; L858R, n = 391). An apparent OS difference was observed between Del19 and L858R tumors in the pooled cBioPortal cohort; however, this association was attenuated after accounting for study-origin heterogeneity and was therefore interpreted as exploratory. TP53 mutation was the most robust adverse prognostic factor and remained independently associated with inferior survival after adjustment for study origin. PIK3CA mutation also remained associated with poorer OS in the study-origin-adjusted model, whereas EGFR subtype and CDKN2A mutation were not retained as independent prognostic factors after accounting for study-level heterogeneity. Increasing co-mutation burden was associated with progressively shorter OS. TP53/ATM-defined DDR-related alterations were associated with inferior OS in exploratory analysis, but this result was largely driven by TP53 because ATM-only alterations were rare and not significantly associated with OS. CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates that prognosis in EGFR-mutant NSCLC is strongly influenced by broader genomic context, particularly TP53 mutation and overall co-mutation burden. EGFR subtype-specific survival differences and TP53/ATM-defined DDR-related findings should be interpreted cautiously because of study-origin heterogeneity, incomplete clinical annotation, and the limited DDR gene definition.

papers.title_zh: Plasma nucleosome profiling reports on tumor burden and molecular subtypes in small cell lung cancer.
papers.title_en: Plasma nucleosome profiling reports on tumor burden and molecular subtypes in small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Fialkoff G, Takahashi N, Sharkia I, Gutin J, Hermoni N, Nirula M, Kumar R, Pongor L et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: School of Computer Science and Engineering, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Jerusalem, Israel.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUNDSmall-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis and marked transcriptional heterogeneity that may drive distinct therapeutic vulnerabilities. Clinical translation of molecular subtyping has been limited by restricted access to tumor biopsies, particularly at relapse.METHODSWe applied chromatin immunoprecipitation of cell-free nucleosomes carrying active histone modifications followed by sequencing (cfChIP-seq) to 441 plasma samples from individuals with advanced SCLC, other neuroendocrine carcinomas, or non-SCLC cancers, as well as from healthy controls. Plasma cfChIP-seq profiles were integrated with matched tumor transcriptomes from 73 samples, including 41 time-matched pairs.RESULTScfChIP-seq captured the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape of tumor-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA), including SCLC tissue- and cell-of-origin signatures. A quantitative cfChIP-seq-derived SCLC score tracked radiographic tumor burden and was associated with prognosis. Signals at promoters of lineage-defining transcription factor genes, including ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, and ATOH1, correlated strongly with matched tumor RNA expression and supported noninvasive inference of SCLC transcriptional subtypes directly from plasma.CONCLUSIONPlasma cfChIP-seq provides a practical liquid biopsy platform for real-time assessment of tumor burden, tumor state, and molecular subtype in SCLC. These findings support further development of cfChIP-seq for precision monitoring and subtype-informed therapeutic stratification in SCLC.TRIAL REGISTRATIONClinicalTrials.gov NCT02484404, NCT02487095, NCT02769962, NCT03554473, NCT03896503, and NCT02146170.FUNDINGCenter for Cancer Research; Intramural Program of the NCI (ZIA BC 011793); European Research Council (ERC) (Adg no. 101019560 "cfChIP").

papers.title_zh: Lung cancer after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
papers.title_en: Lung cancer after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
papers.authors: Rost M, Wehr C, Mozaffari Jovein M, Kemper M, Bleckmann A, Overbeck TR, Brauß A, Stölzel F et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Goethe University Frankfurt, University Hospital, Department of Hematology and Medical Oncology, Frankfurt, Germany.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Long-term outcomes of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are improving, increasing the relevance of secondary malignancies, including lung cancer. The clinical utility of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in this setting remains unclear and concerns regarding graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) persist. METHODS: In this international cohort study, we evaluated clinical characteristics, survival outcomes, and toxicities in patients diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) or small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) and a history of HCT. RESULTS: A total of 77 patients from 18 centers in six countries were included. Median time from HCT to diagnosis was 4.2 years (95%CI, 0.5-30.4), 64% of patients were male, and 81% were current or former smokers. In advanced NSCLC, patients treated with ICI-based therapies (n=20) had longer overall survival than those receiving chemotherapy alone (n=16) (median 17.4 vs 4.7 months; HR 0.32, 95%CI: 0.13-0.77). Across 77 lines of therapy in 54 patients receiving systemic treatment, grade 3-5 immune-related adverse events (irAEs) or GvHD occurred in 2/30 ICI-containing lines (7%) and 1/47 lines that did not include ICIs (2%). However, patients receiving ICIs had longer intervals from HCT to treatment initiation (median, 7.1 vs 3.0 years) and did not require GvHD treatment (0% vs 25%), indicating improved host immune tolerance. CONCLUSIONS: In our study, ICI-based therapies were associated with prolonged survival in selected patients with advanced NSCLC and presumed host immune tolerance. We did not observe a clear signal of excess irAEs/GvHD. Our results support considering the use of ICIs in this population.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) has emerged as a promising non-invasive biomarker for cancer detection, including non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). While these approaches have demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy in controlled settings, their performance in real-world clinical populations remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a plasma cfDNA assay for early-stage NSCLC detection and to explore its association with clinicopathological parameters. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a single-center, crosssectional study involving 61 patients with radiologically suspected lung lesions, of whom 52 were confirmed NSCLC. Plasma samples were analyzed using a shallow genomewide sequencing-based cfDNA assay incorporating fragmentomic and copy number features. cfDNA results were compared against histopathological diagnosis to determine sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Associations between cfDNA detection and clinical variables were evaluated using appropriate statistical tests. RESULTS: The cfDNA assay demonstrated a sensitivity of 75% and a PPV of 84.8% with a specificity of 22.2% and NPV of 13.3%. cfDNA detection rates increased with advancing disease stage, although a relatively high sensitivity was observed even in stage I disease (79.4%). No statistically significant associations were found between cfDNA positivity and conventional markers of tumour burden, including tumour size, serum carcinoembryonic antigen, and SUVmax. CONCLUSION: The cfDNA assay evaluated in this study demonstrated limited clinical utility as a standalone screening tool due to its low specificity and NPV in a realworld early-stage NSCLC population. Future efforts should focus on improving assay specificity through the incorporation of multi-omic tumour-specific biomarkers and validation that includes early-stage lung cancer cases and benign pulmonary conditions.

papers.title_zh: Population Pharmacokinetics and Exposure-response Analysis of Durvalumab in Patients with Limited-stage Small-cell Lung Cancer in the Phase 3 ADRIATIC Study.
papers.title_en: Population Pharmacokinetics and Exposure-response Analysis of Durvalumab in Patients with Limited-stage Small-cell Lung Cancer in the Phase 3 ADRIATIC Study.
papers.authors: Su H, Zhao BJ, Fu Y, Zhang YY, Chugh P, Casson E, Lim K, Ren S et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Clinical Pharmacology, Development Science, R&D China, AstraZeneca, Shanghai, China.
papers.abstract_en: Durvalumab monotherapy as a consolidation treatment for limited-stage small-cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC) demonstrated a favourable benefit-risk profile in the ADRIATIC study. We evaluated population pharmacokinetics (PopPK) and exposure-response (E-R) relationships of durvalumab in patients with LS-SCLC. The durvalumab PopPK model was updated by integrating PK data from the ADRIATIC study. Individual exposure metrics were derived from empirical Bayes estimates for E-R analyses relating to safety (adverse events [AEs]) and efficacy (progression-free survival [PFS] and overall survival [OS]). A two-compartment model with a time-dependent clearance adequately characterized durvalumab PK data. The typical parameter estimates for baseline clearance, central and peripheral volume of distribution were 0.273 L/day, 3.49 L and 2.35 L, respectively. All identified covariates are considered to have minimal clinical impact on durvalumab PK parameters with effect within 80-125% of typical values. Kaplan Meier plots of PFS or OS stratified by exposure quartiles suggested a plateaued relationship between durvalumab exposure and PFS or OS at the selected dose level of 1500 mg. The Cox PH model analysis did not identify exposure metrics as significant prognostic factors for the OS or PFS hazard. At 1500 mg IV Q4W, a flat E-R relationship was observed between durvalumab PK exposure and safety endpoints including Grade 3 + treatment-related AEs, Grade 3 + treatment-related AEs of special interest, and AEs leading to treatment discontinuation. The results support the use of durvalumab monotherapy for the patients with LS-SCLC, and no dose adjustment is considered necessary based on the PopPK and E-R analyses. NCT03703297.

papers.title_zh: Risk Factors for Pneumonitis Induced by Combined Radiotherapy and Immunotherapy: A Multicenter Prospective Study.
papers.title_en: Risk Factors for Pneumonitis Induced by Combined Radiotherapy and Immunotherapy: A Multicenter Prospective Study.
papers.authors: Xiao L, Li Q, Li Y, Wang D, Wang S, Fan Z, Xu D, Yu Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: 1Department of Oncology, Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, …
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The combination of radiotherapy (RT) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has become an important therapeutic approach for lung cancer. However, pneumonitis remains a major treatment-related toxicity of this therapeutic approach, and the risk factors for pneumonitis associated with combined RT and ICIs under different treatment sequences have not been clearly defined. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with lung cancer who received thoracic RT were prospectively enrolled from 3 centers. Pneumonitis was assessed according to CTCAE version 4.0 by a multidisciplinary team. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify factors associated with pneumonitis. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 28.2 months, 133 of 380 (35.0%) patients developed symptomatic pneumonitis (grade ≥2). Treatment with ICIs was associated with an increased risk of symptomatic pneumonitis (hazard ratio [HR], 1.69; 95% CI, 1.20-2.39; P=.003). Among 170 patients treated with ICIs, 89 received ICIs before RT (ICI-first group) and 81 received ICIs after RT (RT-first group). In the ICI-first group, 42 (47.2%) patients developed symptomatic pneumonitis, and an interval of <21 days between ICI administration and RT and a higher percentage of lung volume receiving ≥20 Gy (V20) were associated with an increased risk of pneumonitis. In the RT-first group, 32 (39.5%) patients developed symptomatic pneumonitis, with older age and higher V20 identified as risk factors. CONCLUSIONS: Administration of ICIs before RT significantly increases the risk of pneumonitis in patients receiving thoracic RT. The dosimetric factor V20 consistently emerged as a key determinant of pneumonitis risk in both the ICI-first and RT-first groups. These findings aid in preventing the occurrence of pneumonitis induced by combined RT and ICIs, thereby improving patients' quality of life and survival outcomes.

papers.title_zh: Real-World Association Between Up-Front Next-Generation Sequencing and Overall Survival in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer in the United States.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center, Washington, DC.
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Clinical guidelines recommend next-generation sequencing (NGS) before initiation of first-line (1L) therapy as the standard of care for patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (aNSCLC). This study examined the impact of timing of molecular testing in relation to treatment initiation on overall survival (OS) to help inform clinical decision making for aNSCLC treatment. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed the Flatiron Health aNSCLC deidentified database from 2019 to 2021. Patients with aNSCLC and 1L systemic therapy were grouped into three cohorts based on timing of testing: (1) up-front NGS; (2) up-front non-NGS genomic testing; and (3) NGS after 1L therapy initiation. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox Proportional Hazards models were used to compare OS from the date of aNSCLC diagnosis between cohorts. RESULTS: Overall, 13,139 patients with aNSCLC treated with systemic therapy were identified, including 6,210 patients with up-front tumor NGS, 2,697 patients with up-front non-NGS testing, and 2,824 patients with NGS after 1L initiation. A higher proportion of patients with up-front NGS received targeted therapy compared with patients with NGS after 1L initiation (22.6% v 14.8%, P < .0001). Median OS was significantly longer (20.9 months) with up-front NGS compared with up-front non-NGS (17.5 months) and NGS testing after 1L (18.2 months, P < .005). Multivariable analyses suggest that OS benefits associated with up-front NGS were primarily attributable to treatment. CONCLUSION: NGS testing before 1L therapy was observed to be associated with earlier use of targeted therapy and longer survival when compared with other testing strategies. Future studies are warranted given the rapidly evolving treatment landscape in aNSCLC.

papers.study_type: 单中心准实验研究（非随机对照设计）
papers.title_zh: 肺癌日间手术患者ERAS护理路径的开发与应用：单中心准实验研究报告护理依从性及术后恢复改善
papers.title_en: Development and application of an ERAS nursing pathway for lung cancer patients following day-surgery.
papers.authors: Yuan H, Gao L, Han N, Hong L, He H
papers.affiliation_highlight: Nursing Department, The Second Affiliated Hospital Zhejiang University School of Medicine, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: The ERAS nursing pathway effectively improves perioperative nursing compliance and postoperative recovery outcomes in lung cancer day-surgery patients, while reducing complications and delayed discharge. It also enhances nursing workflow standardization and staff satisfaction, supporting its clinical value and broader implementation in surgical nursing practice.
papers.ai_note: 摘要称多项指标“显著改善”，但未给出任何效应量、置信区间或P值；未明确主要终点，多个依从性指标并列报告，存在以过程指标替代临床终点的可能；准实验设计的分组方法、基线可比性、日间手术准入标准及护士满意度测量方式均未交代；单中心设计限制外推性。
papers.abstract_en: ObjectivesTo develop and implement an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) nursing pathway for lung cancer patients undergoing day surgery, and to evaluate its impact on perioperative nursing compliance, postoperative outcomes, and nurse satisfaction.MethodsA quasi-experimental study was conducted in a tertiary-level hospital in Zhejiang Province from September 2021 to March 2022. A total of 671 lung cancer patients and 57 nurses were included. Patients were assigned to either a control group receiving routine perioperative care or a study group managed under an ERAS nursing pathway. The ERAS intervention included structured training, standardized perioperative nursing procedures, and a visual pathway-based guidance system. Key perioperative compliance indicators and clinical outcomes were collected and compared between groups.ResultsImplementation of the ERAS nursing pathway significantly improved multiple compliance indicators, including preoperative education rate, early postoperative feeding rate, early ambulation rate, elastic stocking usage rate, ankle pump exercise compliance, and breathing training compliance. In addition, postoperative complication rates and delayed discharge rates were reduced in the ERAS group compared with the control group. Nurses reported a high level of satisfaction with the ERAS system.ConclusionThe ERAS nursing pathway effectively improves perioperative nursing compliance and postoperative recovery outcomes in lung cancer day-surgery patients, while reducing complications and delayed discharge. It also enhances nursing workflow standardization and staff satisfaction, supporting its clinical value and broader implementation in surgical nursing practice.

papers.study_type: 叙述性综述 · NSCLC胸外科质量指标框架（非原始研究）
papers.title_zh: 非小细胞肺癌胸外科肿瘤学质量指标（第一部分）：基于结构-过程-结果框架的指标综述
papers.title_en: Thoracic Surgery Oncology Quality Indicators (Part 1: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer).
papers.authors: Plourde M, Chen A, Brownstone R
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Thoracic Surgery, Department of Surgery, Dalhousie University, Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada.
papers.authors_conclusion: In non-small cell lung cancer, key themes include timely multidisciplinary treatment-driven care, accurate staging, appropriate surgery and adjuvant therapy, Enhanced Recovery after Surgery use, systematic quality review, and integration of patient-reported outcome measures to complement traditional outcomes.
papers.ai_note: 摘要为叙述性概述，未描述系统检索、指标遴选与验证方法，也未报告任何指标的性能数据或临床结局；不能据此推断质量指标实施对结局的影响。
papers.abstract_en: Modern performance measurement in health care builds on Codman's "end result" concept and Donabedian's triad of structure, process, and outcomes as interdependent components of quality. These domains support perioperative thoracic oncology care by guiding the selection of validated, measurable key performance indicators. Structure indicators address capacity and resources; process indicators assess adherence to evidence-based pathways; and outcome indicators capture clinical results. In non-small cell lung cancer, key themes include timely multidisciplinary treatment-driven care, accurate staging, appropriate surgery and adjuvant therapy, Enhanced Recovery after Surgery use, systematic quality review, and integration of patient-reported outcome measures to complement traditional outcomes.

papers.study_type: 单臂、多中心、II期试验方案（尚无疗效结果）
papers.category_label: 局晚期与晚期靶向/免疫
papers.title_zh: 信迪利单抗联合诱导化疗后适应性同步放化疗及巩固治疗不可切除III期NSCLC：单臂多中心II期试验方案（ART-LUNG 01）
papers.title_en: Single-arm, multicentre phase II trial of sintilimab plus platinum-based doublet chemotherapy followed by adaptive radiotherapy strategy for patients with unresectable stage III non-small-cell lung cancer in China: the ART-LUNG 01 study protocol.
papers.authors: Wu L, Ma S, Zhang X, Song Z, Liu X
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Oncology, Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University, Changsha, Hunan, China.
papers.ai_note: 仅为试验方案，摘要未报告任何疗效或安全性结果；单臂设计、样本量35例、无同期对照，疗效无法归因于诱导免疫+适应性放疗策略；摘要未明确主要终点；放疗设置三种可选方案且根据肿瘤体积和分布选择，可能增加治疗异质性并影响结果解释。
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Consolidation immunotherapy postchemoradiotherapy is standard for unresectable stage III non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) per PACIFIC and GEMSTONE-301, but optimal integration with chemoradiotherapy is unclear, especially for large tumours. Induction immunotherapy before concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) may enhance tumour downstaging and immune synergy, while adaptive radiotherapy with strict lung constraints (V20 ≤20%) could reduce toxicity. This trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of sintilimab with induction chemotherapy followed by adaptive radiotherapy and consolidation sintilimab in patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This prospective, multicentre, single-arm phase II trial will enrol 35 patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed unresectable stage III NSCLC, without sensitising mutations, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group(ECOG) performance status 0-1. Patients will receive two cycles of induction sintilimab (200 mg, day 1, every 3 weeks) plus platinum-based doublet chemotherapy, followed by definitive cCRT with adaptive radiotherapy planning strictly limiting both lung V20 ≤20%. Radiotherapy dose can be delivered in three optional regimens based on tumour volume and distribution: (1) planning gross tumour volume (PGTV) 60-66 Gy/2.0-2.2 Gy/30F with planning target volume (PTV) 54 Gy/1.8 Gy/30F; (2) PGTV 54-66 Gy/2.0-2.2 Gy/30F without PTV irradiation or (3) PGTV 50 Gy/2.0 Gy/25F without PTV irradiation. During radiotherapy, patients will receive two additional cycles of sintilimab plus chemotherapy. Consolidation sintilimab will continue for up to 1 year or until disease progression/unacceptable toxicity. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study was approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee of The Third Xiangya Hospital, Central South University (approval number: R25063; the approval letter is provided as online supplemental file 1). The study results will be disseminated through publication in peer-reviewed journals, presentations at national and international scientific conferences and communication to participants and the public via institutional channels and patient advocacy groups. Individual participant data will be available on reasonable request after study completion, subject to institutional and ethical approvals. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT07138755.

papers.study_type: 临床样本结合细胞与动物实验的转化机制研究
papers.category_label: 局晚期与晚期靶向/免疫
papers.title_zh: FEN1通过EIF4A3介导MUC1-C自调控促进肺腺癌进展并参与免疫逃逸的临床前研究
papers.title_en: Targeting FEN1 disrupts EIF4A3-mediated MUC1-C autoregulation: a novel strategy to suppress lung adenocarcinoma progression.
papers.authors: Wu M, Wu B, Yan X, Wang Z, Mei C, Huang X, Li G, Pang J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Oncology, The Affiliated Hospital of Yangzhou University, Yangzhou University, Yangzhou, PR China.
papers.authors_conclusion: FEN1/EIF4A3/MUC1-C轴是驱动LUAD进展的新机制，可同时调控内在恶性与外在免疫逃逸，FEN1靶向是有前景的双重打击治疗策略。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未报告样本量、效应量、生存HR/CI及P值，无法评估结果稳健性与临床可推广性；“独立预后因素”“显著上调”“协同上调”等均无具体统计数值；从细胞/动物机制与外推至“有前景的治疗策略”存在转化跳跃；FEN1、MUC1-C、PD-L1共表达与EGFR突变状态无关的结论缺少分层数据；信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: Flap endonuclease 1 (FEN1), a key enzyme in DNA metabolism, exhibits oncogenic properties in various cancers. However, its functional role and underlying mechanisms in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) progression and tumor immunity remain poorly defined. Here, we demonstrate that FEN1 is significantly upregulated in LUAD tissues and serves as an independent prognostic factor for poor survival. Genetic depletion of FEN1 suppressed LUAD cell proliferation by inducing G0/G1 cell cycle arrest and cellular senescence, while significantly impairing migration and invasion capabilities. Mechanistically, integrated proteomic and molecular analyses revealed that FEN1 knockdown disrupts the carboxyl-terminal subunit of mucin 1 (MUC1-C)/PI3K/AKT autoregulatory loop, a critical driver of oncogenic signaling. Furthermore, FEN1 downregulation inhibited the MUC1-C/p65/ programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) signaling axis, thereby alleviating tumor-mediated immunosuppression. This was evidenced by enhanced antitumor immunity, characterized by the local expansion of CD4+ T cells and restored effector function of CD8+ T cells, both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, independent of its nuclease activity, FEN1 interacts with the N-terminus of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3) to facilitate its binding to MUC1-C mRNA. Specifically, FEN1 is required for EIF4A3-mediated maintenance of both the transcript stability and translation efficiency of MUC1-C. Clinically, FEN1, MUC1-C, and PD-L1 are coordinately upregulated in LUAD tissues, and their co-expression predicts poor patient survival irrespective of EGFR mutation status. Our findings establish the FEN1/EIF4A3/MUC1-C axis as a novel mechanism driving LUAD progression by concurrently regulating intrinsic malignancy and extrinsic immune evasion, presenting FEN1 targeting as a promising dual-hit therapeutic strategy.

papers.study_type: 叙述性综述（非系统评价，无原始研究数据）
papers.category_label: 局晚期与晚期靶向/免疫
papers.title_zh: 小细胞肺癌五十年历程：机制、分子分型与治疗进展的叙述性综述
papers.title_en: The Five-Decade Journey of Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Chen R, Xue C, Zhong Y, Huang Q, Fan Q, Li Y, Wu J, Dong S et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Oncology, Tongji Medical College, Hubei Cancer Hospital, Huazhong University of Science and Techno…
papers.authors_conclusion: 2018年一线化疗联合免疫检查点抑制剂及后线tarlatamab开启了SCLC治疗新时代，但生存改善虽然真实可及，仍不令人满意；本综述聚焦肿瘤起始、进展尤其是转移机制，以及表观遗传视角下的分子分型与耐药新进展，并梳理临床药物、策略与分子标志物及在研 promising agents，最后讨论利用人工智能与创新生物医学技术改善SCLC治疗格局。
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，未描述系统检索策略、纳入排除标准或证据分级，药物与生物标志物进展的呈现可能存在选择性；摘要未给出任何疗效数值，无法核验其'生存改善仍不满意'的量化依据；将AI与创新技术列为展望但无对应证据支撑。
papers.abstract_en: Over the past 5 decades, small cell lung cancer (SCLC) has persisted as one of the most formidable malignancies, largely attributed to its aggressive early metastasis, limited therapeutic arsenal in both first-line and subsequent treatments, and rapid onset of treatment resistance. The dawn of a new era in the treatment of SCLC appeared in 2018, with the introduction of first-line chemotherapy combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors, as well as tarlatamab for later-line treatment. However, the improvements in survival, although tangible, were still unsatisfactory. Therefore, this review focuses on unraveling the mechanisms underlying cancer initiation, progression, and particularly metastasis, as well as emerging advances in molecular subtyping and drug resistance from the epigenetic perspective. Simultaneously, we outline their hallmark characteristics-high plasticity, heterogeneity, redundancy, and ambiguity driven by intercellular crosstalk under spatiotemporal dependency. Furthermore, we highlight the evolving progress of various successful drugs or therapeutic strategies and molecular biomarkers in clinical practice for SCLC, as well as promising agents under investigation. Finally, we also discuss how to leverage artificial intelligence and innovative biomedical technologies, as well as learn from various challenges in order to improve the therapeutic landscape of SCLC.

papers.study_type: 临床前+生物信息学研究：LUAD细胞系体外功能实验（敲低/抑制剂±Fer-1）联合TCGA/CPTAC/GEO队列分析及预后基因特征建模
papers.category_label: 局晚期与晚期靶向/免疫
papers.title_zh: FURIN通过抑制NRF2-xCT-GPX4轴介导的铁死亡促进肺腺癌进展，并构建多细胞死亡相关基因预后特征（AUC 0.73–0.78）
papers.title_en: Multi-cell death gene signature predicts lung adenocarcinoma prognosis and reveals FURIN regulates ferroptosis via NRF2-xCT-GPX4 axis.
papers.authors: Ning J, Xiao G, Wen S, Chen L, Wang C, Zhang K, Wen H, Tanzhu G et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiation Oncology, Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, Changsha, 410008, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: FURIN通过抑制NRF2-xCT-GPX4轴介导的铁死亡促进LUAD进展；靶向FURIN-铁死亡轴并采用基于铁死亡的风险分层，可能为预后判断与个体化治疗提供新策略。
papers.ai_note: 机制表述为“preliminarily demonstrated”，NRF2核转位仅有共聚焦显微镜初步证据；铁死亡依赖性主要依据Fer-1逆转，缺乏体内模型与铁死亡特异性阻断/ rescue 的完整链条；预后特征未见明确的外部独立队列验证，AUC 0.73–0.78 属中等判别力；摘要未报告任何具体P值、样本量与多因素HR，免疫浸润与突变差异均为关联性描述；体外药效（Decanoyl-RVKR-CMK）无剂量、IC50或正常细胞毒性数据。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: FURIN, a proprotein convertase, has been implicated in tumor progression. Nevertheless, how it contributes to lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and ferroptosis is still not well understood. METHODS: We investigated FURIN expression and its prognostic value using the TCGA-LUAD cohort, CPTAC, and GEO datasets. In vitro functional assays, including CCK-8, colony formation, EdU, wound healing, invasion, and tube formation, were conducted in HCC827, PC9 and H460 cells following FURIN knockdown, with or without the ferroptosis inhibitor Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1). RNA-seq, ferroptosis signature scoring, and GSEA were used to explore mechanisms. Ferroptosis was assessed by ROS and Fe accumulation, MDA and GSH/GSSG ratio, T-AOC, and ferroptosis-related protein expression. Preliminary exploration of the mechanism by which FURIN regulates NRF2 was performed using confocal microscopy. A multiple cell death-related gene signature was developed for prognostic prediction and immune/mutational landscape analysis. RESULTS: In LUAD, FURIN was highly expressed and linked to poor prognosis. Knockdown of FURIN suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and angiogenesis, accompanied by increased ROS, Fe2+, elevated MDA, and decreased GSH/GSSG ratio and T-AOC. RNA sequencing showed downregulation of SLC7A11, GPX4, FTH1, and GSS, accompanied by upregulation of ACSL4, PTGS2, NCOA4, and DPP4. Furthermore, Fer-1 treatment reversed these changes, supporting a ferroptosis-dependent mechanism. Western blot confirmed FURIN knockdown may inhibit the NRF2-xCT-GPX4 axis, which lead to ferroptosis. Mechanistically, we preliminarily demonstrated that FURIN promotes NRF2 nuclear translocation and upregulates xCT and GPX4. The FURIN inhibitor Decanoyl-RVKR-CMK effectively inhibits the growth of LUAD in vitro. The cell death-related gene signature showed robust predictive performance (AUC 0.73-0.78) and served as an independent prognostic factor. Risk stratification revealed distinct immune infiltration, with high-risk patients enriched in immunosuppressive macrophages and low-risk patients in CD8⁺ T and NK cells. High-risk patients also exhibited increased tumor mutational burden and driver mutations. CONCLUSIONS: FURIN promotes LUAD progression by suppressing ferroptosis through the NRF2-xCT-GPX4 axis. Targeting the FURIN-ferroptosis axis and using ferroptosis-based risk stratification may offer novel strategies for prognosis and individualized therapy.

papers.study_type: 基于人群的回顾性登记研究（描述性流行病学与生存分析）
papers.category_label: 局晚期与晚期靶向/免疫
papers.title_zh: 意大利普利亚地区恶性间皮瘤33年人群登记研究：职业与环境石棉暴露模式、地区高发分布及生存仍差
papers.title_en: Epidemiology, exposure patterns and survival of malignant mesothelioma in Apulia, Italy (1993-2025): a population-based retrospective registry study.
papers.authors: De Maria L, Cavone D, Delvecchio G, Serio G, Caputi A, Sole S, Aloia G, Lupariello V et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Section of Occupational Medicine, Interdisciplinary Department of Medicine, University of Bari, Bari, Italy.
papers.authors_conclusion: 普利亚地区间皮瘤反映了历史石棉使用持续存在的职业与环境后果；地理热点与较差生存支持继续开展登记监测、污染场地修复以及对既往暴露工人和社区进行有针对性的健康监测
papers.ai_note: 暴露类别合计仅约61.1%，其余病例的暴露归类（未知/非暴露）未在摘要中说明，可能影响归因比例解读；生存“随诊断时期改善”仅给出p<0.001，未报告效应量与置信区间，且未校正年龄、组织学、治疗等混杂，不能排除登记完整性提高或早诊带来的领先时间偏倚；发病率与暴露比例均为描述性，无对照人群；5年生存10.1%及中位1.0年未给出置信区间。
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To characterise the epidemiology, asbestos-exposure patterns, spatial distribution and survival of malignant mesothelioma in Apulia, Italy. DESIGN: Population-based retrospective registry study. SETTING: Apulian Regional Mesothelioma Registry, a regional operating centre of the Italian National Mesothelioma Registry. PARTICIPANTS: All 2281 malignant mesothelioma cases recorded between 1993 and 2025. INTERVENTIONS: None. PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOMES: Primary outcomes were case distribution, population-adjusted incidence, asbestos-exposure category and overall survival. Secondary outcomes included temporal trends, municipal patterns, proximity of environmentally exposed cases to the former Fibronit plant in Bari and factors independently associated with mortality. RESULTS: Overall, 1689 cases (74.0%) occurred in men; mean age at diagnosis was 67.8 years and 2018 cases (88.5%) were pleural. Occupational exposure accounted for 49.8% of cases, environmental exposure for 8.9% and familial exposure for 2.4%. Taranto had the highest municipal annual incidence (7.43 per 100 000), followed by Bari (4.59). Among 112 environmentally exposed Bari cases with reconstructed residential distance, 89.3% lived within 1 km of the former Fibronit plant. Kaplan-Meier median survival was 1.0-year and 5-year survival was 10.1%. Survival improved across diagnostic periods (p<0.001). Older age, male sex and pleural site independently predicted higher mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Mesothelioma in Apulia reflects persistent occupational and environmental consequences of historical asbestos use. Geographical hotspots and poor survival support continued registry surveillance, remediation of contaminated sites and targeted health monitoring of formerly exposed workers and communities.

papers.study_type: 临床前机制探索研究 · 网络药理学+多组学+机器学习筛选，辅以分子对接/动力学、孟德尔随机化、单细胞分析与小鼠原位LUAD模型验证
papers.category_label: 胸外科 AI 与三维重建
papers.title_zh: 整合多组学与小鼠原位移植模型筛选葛根素相关候选靶点：ALDH2与肺腺癌巨噬细胞浸润相关，但直接结合与功能因果未获验证
papers.title_en: Integrative multi-omics analysis prioritizes ALDH2 as a candidate Puerarin-associated target linked to macrophage infiltration in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Zhong Z, Ju G, Cai Y, Zhou L, Wang Q, Yang B
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pathology, Jiangsu Province (Suqian) Hospital, Suqian, Jiangsu, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: 葛根素在小鼠LUAD模型中抑制肿瘤生长，并与ALDH2上调及巨噬细胞浸润增加相关；整合分析将ALDH2优先列为可能连接葛根素治疗与肿瘤免疫微环境变化的候选分子；葛根素-ALDH2直接结合、巨噬细胞特异性ALDH2调控及对巨噬细胞极化的功能后果仍需进一步实验验证
papers.ai_note: 主要终点（体内抗肿瘤效应与ALDH2/巨噬细胞变化）仅作定性描述，无肿瘤负荷、免疫细胞比例的具体数值、效应量与统计检验，无法评估效应大小；分子对接/动力学为模拟预测，作者已承认未建立直接靶点结合，但标题与摘要“candidate target”表述仍可能被过度引用；MR以表达量作暴露、结局数据集细节未给出，且与体内“葛根素升高ALDH2”方向关系需谨慎衔接；原位LUAD移植模型若为免疫缺陷小鼠，则F4/80+CD11b+细胞与外周血结果向免疫微环境结论外推受限（摘要未说明小鼠免疫状态）；机器学习特征基因筛选与诊断性能缺乏独立外部队列与校准信息；整体为假说生成级证据，不支持任何临床决策。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Puerarin is a bioactive isoflavone with reported anti-tumor and immunomodulatory activities; however, its candidate molecular targets and associations with the immune microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma(LUAD) remain incompletely defined. This study integrated computational analyses with a murine LUAD model to prioritize candidate puerarin-associated targets and evaluate their relationships with immune-cell changes. METHODS: We first identified puerarin targets, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)-associated genes, and differentially expressed genes (DEGs). An integrative strategy combining network pharmacology, multi-omics, and machine learning algorithms (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, Support Vector Machine-Recursive Feature Elimination, and Random Forest) was employed to screen feature genes. Feature genes were further evaluated by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Mendelian randomization(MR), cellular origins and immune infiltration analyses, and in vivo animal experiments using an orthotopic LUAD xenograft model. RESULTS: A comprehensive analysis identified 130 targets associated with puerarin, 10,871 genes related to NSCLC, and 4,690 DEGs, resulting in an intersection comprising 39 candidate genes. Five feature genes (ABCG2, ALDH2, MIF, PTGS1, and SELP) were retained by three machine-learning approaches and ABCG2, ALDH2, MIF, and SELP showed consistent diagnostic performance in the training and validation cohorts. Docking and molecular dynamics simulations predicted favorable and stable modeled interactions of puerarin with ABCG2 and ALDH2, but did not establish direct target engagement. MR using a LUAD outcome dataset suggested an inverse association between genetically predicted ALDH2 expression and LUAD risk. Single-cell analysis indicated relative enrichment of ALDH2 transcripts in macrophages. In vivo, puerarin reduced orthotopic tumor burden and was accompanied by increased total ALDH2 expression and higher proportions of F4/80+CD11b+ cells in peripheral blood and tumor tissue. CONCLUSION: Puerarin suppressed tumor growth in a murine LUAD model and was associated with ALDH2 upregulation and increased macrophage infiltration. Integrated analyses prioritize ALDH2 as a candidate molecule potentially linking puerarin treatment to changes in the tumor immune microenvironment. Direct puerarin-ALDH2 binding, macrophage-specific ALDH2 regulation, and the functional consequences for macrophage polarization require further experimental validation.

papers.study_type: 队列研究（启发式判定）
papers.title_zh: Efficacy and Safety of CyberKnife-Based SBRT and Linear Accelerator-Based IMRT/VMAT for Thoracic Radiotherapy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Propensity Score-Matched Real-World Analysis.
papers.title_en: Efficacy and Safety of CyberKnife-Based SBRT and Linear Accelerator-Based IMRT/VMAT for Thoracic Radiotherapy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Propensity Score-Matched Real-World Analysis.
papers.authors: Sun S, Duan Y, Yang G, Xiao H, Chen X, Wang Z, Ma J, Su K et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Cancer Center, Daping Hospital & Army Medical Center of PLA, Army Medical University, Chongqing, China.
papers.abstract_en: IntroductionCyberKnife-based stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) has demonstrated favorable outcomes in multiple tumors. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of CyberKnife-based SBRT versus linear accelerator (LINAC)-based IMRT/VMAT for thoracic radiotherapy in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a retrospective study.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, we retrospectively analyzed 461 NSCLC patients treated in our hospital. After propensity score matching (PSM), 138 patients (CyberKnife: 46; LINAC: 92) were matched. Median follow-up was 16.4 months (by reverse Kaplan-Meier method), and the short-term local control and early toxicity were compared.ResultsAfter PSM, baseline characteristics were well-balanced. No significant differences were observed in objective response rate (P=0.838), disease control rate (P=0.832), distribution of response categories (P=0.972), or local progression-free survival (Log-Rank P=0.450). However, the CyberKnife group demonstrated superior safety. Symptomatic radiation pneumonitis (RP) (Grade≥2) was significantly lower (6.5% vs. 27.2%; OR=0.214, P=0.004). Notably, no Grade≥2 radiation esophagitis (RE) occurred in the CyberKnife group versus 18.5% with LINAC (P<0.001). Multivariate analyses further confirmed CyberKnife treatment as an independent protective factor against both symptomatic RP (OR=0.208, P=0.021) and symptomatic RE (OR=0.051, P=0.002). Dosimetrically, CyberKnife achieved superior sparing of lung tissue and esophageal tissue (all P<0.001). CyberKnife remained the sole independent predictor for symptomatic RP, while for RE, treatment group (OR=0.068, P=0.041) and esophagus V50EQD2 (OR=1.073, P=0.019) were independent prognostic factors.ConclusionIn this PSM cohort, CyberKnife and LINAC demonstrated comparable short-term tumor control and local progression outcomes for thoracic radiotherapy in NSCLC. However, CyberKnife was associated with a significantly lower risk of severe radiation-induced toxicities, suggesting a clinically meaningful safety advantage.

papers.title_zh: Perioperative recovery and survival after lobectomy versus sublobar resection in adults aged ≥ 70 years with NSCLC ≤ 3 cm: complementary SEER and real-world cohort analyses.
papers.title_en: Perioperative recovery and survival after lobectomy versus sublobar resection in adults aged ≥ 70 years with NSCLC ≤ 3 cm: complementary SEER and real-world cohort analyses.
papers.authors: Chen F, Yu H, Xia W, Ren F, Li X, Chen J, Xu Y
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Tianjin Chest Hospital & Tianjin University Affiliated Chest Hospital, No.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: For older adults with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the choice of resection must balance durable cancer control against physiological reserve and postoperative recovery. We combined population-level long-term survival data with granular real-world perioperative data to examine this trade-off. METHODS: The Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) cohort included 2,630 patients aged ≥ 70 years with NSCLC ≤ 3 cm diagnosed in 2010-2015 (855 lobectomy, 1,421 wedge resection, and 354 segmentectomy). Optimal 1:1 propensity-score matching retained 809 patients per group. The two-center cohort included 223 patients treated by video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery in 2017-2020 (145 lobectomies and 78 sublobar resections: 73 wedge resections and five segmentectomies). Overlap weighting used age, sex, tumor size, clinical stage, consolidation-to-tumor ratio, smoking, and recorded cardiopulmonary comorbidities. The primary real-world survival analysis was restricted to tumors ≤ 2 cm and 36 months. RESULTS: In SEER, matched sublobar resection was not associated with a statistically significant OS difference for tumors ≤ 2 cm (hazard ratio [HR] 1.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.93-1.51; P = 0.177), whereas OS was lower after sublobar resection for tumors > 2-3 cm (HR 1.31, 95% CI 1.03-1.66; P = 0.028). Procedure-specific models showed no significant difference between segmentectomy and lobectomy for tumors ≤ 2 cm (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.83-1.26), while wedge resection was associated with lower OS (HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.14-1.53). In the real-world cohort, patients selected for wedge-dominant sublobar resection were older and had more recorded comorbidities. After overlap weighting, wedge-dominant sublobar resection was associated with shorter chest-tube duration (mean difference - 2.49 days, 95% CI - 3.56 to - 1.37) and less hypoproteinemia (risk difference - 14.4% points, 95% CI - 27.6 to - 1.7). The composite in-hospital complication risk was 16.4% points lower (95% CI - 34.7 to 1.3), whereas total hospital stay did not differ significantly (mean difference - 1.60 days, 95% CI - 4.62 to 2.04). For tumors ≤ 2 cm, adjusted 3-year OS was 93.0% after lobectomy and 88.5% after wedge-dominant sublobar resection (HR 1.73, 95% CI 0.19-15.63; P = 0.558). CONCLUSIONS: In routine practice, wedge-dominant sublobar resection was selected for older adults with greater comorbidity burden and was associated with shorter chest drainage and less hypoproteinemia, while total hospital stay was similar after adjustment. Among patients with tumors ≤ 2 cm, the real-world cohort showed no statistically significant 3-year OS difference. In the longer-term SEER analysis, segmentectomy showed no significant adjusted OS difference from lobectomy for tumors ≤ 2 cm, whereas wedge resection warrants greater oncologic caution.

papers.title_zh: 空气污染与早发型肺癌：从环境致癌机制到早期干预策略的叙述性综述
papers.title_en: Air pollution and early-onset lung cancer: from environmental carcinogenesis to early intervention strategies.
papers.authors: Gao YY, Xu JJ, Wu YX, Xu HM, Wang GZ, Zhou GB
papers.affiliation_highlight: Institute of Cancer Research, Henan Academy of Innovations in Medical Science, Zhengzhou 451162, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: 未来研究应探索基因-环境交互作用、对生物标志物与治疗靶点进行临床验证、将基础发现转化为临床实践，并开发高危人群精准预防策略；最终，将生物标志物引导的早期检测与多靶点化学预防相结合，对降低全球空气污染所致早发型肺癌负担至关重要。
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，未报告检索策略、纳入排除标准与证据分级，结论属观点性整合；'一组早期生物标志物已被验证用于预防干预''多标志物组合疗效更优''多个化学预防靶点已被识别'等关键论断缺乏具体验证研究、效应量与置信区间支撑；标题聚焦'早发型肺癌'，但所引流行病学与机制证据多为总体肺癌，人群限定存在松动；机制推断向临床预防策略的转化被表述得较为顺畅，存在乐观外推。
papers.abstract_en: Air pollution remains a global public health challenge, with nearly the entire global population (99%) breathing air that exceeds World Health Organization guideline limits-annual means of 5 μg/m3 for PM2.5 and 15 μg/m3 for PM10. Both household and ambient air pollution are classified as Group 1 carcinogens and contain hazardous components, including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, heavy metals, and volatile organic compounds. Exposure contributes to a broad spectrum of systemic diseases and is responsible for more than 14% of global lung cancer deaths while also elevating risks for breast, gastrointestinal, and brain cancers. Mechanistically, air pollutants drive early lung carcinogenesis through intrinsic genomic instability, manifesting as DNA damage, telomere dysfunction, mitochondrial impairment, and specific mutational signatures, alongside epigenetic dysregulation. Concurrently, they foster a tumor-promoting niche via chronic inflammation mediated by CXCL13 and IL-1β and facilitate early immune evasion through activation of the PD-L1 and CD47-SIRPα axes. In addition, air pollution disrupts the respiratory-gut microbiome, reducing microbial diversity and promoting pathogenic enrichment. A range of early biomarkers-including genomic, epigenomic, inflammatory, and microbiome profiles-have been validated for preventive interventions, with multimarker combinations demonstrating improved efficacy. Multiple chemopreventive targets have also been identified to counteract oxidative stress, inflammation, and immune evasion. Looking ahead, research priorities should include exploring gene-environment interactions, clinically validating biomarkers and therapeutic targets, translating basic discoveries into clinical practice, and developing precision prevention strategies for high-risk populations. Ultimately, integrating biomarker-guided early detection with multi-target chemoprevention will be essential to reducing the global burden of air pollution-induced early-onset lung cancer.

papers.title_zh: Context-dependent value of HLA class I diversity in advanced non-small cell lung cancer treated with immune checkpoint blockade.
papers.title_en: Context-dependent value of HLA class I diversity in advanced non-small cell lung cancer treated with immune checkpoint blockade.
papers.authors: Ramos-Paradas J, Carrizo N, Álvarez E, Martín-Arriscado C, López M, Ortiz N, Herrera M, Rey M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Cancer Area, Health Research Institute Hospital 12 de Octubre (lmas 12), Madrid, Spain.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), alone or in combination with chemotherapy, are the standard first-line treatment for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable oncogenic drivers. Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression and tumor mutational burden (TMB) are routinely used biomarkers, yet both show limited predictive accuracy at the individual level, particularly in the context of chemo-immunotherapy. HLA class I diversity has been proposed as a biomarker of response to ICI monotherapy, although its role in first-line chemo-immunotherapy remains unclear. METHODS: We performed a retrospective validation and exploratory study including patients with stage IV NSCLC treated with ICI monotherapy or platinum-based chemo-immunotherapy in the first-line setting. Tumors were profiled using a single clinically-validated targeted sequencing assay (TruSight Oncology 500), allowing simultaneous assessment of TMB and HLA class I diversity. Furthermore, tumors had a complete clinical annotation, including the level of PD-L1 expression. Associations with objective response rate (ORR) and progression-free survival (PFS) were evaluated. RESULTS: PD-L1 expression and TMB showed limited discriminative performance for ORR, particularly in chemo-immunotherapy-treated patients. Composite HLA class I diversity did not predict ORR or PFS. A triple-negative biomarker profile identified a subgroup with reduced likelihood of response, although statistical significance was not reached. Exploratory analyses suggested that locus-specific HLA-B diversity, when combined with TMB, was associated with numerically longer PFS, whereas HLA-A, HLA-C, and composite HLA metrics showed no consistent association. CONCLUSIONS: In advanced NSCLC treated predominantly with first line chemo-immunotherapy, composite HLA class I diversity does not improve outcome prediction beyond established biomarkers. Locus-specific HLA metrics, particularly HLA-B, may warrant further investigation.

papers.title_zh: Association of PET/CT Metabolic Parameters with Histologic Grade of Lung Adenocarcinoma: Implications for Surgical Decisions.
papers.title_en: Association of PET/CT Metabolic Parameters with Histologic Grade of Lung Adenocarcinoma: Implications for Surgical Decisions.
papers.authors: Shen X, Shi H, Wan Z, Yang M, Yu B, Song Y, Chen T, Wen J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital, Tongji University School of Medicine, Shanghai 200433, Chin…
papers.abstract_en: Background The grading system for invasive lung adenocarcinoma proposed by the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) has been widely validated. However, the association of PET/CT with IASLC grade and its value in clinical decision-making is unknown. Purpose To investigate the association of PET/CT metabolic parameters with IASLC grade and determine the complementary clinical value of PET/CT in optimizing preoperative surgical decision-making in clinical stage IA (cIA) lung adenocarcinoma. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent preoperative PET/CT and complete resection for cIA lung adenocarcinoma between September 2020 and March 2022. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma. Multivariable Cox models assessed prognostic effects and interactions between maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and surgical strategy. Propensity score matching was used to balance clinicopathologic characteristics across surgical strategies. Results The study included 2789 patients (median age, 62 years [IQR, 55-68 years]; 1574 women). Logistic regression analysis demonstrated a positive interaction between radiologic type and SUVmax (P = .008) in predicting grade 3 adenocarcinoma. Specific cutoff values for pure solid (cutoff of 4.25) and subsolid (cutoff of 2.30) nodules were identified. Positive interactions between SUVmax and surgery were observed exclusively in pure solid nodules (SUVmax-resection extent for overall survival [OS], P = .048; SUVmax-nodal dissection for OS, P = .045). Stratified analyses showed that segmentectomy and limited lymph node dissection were associated with worse outcomes only in hypermetabolic lesions (SUVmax > 4.25; resection extent hazard ratio [HR] for OS, 2.06 [P = .03]; nodal dissection HR for OS, 2.06 [P = .005]). SUVmax maintained robust predictive efficacy for grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma in the external cohort (area under the receiver operating curve, 0.72 for pure solid nodules and 0.74 for subsolid nodules). Conclusion In patients who underwent PET/CT and complete resection for clinical stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, maximum standardized uptake value was an independent predictor of grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma and helped identify high-risk patients treated with segmentectomy or limited nodal dissection. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

papers.title_zh: TLS-related immune organization and regional IRF4 expression in pretreatment biopsies of advanced lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.title_en: TLS-related immune organization and regional IRF4 expression in pretreatment biopsies of advanced lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Luo J, Lin S, Tang W, Guo R, Zeng Y
papers.affiliation_highlight: Nanjing Medical University, Nanjing, Jiangsu, PR China; Oncology Medical Center, The Second Affiliated Hospital of Haina…
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) assessment is challenging in advanced lung adenocarcinoma because pretreatment diagnosis often relies on limited biopsy tissue that may incompletely represent lymphoid architecture. We investigated whether biopsy-captured B-cell organization and regional interferon regulatory factor 4 (IRF4) expression could provide complementary information on TLS-related immunity in this setting. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A TLS-related transcriptional program was analyzed in TCGA-LUAD to prioritize candidate genes, followed by tissue-level and functional evaluation of IRF4 in a murine tumor model and A20 B cells. Pretreatment small-biopsy specimens from 34 patients with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma receiving first-line immunotherapy plus chemotherapy were evaluated for CD20+ B-cell aggregation patterns, regional IRF4 expression, and clinical outcomes. RESULTS: Within pretreatment small biopsies, CD20+ B cells showed distinct patterns of local organization. Regional IRF4 expression differed among aggregation grades (p = 0.0216), with higher expression in Grade 3 than Grade 2 (adjusted p = 0.0260), but did not increase monotonically with morphological organization. Grade 3 aggregation was associated with longer overall survival (HR, 0.372; 95% CI, 0.172-0.807; p = 0.0177) and post-progression survival (HR, 0.307; 95% CI, 0.142-0.663; p = 0.0042), but not progression-free survival. Transcriptomic analysis placed IRF4 within a TLS-related immune context, while IRF4 manipulation in A20 cells altered Cxcr5, Ccr7, Lta, and Ltb expression and Tfh-like/IL-21 responses. CONCLUSION: Biopsy-captured B-cell organization and regional IRF4 expression may provide complementary information on TLS-related immunity when comprehensive TLS characterization is limited by small-biopsy sampling.
