papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Pulmonary fungal infections are increasingly recognized as important complications of acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but early identification remains challenging. This study investigated the independent association between peak expiratory flow (PEF) and pulmonary fungal infection in hospitalized patients with AECOPD. METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 729 adult inpatients with AECOPD admitted to a tertiary hospital in Chongqing from January to December 2023. PEF was measured after admission and before treatment initiation. Pulmonary fungal infection was diagnosed based on host risk factors, microbiological evidence, clinical findings, and histopathology. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between PEF and pulmonary fungal infection. Subgroup and mediation analyses were also performed. RESULTS: The mean age was 71.7 years, and 68.4% were male. Patients with pulmonary fungal infection were older and had lower PEF values than those without infection (2.1 ± 0.9 vs 2.4 ± 1.3, respectively), and showed higher ESR, CRP, and IL-6 levels. After covariate adjustment, higher PEF was independently associated with a lower risk of pulmonary fungal infection (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.66-0.98, P = 0.034). This association remained consistent across age, sex, and smoking subgroups, without significant interactions. Age partially mediated this association, accounting for 15.68% of the total effect. CONCLUSION: Lower PEF was independently associated with increased pulmonary fungal infection risk in hospitalized patients with AECOPD. PEF may serve as a simple bedside indicator for early risk stratification and targeted clinical evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are at an elevated risk of fungal infections, yet reliable tools for early risk stratification are lacking. This study aimed to analyze the risk factors associated with fungal infections in patients with COPD and to develop a predictive model. METHODS: This study retrospectively analyzed patients with COPD who were admitted to Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital, between June 2021 and June 2023. Demographic and clinical data were extracted from electronic medical records. The risk factors were explored by univariate logistic regression and stepwise multivariate logistic regressions. Model performance was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic curve and area under the curve (AUC), along with calibration and decision curve analyses. The internal validation was performed using Bootstrap (n=1000) method. RESULTS: A total of 498 patients with COPD were enrolled, with 78 patients in the fungal infection group. Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that PaO2 within the normal range (OR=2.04, 95% CI: 1.12-3.71, P=0.02) and mold mix specific IgE above the normal threshold (OR=2.37, 95% CI: 1.04-5.36, P=0.04) were independently associated with an increased risk of fungal infections, whereas lymphocyte counts within the normal range (OR=0.37, 95% CI: 0.21-0.63, P<0.01) were associated with a reduced risk. Procalcitonin, albumin, and medical history of COPD duration were also included in predictive model based on the regression analysis. The AUC was 0.74 (95% CI: 0.68-0.79), and the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test and decision curves indicated good differentiation and calibration. CONCLUSION: This study identifies elevated PaO2, mold mix specific IgE and lymphocyte counts as risk factors for fungal infections. The predictive model incorporating PaO2, mold mix specific IgE, lymphocyte counts, procalcitonin, albumin, and medical history of COPD duration demonstrated good predictive performance, offering a potential tool for early identification of high-risk patients in clinical practice.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medicine, Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center, Shreveport, USA.
papers.abstract_en: The radiology report is essential for directing the course of treatment for a patient. However, writing radiology reports is a huge burden for radiologists. Manual reporting faces challenges due to intra-labeler and inter-labeler variability, causing inconsistent patient treatment and diagnostic results, and complicating matters due to alertness and changing judgment. To address these challenges, we propose an automated radiology report generation model tailored for chest X-ray imaging. We introduce BLIX-Ray, a vision-language model (VLM) designed to generate radiology reports using a transfer learning approach. BLIX-Ray fine-tunes the pre-trained BLIP model to extract and align rich visual and textual representations suited to the medical imaging domain. We use reinforcement learning (RL) to directly optimize report generation based on language evaluation metrics in order to further enhance performance. We evaluate BLIX-Ray on two publicly available datasets: IU-Xray and CheXpert Plus. Experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves the highest CIDEr and BERTScore on both datasets, while n-gram-oriented baselines retain an advantage on BLEU. BLIX-Ray integrates reinforcement learning and transfer learning to improve medical report generation under limited and heterogeneous data conditions. The results highlight the potential of vision-language models to support automated and standardized radiology reporting. Notably, BLIX-Ray achieves the best reported CIDEr (0.6534) and BERTScore (0.8765) among the compared methods on IU-Xray and leads on CIDEr, METEOR, and BERTScore on CheXpert Plus (BERTScore 0.8407), demonstrating strong report-level consensus and semantic similarity with the reference reports.

papers.title_zh: Comparing a straight-to-biopsy versus pleural aspiration-first approach in malignant and tuberculous pleural effusions.
papers.title_en: Comparing a straight-to-biopsy versus pleural aspiration-first approach in malignant and tuberculous pleural effusions.
papers.authors: Goh KJ, Tang KJY, Chia NAME, Chua BLW, Tan QL, Rahman NM, Young SL
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, Singapore General Hospital, Singapore, Singapore.
papers.abstract_en: BackgroundPleural aspiration has limited diagnostic yield in malignant (MPE) and tuberculous pleural effusions (TPE), more so when requiring molecular profiling in MPE and due to the paucibacillary nature of TPE. In our institution, patients with suspected MPE or TPE are offered a straight-to-biopsy approach with pleural biopsy as the initial diagnostic procedure, or a pleural aspiration-first approach, through shared decision-making.ObjectivesTo compare clinical outcomes between a straight-to-biopsy strategy and a pleural aspiration-first approach in patients diagnosed with MPE or TPE.DesignWe performed a retrospective study of patients who underwent pleural procedures for unilateral effusions between January 2022 and February 2025 and were diagnosed with MPE or TPE. We excluded patients with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group status ≥ 3 and patients with a pre-existing, established diagnosis of metastatic cancer who had pleural procedures performed for non-diagnostic intent.MethodsClinical outcomes were compared between a straight-to-biopsy versus pleural aspiration-first approach.Results271 patients were included (mean age 67 years, SD 15); 74.9% had MPE and 25.1% had TPE. Straight-to-biopsy and pleural aspiration-first approaches were undertaken in 44.3% and 55.7% of patients, respectively. Most patients in the straight-to-biopsy group underwent medical thoracoscopy (92.5%, 111/120), with concurrent talc pleurodesis performed in 55 patients. Compared with pleural aspiration-first, a straight-to-biopsy approach was associated with a shorter time to actionable diagnosis (16 (IQR:9-21) vs 23 (IQR:16-40) days; p<0.001), earlier treatment initiation (22 (IQR:16-33) vs 27 (IQR:18-43) days; p=0.023), shorter hospitalisation for diagnostic evaluation (4 (IQR:3-5) vs 8 (IQR:5-13) days; p<0.001), and were less likely to require ≥2 diagnostic (3.3% vs 42.4%; p<0.001) or therapeutic pleural procedures (21.1% vs 50.0%; p<0.001).ConclusionIn patients with MPE or TPE, a straight-to-biopsy approach was associated with earlier diagnosis and treatment initiation, fewer repeat procedures, and shorter hospitalisation. Prospective studies are needed to establish its safety, clinical utility, and cost-effectiveness.

papers.title_en: PLD1-driven oncogenic secretion creates a therapeutic vulnerability in chromosome 3q-amplified NSCLC.
papers.authors: Tan X, Wang S, Lee S, Xiao GY, Cardin DL, Zhang D, Xu Y, Wu C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Section of Hematology and Medical Oncology, Department of Medicine, Tulane University School of Medicine, New Orleans, L…
papers.abstract_en: Chromosome 3q (3q) amplification is a frequent event in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and other cancer types, yet therapeutic strategies targeting oncogenic drivers within this amplicon have been unsuccessful. Our study revealed that the 3q amplicon encodes multiple Golgi-related proteins, including Phospholipase D1 (PLD1), which catalyzes the production of a potential oncogenic lipid, phosphatidic acid. We found that PLD1 is highly expressed in 3q-amplified NSCLC (3q-NSCLC) and its enzymatic activity is further boosted by coamplified PLD1 activator, ARF-like GTPase 14. High PLD1 activity is essential for 3q-NSCLC growth and metastasis. Mechanistically, PLD1 drives secretion of oncogenic factors via the carriers from the trans Golgi network to the cell surface pathway to support tumor growth. Transferrin receptor 1 (TFRC), which encodes a membrane protein, is coamplified with PLD1 and overexpressed in 3q-NSCLC. A TFRC antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) carrying a PLD1 inhibitor exhibited potential antitumor activity in mouse models. These findings establish PLD1 as a promoter of 3q-NSCLC and provide proof of concept for the development of PLD1-targeted therapies, including ADC-based approaches, for this challenging cancer subtype.

papers.title_en: Salvage gastrectomy for perforated gastric intramural metastasis after definitive chemoradiotherapy for distal esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a case report.
papers.authors: Leelapatanadit J, Sangthong S, Waratchanont R, Asanprakit W, Kaewkangsadan V, Satthaporn S
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Surgery, Phramongkutklao Hospital, Thung Phaya Thai, Ratchathewi, Bangkok 10400, Thailand.
papers.abstract_en: Gastric intramural metastasis from esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is rare, and chemotherapy-associated perforation is exceptionally uncommon. We report a case of a 67-year-old man with distal ESCC and a separate cardia squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). He declined esophagectomy and received definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT) with paclitaxel, carboplatin, and 50.4 Gy radiotherapy. During the second chemotherapy cycle, the cardia tumor perforated and was treated by emergency omental patch repair. Chemoradiotherapy was subsequently completed. Three months after completion of dCRT, the esophageal lesion showed a clinical complete response, whereas residual cardia disease persisted. Extended total gastrectomy with splenectomy achieved R0 resection; pathology showed a 6-cm pT3 moderately differentiated SCC with partial treatment response and 0/12 positive nodes. Postoperative nivolumab was administered. This case illustrates a staged salvage strategy for persistent gastric intramural disease after definitive chemoradiotherapy.

papers.title_en: Design, synthesis, and anticancer evaluation of Biginelli-derived DHPM-amide hybrids bearing clinically inspired kinase-directed pharmacophores: EGFR docking and DFT studies.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Chemistry, Atamiya University Rajkot 360005 Gujarat India Suresh.koradiya@gmail.com.
papers.abstract_en: A series of twelve novel dihydropyrimidine (DHPM)-amide hybrid conjugates (6a-c, 8a-c, 10a-c, and 12a-c) were rationally designed, synthesized, and biologically evaluated as potential EGFR-targeted anticancer agents against A549 non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) cells. The target compounds were constructed via a convergent two-step protocol: Biginelli multicomponent condensation to assemble the DHPM-carboxylic acid core (4a-c), followed by EDC·HCl/HOBt-mediated chemoselective amide coupling with four clinically inspired amine fragments derived from erlotinib/gefitinib (series 10), cabozantinib (series 8), imatinib (series 12), and a sorafenib bioisostere (series 6). All compounds were characterized by IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and low-resolution ESI-MS. MTT cytotoxicity screening identified compound 10b as the most potent analogue (IC50 = 16.11 ± 0.11 µg mL-1, equivalent to 23.31 µM), exceeding the molar potency of the reference methotrexate (IC50 = 15.00 ± 0.48 µg mL-1, equivalent to 33.01 µM). It should be noted that methotrexate is a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor included solely as a general cytotoxicity control and is not a mechanistically matched EGFR comparator; the comparison therefore reflects relative cytotoxic potency only and does not imply EGFR selectivity. Molecular docking against EGFR (PDB 1M17), an erlotinib-bound inactive-conformation structure, returned the most favourable score for 10b (score = -7.819 kcal mol-1), with predicted hydrogen bonds to ASP831 and LYS721, a halogen contact at ILE765, and an extensive 15-residue hydrophobic network; these poses indicate compatibility with the erlotinib-binding pocket rather than a confirmed ATP-competitive binding mode. DFT calculations at B3LYP/6-311G(d,p) characterised the electronic structure of the isolated molecule (ΔE = 4.045 eV; ω = 3.155 eV) and are reported as a physicochemical description only, without implying a causal link to cellular activity. Normal mode analysis indicated conformational stability of the 10b-EGFR complex, collectively identifying 10b as a promising lead for further optimisation and mechanistic evaluation, for which direct EGFR kinase assays remain necessary.

papers.abstract_en: Thoracic surgery-related malpractice claims recorded in Catalonia (Spain) were collected from the Council of Medical Associations of Catalonia (CCMC, 1986-2024) and the Catalan Health Service (CatSalut, 2017-2024) databases. Of a total of 15,696 claims, 56 (0.4%) corresponded to the field of thoracic surgery. Lung cancer (51.8%) and pneumothorax (8.9%) were the most common diagnoses. Death occurred in 18 patients (31.2%). In relation to the reasons of allegations, in one patient with lung cancer undergoing lobectomy who died in the postoperative period, this information was missing. In the remaining 55 patients, causes of allegations included incorrect treatment in 31 (56.4%), diagnostic error in 11 (20%), unexpected complication in 8 (14.5%), infection in 4 (7.3%), and insufficient follow-up in 1 (1.8%). Of the 43 claims with a closed status, malpractice was established in 11 cases, with compensation ranging from €2000 to €154,581.44. Malpractice claims in thoracic surgery predominantly involved elective oncological procedures.

papers.title_zh: ADH7 and plasma proteins mediate smoking-related esophageal cancer: genetic causality and therapeutic insight.
papers.title_en: ADH7 and plasma proteins mediate smoking-related esophageal cancer: genetic causality and therapeutic insight.
papers.authors: Pan L, Yang X, Hao Q, Xie K, Ma H
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University, Suzhou, China.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Smoking has been linked to alterations in plasma protein profiles and increased risk of esophageal cancer (EC). However, the precise mediating roles of plasma proteins in this relationship remain unclear. This study explores the mediation effects of plasma proteins in smoking-associated EC, utilizing genetic proxies to uncover potential biological mechanisms underpinning this association. METHODS: Genetic correlation and Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses were applied to examine the association between smoking traits and EC. Pathway enrichment analysis explored circulatory protein changes in smokers. A two-step mediation MR analysis identified key plasma proteins involved in smoking-related EC pathogenesis. Survival analysis assessed the impact of transcriptional levels of mediators on EC prognosis, while phenome-wide association studies (PheWAS) evaluated the safety of targeted molecules and investigated potential pleiotropy. The expression and function of ADH7 were evaluated by qRT-PCR and in vitro experiments. RESULTS: Genetic correlation analysis showed significant links between smoking and EC, supported by MR findings that confirmed a causal relationship. Smoking was found to influence pathways related to cytokine signaling, immune activation, and the STAT pathway. Five plasma proteins (ADH7, CPXM1, FUT3, GZMM, LYPD3) were identified as mediators in smoking-driven EC risk. Among these, ADH7 emerged as a key protein and was consistently associated with smoking traits; high ADH7 mRNA expression in EC tumor tissue was associated with reduced progression-free survival. PheWAS inferred that ADH7-targeted interventions might pose risks of neurological or psychiatric side effects, though these were not statistically significant. qRT-PCR and immunohistochemistry showed that ADH7 was downregulated in EC tissues relative to adjacent normal mucosa, and functional assays demonstrated that overexpression of ADH7 suppressed the proliferative and migratory capacity of EC cells. Serum ELISA further revealed that circulating ADH7 concentrations were elevated in smokers and in EC patients, with the highest levels observed in smoking EC patients, supporting a role for smoking-driven elevation of circulating ADH7 in EC risk. CONCLUSIONS: This study reveals a compartment-specific, dual role for ADH7 in smoking-related EC: elevated circulating ADH7, driven in part by smoking, is associated with increased EC risk, whereas ADH7 acts as a tumor suppressor within esophageal tumor tissue. These findings provide novel genetic and mechanistic insights into smoking-related EC pathogenesis and highlight the importance of distinguishing circulating from tissue-level protein function when interpreting biomarker-disease associations.

papers.title_en: Integrating DWI Parameters with RECIST 1.1 for Early Assessment of Systemic Therapy Response in Lung Cancer Pelvic Bone Metastases.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiology, Seoul St.
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To determine preliminary quantitative ADC thresholds for functional response and to evaluate whether integrating DWI metrics with RECIST 1.1 provides complementary information for early systemic therapy response assessment in bone metastases. METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included lung cancer patients with pelvic bone metastases who underwent three MRIs between November 2015 and November 2023: baseline, early time point (<4 months, TP1), and late (6-15 months, TP2) time points. ROC analysis based on lesion size change at TP2 determined ADC thresholds defining DWI response. A DWI response was defined as ADC >1300 µm²/s or ΔADC >0.14. An integrated response scheme (DWI-RECIST) combined this DWI-based response with RECIST assessment. Early responses at TP1 were compared between RECIST and DWI-RECIST using RECIST at TP2 as reference standard. Interobserver agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using net reclassification improvement and AUCs. RESULTS: Seventy-eight lesions from 27 patients were included. Compared with RECIST, DWI-RECIST yielded net classification gains of 7.4% (reader 1) and 11.1% (reader 2). DWI-RECIST showed higher AUCs than RECIST (reader 1: 0.6964 vs. 0.6184, p = 0.472; reader 2: 0.6415 vs. 0.6184, p = 0.781). Interobserver agreement for ADC was good (ICC 0.83-0.86). CONCLUSIONS: Integrating ADC-derived DWI metrics with RECIST 1.1 may provide complementary information for early assessment of pelvic bone metastases from lung cancer, particularly in lesions categorised as stable disease. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This pilot study proposes quantitative ADC thresholds and introduces a framework integrating these with RECIST 1.1 to support more objective response assessment in lung cancer pelvic bone metastases.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Black and Hispanic people with cystic fibrosis (PwCF) experience worse health outcomes. Health disparities are exacerbated by clinical research that does not adequately represent the diversity of the CF population. RESEARCH QUESTIONS: How do Black/African American and Hispanic/Latino(a) PwCF perceive clinical research? What are the barriers and facilitators to participation in research? Are there viable solutions to improve inclusion? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Semi-structured, individual interviews were conducted with PwCF aged ≥18 years who identify as Black/African American race and/or Hispanic/Latino(a) ethnicity. Participants were recruited from six geographically diverse CF centers and through CF Foundation Community Voice, a CF community partner organization. The interview guide was created by a committee that included minoritized PwCF, research coordinators, and physician-scientists. Thematic analysis with inductive and deductive coding was used to analyze interview transcripts. RESULTS: Twenty PwCF were interviewed from 2024 to 2025. Drawing from a race-conscious adaptation of the Behavioral Model for Vulnerable Populations, we used domains of predisposing, need-based, and healthcare environment factors, as well as emergent themes relating to information and support needs. Participants discussed barriers to research participation that included narrow eligibility criteria (e.g., genotype requirements, health status) and logistical challenges such as time and cost. PwCF described a sense of isolation as persons of color with CF, which impacted sense of trust in CF care and research studies. They highlighted that racialized experiences, especially doubt surrounding their CF diagnosis, significantly impact willingness to participate. Solutions center around providing community support to address feelings of isolation and information needs to provide transparency about study design and intent. INTERPRETATION: Participation in clinical research is strongly influenced by an interplay of social, cultural, health, and systemic factors. Solutions to improve inclusion in trials center the needs of marginalized communities across all phases of study design and implementation.

papers.abstract_en: Organoid technology has emerged as a research hotspot in the biomedical field in recent years, providing important methodologies for disease modeling, drug screening, and regenerative medicine. Alveolar organoids serve as crucial models for studying respiratory diseases, and their technological evolution and application expansion reflect key advances in this field. This article systematically reviews the developmental history of organoids, provides an in-depth comparison of the applicability and limitations of different culture and characterization strategies for alveolar organoids, summarizes and critically analyzes alveolar organoid models established for common respiratory diseases, and offers perspectives on future directions in this area.

The neurological exam was notable for subtle sustained nystagmus on right and upward gaze. A code stroke was called and CT brain revealed no acute intracranial abnormality. MRI brain demonstrated new subtle restriction diffusion and FLAIR hyperintensity along the anterior surface of the brainstem and the middle cerebellar peduncles without evidence of enhancement, concerning for leptomeningeal disease. The remainder of the supratentorial metastases were stable. Lumbar puncture was performed and CSF analysis confirmed metastatic adenocarcinoma.

papers.abstract_en: Enteric‑type thymic adenocarcinoma (ETAC) is a rare subtype of thymic carcinoma. It shares highly similar histological and immunophenotypic features with intestinal adenocarcinoma, and is therefore prone to being misdiagnosed as metastatic carcinoma of gastrointestinal origin. Herein, we report a case of advanced ETAC with axillary lymph node oligometastasis. Positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) and gastrointestinal endoscopy were performed to rule out primary gastrointestinal malignancy. The patient underwent median sternotomy with extended thymectomy, which effectively relieved superior vena cava obstruction and cardiopulmonary compressive symptoms. Postoperatively, systemic chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy, as well as regional radiotherapy targeting the primary tumor bed and metastatic lymph nodes, were administered. The patient remained disease‑free during the 24‑month postoperative follow‑up. This case suggests that aggressive local therapy combined with molecular‑subtype‑based systemic treatment may offer novel therapeutic opportunities for carefully selected patients with advanced ETAC and oligometastases. .

papers.abstract_en: Atomically precise metal clusters hold great promise for cancer theranostics, yet current strategies for introducing tumor-targeting functionality often compromise their structural precision. Herein, an erlotinib (Er)-functionalized gold cluster, Au8-Er, is constructed through ligand engineering for targeted non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) theranostics. The Er ligands endow Au8-Er with high affinity toward the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), enabling selective tumor targeting and preferential accumulation at lung tumor sites. Under the glutathione-rich tumor microenvironment, Au8-Er releases Er to achieve chemotherapy. Simultaneously, the cluster exhibits strong X-ray attenuation and oxygen-sensitive phosphorescence, allowing it to function as both an X-ray scintillator and a photosensitizer for efficient X-ray-induced photodynamic therapy (X-PDT) under low-dose irradiation. Moreover, its X-ray-excited luminescence enables high-contrast imaging. The synergistic integration of targeted chemotherapy, X-PDT, and imaging within a structurally precise nanoplatform results in enhanced therapeutic efficacy against NSCLC. This work highlights ligand engineering as an effective strategy for imparting biological functionality to atomically precise metal clusters and advances their application in precision cancer theranostics.

papers.authors: Venkatesharao SM, Jayaraman A
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pharmacology, M.
papers.authors_conclusion: 提出的MUC5B/TGF-β/KL-6机制信号提供了连接遗传易感性、上皮功能障碍、生物标志物升高和IPF进展的整合分子网络；这些相互关联的分子机制可为生物标志物驱动的预后方法和靶向精准治疗提供重要见解。

papers.abstract_en: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic lung disorder strongly mediated by genetic susceptibility and aberrant epithelial repair mechanisms. Among the identified genetic factors, the MUC5B promoter polymorphism rs35705950 represents the most significant and frequently replicated risk variant associated with both familial and sporadic IPF. This review focuses on the mechanistic role of MUC5B dysregulation in promoting epithelial dysfunction and profibrotic signalling, with particular emphasis on its interaction with transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signalling and KL-6-associated epithelial injury. Excessive MUC5B expression within distal airways disrupts mucociliary homeostasis, prolongs epithelial exposure to inhaled toxic stimuli, and enhances persistent alveolar stress, thereby facilitating chronic epithelial injury and aberrant tissue repair. Sustained epithelial damage subsequently activates TGF-β-mediated SMAD signalling pathways, promoting fibroblast activation, myofibroblast differentiation, and extracellular matrix deposition. Emerging evidence further suggests a close relationship between MUC5B-associated epithelial dysfunction and elevated KL-6 expression, indicating that KL-6 may function as a downstream biomarker indicating ongoing epithelial injury and fibrotic progression. The proposed MUC5B/TGF-β/KL-6 mechanistic signaling provides an integrated molecular network linking genetic susceptibility, epithelial dysfunction, biomarker elevation, and progressive fibrosis in IPF. In addition, telomere-related and surfactant-associated gene mutations further lead to epithelial instability and impaired regenerative capacity. Together, these interconnected molecular mechanisms provide significant insights into IPF progression and may support the development of biomarker-driven prognostic approaches and targeted precision therapies for improved disease management.

papers.abstract_en: Respirable crystalline silica (RCS) is a major occupational health hazard associated with silicosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), lung cancer, autoimmune diseases, and other systemic disorders. Saudi Arabia is undergoing rapid industrial expansion in sectors with substantial potential for RCS exposure, including mining, construction, cement production, glass manufacturing, oil and gas, engineered stone fabrication, and photovoltaic manufacturing. This review evaluates the potential risk of occupational RCS exposure in Saudi Arabia by integrating evidence from the scientific literature, government reports, labor and mining statistics, mineralogical data, and regulatory documents. The novel silica Hazard triangle framework was applied to assess three principal determinants of occupational exposure: workforce distribution, silica-containing materials, and high-risk industrial activities. Saudi Arabia possesses extensive reserves of high-purity silica sand, and continued expansion of mining and downstream silica-based industries may increase occupational exposure potential. The kingdom's arid climate may also contribute to dust generation and increase the occupational exposure of RCS. Although documented cases of silicosis confirm that silica-related disease exists in Saudi Arabia, published evidence on occupational exposure assessment, epidemiology, and health surveillance remains limited. International regulatory developments demonstrate the importance of health-based occupational exposure limits (OELs), exposure monitoring, engineering controls, and medical surveillance. Current Saudi labor law, National Council for occupational safety and health (NCOSH) policies, and General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI) occupational disease frameworks provide an important legal and institutional foundation for the future development of silica-specific occupational health regulations. This review identifies important knowledge gaps and highlights the need for comprehensive exposure assessment, strengthened industrial hygiene capacity, and evidence-based regulatory strategies to reduce the future burden of silica-related diseases while supporting sustainable industrial development in Saudi Arabia.

papers.authors: Sun J, Bao P, Bai Y, Chen C, Lv H, Lin J, Wang C, Shen J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Tangdu Hospital, The Fourth Military Medical University, Xi'an, China.

papers.ai_note: 主要终点之一OS为阴性（P=0.058），结论与标题表述均以DFS及亚组获益为主，且亚组为事后探索性分层（交互P=0.025），样本量有限；回顾性设计下辅助免疫治疗的选择存在未测混杂（PSM仅平衡已知变量），非MPR/ypN+亚组的HR基于小样本，需前瞻性验证；摘要未提供各亚组例数及多因素HR/CI，信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT) plus high-quality surgery (R0 resection with systematic lymphadenectomy >19 nodes) is a promising strategy. However, the value of adjuvant immunotherapy remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between postoperative adjuvant immunotherapy and survival outcomes in a multicenter cohort. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study enrolled LA-ESCC patients receiving NCIT from eight high-volume Chinese centers between 2019 and 2023. After screening for high-quality surgery, propensity score matching (PSM) balanced characteristics between the two groups: NCIT plus surgery (NCIT+S) and NCIT plus surgery followed by adjuvant immunotherapy (NCIT+S+ICI). The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). A prognostic framework based on major pathological response (MPR) and postoperative pathological N stage (ypN) was constructed to refine patient selection. RESULTS: Among 724 patients with a median follow-up of 40.3 months, 3-year OS and DFS rates were 73.0% and 67.7%, respectively. After PSM, adjuvant immunotherapy significantly improved DFS (77.1% vs 65.8%, log-rank P=0.037), but not OS (83.4% vs 69.4%, log-rank P=0.058). Multivariate analysis identified ypN, MPR, and postoperative adjuvant immunotherapy as independent prognostic factors for DFS. Stratification by MPR and ypN status showed that DFS benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy was restricted to the non-MPR/ypN+ subgroup (HR=0.339; 95% CI: 0.173-0.662; log-rank P<0.001), with a significant treatment-by-subgroup interaction (P for interaction=0.025). CONCLUSIONS: Among LA-ESCC patients receiving NCIT and high-quality surgery, adjuvant immunotherapy significantly improves 3-year DFS in the non-MPR/ypN+ subgroup, with no significant benefit in other subgroups.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To develop quality assurance models for adverse procedural events after lung resection and esophagectomy for cancer. METHODS: Using procedural outcomes after 16,430 lung resections and 3,068 esophagectomies for cancer at 9 hospitals in 7 hospital systems, we developed 5 individual and 2 composite outcome models from preoperative information. Random forest quantile classification for imbalanced data with model-free variable priority screening identified predictors. Out-of-bag prediction provided regularized estimates and internal validation. Hospital-holdout analysis assessed institutional benchmark stability. RESULTS: Of 71 lung resection and 63 esophagectomy preoperative variables, 35 and 29, respectively, were identified as important predictors across the 7 outcome models. These included demographics, advanced cancer, organ dysfunction, higher acuity, and planned surgical approach and resection extent. Out-of-bag calibration covered a modest range of probabilities. Out-of-bag geometric mean ranged from 0.588 to 0.713 for lung resection and 0.517 to 0.649 for esophagectomy. Continuous risk factors, particularly pulmonary function, provided high-importance information content, with complex dependency and interaction structure among predictors. Risk-factor magnitude differed among hospitals, as did their risk-adjusted outcomes according to patient risk as determined by counterfactual inference within a framework of virtual twins. For lung resection operative mortality, hospital-specific contrasts were stable when each focal hospital was excluded from the aggregate benchmark. CONCLUSIONS: Using contemporary machine learning, initial models for adverse procedural events after lung resection and esophagectomy for cancer have been developed. They provide surgeons, their patients, and hospital and hospital systems tools for patient risk assessment and for informing quality improvement initiatives in general thoracic surgery.

papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要未报告样本量、效应量及统计值；CDK9高表达与不良生存相关未给出HR/CI及校正因素；疗效与协同结论主要基于体外和动物前临床模型，尚不能直接外推至临床。
papers.abstract_en: Gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEAC) remains a highly aggressive malignancy with limited effective targeted therapies. Cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (CDK9), a key regulator of transcriptional elongation, has been implicated in oncogenic processes across multiple cancer types; however, its functional role and therapeutic potential in GEAC remain poorly defined. In this study, we systematically investigated CDK9 expression, function, and therapeutic targeting in GEAC, with particular emphasis on its interaction with the YAP/TEAD signaling axis. Immunohistochemical analysis of primary GEAC tumors and patient-derived xenografts revealed elevated CDK9 expression, which correlated with poor patient survival. Mechanistic studies using immunofluorescence and co-immunoprecipitation demonstrated a reciprocal regulatory interaction between CDK9 and YAP1, promoting transcriptional programs associated with tumor progression and radiation resistance. We developed novel CDK9-targeting proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) and identified YX0597 as a potent CDK9 degrader. YX0597 effectively suppressed RNAP II Ser2 phosphorylation (RNAP II P-S2) and downregulated oncogenic drivers, including MCL-1. Functionally, CDK9 degradation markedly inhibited GEAC cell proliferation, invasion, and tumor sphere formation, with enhanced efficacy in radiation-resistant cells. Integrated RNA sequencing and ATAC sequencing revealed that CDK9 degradation increased chromatin accessibility, reactivated epigenetically silenced genes, and profoundly suppressed YAP/TEAD transcriptional activity. These coordinated transcriptional and epigenetic alterations disrupted oncogenic homeostasis, resulting in broad cytotoxicity. Importantly, co-targeting CDK9 and YAP/TEAD signaling produced strong synergistic antitumor effects in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, our findings identify CDK9 as a critical oncogenic driver in GEAC and highlight CDK9 degradation, particularly in combination with YAP/TEAD inhibition, as a promising therapeutic strategy for refractory GEAC.

papers.abstract_en: While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized treatment of the patients with aero-upper digestive squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs), including esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), only a subset of patients benefit from ICIs, therefore entailing exploration of the mechanisms to regulate treatment responsiveness. POLE, as a subunit of DNA polymerase ε, possesses 3'-5' proofreading activity, and its mutations have been associated with favourable response to ICIs in several solid tumors. However, post-translational modification (PTM) of POLE and its impact on the therapeutic efficacy of ICIs are unknown. Here, this study demonstrates that ubiquitin-like protein 3 (Ubl3), whose expression is markedly downregulated in SCCs, covalently binds to Pole, reduces nuclear Pole levels, triggers DNA damage, and activates cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Notably, Ubl3 modification of Pole significantly primes the local immune microenvironment to mitigate the growth of murine aero-upper digestive SCC cells and boost the efficacy of αPD-1 treatment in vivo. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis further revealed that UBL3 expression is positively correlated with better clinical outcomes in a cohort of ESCC patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy combined with αPD-1. Together, our findings unravel UBL3 modification as a novel PTM mechanism governing subcellular location of POLE and its influence on immunotherapy responsiveness, thus making UBL3 modification as a promising immunomodulatory approach to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in patients with aero-upper digestive SCCs.

papers.abstract_en: Patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) have an unmet need for new therapies that improve survival. In this phase II trial, patients received ociperlimab and tislelizumab (A) or placebo and tislelizumab (B) (NCT04732494). The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) assessed by the investigator per RECIST v1.1. A total of 125 patients were randomized to A (N = 62) and B (N = 63). The primary endpoint was not met, with an ORR (95% confidence interval [CI]) assessed by the investigator of 30.6% (19.6-43.7) for A and 20.6% (11.5-32.7) for B (stratified risk difference: 9.9% [95% CI - 5.4 to 25.3]; stratified 2-sided p = 0.2114). At the final analysis, median OS (95% CI) was 10.2 (7.9-19.5) months for A and 9.3 (6.4-14.8) months for B (stratified HR [95% CI]: 0.92 [0.58-1.45]). A total of 25.8% (16/62) and 20.6% (13/63) of patients in A and B, respectively, experienced grade ≥3 treatment-related treatment-emergent adverse events. Exploratory biomarker analyses showed that patients with an inflamed tumor microenvironment, shown by the enriched expression of natural killer (NK) cells, T cells, macrophages, dendritic cells, and B-cell signatures, and NK cell signature enrichment, may benefit from ociperlimab plus tislelizumab. Adding ociperlimab to tislelizumab did not provide significant efficacy improvement in recurrent/metastatic second-line ESCC; the addition of ociperlimab to tislelizumab was generally well-tolerated. Trial registration: Clinicaltrials.gov: NCT04732494.

papers.title_zh: Brief Report: Characterization of the Potentially Actionable TP53 Y220C Mutation in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer. A Multicenter, European Thoracic Oncology Platform Study.
papers.title_en: Brief Report: Characterization of the Potentially Actionable TP53 Y220C Mutation in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer. A Multicenter, European Thoracic Oncology Platform Study.
papers.authors: Molina-Vila MA, Tsourti Z, Stenzinger A, Thüsen JV, Hillen LM, Hofman P, Rahmani-Khajouei S, Hegedüs B et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Laboratory of Oncology, Pangaea Oncology, Dexeus University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: The tumor suppressor TP53 is the most frequently mutated gene in human cancer, and drugs targeting specific mutant p53 proteins have been developed. Rezatapopt, which reactivates the Y220C p53 protein, was recently evaluated in the Phase I PYNNACLE trial in patients with solid tumors, with promising results. The trial did not enrol any non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cases, and little is known about the clinicopathological characteristics and genetic profile of the TP53 Y220C NSCLC patients. METHODS: In this multicenter, European Thoracic Oncology Platform-sponsored study, we retrospectively collected data from NSCLC patients from several European institutions with Next Generation Sequencing data available. RESULTS: The study included 28,244 NSCLC patients. We found that 195 (0.7%) harbored the TP53 Y220C mutation, a prevalence higher than the average in solid tumors (0.4%). Half of these TP53 Y220C NSCLC patients did not carry any known drivers. No significant association was observed between the TP53 Y220C and gender, smoking status, histology or stage. However, the mutation was significantly more prevalent in EGFR-mutant than EGFR-wild-type tumors (1.7% vs. 0.7%; p=0.029). Finally, 17.0% of Y220C patients carried a second mutation in TP53. CONCLUSIONS: The TP53 Y220C has a frequency similar to other low abundance, actionable alterations in NSCLC. Patients with NSCLC should be screened and included in future trials of Y220C reactivators. Co-mutations in TP53 should also be analyzed, since they might be associated with intrinsic resistance.

papers.title_zh: Predicting global and regional respiratory response in ARDS patients through individualized physics-based computational lung models: a prospective clinical pilot study.
papers.title_en: Predicting global and regional respiratory response in ARDS patients through individualized physics-based computational lung models: a prospective clinical pilot study.
papers.authors: Sablewski A, Ludwig M, Eichinger C, Lindner M, Frerichs I, Langguth P, Schädler D, Wall WA et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Anesthesiology and Intensive Care Medicine, University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein, Campus Kiel, Kie…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung-protective ventilation is essential in the management of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), but current approaches are limited by the heterogeneity of lung pathology and a lack of individualized strategies. Patient-specific computational models may overcome these limitations by providing predictive and physiologically interpretable insights into global and regional lung behavior. METHODS: Ten mechanically ventilated patients with ARDS were evaluated in a monocentric prospective pilot study. A predefined study protocol included ventilatory maneuvers with systematic changes in ventilator mode, tidal volume, positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), and driving pressure. For each patient, a personalized, regionally resolved physics-based computational lung model was generated and calibrated to reproduce the individual respiratory system mechanics. Model predictions of tidal volume, airway and transpulmonary pressures, end-expiratory lung volume (EELV), and electrical impedance tomography (EIT)-derived regional ventilation distribution were simulated for different PEEP levels and evaluated against clinically assessed reference values. Model predictions were compared to clinical data using Pearson correlation coefficients (r), root mean square error (RMSE), and Bland-Altman analyses. RESULTS: A strong agreement was observed between simulated and clinical data for tidal volumes (r = 0.925, p < 0.001, RMSE = 0.053 l) and driving pressures (r = 0.940, p < 0.001, RMSE = 1.328 mbar) across all PEEP levels. At initial PEEP level, a high image correlation (r > 0.8) was found between measured and simulated regional ventilation in five of seven patients where EIT data were available. CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study demonstrates the capability of the individualized, regionally resolved physics-based computational lung model to reproduce patient-specific respiratory mechanics and key features of regional ventilation patterns in ARDS. The strong agreement between simulated and measured data supports the potential of this approach to estimate the physiological response to ventilator adjustments and lays the groundwork for future studies integrating computational modeling into clinical decision-making. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered at the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00017151, https://drks.de/search/en/trial/DRKS00017151 ) at 12th April 2019.

papers.title_zh: Bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery for craniofacial hyperhidrosis: a 10-year retrospective cohort study on long-term outcomes and development of a prognostic predictive model.
papers.title_en: Bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery for craniofacial hyperhidrosis: a 10-year retrospective cohort study on long-term outcomes and development of a prognostic predictive model.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Chen H, Lin M, Lin J, Du Q, Chen J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University, 20 Chazhong Road, Fuzhou, 35…
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery for CFH, to characterize the 10-year longitudinal trajectory of postoperative CH and recurrence, and to identify clinically accessible predictors of CH and postoperative satisfaction that may assist in preoperative risk communication. Preliminary nomograms were developed and internally validated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration plots, sensitivity, and specificity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 127 patients who underwent bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery for CFH between April 2013 and April 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Baseline characteristics, operative details, and follow-up outcomes were extracted from medical records and structured telephone interviews. Predictive features were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Cox proportional hazards and multivariate logistic regression models were subsequently applied to identify independent predictors of CH and satisfaction, respectively. Nomograms were developed and internally validated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, sensitivity, and specificity. RESULTS: All patients achieved immediate resolution of craniofacial sweating, accompanied by a significant postoperative heart rate reduction (84.8 ± 11.68 → 72.17 ± 7.54 bpm, P < 0.001). Severe CH (grade IV) developed in 70.1% of patients, predominantly involving the thoracoabdominal (84.3%) and thigh (54.3%) regions. Cox regression identified preoperative heart rate > 79.5 bpm (HR = 2.46, 95% CI 1.61-3.75, P = 0.0002) and sympathetic clamping (HR = 5.69, 95% CI 3.03-10.67, P = 0.001) as independent risk factors for severe CH. Logistic regression showed that lower preoperative thoracoabdominal sweating was associated with higher postoperative satisfaction (OR = 0.05, 95% CI 0.01-0.23, P = 0.001). The nomograms demonstrated adequate discrimination and calibration. CONCLUSION: Bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery achieves rapid and durable relief of craniofacial hyperhidrosis with sustained high satisfaction over 10 years. Beyond confirming efficacy, the extended follow-up uniquely demonstrates that CH severity stabilizes within the first postoperative year and does not worsen over time-a critical finding for patient reassurance. Preoperative resting heart rate > 79.5 bpm and the use of sympathetic clamping independently predict severe CH, whereas lower baseline thoracoabdominal sweating predicts superior satisfaction. Although the proposed nomograms require external validation before routine adoption, they offer a practical, individualized reference for preoperative risk communication and, combined with the intraoperative choice of electrocautery, support a dual-phase strategy for optimizing surgical outcomes in CFH patients.

papers.title_zh: Early transcriptional divergence and spatial remodeling toward immune activation and evasion shape lung adenocarcinoma precancer evolution.
papers.title_en: Early transcriptional divergence and spatial remodeling toward immune activation and evasion shape lung adenocarcinoma precancer evolution.
papers.authors: Li JR, Zhu B, Chi Y, Chen H, Chen P, Hemaych JV, Tian Y, Hu X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Graduate Institute of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine, Chang Gung University, Taoyuan, Taiwan; Molecular Medici…
papers.abstract_en: Tumor heterogeneity is a universal feature of cancer and may arise as early as precancer stages during lung adenocarcinoma evolution, yet the emergence of aggressive transcriptional programs remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomics with single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity across hyperplasia, adenoma, and invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC) in a genetically engineered mouse model (129S4/Sv KrasLSL-G12D/+). Disease progression was accompanied by coordinated remodeling of epithelial, stromal, and immune compartments, along with dynamic changes in proliferation, immune response, and metabolic pathways. Notably, lesions of the same histological stage exhibited substantial transcriptional heterogeneity. By quantifying dedifferentiation states, we identified a subset of adenomas that had already diverged toward highly proliferative and metabolically active programs despite lacking invasive features. These lesions were further marked by early chromosome 6 amplification, whose corresponding human ortholog signature recapitulated aggressive proliferation-associated programs in early-stage human lung adenocarcinoma. Spatial analyses further revealed pronounced intratumoral heterogeneity within IAC, with tumor core regions showing increased proliferation and metabolism but reduced immune signaling compared to peripheral regions. In addition, immune checkpoint gene expression in T cells was transiently elevated at the hyperplasia stage, suggesting early immune modulation prior to overt malignancy. Together, these findings indicate that aggressive transcriptional divergence can emerge early during lung adenocarcinoma evolution and that spatial organization critically shapes tumor and immune programs before and after invasion.

papers.title_zh: Spatiotemporal Analysis of Molecular Continuity in Pathogenesis of Squamous Cell Carcinoma: From Normal Epithelium to Precancerous Lesions and Carcinoma.
papers.title_en: Spatiotemporal Analysis of Molecular Continuity in Pathogenesis of Squamous Cell Carcinoma: From Normal Epithelium to Precancerous Lesions and Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Lan L, Wang X, Jiang X, Lin X, Lai Y, Tan W, Zhang S, Lin D et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Etiology and Carcinogenesis, National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center/Cancer Hospital, Chi…
papers.abstract_en: Squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) develop from the stratified epithelia of the esophagus, head and neck, lung, and skin, providing a tractable model to investigate how altered epithelial fields progress toward invasive cancer. Across SCC subtypes, evolution often begins before overt malignancy, with age- and exposure-associated mutant clones expanding within histologically normal epithelia. As lesions advance, early driver selection becomes coupled to copy number alterations, chromosomal instability, and epigenetic remodeling, whereas later stages are shaped by branching diversification, cellular plasticity, and regionally constrained selection. Despite tissue-specific differences, several recurrent principles emerge, including clonal expansion within mutated normal fields, transition bottlenecks marked by genome-scale instability, and the spatial organization of subclonal architecture and invasive-front states. In this review, we synthesize recent progress in the temporal ordering and spatial patterning of SCC evolution and discuss how genetic alterations, epigenetic remodeling, and tissue ecology jointly drive disease progression. We further highlight the implications for early interception, biomarker development, immune evasion, and evolution-informed prevention and therapy.

papers.title_zh: Genome-wide identification and characterization of the PE/PPE gene family in Mycobacterium abscessus.
papers.title_en: Genome-wide identification and characterization of the PE/PPE gene family in Mycobacterium abscessus.
papers.authors: Gao P, Wang X, Xie L, Long Q
papers.affiliation_highlight: Key Laboratory of Molecular Biology for Infectious Diseases (Ministry of Education), Institute for Viral Hepatitis, Depa…
papers.abstract_en: Mycobacterium abscessus (Mab) is a rapidly growing non-tuberculous mycobacterium that causes opportunistic infections and exhibits extensive intrinsic antibiotic resistance. The proline-glutamate (PE) and proline-proline-glutamate (PPE) protein families are mycobacteria-specific virulence factors implicated in immune modulation, antigenic variation, and persistence. While Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) harbors approximately 170 PE/PPE members, the repertoire of PE/PPE genes in Mab remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we performed a genome-wide survey of PE/PPE genes in Mab ATCC 19,977 and identified 18 candidate family members, representing a relatively small fraction of the genome compared with slow-growing mycobacteria. Most predicted proteins harbor canonical PE or PPE domains and display acidic physicochemical properties. Phylogenetic analysis resolved the proteins into three subfamilies: PE, PPE, and PE-PPE, revealing moderate structural diversity but limited family expansion. Motif and gene structure analyses supported the evolutionary conservation. Notably, no PE_polymorphic GC-rich repetitive sequence (PE_PGRS) or PPE_major polymorphic tandem repeat (PPE_MPTR) members were detected, suggesting lineage-specific genomic reduction relative to other pathogenic mycobacteria. AlphaFold predictions revealed conserved N-terminal folds and variable C-terminal regions, which may contribute to functional diversification. Subcellular localization predictions indicated that most proteins are extracellular. Synteny analysis revealed no detectable collinearity among these genes. Transcriptomic analyses revealed condition-dependent expression of PE/PPE genes during amoeba and macrophage infection and under artificial sputum medium and metal ion stress, suggesting roles in environmental adaptation and host interaction. This study provides the first systematic overview of PE/PPE gene repertoire in Mab and lays the groundwork for elucidating their roles in intracellular survival, host interaction, and antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title_zh: Deleted in lymphocytic leukemia 2 contributes to lung fibroblast activation and pulmonary fibrosis by interacting with and triggering focal adhesion kinase phosphorylation.
papers.title_en: Deleted in lymphocytic leukemia 2 contributes to lung fibroblast activation and pulmonary fibrosis by interacting with and triggering focal adhesion kinase phosphorylation.
papers.authors: Zhu H, Lan J, Wu X, Gao Y, Ran X, He R, Luo Z, Cheng Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, Guizhou Provincial People's Hospital, Guiyang, Guizhou, 550002, P.…
papers.abstract_en: The etiology of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains unknown, and therapeutic interventions are currently restricted. The activation of lung fibroblasts and the focal adhesion kinase (FAK) signaling pathway are crucial to the pathogenesis of IPF, yet the exact molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Our study shows that the deleted in lymphocytic leukemia 2 (DLEU2) is elevated in the peripheral blood of patients with IPF, as well as in the lung tissues of mice with pulmonary fibrosis. Functional assays revealed that overexpression of DLEU2 facilitated fibrogenesis, whereas its suppression attenuated lung fibrosis in vivo and impeded fibroblast activation in vitro, predominantly through the regulation of FAK phosphorylation. Mechanistically, our findings reveal that DLEU2 regulates lung fibroblast activation by targeting miR-29a-3p. Conversely, inhibition of miR-29a-3p reversed the anti-fibrotic effects observed upon DLEU2 knockdown. Furthermore, DLEU2 was shown to directly interact with FAK, enhancing its phosphorylation and thereby facilitating fibrogenesis; inhibition of FAK phosphorylation counteracted the pro-fibrotic effects induced by DLEU2 overexpression. Taken together, these findings clarify the function of DLEU2 in facilitating FAK phosphorylation via its interactions with miR-29a-3p and FAK. The findings of this study suggest that DLEU2 may serve as a novel diagnostic biomarker and a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of IPF.

papers.title_zh: Apnea-hypopnea index-oxygen desaturation index (AHI-ODI) discordance in obstructive sleep apnea: association with symptom burden and cardiometabolic comorbidity: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
papers.title_en: Apnea-hypopnea index-oxygen desaturation index (AHI-ODI) discordance in obstructive sleep apnea: association with symptom burden and cardiometabolic comorbidity: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Ehab A, Abdelwahab HW, Hamoda M, Elhosiny MM
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Chest Medicine, Faculty of Medicine, Mansoura University, Mansoura, Egypt; DGD Hemer Lung Center, Hemer, G…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) counts respiratory events but not the depth or duration of accompanying desaturation. We examined AHI-ODI discordance (AHI minus oxygen desaturation index, ODI) and its associations with daytime symptom burden and prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity. METHODS: Single-center retrospective cross-sectional study of 200 adults with OSA (January 2023-January 2025). Five indices (AHI, ODI, mean SpO2, T90 and AHI-ODI discordance) were examined; excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS; Epworth Sleepiness Scale ≥ 11) was the primary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI and an AHI-ODI × sex interaction. RESULTS: The cohort was 77.5% male, median age 57 years (48.8-64.2). For EDS, AHI-ODI discordance showed the numerically highest AUC (0.639, p < 0.001), followed by T90 (0.627), and mean SpO2 and ODI (0.609 each); AHI was not significant (0.546, p = 0.264). No pairwise difference was significant. AHI-ODI discordance remained independently associated with EDS after adjustment (OR 1.04 per event/h, 95% CI 1.01-1.07, p = 0.008), with no significant sex interaction. Among secondary outcomes, T90 showed the highest AUCs for diabetes mellitus (0.644) and hypertension (0.615), and mean SpO2 for heart failure (0.608). No index discriminated against previous stroke or atrial fibrillation. CONCLUSIONS: AHI-ODI discordance was independently, but only modestly, associated with EDS, whereas oxygenation indices were related to prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity. The discrimination was insufficient, and all reported cut-offs are exploratory. AHI-ODI discordance is not a measure of sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden.

papers.title_zh: Recurrence Risk After Resection of Typical and Atypical Pulmonary Carcinoids: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.title_en: Recurrence Risk After Resection of Typical and Atypical Pulmonary Carcinoids: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.authors: Guevara-Tirado A, Barra GG, Espinoza MFXB
papers.affiliation_highlight: Universidad Científica del Sur, Lima, Peru.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary carcinoids generally have favorable outcomes after surgery, but postoperative recurrence differs substantially by histological subtype. Existing guidance recognizes atypical histology and nodal involvement as adverse features, yet a focused quantitative synthesis of the magnitude and consistency of this association remains limited. METHODS: MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception to July 12, 2026 for surgical cohorts reporting postoperative recurrence. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts and assessed full-text eligibility, with disagreements resolved by consensus. The primary meta-analysis emphasized the risk ratio (RR) of observed recurrence in atypical versus typical carcinoids using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp intervals; odds ratios (ORs) and risk differences were complementary measures. Time-defined recurrence, adjusted prognostic factors, and anatomical patterns were synthesized separately because of incompatible outcome definitions and effect measures. RESULTS: Eighteen reports were included in the review, 11 contributed structured quantitative evidence, and 7 independent comparative cohorts entered the primary meta-analysis. Among 1074 resected tumors, recurrence occurred in 24 of 816 typical carcinoids and 51 of 258 atypical carcinoids. The pooled RR of observed recurrence was 6.57 (95% CI, 3.65-11.84), with a complementary OR of 8.08 (95% CI, 4.20-15.53). No statistical heterogeneity was detected (I2 = 0%), but this result was interpreted cautiously because only seven studies were available and clinically important differences in follow-up, staging, pathological review, and surveillance remained. Leave-one-out RR estimates ranged from 5.77 to 7.48. Time-defined evidence suggested recurrence of approximately 18%-25% by 5 years and 29%-32% by 10 years in atypical tumors, whereas node-negative typical tumors generally remained below 5% at 10 years, although late events occurred. Nodal involvement, advanced pT category, and larger tumor size were adverse prognostic features. CONCLUSION: Observed recurrence after resection was substantially more frequent in atypical than in typical pulmonary carcinoids. Histology and nodal status provide a clinically useful basis for postoperative risk stratification, but the available evidence does not establish the optimal surveillance modality, interval, or duration.

papers.title_zh: Eosinophilic Oesophagitis and Incidence of Gastrointestinal Cancer: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
papers.title_en: Eosinophilic Oesophagitis and Incidence of Gastrointestinal Cancer: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
papers.authors: Kurt G, Farkas DK, Dellon ES, Jensen ET, Sørensen HT
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Clinical Epidemiology, Center for Population Medicine, Aarhus University and Aarhus University Hospital, A…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Evidence concerning gastrointestinal cancer risk after eosinophilic oesophagitis (EoE) diagnosis is limited. AIMS: To examine the association between EoE and incident gastrointestinal cancer in a population-based cohort. METHODS: Using nationwide Danish health registries, we identified all patients diagnosed with EoE between 1997 and 2024, using a validated algorithm. We computed standardised incidence ratios (SIRs) for gastrointestinal cancers overall and site-specific cancers compared with the general population. To distinguish short-term diagnostic activity from longer-term risk, we stratified analyses by < 1 and ≥ 1 year after EoE diagnosis. Secondary analyses examined oesophageal cancer incidence among EoE patients with coexisting Barrett's oesophagus (BE). RESULTS: Among 9115 EoE patients, 170 developed gastrointestinal cancers. During the first year after EoE diagnosis, the SIR was 2.83 (95% confidence interval: 2.10-3.74). Beyond 1 year, the overall SIR attenuated (1.03 [0.85-1.23]) but remained elevated for oesophageal cancer (2.40 [1.42-3.79]) and hepatocellular carcinoma (2.05 [0.98-3.77]). Among patients who developed oesophageal cancer ≥ 1 year after EoE diagnosis (n = 18), most had prior BE. The SIR for oesophageal cancer was 5.44 (2.90-9.31) among patients with both EoE and BE and 4.84 (4.36-5.37) among patients with BE alone. SIR for patients with EoE alone could not be reported due to the low number of cancer cases. CONCLUSIONS: One year after EoE diagnosis, oesophageal cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma rates remained elevated. Most oesophageal cancers occurred in patients with prior BE, suggesting that the association between EoE and oesophageal cancer may be mediated largely through BE.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pathology, Medical School of Nantong University, Nantong, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: We propose that a network pharmacology perspective can be adopted to understand the application of BsAbs in NSCLC and to guide their subsequent development.

papers.abstract_en: Over the past few decades, the emergence of immunotherapy and single-target drugs has brought new promise to the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Yet the high heterogeneity of NSCLC leads to both primary and acquired resistance that neither sequential monotherapy nor empirical combinations can effectively overcome. In contrast to the conventional coadministration of two separate monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) feature a series of molecular engineering designs that confer inherent synergistic antitumor effects. We propose that a network pharmacology perspective can be adopted to understand the application of BsAbs in NSCLC and to guide their subsequent development.

papers.title_zh: Predictive factors for prolonged hospitalization related to pneumothorax after CT-guided transthoracic needle biopsy.
papers.title_en: Predictive factors for prolonged hospitalization related to pneumothorax after CT-guided transthoracic needle biopsy.
papers.authors: Ko UW, Heo M, Park S, Hwang JH, Shin B
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Allergy, Pulmonology and Critical Care Medicine, Gil Medical Center, Gachon University College of Medicine…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pneumothorax is consistently reported as the most prevalent complication of computed tomography-guided transthoracic needle biopsy. While most cases of pneumothorax resolve with conservative management strategies, some cases are linked to a more protracted clinical trajectory necessitating active intervention. However, few reports have described the clinical and procedural determinants of prolonged hospitalization after post-biopsy pneumothorax. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 1,457 CT-guided TTNB procedures performed at a tertiary referral center between January 2021 and December 2025. The incidence of post-biopsy pneumothorax was 20.5%. Among 82 patients with prolonged hospitalization due to pneumothorax, their management strategies were categorized into two groups: (1) high-concentration oxygen therapy (n = 54) and (2) invasive interventions, including percutaneous catheter drainage (PCD) or chest tube insertion (n = 28). Logistic regression models with backward selection were used to identify predictive factors for prolonged hospitalization. RESULTS: Among the 82 patients with prolonged hospitalization due to pneumothorax, the median age was 75 years and 75.6% were male. In multivariable analysis, a lower diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) was independently associated with prolonged hospitalization (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.980; P = 0.004). In the high-concentration oxygen group, lower DLCO (aOR, 0.974; P = 0.007) and a trans-fissural needle route (aOR, 3.968; P = 0.028) were independently associated with prolonged hospitalization. Conversely, in the PCD/chest tube group, reduced forced expiratory volume in 1 s was independently associated with prolonged hospitalization (aOR, 0.961; P = 0.002). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with post-biopsy pneumothorax, impaired pulmonary function may be linked to a prolonged clinical course. Incorporating these pre-procedural physiological markers may facilitate improved risk stratification and optimized hospital resource allocation.

papers.title_zh: M4DTrack: A DICOM-Based Imaging Informatics Workflow for User-Supervised 4DCT Lung Tumor Motion Reporting.
papers.title_en: M4DTrack: A DICOM-Based Imaging Informatics Workflow for User-Supervised 4DCT Lung Tumor Motion Reporting.
papers.authors: Lee TK
papers.affiliation_highlight: Indiana University Health Arnett, Lafayette, IN, USA.
papers.abstract_en: Four-dimensional computed tomography (4DCT) is routinely used in radiotherapy simulation to evaluate respiration-induced tumor motion, but the motion information is often reviewed visually rather than captured as structured, phase-resolved data. We developed and evaluated M4DTrack, a DICOM-based imaging-informatics workflow for user-supervised 4DCT lung tumor motion analysis and structured, exportable three-dimensional center-of-mass (CoM) motion reporting. M4DTrack imports phase-resolved DICOM CT images, groups images by respiratory phase, displays linked axial/coronal/sagittal views, supports crosshair-based tumor localization and HU inspection, and applies seed or linked 3D-box initialization with sequential phase-to-phase HU-volume propagation. An 8-case lower-lobe lung 4DCT dataset (80 respiratory phases) was analyzed. Directional amplitudes, 3D vector amplitude, maximum phase-wise displacement, and agreement with independent ITV-GTV reference amplitudes were quantified. HU-weighted CoM amplitudes were 2.44 ± 1.44 mm, 2.64 ± 1.37 mm, and 6.04 ± 2.48 mm in X, Y, and Z patient-coordinate directions, respectively. Mean 3D vector amplitude was 7.26 ± 2.50 mm, and mean maximum phase-wise 3D displacement was 6.20 ± 2.10 mm. Biases versus ITV-GTV reference amplitudes were 0.01, - 0.84, and 0.23 mm for X, Y, and Z, respectively, with a 3D vector amplitude bias of - 0.29 mm. M4DTrack provides a user-supervised imaging-informatics bridge between qualitative 4DCT cine review and structured quantitative motion documentation. The pilot results support feasibility for generating exportable, phase-resolved tumor-motion metrics while preserving user-supervised review of 4DCT artifacts, HU-capture uncertainty, adjacent anatomy, and differences between CoM-based and extent-based measurements.

papers.title_zh: 3D-DDN Faster R-CNN: Pulmonary Nodule Detection Through Cross-Slice Feature Fusion and Dynamic Displacement Modeling.
papers.title_en: 3D-DDN Faster R-CNN: Pulmonary Nodule Detection Through Cross-Slice Feature Fusion and Dynamic Displacement Modeling.
papers.authors: Guan C, Yang D, Leng Z, Liu S, Zu A, Luo D, Chen H, Wang J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: School of Microelectronics and Data Science, Anhui University of Technology, Ma'anshan, Anhui, China.
papers.abstract_en: Accurate pulmonary nodule detection in computed tomography (CT) remains challenging because small- and low-contrast nodules may resemble vessels and other anatomical structures on individual axial slices. We propose 3D-DDN Faster R-CNN, a multi-slice detection framework that incorporates structured local axial context into a two-stage detector. The five-slice interactive blending (5-SIB) strategy organizes five consecutive CT slices as an ordered contextual group and preserves slice-specific feature streams extracted by a shared two-dimensional backbone. The cross-slice feature fusion (CSFF) module applies slice-wise spatial self-attention at shallow feature levels and learnable cross-slice aggregation at deep feature and region-of-interest levels. The dynamic displacement constraint (DDC) models proposal displacement across adjacent slices using a positive-sample regression loss and a margin-based negative-sample contrastive loss, while a class-weighted focal loss alleviates foreground-background imbalance. The model was evaluated on a private hospital dataset, LIDC-IDRI, and LNDb using patient-level data partitions. On the private hospital dataset, 3D-DDN achieved an average precision at an IoU threshold of 0.5 (AP0.5) of 75.80% ± 1.05%, a sensitivity of 89.33% ± 1.91%, and a competition performance metric (CPM) of 91.20% ± 1.50%. The corresponding AP0.5 values on LIDC-IDRI and LNDb were 66.27% ± 0.45% and 48.20% ± 0.30%, respectively. Ablation experiments showed that direct five-slice stacking degraded performance, whereas structured feature fusion and displacement supervision recovered the performance loss and improved the overall detection profile. These results indicate that ordered cross-slice representation, hierarchical feature fusion, and proposal-displacement supervision provide complementary mechanisms for incorporating local three-dimensional context.

papers.title_zh: Foot-to-foot lower-limb phase angle as a predictor of reduced exercise capacity in patients with interstitial lung disease: A comparative study with muscle mass and pulmonary function.
papers.title_en: Foot-to-foot lower-limb phase angle as a predictor of reduced exercise capacity in patients with interstitial lung disease: A comparative study with muscle mass and pulmonary function.
papers.authors: Kaneko K, Ishizaka M, Hara T, Chiba K, Takei K, Ishikawa F, Sakamoto K, Awano N et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Rehabilitation Technology Department, Japanese Red Cross Medical Center, 4-1-22 Hiroo, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, 150-8935, Japa…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Reduced exercise capacity, measured by the 6-min walk distance (6MWD), is a critical prognostic factor in interstitial lung disease (ILD). However, conventional physiological markers often fail to identify early functional decline. We aimed to evaluate whether the foot-to-foot lower-limb phase angle (F-F PhA), a non-invasive surrogate marker of muscle quality, predicts reduced exercise capacity better than traditional muscle mass and pulmonary function indices. METHODS: In this retrospective study of 68 patients with ILD, F-F PhA was measured using bioelectrical impedance analysis, and erector spinae muscle area (ESM_CSA) via computed tomography. Reduced exercise capacity was defined as 6MWD < 450 m. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age and pulmonary function (%DLCO or %FVC), with internal validation performed via 1000-resample bootstrapping. RESULTS: In multivariable analysis, F-F PhA was independently associated with a 6MWD < 450 m when adjusted for age and %DLCO (OR: 0.228, 95% CI: 0.088-0.591, p = 0.002; bootstrap p = 0.005) or %FVC (OR: 0.213, 95% CI: 0.091-0.496, p = 0.001; bootstrap p = 0.001). ROC analysis showed F-F PhA had the highest discriminative accuracy (AUC: 0.802), outperforming %DLCO (AUC: 0.729) and ESM_CSA (AUC: 0.701). Combining age, %DLCO, and F-F PhA achieved the highest performance (AUC: 0.833). CONCLUSIONS: F-F PhA serves as a robust, independent indicator for predicting reduced exercise capacity in ILD, outperforming conventional muscle mass. As a non-invasive tool, F-F PhA complements established functional tests in screening for early physical decline.
