papers.title_zh: Improving equity in respiratory disease outcomes in Africa using data-driven tools: National Institute of Health Care and Research's (NIHR) EQUI-RESP-AFRICA project.
papers.title_en: Improving equity in respiratory disease outcomes in Africa using data-driven tools: National Institute of Health Care and Research's (NIHR) EQUI-RESP-AFRICA project.
papers.authors: Rudan I, Ozoh OO, Agbre-Yace ML, Bigogo G, Dangor Z, Saidu Y, Uneke C, Kourouma KR et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Centre for Global Health, Usher Institute, University of Edinburgh, UK.
papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pneumonia, influenza, asthma, tuberculosis, lung cancer, and COVID-19 are all prevalent in Africa, where they cause a very large burden on the population's health, but are managed by health systems with a limited capacity for prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. They are also underlaid by substantial inequities in outcomes, with the poorest who have no access to care being affected the most. An interdisciplinary group of academics, policymakers, representatives of non-governmental organisations (NGOs), patients, and civil society are implementing a programme to address key respiratory diseases (RD) in five African countries where morbidity and mortality from RD is very large: Nigeria, Kenya, Cameroon, Cote d'Ivoire, and South Africa. The aim is to build capacity, conduct quality research and an intervention trial, and engage communities and policymakers in order to achieve demonstrable and equitable reductions in morbidity and mortality from RD through evidence-based improvements in prevention, diagnosis, treatment, interventions, and policies. The EQUI-RESP-AFRICA project will map the landscape of respiratory medicine in partner countries through rapid reviews of the available literature and data; engage relevant in-country stakeholders; study patients' and providers' preferences and needs; identify research priorities using the Child Health and Nutrition Research Initiative method; and conduct summer schools for capacity building in data science and machine learning/artificial intelligence, in community engagement, and in advocacy for and the use of the Equitable Impact Sensitive Tool (EQUIST) and Pathways to Survival (PATHS) tool. The project will also assess national health system preparedness for emerging infections, identify bottlenecks for early response, assess oxygen capacity and security, study adherence to international guidelines, and conduct qualitative studies to understand barriers to seeking care. It will also explore the feasibility of delivering a pulmonary rehabilitation programme through a randomised controlled trial. Ultimately, the programme will link evidence with policy using the EQUIST and PATHS tools to improve equity in outcomes and identify bottlenecks that lead to morbidity and mortality from respiratory causes. Through high-level meetings, it will prioritise the implementation of equitable interventions that are appropriate to each African context and tailored to patients' needs. A team of social scientists and NGOs, joined by a team of researchers of diverse backgrounds, will engage communities, stakeholders and policymakers to build capacity through summer schools, and disseminate the results through a dedicated project website, the Journal of Global Health, the Journal of the Pan-African Thoracic Society, collaborating NGOs, and mainstream and social media.

papers.title_en: Atypical Type A Thymoma Identified in Slowly Growing Pulmonary Metastases from Type A Thymoma: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Shintani H, Wakama S, Tokuhara K, Kataoka N
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Surgery, Kishiwada Tokushukai Hospital, Osaka, Japan.
papers.authors_conclusion: 即使表面低风险的A型胸腺瘤也可能表现为惰性但转移性的生物学行为，并可在长期病程中出现非典型组织学特征；对A型胸腺瘤患者进行仔细的长期监测和详细病理评估（包括Ki-67标记指数）可能很重要
papers.ai_note: 单例病例报告，无分母、无对照，不能据此推断A型胸腺瘤的转移风险、最佳随访间隔或Ki-67阈值；PET阴性而病理证实转移，提示影像随访策略需结合病史，但该推断的证据级别很低；非典型A型胸腺瘤为较新实体，本例原发灶为常规A型胸腺瘤而转移灶呈非典型特征，其诊断可重复性与临床意义信息不足
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Type A thymoma is generally considered a low-risk thymoma subtype with an excellent prognosis and low rates of distant metastasis. Atypical type A thymoma is a recently established entity characterized by more aggressive biological behavior despite retaining the morphology of conventional type A thymoma. Patients with primary conventional type A thymoma who subsequently develop recurrence with atypical histological features are extremely rare. CASE PRESENTATION: A 79-year-old man was referred to our hospital due to gradual enlargement of bilateral pulmonary nodules. Seven years earlier, he had undergone complete resection of an anterior mediastinal tumor, which had been diagnosed as conventional type A thymoma. Retrospective review of preoperative computed tomography images revealed that small pulmonary nodules had already been present at the time of the initial surgery but had yet to be identified. The nodules enlarged slowly from 3 mm to 10 mm and from 3 mm to 7 mm over the 7-year period. Positron emission tomography showed no abnormal fluorodeoxyglucose uptake. After thoracoscopic wedge resection of the left lower lobe lesion, histopathological examination demonstrated pulmonary metastasis of type A thymoma with focal hypercellularity and increased mitotic activity, consistent with atypical type A thymoma. No necrosis was identified. The Ki-67 labeling indices of the primary and metastatic lesions were 7% and 20%, respectively. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that even apparently low-risk type A thymoma may exhibit indolent but metastatic behavior and may develop atypical histological features during a prolonged clinical course. Careful long-term surveillance and detailed pathological evaluation, including assessment of the Ki-67 labeling index, may be important in patients with type A thymoma.

papers.title_zh: Intrapleural anti-PD-1 injection enhances T-cell immune responses and improves clinical outcomes in elderly patients with advanced lung cancer and malignant pleural effusion.
papers.title_en: Intrapleural anti-PD-1 injection enhances T-cell immune responses and improves clinical outcomes in elderly patients with advanced lung cancer and malignant pleural effusion.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Cong Y, Liang M, Hou X, Ding H
papers.affiliation_highlight: The First Dongguan Affiliated Hospital, Guangdong Medical University Dongguan, Guangdong, China.
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the efficacy of intrapleural anti-PD-1 therapy in elderly patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) complicated by malignant pleural effusion (MPE), and to assess its impact on T-cell subset dynamics. METHODS: A total of 152 elderly patients (≥65 years) with advanced NSCLC and MPE were enrolled. All patients received a single intrapleural injection of anti-PD-1 antibody (Sintilimab, 100 mg) after thoracentesis and drainage. Clinical outcomes, adverse events, and quality-of-life measures were evaluated at baseline, 5 weeks, and 10 weeks after treatment. Concurrently, peripheral blood and pleural effusion T-cell subsets, as well as pleural effusion levels of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and interleukin-6 (IL-6) were also measured. RESULTS: The pleural atresia rates at 5 and 10 weeks were 75.7% and 64.5%, respectively. The objective response rate (ORR) increased from 29.0% at 5 weeks to 38.2% at 10 weeks, and disease control rate (DCR) from 59.9% to 76.4%. Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score improved significantly from baseline (57.3 ± 9.6) to 5 weeks (66.5 ± 9.2) and 10 weeks (74.5 ± 8.3), Borg scores decreased from (6.1 ± 1.3) to (3.8 ± 0.9) and (3.1 ± 0.7), and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores decreased from (4.5 ± 1.1) to (2.8 ± 0.5) and (2.2 ± 0.6) (all P<0.01). At 5 weeks, peripheral blood CD3+, CD4+, and CD8+ T cells increased from baseline (53.3 ± 8.6%, 28.25 ± 5.64%, 20.5 ± 4.6%) to (60.5 ± 9.5%, 32.5 ± 7.2%, and 25.2 ± 6.3%), while the CD4+/CD8+ ratio decreased from (1.38 ± 0.11) to (1.29 ± 0.12) (all P<0.01); in pleural effusion, corresponding values rose to (69.5 ± 4.3%, 34.5 ± 6.4%, and 28.8 ± 7.7%), with the ratio falling to (1.19 ± 0.04) (P<0.01). By 10 weeks, peripheral values further increased to (68.7 ± 8.4%, 36.2 ± 6.9%, and 30.5 ± 5.2%), and the ratio dropped to (1.19 ± 0.06) (P<0.01); pleural effusion values reached 74.5 ± 7.4% (CD3+), 37.1 ± 6.2% (CD4+), and 32.9 ± 7.3% (CD8+), with a ratio of 1.13 ± 0.05 (P<0.001). Pleural effusion levels of LDH, TNF-α, and IL-6 all declined from baseline (856.6 ± 130.2 U/L, 48.4 ± 2.3 pg/mL, 74.81 ± 9.17 pg/mL) to 5 weeks (512.5 ± 95.7 U/L, 32.3 ± 3.8 pg/mL, 52.8 ± 7.1 pg/mL) and 10 weeks (385.6 ± 74.8 U/L, 24.9 ± 2.6 pg/mL, 36.6 ± 5.4 pg/mL) (all P<0.01). Multivariable logistic regression identified that a higher baseline KPS score (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.05-1.32, P<0.01) and a lower baseline pleural effusion LDH level (OR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.58-0.89, P<0.01) were independent protective factors, while a higher baseline peripheral blood CD4+/CD8+ ratio (OR = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.48-0.88, P<0.01) was an independent negative predictor for 10-week DCR. CONCLUSION: Intrapleural administration of anti-PD-1 antibody is relatively safe and demonstrates effective control of MPE in elderly patients with advanced NSCLC. It improves performance status and quality of life, enhances both systemic and local T-cell immune responses, and reduces inflammatory cytokines and LDH levels in pleural effusion.

papers.title_zh: Persistent atherogenic lipoprotein changes during lorlatinib therapy.
papers.title_en: Persistent atherogenic lipoprotein changes during lorlatinib therapy.
papers.authors: Shibue K, Kunimasa K, Hamasaki A
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Diabetes and Endocrinology, Medical Research Institute KITANO HOSPITAL, PIIF Tazuke-Kofukai, Osaka 530-848…
papers.abstract_en: Lorlatinib, a third-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)/ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor, frequently induces hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia, but longitudinal qualitative lipoprotein changes remain incompletely characterized. We describe a 52-year-old woman with ALK-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer who developed persistent dyslipidemia despite lipid-lowering therapy. Before lorlatinib, total cholesterol was 164 mg/dL (SI [International System of Units]: 4.24 mmol/L) (reference range, 148-248 mg/dL [SI: 3.83-6.41 mmol/L]), low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol was 52 mg/dL (SI: 1.34 mmol/L) (reference range, 65-139 mg/dL [SI: 1.68-3.59 mmol/L]), and triglycerides were 54 mg/dL (SI: 0.61 mmol/L) (reference range, 30-117 mg/dL [SI: 0.34-1.32 mmol/L]). Within 3 weeks after lorlatinib initiation, these increased to 340, 245, and 166 mg/dL, respectively. Longitudinal profiling showed persistent apolipoprotein B (ApoB) elevation, increased oxidized LDL, and a prominent pre-β-lipoprotein fraction. Subclinical hypothyroidism was later detected, and pitavastatin was switched to rosuvastatin. This case highlights the potential value of ApoB and qualitative lipid assessment during prolonged lorlatinib therapy.

papers.title_zh: Predicting COVID-19 hospitalisation and common disease risk from comorbid diagnoses in 13 million individuals.
papers.title_en: Predicting COVID-19 hospitalisation and common disease risk from comorbid diagnoses in 13 million individuals.
papers.authors: Liu H, Mizani MA, Zhao Y, Wood A, Inouye M, Price AL, Jiang X
papers.abstract_en: Predicting disease risk from prior diagnoses is fundamental to clinical decision-making, particularly during health emergencies such as the COVID-19 pandemic, when individuals with long-term conditions may be disproportionately vulnerable to adverse outcomes. Despite intense interest in developing models to predict disease risk from prior diagnoses 1-3 , most prediction models do not estimate effects of each prior diagnosis on disease risk conditional on other diagnoses, limiting interpretability and clinical utility. We developed the Comorbidity Risk Score (CRS), trained on 13 million individuals (age 40-69) from linked electronic health record (EHR) datasets of the entire population of England, to predict COVID-19 hospitalisation and 87 other disease outcomes. CRS was trained at close to saturated sample size and precisely estimated the effects of 212 prior diagnoses on the 88 disease outcomes, conditional on all other prior diagnoses. Correlations of CRS effect sizes across outcomes (e.g. 0.76 for myocardial infarction vs. hyperlipidaemia) matched the corresponding genetic correlations (e.g. 0.79 for myocardial infarction vs. hyperlipidaemia), confirming that comorbidity architectures capture disease aetiology. On average, CRS identified 5% of the population with 3.4-fold higher disease risk, including myocardial infarction (4.4-fold), lung cancer (6.5-fold), and COVID-19 hospitalisation (6.3-fold). Using prior diagnoses alone, CRS outperformed state-of-the-art clinical COVID-19 models 4 . Furthermore, CRS ( N =13 million) substantially outperformed state-of-the-art AI 1 ( N =0.5 million) and linear 3 ( N =0.5 million) models in predicting disease risk, suggesting that training sample size outweighs model complexity. CRS attained near-perfect transferability across self-reported ethnicities (e.g., Black vs. White: AUROC ratio = 97.3%). Finally, CRS distinguished independently predictive comorbidities from indirect associations, e.g., lipid metabolism disorder was a strong predictor of myocardial infarction risk but not ischaemic stroke, after conditioning on other prior diagnoses. In conclusion, CRS provides a comprehensive resource for understanding the impact of comorbidities on COVID-19 and other future diseases, revealing disease aetiology while enabling powerful prediction of disease risk.

papers.title_zh: Disparities in lung cancer case registration, treatment, and mortality: descriptive study, Brazil, 2013-2019.
papers.title_en: Disparities in lung cancer case registration, treatment, and mortality: descriptive study, Brazil, 2013-2019.
papers.authors: Faria LV, Emmerick IM, Campos MR
papers.affiliation_highlight: Fundação Oswaldo Cruz, Escola Nacional de Saúde Pública Sérgio Arouca, Rio de Janeiro, RJ, Brazil Fundação Oswaldo Cruz …
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To analyze factors associated with lung cancer case registration, treatment and mortality in Brazil, 2013-2019. METHODS: This was a retrospective study using the Brazilian Mortality Information System (Sistema de Informação de Mortalidade - SIM) and the Hospital Cancer Registries (Registros Hospitalares de Câncer - RHC). Outcomes analyzed were: (Model 1) "absence of lung cancer case registration" in the RHC, and (Model 2) "rate of registered cases above the 3rd quartile." Descriptive and bivariate analyses were performed to compare groups, as well as multivariate logistic regression, identifying, at the municipal level, factors associated with the outcomes. Adjusted odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) were obtained. RESULTS: A total of 206,703 deaths and 89,265 cases (43% coverage) were analyzed. Approximately 85.7% of patients were diagnosed at a late stage, and half of the cases with initial staging did not receive adequate treatment. In Model 1, a lack of RHC coverage was associated with municipalities in the Central-West region compared to those in the North [OR 3.9; 95%CI 2.7; 5.7] and with those having a Gross Domestic Product below the national average [OR 1.3; 95%CI 1.1; 1.7]. In Model 2, municipalities in the South [OR 9.1; 95% CI 6.8; 12.2], small-sized municipalities [OR 7.1; 95%CI 4.0; 12.3], and those with below-average travel distances for treatment [OR 4.2; 95%CI 2.3; 7.7] had increased odds of a high registration rate. CONCLUSION: Localities with better infrastructure were more likely to register cases and have greater coverage of registries, while areas with poorer infrastructure were more likely not to register cases, despite presenting deaths due to lung cancer.

papers.title_zh: Point-of-Care Breath Volatile Organic Compound Analysis as a Tool for Lung Cancer Screening: A Pilot Feasibility Study.
papers.title_en: Point-of-Care Breath Volatile Organic Compound Analysis as a Tool for Lung Cancer Screening: A Pilot Feasibility Study.
papers.authors: Pichkar Y, Manolakos S, Phillips KM, Schabath MB, Chaudhary A
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening reduces lung cancer mortality but is limited by low uptake and associated with high rates of false-positives and indeterminate-nodules. Breath volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis is a non-invasive candidate biomarker approach that could complement LDCT, but prior work has relied on laboratory-based high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), limiting point-of-care deployment. METHODS: In this pilot study, breath samples were collected from 40 patients with treatment-naïve, pathologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and 25 lung-cancer-screening-eligible healthy controls. Paired samples were analyzed via a compact point-of-care GC-MS platform (CLARION) and a laboratory HRMS reference. Diagnostic classification models were built independently for each platform using elastic net logistic regression with leave-one-out cross-validation, and performance was evaluated by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: CLARION identified 103 VOCs across breath specimens, compared to over 900 identified by HRMS. Despite this difference in panel size, CLARION achieved diagnostic performance nearly identical to HRMS for distinguishing NSCLC cases from controls (AUC 0.864 vs. 0.863). Compared to controls, performance statistics were similar for early-stage NSCLC (AUC 0.854 vs. 0.841) and adenocarcinoma (AUC 0.770 vs. 0.787). VOCs of interest include p-cymene, phenol, propylbenzene, tetradecane, β-ocimene, 2,3-dihydro-indole, and 1-methylthio-(Z)-1-propene. CONCLUSION: A compact, point-of-care breath GC-MS platform achieved diagnostic performance for NSCLC detection comparable to a laboratory HRMS reference despite a substantially smaller detected VOC panel. These findings support continued development of point-of-care breath VOC testing as a non-invasive, field-deployable complement to LDCT-based lung cancer screening.

papers.title_zh: Immunizing small cell lung cancer mice with isoaspartylated Elavl4 after chemotherapy mimics improved survival of anti-ELAVL4 antibody-positive small cell lung cancer patients.
papers.title_en: Immunizing small cell lung cancer mice with isoaspartylated Elavl4 after chemotherapy mimics improved survival of anti-ELAVL4 antibody-positive small cell lung cancer patients.
papers.authors: Velarde DA, Valdes JA, Lee H, Yan C, Elmalh S, Moreno AD, Mullen DJ, Gladstone MA et al.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) patients have an ∼8% 5-year survival; new therapies are urgently needed. Approximately 15% of SCLC patients have naturally-occurring low-titer antibodies against neuronal ELAVL proteins, associated with improved response to therapy and significantly improved survival. We previously determined that the anti-ELAVL4 response is triggered by isoaspartylation in the unstructured ELAVL4 N-terminal region. METHODS: We used a Tp53 fl/fl ; Rb1 fl/fl inducible SCLC mouse model to test whether 1) immunization with isoaspartylated Elavl4 (isoAsp-Elavl4) prior to SCLC induction improves survival in the absence of any other treatment, and 2) immunization with isoAsp-Elavl4 following completion of 3 rounds of cisplatin+etoposide therapy improves survival. Immunizations contained incomplete Freund's adjuvant with either a recombinant N-terminal fragment of Elavl4 (amino acids 1-117), incubated under isoaspartyl-inducing conditions, or phosphate-buffered saline (used as the negative control, since Elavl4 spontaneously isoaspartylates). Mice were monitored by blinded assessors until euthanasia was indicated. RESULTS: IsoAsp-Elavl4-immunized animals all became immune responsive, and spontaneous anti-isoAsp-Elavl4 antibodies were observed in 7% of the control animals. Kaplan-Meier analyses revealed that pre-SCLC immunization with isoAsp-ELAVL4 in the absence of other treatments did not affect survival. In contrast, immunization of SCLC mice following chemotherapy significantly improved survival. CONCLUSIONS: An anti-isoAsp-ELAVL4 response can be actively induced in mice and significantly increases SCLC survival when given following chemotherapy. This indicates that the anti-isoAsp-ELAVL4 immune response can be leveraged to develop new therapies for SCLC patients.

papers.title_zh: A longitudinal study of lung cancer stigma across 6 months in a trial of supportive care interventions.
papers.title_en: A longitudinal study of lung cancer stigma across 6 months in a trial of supportive care interventions.
papers.authors: Rose S, Boyes A, Kelly B, Cox M, Palazzi K, Paul C
papers.affiliation_highlight: The University of Sydney, and Cancer Council NSW, Sydney, NSW, Australia.
papers.abstract_en: People with lung cancer commonly experience stigma, however, the temporal impacts are poorly understood. This study investigated changes (using linear mixed modelling) and trajectories (using latent growth modelling) of stigma over a 6-month period in people newly diagnosed with lung cancer, who were participants of a larger trial of supportive care interventions (ACTRN12615000932561). Participants (n = 192) completed surveys which included the Cataldo Lung Cancer Stigma Scale. Lung cancer stigma did not vary significantly over time, with mean scores of 53.2 ± 15.6 and 54.0 ± 16.7 reported at recruitment and 6 months respectively (range 31-124, higher scores indicate greater stigma). Two main trajectory patterns were identified: (1) 'Relatively lower stigma trajectory'; and (2) 'Relatively higher stigma trajectory'. Relatively higher stigma trajectories were associated with younger age and a history of smoking. Further research is warranted to identify strategies to reduce lung cancer stigma and explore differences across sub-groups and stages of the lung cancer continuum.

papers.title_zh: Two-Stage Deep Learning Framework for Histopathological Subtyping of Non-Small Cell Lung Carcinoma in Small Biopsies.
papers.title_en: Two-Stage Deep Learning Framework for Histopathological Subtyping of Non-Small Cell Lung Carcinoma in Small Biopsies.
papers.authors: Ozbek B, Dogan HN, Vural C, Yetim K, Celik A, Urhan O, Yaprak Bayrak B
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pathology, Kocaeli University School of Medicine, Kocaeli, Turkey.
papers.abstract_en: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based technologies have the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy while reducing tissue loss in small biopsies. In non-small-cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC), small biopsies often limit ancillary testing. We aimed to develop a deep learning-based framework for automated histopathological classification of NSCLC subtypes. Archived hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images from 341 NSCLC and benign specimens were digitized and annotated by two expert pathologists. A two-stage Dense Net121-based cascade was employed: Stage 1 differentiated not otherwise specified (NOS) from not-NOS specimens; Stage 2 classified not-NOS into adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, or non-cancerous tissue. Patient-level predictions were derived via majority voting. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. In Stage 1, NOS versus not-NOS classification achieved 0.92 patient-level accuracy. In Stage 2, accuracy for adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and non-cancer was 0.94, with perfect classification of non-cancer patients (precision, recall, and F1 = 1.00). In the final step, the combined analysis demonstrated an overall accuracy of 0.88, with recall rates of 1.00 for adenocarcinoma and non-cancer, 0.83 for squamous cell carcinoma, and 0.67 for NOS. The proposed two-stage model demonstrated strong performance across NSCLC subtypes, including the diagnostically challenging NOS group. This approach may reduce reliance on ancillary tests, accelerate diagnosis, and optimize tissue preservation.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is a dynamically evolving disease characterized by marked temporal heterogeneity across tumor progression, treatment response, resistance development, and clinical outcomes. Nevertheless, the majority of existing artificial intelligence (AI) systems continue to rely predominantly on single time-point imaging, imposing inherent constraints on their capacity to characterize disease evolution and capture continuously shifting risk states. The growing availability of longitudinal imaging data, combined with ongoing advances in temporal deep learning, is driving a transition in lung cancer AI from static image interpretation toward dynamic risk prediction. In this narrative review, relevant literature was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus from database inception to September 2026, using terms related to lung cancer, longitudinal imaging, temporal deep learning, and dynamic risk prediction, with representative studies selected according to their methodological relevance, clinical applications, and implications for clinical translation. Longitudinal imaging tracks disease trajectories over time and offers distinct opportunities to characterize tumor growth dynamics, treatment-induced changes, and evolving recurrence risk. Temporal deep learning, in turn, enables the modelling of complex time-dependent relationships that conventional static approaches are poorly suited to represent. The field has progressed from early dual time-point analyses to long-range temporal modelling, multimodal temporal fusion, and continuous risk updating, with encouraging applications spanning pulmonary nodule management, treatment response assessment, recurrence surveillance, survival prediction, and individualized disease management. Nonetheless, substantial obstacles persist, including the scarcity of large-scale longitudinal datasets, irregular temporal sampling, limited model generalizability, insufficient causal interpretability, and a lack of robust evidence supporting real-world clinical deployment. Addressing these challenges will require coordinated efforts toward standardized longitudinal data infrastructure, continuous-time modelling frameworks, multimodal integration strategies, and closer alignment of AI systems with clinical workflows. Taken together, longitudinal imaging and temporal deep learning are steering lung cancer AI away from static image analysis and toward dynamic disease management, with the potential to support continuous risk assessment and potentially inform adaptive clinical decision-making throughout the full spectrum of lung cancer care.

papers.title_zh: Epigenetic age acceleration enhances prediction of overall survival in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.title_en: Epigenetic age acceleration enhances prediction of overall survival in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Gandara I, Du M, Li Y, Su L, Kothari J, Lanuti M, Gainor JF, Christiani DC et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Biological Engineering, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge MA, USA.
papers.abstract_en: Epigenetic age, influenced by environmental factors like smoking, predicts mortality in general populations but remains under-explored in early-stage lung cancer. We analyzed blood DNA methylation from 75 Boston Lung Cancer Study participants with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), of whom 63 died during follow-up. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was estimated using Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, and GrimAge2 clocks and assessed using Cox models and random survival forests (RSFs). Across clocks, EAA significantly predicted survival in early-stage NSCLC. GrimAge2 EAA achieved the highest predictive accuracy (C index = 0.73±0.04) and emerged as the dominant predictor of survival among RSF models (variable importance = 5.7%), surpassing smoking and age. GrimAge2 EAA showed a non-linear association with mortality in which current smokers had >10% higher predicted mortality risk than former or never smokers at equivalent EAA, a pattern confirmed in Kaplan-Meier analyses. GrimAge2 EAA is a promising biomarker for personalizing risk stratification alongside traditional clinical factors.

papers.title_zh: Garsorasib (D-1553) in Combination With Pembrolizumab and Chemotherapy for First-Line Metastatic NSCLC With KRAS G12C Mutation: Results of a Phase 1b Study.
papers.title_en: Garsorasib (D-1553) in Combination With Pembrolizumab and Chemotherapy for First-Line Metastatic NSCLC With KRAS G12C Mutation: Results of a Phase 1b Study.
papers.authors: Yan D, Liu C, Li X, Moore M, Xu R, Sanborn RE, Gadgeel SM, Millward M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Oncology, Beijing Luhe Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, People's Republic of China.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Garsorasib (D-1553) is an orally administered selective KRAS G12C inhibitor. We report results from group 1 of the phase 1b D1553-101 study assessing garsorasib plus pembrolizumab and platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC. METHODS: Eligible participants had locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with KRAS G12C mutation and were candidates for pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy. Participants received garsorasib 600 mg once daily or twice daily combined with pembrolizumab 200 mg once every 3 weeks plus 4 to 6 cycles of cisplatin or carboplatin and pemetrexed (nonsquamous histology) or carboplatin and paclitaxel (squamous histology). The primary end points were safety and the incidence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs). RESULTS: As of February 24, 2024, 17 participants received garsorasib 600 mg once daily (n = 10) or twice daily (n = 7) combined with pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy. Overall, 94% of participants experienced grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (AEs), and 88% had a dose reduction or interruption due to treatment-related AEs. One participant in the twice-daily group experienced a DLT of grade 2 diarrhea; no other DLTs occurred. Among all participants, the objective response rate was 59%, and the median progression-free survival was 7.4 months. CONCLUSION: In participants with KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, despite an encouraging signal of efficacy, the incidence of treatment-related AEs with garsorasib plus pembrolizumab and platinum-based chemotherapy was high, and participants frequently had dose modifications or interruptions due to treatment-related AEs. Based on these findings, the study did not proceed to phase 2. CLINICALTRIALSGOV IDENTIFIER: NCT04585035.

papers.title_zh: Case Report: Coexpression of somatic EGFR, BRCA1, and BRCA2 mutations in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.title_en: Case Report: Coexpression of somatic EGFR, BRCA1, and BRCA2 mutations in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Negin A, Sachdeva K, Weiss J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Southern Oncology Hematology Associates, Inspira Health System, Vineland, NJ, United States.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved dramatically over the past decade with the advent of widespread genetic testing, immunotherapy, and targeted therapies. Treatments directed against epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and other driver mutations have reduced toxicity and improved efficacy for selected patients. CASE PRESENTATION: We present a 59-year-old man with metastatic NSCLC harboring coexisting EGFR, BRCA1, and RNA-binding motif protein 10 (RBM10) mutations and high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. A BRCA2 mutation was later detected on peripheral blood testing. The patient presented with a debilitating stroke that included dysphagia and hemiparesis. During his course of care, he received osimertinib, after which EGFR and RBM10 variant allele frequencies (VAFs) increased on peripheral blood testing. He also received immunotherapy and olaparib. Despite high response rates reported in the literature, he did not respond to these agents. He had a response to chemotherapy but tolerated it poorly. Ultimately, given the lack of durable response and his inability to tolerate chemotherapy, the patient opted for palliative care. DISCUSSION: Patients with actionable targets such as EGFR, BRCA1/2, or elevated PD-L1 generally have superior outcomes with targeted and combination therapy compared with patients who lack targetable options. However, coexisting mutations can interact and provide escape mechanisms. The lack of response in our patient is consistent with studies showing reduced efficacy of EGFR-directed therapy in the presence of RBM10 loss-of-function (LOF) alterations. Further research in patients with multiple concurrent mutations is needed to improve treatment options for this group.

papers.title_zh: N-WASP deficiency enhances oncogenic KRAS-mediated lung adenocarcinoma progression in mice.
papers.title_en: N-WASP deficiency enhances oncogenic KRAS-mediated lung adenocarcinoma progression in mice.
papers.authors: Verma A, Li N, Kalailingam P, Kim C, Sharma A, Lee YH, Thanabalu T
papers.affiliation_highlight: School of Biological Sciences, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, Singapore.
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Oncogenic KRAS mutations drive 25-30% of western lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) cases, however the mechanisms that restrain tumor progression remain poorly defined. N-Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein (N-WASP) regulates actin cytoskeleton dynamics and epithelial architecture, but its role in KRAS-driven lung tumorigenesis is unclear. METHODS: We generated a conditional N-WASP knockout in KRASG12D-driven lung adenocarcinoma mice (N-WASPLKO/KRASG12D) using Sftpc-CreERT2, and assessed N-WASP knockdown A549 cells (A549KD) in 3D culture for tumor burden, ERK signaling, transcriptomic changes, and E-cadherin expression. RESULTS: Conditional deletion of N-WASP in type II alveolar cells (N-WASPLKO) markedly increased tumor number and size in KRASG12D mice. The tumors isolated from these mice retained strong pro-surfactant protein C expression, confirming alveolar epithelial origin and predominantly adopted a solid growth pattern, indicative of disrupted epithelial organization. Mechanistically, N-WASP loss enhanced KRAS-driven ERK1/2 activation in lung tissue, consistent with increased mitogenic signaling. In A549 cells, N-WASP deficiency disrupted cytoskeletal architecture, promoted proliferation, and impaired cell-cell adhesion, recapitulating in vivo tumor phenotypes. A kinase inhibitor screen identified Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) activity as a driver of this hyperproliferative phenotype, with ROCK inhibition normalizing proliferation in N-WASP-deficient cells, linking elevated Rho/ROCK signaling to the increased ERK1/2 activation observed upon N-WASP loss. Transcriptomic profiling of N-WASP-deficient lungs revealed coordinated upregulation of genes regulating proliferation, cytoskeletal remodeling, and tumor-promoting pathways, alongside downregulation of epithelial differentiation and adhesion programs. CONCLUSION: These results establish N-WASP as a critical suppressor of KRAS-driven lung adenocarcinoma, linking cytoskeletal integrity to oncogenic signaling and transcriptional regulation. Our findings highlight the interplay between actin dynamics, epithelial architecture, and KRAS signaling, suggesting that targeting N-WASP dependent pathways could modulate lung cancer aggressiveness and offer novel therapeutic opportunities.

papers.title_zh: A large animal lung cancer model for the evaluation of intratumoural cisplatin delivery strategies.
papers.title_en: A large animal lung cancer model for the evaluation of intratumoural cisplatin delivery strategies.
papers.authors: Meehan J, Collie D, Chang Z, Gregson R, Clutton RE, Greenhalgh SN, Grant L, Kennedy S et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: The Royal (Dick) School of Veterinary Studies and Roslin Institute, University of Edinburgh, Edinburgh, United Kingdom.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Cisplatin has been a standard chemotherapeutic agent for advanced non-small cell lung cancer for decades. Conventionally administered intravenously, it undergoes systemic distribution, exposing both tumour and healthy tissues to the drug. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle injection of cisplatin is emerging as a potential intratumoural drug delivery (ITDD) strategy. However, rigorous preclinical research is needed before ITDD can be more widely adopted. METHODS: We used our experimentally induced ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (OPA) model, generated by Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus (JSRV) infection, to evaluate transthoracic and transbronchial ITDD techniques. We compared systemic platinum exposure following intravenous cisplatin delivery with that following intratumoural cisplatin administration. Both non-recovery and recovery studies were conducted in a total of eight sheep. RESULTS: ITDD techniques were successfully developed and performed in three tumour bearing sheep during non-recovery procedures. To provide a reference for systemic platinum exposure, intravenous cisplatin was administered to three JSRV-infected sheep that did not develop OPA. Intravenous administration produced a rapid plasma platinum peak followed by a rapid decline. ITDD resulted in preferential platinum deposition within targeted lung tumours while producing substantially lower systemic platinum exposure compared with intravenous administration. Intratumoural cisplatin delivery was also evaluated in a recovery procedure using a single sheep, comparing single-site and fractionated administration over a 28-day period, with tumour biopsies confirming lesion presence before treatment. Following ITDD, tumour volumes were observed to decrease over the study period. The recovery experiments demonstrated the feasibility of repeated tumour biopsies, intratumoural injections, longitudinal CT monitoring and recovery anaesthesia using the OPA model. DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first report of direct intratumoural cisplatin administration into ovine lung tumours. This study also provides proof-of-concept that this clinically relevant large animal lung cancer model can serve as a translational platform for evaluating intratumoural therapeutic delivery strategies relevant to human lung cancer.

papers.title_en: Wrap53-1α and Wrap53-1β exert distinct p53-dependent effects on radiosensitivity in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Zhu Y, Hu Y, Wen Q, Zhao X, Guan B
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Oncology, The First People's Hospital of Jingzhou, The First Affiliated Hospital of Yangtze University Jin…
papers.authors_conclusion: Our findings reveal a previously unappreciated inverse correlation between Wrap53-1α and p53 in LUAD cells and establish a molecular network where Wrap53 isoforms and p53 status collectively determine LUAD radiosensitivity.
papers.ai_note: 摘要未给出任何效应量、置信区间或P值，主要结论基于两种细胞系的沉默实验和相关性生物信息学分析；无体内模型或临床放疗样本验证；仅凭TCGA药物敏感性推断化疗反应需谨慎；将Wrap53-1α与p53描述为“反向相关”及“决定放射敏感性”存在过度外推风险。
papers.abstract_en: This study elucidates the distinct roles of Wrap53 isoforms (1α/1β) in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) radiosensitivity through integrated bioinformatics and functional analyses. Bioinformatics revealed Wrap53-associated enrichment in DNA repair and p53 pathways, with TCGA data linking its expression to prognosis and chemotherapy response. Functional studies demonstrated isoform- and p53 context-dependent effects: In p53-wild type A549 cells, Wrap53-1α silencing upregulated p53, enhanced radiosensitivity through Bax/Bcl-2-mediated apoptosis, and impaired DNA repair through RAD51 recombinase (RAD51)/Breast cancer susceptibility gene 1 (BRCA1) regulation. Conversely, in p53-mutant H1975 cells, silencing either Wrap53-1α or Wrap53-1β individually increased colony formation. Wrap53-1α was found to modulate post-radiation G2/M arrest through cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1) regulation, with effects contingent on p53 status. Importantly, Wrap53 expression correlated with differential chemosensitivity. High Wrap53 tumors showed increased cisplatin sensitivity but resistance to docetaxel, while low-expressing tumors were resistant to paclitaxel and vinca alkaloids. Our findings reveal a previously unappreciated inverse correlation between Wrap53-1α and p53 in LUAD cells and establish a molecular network where Wrap53 isoforms and p53 status collectively determine LUAD radiosensitivity.

papers.title_zh: 前纵隔感染性表皮样囊肿误诊为成熟囊性畸胎瘤并粘连心包：一例VATS完整切除病例报告
papers.title_en: Infected Anterior Mediastinal Epidermoid Cyst Mimicking Mature Cystic Teratoma and Adherent to the Pericardium: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Abbas Y, Aldakak MA, Al-Jawalah R, Abo Dakka YA, Mahmoud R, Dandashy A, Chaban H
papers.affiliation_highlight: National University Hospital, Faculty of Medicine, Damascus University, Damascus, Syrian Arab Republic.
papers.authors_conclusion: 完整手术切除可提供明确诊断和有效治疗；囊性前纵隔肿物的鉴别诊断应包括表皮样囊肿；在仔细选择的患者中，即使存在致密心包粘连，VATS切除可能可行。
papers.ai_note: 单例病例报告，无对照，不能评估VATS在致密心包粘连条件下的可行性或安全性；术前活检与最终病理不一致，提示取样和诊断局限；肉眼毛发样物及软骨样区未获组织学证实，与畸胎瘤鉴别仍有不确定性；“carefully selected patients”的选择标准未说明；随访、复发和并发症信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Mediastinal epidermoid cysts are exceptionally rare benign lesions, particularly in the anterior mediastinum. Their nonspecific clinical and radiological features may resemble other anterior mediastinal masses, including thymic lesions and mature cystic teratomas, making preoperative diagnosis challenging. CASE PRESENTATION: A 35-year-old man with no relevant medical or surgical history presented with a 2-month history of retrosternal chest pain. Clinical examination and cardiac evaluation were unremarkable. Chest radiography demonstrated mediastinal widening, while contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed a well-defined anterior mediastinal mass measuring approximately 7 × 5 × 3 cm. CT-guided biopsy and fluid aspiration initially suggested a mature cystic teratoma without immature or malignant elements. The patient underwent complete excision using a three-port video-assisted thoracoscopic approach. Intraoperatively, the cyst was densely adherent to the pericardium and contained thick purulent material. Hair-like material and firm cartilage-like areas were observed grossly but were not confirmed histologically. Culture of the cyst contents yielded Staphylococcus aureus. Histopathological examination demonstrated a squamous epithelial lining with chronic inflammation, granulation tissue, and fibrosis, confirming an infected mediastinal epidermoid cyst. The discrepancy between the initial cytological impression and the final histopathological diagnosis highlights the limitations of imaging and needle biopsy in evaluating rare cystic mediastinal lesions. CONCLUSION: Complete surgical excision provides both definitive diagnosis and effective treatment. Epidermoid cysts should be considered in the differential diagnosis of cystic anterior mediastinal masses. Video-assisted thoracoscopic excision may be feasible in carefully selected patients, even in the presence of dense pericardial adhesions.

papers.study_type: 单例个案报道 · 新辅助靶向治疗后手术可行性观察
papers.title_zh: ALK阳性肺鳞癌新辅助劳拉替尼治疗后病理完全缓解并接受微创肺叶切除的个案报道
papers.title_en: Minimally invasive lobectomy following pathologic complete response to neoadjuvant Lorlatinib in ALK-positive squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Molkova A, Li R, Li S
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University, Guangzhou, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: 本病例提示，尽管存在治疗相关肺门纤维化及血管-支气管粘连，新辅助劳拉替尼后行微创解剖性肺切除仍可行且安全。
papers.ai_note: 单例、无对照、无统计推断，“可行且安全”仅基于1例经验，不可外推；未量化手术时间、出血量、并发症分级等安全性指标；未报告pCR的独立病理复核、影像评效标准与随访时长；ALK阳性肺鳞癌罕见，需排除腺鳞癌或腺癌伴鳞状分化方能确立组织学前提；61%缩瘤与pCR属描述性结果，存在选择性报告阳性结局的倾向。
papers.abstract_en: ALK rearrangements are uncommon in lung squamous cell carcinoma, and neoadjuvant ALK inhibition remains investigational. We report a 52-year-old never-smoking female with stage IIIB ALK-positive squamous cell carcinoma treated with neoadjuvant lorlatinib for 12 weeks. Serial imaging demonstrated a 61% reduction in tumor size with nodal regression. The patient subsequently underwent a uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic (uVATS) lobectomy, and final pathology revealed a complete pathological response (pCR) of the primary tumor. This case highlights the feasibility and safety of minimally invasive anatomical lung resection following neoadjuvant lorlatinib despite treatment-related hilar fibrosis and vascular-bronchial adhesions.

papers.title_zh: 胸腺囊肿旁偶发0.6 mm显微镜下胸腺瘤与2.0 mm A型微胸腺瘤的罕见病例报告
papers.title_en: Synchronous Nodular Epithelial Hyperplasia and Type A Microthymoma Adjacent to a Thymic Cyst: A Report of a Rare Case.
papers.authors: Bunno Y, Yamamoto M, Miyazaki R, Okada H, Tamura M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Kochi Medical School, Kochi University, Nankoku, JPN.
papers.authors_conclusion: 据作者所知，显微镜下胸腺瘤与A型微胸腺瘤并存于胸腺囊肿旁极为罕见；病变位置邻近且组织学特征相似，提示它们可能代表显微胸腺上皮增生连续形态谱中的不同阶段而非完全独立实体；本病例还提示对切除胸腺囊肿邻近胸腺组织进行仔细病理检查以发现隐匿显微上皮病变并改进病理评估的潜在价值。
papers.ai_note: 单例病例报告，无对照与系统取样，不能验证“连续形态谱”假说；摘要称两处病变依据大小和组织学特征而未行额外免疫组化即诊断，诊断阈值与可重复性信息不足；标题提及同步结节性上皮增生，摘要主要描述显微镜下胸腺瘤与A型微胸腺瘤，术语与病变归类存在不一致；18个月随访不足以评估复发风险。
papers.abstract_en: Thymic cysts are uncommon benign lesions of the anterior mediastinum and are frequently detected incidentally on imaging studies. Microscopic thymoma and microthymoma are extremely rare microscopic thymic epithelial proliferations that are usually identified only by histopathological examination. Their relationship to thymic cysts and to each other remains poorly understood. A 54-year-old woman was referred to our institution after an anterior mediastinal lesion was incidentally detected on routine chest computed tomography (CT). Magnetic resonance imaging and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT findings were consistent with a thymic cyst. Robot-assisted thoracoscopic resection of the cyst with the adjacent thymic tissue was performed for definitive diagnosis and treatment. Histopathological examination revealed a unilocular thymic cyst accompanied by two incidental microscopic thymic epithelial lesions within the adjacent thymic tissue: a 0.6-mm microscopic thymoma and a 2.0-mm Type A microthymoma. Based on their characteristic size and histological features, both lesions were diagnosed without additional immunohistochemical analysis. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remains free of recurrence 18 months after surgery. To our knowledge, the coexistence of microscopic thymoma and Type A microthymoma adjacent to a thymic cyst is exceptionally rare. The close proximity and similar histological features of these lesions suggest that they may represent different stages within a continuous morphological spectrum of microscopic thymic epithelial proliferations rather than entirely distinct entities. Furthermore, this case highlights the potential value of careful pathological examination of thymic tissue adjacent to resected thymic cysts for detecting occult microscopic epithelial lesions and improving pathological assessment.

papers.title_zh: 多柔比星联合异环磷酰胺治疗伴气道梗阻的胸部SMARCA4缺陷未分化肿瘤：1例报告显示快速但短暂的瘤体缩小与症状缓解
papers.title_en: Tumor Shrinkage and Symptom Relief with Doxorubicin and Ifosfamide in Thoracic SMARCA4-Deficient Undifferentiated Tumor with Airway Obstruction: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Ueta R, Rikimaru Y, Eba S, Itakura Y, Okita A
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Oncology, Japanese Red Cross Ishinomaki Hospital, Ishinomaki, Japan.
papers.authors_conclusion: 本病例提示多柔比星联合异环磷酰胺或可在伴气道梗阻的胸部SMARCA4-UT中带来快速但短暂的肿瘤缩小与症状改善；当需要紧急减瘤以解除即将发生的气道受压时可考虑该方案。但早期诊断同样可能重要，因为含ICI的一线方案与胸部SMARCA4-UT临床结局改善相关。
papers.ai_note: 单例报告无对照，疗效与症状缓解无法归因于AI方案本身（同期可能使用激素/支持治疗、气道干预未描述）；'部分缓解'与'症状缓解'的具体评价标准与影像学数据未在摘要给出；作者由1例部分缓解外推至'可考虑用于紧急减瘤'，并同时主张早期诊断以使用ICI方案，结论方向存在双向泛化倾向；AI方案的选择本身源于误诊为高级别肉瘤，属偶然性用药，不能作为方案优选证据。
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor (SMARCA4-UT) is a recently recognized, rare, and highly aggressive malignancy. No standard treatment has been established for unresectable disease, and the prognosis is generally poor. These tumors often grow rapidly, and bulky masses can cause clinically significant symptoms. CASE PRESENTATION: A 52-year-old man with a history of heavy smoking presented with chest and back pain. Imaging revealed a large mediastinal mass. A CT-guided biopsy demonstrated an undifferentiated neoplasm with complete loss of BRG1 (SMARCA4) expression, a high proliferative index (Ki-67 labeling index, 80%), and no evidence of specific lineage differentiation, findings consistent with SMARCA4-UT. Subsequent comprehensive genomic profiling revealed a SMARCA4 nonsense mutation and a high tumor mutational burden. The tumor was clinically unresectable and showed rapid progression, resulting in severe dyspnea and syncope due to marked extrinsic airway compression. Because a high-grade sarcoma was initially suspected before the final diagnosis of SMARCA4-UT was established, first-line doxorubicin plus ifosfamide (AI) therapy was administered, resulting in rapid symptomatic relief and a partial response. However, after three cycles of AI therapy, the disease progressed clinically with a left adrenal metastasis. Subsequent treatment with the immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) atezolizumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel showed no objective response, and the patient died 6 months after the initiation of systemic therapy. CONCLUSION: This case suggests that doxorubicin plus ifosfamide may provide rapid but transient tumor shrinkage and symptomatic improvement in thoracic SMARCA4-UT with airway obstruction. This regimen may be considered when urgent tumor reduction is required to relieve impending airway compromise. However, early diagnosis may also be important because first-line ICI-containing regimens have been associated with improved clinical outcomes in thoracic SMARCA4-UT.

papers.study_type: 临床前体外研究 · 纳米硼递送载体制备与细胞学评价
papers.title_zh: 白蛋白/BSH偶联纳米粒用于食管鳞癌BNCT的体外制备与细胞摄取评价
papers.title_en: Albumin/BSH-fused nanoparticle for boron neutron capture therapy of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Qin HM, Cai RW, He YJ, Zhang J, Su XL, Kan YL, Li BS, Li X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: School of Pharmaceutical Sciences & Institute of Materia Medica, Department of Central Laboratory of Binzhou People's Ho…
papers.authors_conclusion: BSH@Alb作为一种安全有效的硼剂，具有均匀粒径、高包封率、高载药量和良好稳定性；显著增强细胞内硼蓄积且细胞相容性可接受，支持其作为BNCT有前景的硼递送候选物。
papers.ai_note: 仅为体外制剂学与细胞摄取/相容性研究，未报告体内抑瘤、安全性、肿瘤靶向或实际中子照射下BNCT疗效；摘要以“安全有效”“有前景”表述超出所展示数据；缺乏样本量、统计比较数值及主要终点预设信息。
papers.abstract_en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly aggressive malignant tumor which suffers from poor prognosis and limited therapeutic remedies. As a physiologically-oriented radiotherapy and highly tumor-specific modality, boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) shows great potential for the treatment of ESCC. Since efficacy of BNCT is critically restricted to boron drugs, novel boron agents with satisfactory boron load and intracellular uptake are highly demanded. Herein, we developed a novel albumin/BSH-conjugated nanoparticle (BSH@Alb) as a safe and effective boron agent. It resulted BSH@Alb displayed uniform particle size, high encapsulation efficiency (93.1 ± 0.39%), loading capacity (15.52 ± 0.41%) and good stability in different solution (water, PBS and plasma). Collectively, BSH@Alb significantly enhanced intracellular boron accumulation and showed acceptable cytocompatibility in comparison with prototype BSH, supporting its potential value for BNCT therapy as a promising boron-delivery candidate.

papers.study_type: 生物信息学整合分析 · 公共数据集探索性研究（TCGA/GEO，非实验验证）

papers.title_zh: BRCA2变异转移性乳腺癌与肺腺癌共享转录组特征的生物信息学分析：候选枢纽基因SERPINA1、PIGR、FGG和FCGBP
papers.title_en: Identification and characterization of shared transcriptomic signatures in BRCA2-mutated metastatic breast cancer and lung adenocarcinoma: An integrative bioinformatics approach.
papers.authors: Abid E, Bilal S, Shahid M, Farooq SMY
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Lab Technology, Green International University, Lahore, Pakistan.
papers.authors_conclusion: BRCA2变异乳腺与肺肿瘤数据集存在部分重叠的上皮转录谱；这些观察为BRCA2改变队列中的关联，不能证明BRCA2功能障碍直接驱动所识别的转录改变；SERPINA1、PIGR、FGG和FCGBP为候选的组织依赖性生物标志物，需独立验证。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未报告样本量、BRCA2变异定义、效应量或P值，所谓“显著标志物”无法量化核验；公共数据集整合分析易受组织来源、上皮成分比例及批次效应影响，且缺乏独立验证；乳腺癌与LUAD队列的转移状态及临床变量匹配信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: Breast cancer and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) are most prevalent forms of malignancies worldwide and are associated with BRCA2 variants. While BRCA2 pathogenic variants are well established in breast cancer, their transcriptional consequences in lung adenocarcinoma remain poorly characterized, and no study has directly compared the shared differentially expressed gene (DEG) signature between BRCA2-variant metastatic breast cancer and BRCA2-variant LUAD. In this study, we used an integrative bioinformatics approach to identify and characterize this shared transcriptomic profile using publicly available TCGA and GEO datasets accessed via cBioPortal. Top dysregulated genes were subjected to protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis using STRING and Cytoscape (CytoHubba, MCC algorithm), functional enrichment through Metascape and survival analysis through UALCAN, with disease associations validated against the DISEASES database. SERPINA1, PIGR, FGG and FCGBP were identified as candidate hub genes, common in both types of malignancies. The breast cancer gene set was associated with impaired BRCA2-RAD51-mediated homologous recombination, and the lung dataset had strong signatures of alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells and signatures specific to lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). SERPINA1 and PIGR were significant markers in breast cancer and FGG was significant marker in LUAD. The findings identify a partially overlapping epithelial transcriptional profile associated with BRCA2-variant breast and lung tumor datasets. However, these observations represent associations within BRCA2-altered cohorts and do not establish that BRCA2 dysfunction directly drives the identified transcriptional changes. SERPINA1, PIGR, FGG, and FCGBP therefore represent candidate tissue-dependent biomarkers requiring independent validation.

papers.title_zh: EGFR突变转移性NSCLC一线奥希替尼治疗后脉络膜转移灶快速消退1例
papers.title_en: Rapid Regression of Choroidal Metastasis under First-Line Osimertinib Therapy in Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor-Mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Hufnagel HJ, Zeitz O, Abdula F, Joussen AM, Zur Bonsen LS
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Ophthalmology, Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin, Corporate Member of Freie Universität Berlin and Humb…
papers.authors_conclusion: 一线奥希替尼可能诱导EGFR突变NSCLC患者脉络膜转移灶快速消退；在部分选择病例中，系统靶向治疗的早期反应可能使局部眼部治疗得以避免。
papers.ai_note: 单例病例报告，无对照，不能建立因果；‘快速消退’仅为描述性时序观察，摘要未提供病灶定量测量、EGFR具体突变亚型及系统疗效评价；存在选择性发表显著应答病例的可能。
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Choroidal metastases may cause substantial visual impairment in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although local ocular treatments are frequently considered, targeted systemic therapy may provide effective control in tumors harboring actionable mutations. We report the rapid regression of a choroidal metastasis following first-line osimertinib therapy in a patient with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated NSCLC. CASE PRESENTATION: A 59-year-old man with metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC presented with progressive visual decline in the left eye. Ophthalmic examination revealed a peripapillary choroidal lesion associated with serous retinal detachment. Optical coherence tomography demonstrated subretinal fluid, consistent with a choroidal metastasis. First-line osimertinib therapy had been initiated 12 days before presentation at our clinic. An early reduction in subretinal fluid was observed during follow-up, followed by complete resolution at the 2-month follow-up. This was accompanied by regression of the choroidal lesion and improvement in visual function. No local ocular treatment was required. CONCLUSION: First-line osimertinib may induce rapid regression of choroidal metastases in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC. In selected cases, an early response to systemic targeted therapy may allow local ocular treatment to be avoided.

papers.title_zh: 82岁重度主动脉瓣狭窄患者先行TAVI、7个月后行肺癌切除术的单例个案报告：术后经过与3个月随访
papers.title_en: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Followed by Lung Cancer Resection in an Older Patient: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Khan L, Qadri SS
papers.affiliation_highlight: General Practice, West Rainton Surgery, County Durham and Darlington NHS Foundation Trust, Durham, GBR.
papers.authors_conclusion: 在评估手术风险、合并症与预后等因素后，先行TAVI处理瓣膜病变、再行肺癌切除是可接受的替代方案；本病例说明该干预顺序在高龄、手术风险增高人群中是合适的。
papers.ai_note: 证据层级为单例个案，n=1，无对照，无法支持“可接受替代方案”的普适性结论；TAVI与肺切除间隔7个月为经验性安排，摘要未给出决策依据或风险量化评分（如STS-PROM/EuroSCORE）；未报告肺癌病理类型、分期路径（是否有病理确认）、切缘、淋巴结采样范围及复发/生存数据；术后房颤与肺不张的发生与处理细节不足；随访仅3个月，无法评估肿瘤学安全性。信息不足处如实标注。
papers.abstract_en: The individual incidences of lung cancer and cardiovascular disease in the elderly population mean that there is a strong likelihood of both occurring simultaneously. Common practice for severe aortic stenosis (AS) would be surgical aortic valve replacement (AVR), unless deemed high-risk for this surgical procedure. Age and lung cancer both increase a patient's surgical risk; hence, the less invasive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) to manage valve disease ahead of lung resection for lung cancer is an acceptable alternative after assessing other factors such as procedural risk, comorbidities, and prognosis. We present the case of an 82-year-old female patient who underwent a TAVI seven months before lung resection for an incidental diagnosis of lung cancer with staging T1b N0 M0. Postoperatively, she was treated for atrial fibrillation and lung collapse, then discharged after resolution of these complications on the eighth day after surgery, and remained well at follow-up three months later. This case report explores a situation when this sequence of interventions was appropriate due to increased surgical risk in the elderly population.

papers.title_en: First Presentation With Impending Cardiac Tamponade Leading to a New Diagnosis of Mediastinal Lymphoma: A Shared Learning Case on the Atypical Presentation of Pericardial Effusion and Cardiac Tamponade.
papers.authors: Israr S, Ilandari Dewa NS, Teo ME
papers.affiliation_highlight: General Medicine, Hinchingbrooke Hospital, Huntingdon, GBR.
papers.authors_conclusion: 本病例提示应识别心脏压塞的不典型表现，并在出现不明原因心肺症状的年轻患者中考虑纵隔恶性肿瘤。
papers.ai_note: 单例病例报告，无对照、无分母，不能推断发生率或诊断效能；“不典型表现”的强调基于个案，缺乏系统病例系列验证；摘要未给出任何可核查的数值型结果（如心包积液量、压力、缓解率），信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: Cardiac tamponade is a life-threatening emergency classically associated with Beck's triad of hypotension, muffled heart sounds, and elevated jugular venous pressure; however, incomplete or atypical presentations may delay diagnosis. We report the case of a previously healthy 28-year-old woman who presented with progressive dyspnoea, pleuritic chest pain, orthopnoea, peripheral oedema, fever, and fatigue. Examination revealed mild tachycardia, soft heart sounds, reduced basal air entry, and ankle oedema, while the patient remained normotensive. Initial investigations demonstrated cardiomegaly with pleural effusions on chest radiograph, low-voltage QRS complexes on electrocardiogram, and markedly raised inflammatory markers. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography identified a large anterior mediastinal mass encasing the great vessels, a significant pericardial effusion with features of cardiac tamponade, and bilateral pleural effusions. Emergency pericardiocentesis resulted in immediate clinical improvement. Histopathological analysis confirmed high-grade B-cell lymphoma, most consistent with primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma. The patient was treated with immunochemotherapy, achieving complete metabolic remission on end-of-treatment PET-CT. This case highlights the importance of recognising atypical presentations of cardiac tamponade and considering mediastinal malignancy in young patients presenting with unexplained cardiorespiratory symptoms.

papers.title_zh: 迷迭香酸通过抑制HSF1-HSP轴增强A549非小细胞肺癌细胞对轻度热疗的凋亡敏感性（体外机制研究）
papers.title_en: Disarming the Heat-Shock Response: Rosmarinic Acid Potentiates Mild Hyperthermia-Induced Apoptosis in A549 Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Cells.
papers.authors: Ahn CR, Baek SH
papers.affiliation_highlight: College of Korean Medicine, Dongguk University, Goyang-si, Gyeonggi-do, Republic of Korea.
papers.authors_conclusion: RA增强热疗诱导的氧化应激并抑制A549细胞中的HSF1-HSP轴，为其作为热疗肺癌治疗中的生化辅助剂进一步开展临床前评估提供了依据。
papers.ai_note: 仅为A549单细胞系体外研究，无动物或临床数据；摘要未报告样本量、重复次数、统计检验、效应量或P值；NAC rescue仅提示ROS相关，不能证明通路特异性；将“biochemical adjuvant in hyperthermic lung cancer therapy”外推至临床为时过早。
papers.abstract_en: This study investigated the biochemical mechanisms by which rosmarinic acid (RA), a natural polyphenol, sensitizes A549 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells to mild hyperthermia (43°C). A549 cells were treated with RA (100 or 200 μM) and exposed to mild hyperthermia (43°C, 30 min), after which we performed a comprehensive analysis of cell viability, clonogenic potential, and migratory recovery. The molecular underpinnings were explored through flow cytometry for reactive oxygen species (ROS) and cell cycle progression, together with western blotting for MAPK signaling (JNK, ERK), apoptosis-related proteins (Bcl-xL, survivin, caspases), and the heat-shock response (HSP27, 70, 90, and HSF1). Our results show that the combination of RA and hyperthermia impaired cell proliferation and migration while promoting S-phase accumulation and apoptosis. At the biochemical level, combined RA and hyperthermia increased intracellular ROS beyond the level produced by either treatment alone. This rise in ROS occurred alongside an altered p-JNK/total JNK profile and caspase activation-associated apoptosis. Importantly, RA suppressed the canonical heat-shock response, lowering the p-HSF1/total HSF1 ratio and reducing the expression of the molecular chaperones HSP27, 70, and 90. Pretreatment with N-acetylcysteine (NAC) attenuated the observed ROS, Annexin V, and immunoblot changes, consistent with a contribution of redox imbalance to this sensitization process. In conclusion, RA enhanced hyperthermia-induced oxidative stress and suppressed the HSF1-HSP axis in A549 cells, providing a rationale for its further preclinical evaluation as a biochemical adjuvant in hyperthermic lung cancer therapy.

papers.title_en: Anticancer Activity and Molecular Docking Analysis of Trans-Cinnamic Acid in Human Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Dursun EN, Akçaalan S, Güneş CE, Şirin S, Dolanbay SN, Kurar E
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Biology, Faculty of Medicine, Necmettin Erbakan University, Konya, Türkiye.
papers.authors_conclusion: tCA抑制A549细胞增殖与克隆形成，调控部分凋亡及ER应激相关基因，并改变氧化应激指标；这些体外结果为tCA的潜在抗癌活性提供初步证据，但仍需蛋白水平、功能学及体内研究证实其机制与治疗潜力。
papers.ai_note: 单一细胞系、无体内/药代数据；IC50 2.59 mM远高于临床可及血药浓度，转化相关性存疑；凋亡/ER应激结论仅基于qRT-PCR基因表达，缺乏蛋白与功能验证；摘要正文称CASP3基因表达上调，而图注文字称caspase-3水平下降，二者矛盾；各终点仅报“显著”而无具体统计量，且未见多重比较校正说明；分子对接为预测性结果，不能支持因果机制。
papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is known to have a very high incidence and mortality rate. Trans-cinnamic acid (tCA) is a phenolic compound found in various fruits and vegetables and is known to have many effects such as antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and anticancer. In this study, molecular docking analysis was performed to predict the binding affinities of tCA toward apoptosis- and ER stress-related target proteins. The effects of tCA on proliferation, apoptosis and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress gene expression, colony forming ability, total antioxidant status (TAS) and total oxidant status (TOS) in A549 human lung cancer cells were investigated. Cell proliferation and, expression levels of genes associated with apoptosis and ER stress determined using XTT and qRT-PCR, respectively. ELISA test was used for TAS, TOS and caspase-3 levels. Molecular docking analysis predicted favorable binding affinities of tCA toward the investigated target proteins. The IC50 value of tCA in A549 cells was found to be 2.59 mM at 48 h. Treatment with tCA significantly increased the expression of apoptosis genes including BAX, CASP3, CASP7, CASP8, CASP9, CYCS, and FADD. Among the ER stress-associated genes analyzed, only PERK and CHOP showed significant upregulation following tCA treatment, while no significant changes were observed in the remaining ER stress-related genes. Furthermore, tCA treatment caused a decrease in TAS level but an increase in TOS level. tCA suppressed the ability to form colonies in A549 cells according to the colony assay. In conclusion, tCA inhibited proliferation and colony formation, modulated selected apoptosis- and ER stress-related genes, and altered oxidative stress parameters in A549 cells. These in vitro findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the potential anticancer activity of tCA; however, further protein-level, functional, and in vivo studies are required to confirm the underlying mechanisms and therapeutic potential. The image outlines a study evaluating the anticancer effects of trans-cinnamic acid (tCA) on A549 lung cancer cells. Molecular docking analysis showed tCA has potential binding affinity to target proteins. In cell experiments, the IC50 of tCA was 2.59 mM at 48 h, determined by an XTT test. Treatment with tCA reduced TAS and caspase-3 levels while increasing TOS. RNA isolation and cDNA synthesis were followed by quantitative RT-PCR analysis, indicating that tCA may induce upregulation of ER stress and apoptotic markers in A549 cells. A colony assay demonstrated that tCA suppressed colony formation in these cells. ELISA assays for TAS, TOS, and caspase-3 were also performed as part of the analysis.

papers.title_en: PSMB7 is associated with DNA damage repair and immune microenvironment features and serves as a prognostic biomarker.
papers.authors: Shen Y, Wan Y, Ren B, Wu L, Jin L, Zhu Y, Huan J, Peng Q et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiation Oncology, Suzhou Research Center of Medical School, Suzhou Hospital, Affiliated Hospital of Medi…
papers.authors_conclusion: PSMB7 是 LUAD 的候选独立预后生物标志物，与恶性进展、免疫微环境特征及细胞对照射的反应相关，符合其在放射抵抗中的潜在作用；这些发现支持 PSMB7 作为 LUAD 潜在治疗靶点。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未给出任何效应量、HR、C-index、P 值或样本量，无法核验“独立预后”与“放射抵抗”的强度；研究横跨表达、表观遗传、共表达网络、通路、免疫浸润、nomogram 与体外实验等多个终点，未见预设主要终点，存在多重比较与选择性报告风险；“独立预后”是否经多因素校正、校正了哪些变量未说明；体外仅见增殖与照射后凋亡表型，向“放射抵抗”“治疗靶点”的推演属外推；免疫相关结论基于浸润估算算法，不能等同于功能证据。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The clinical significance and biological roles of PSMB7 in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize PSMB7 expression, prognostic value, epigenetic regulation, immune associations, and in vitro functions in LUAD. METHODS: PSMB7 expression, clinicopathological associations, prognostic value, epigenetic regulation, co-expression networks, functional pathways, and relationships with the tumor immune microenvironment were systematically evaluated across multiple datasets. External validation was performed in the GSE31210 cohort. Prognostic nomogram performance was additionally evaluated using Harrell's concordance index (C-index) and time-dependent decision curve analysis (DCA). In vitro experiments, including Western blotting, CCK-8 assays, and flow cytometry, were conducted to assess the effects of PSMB7 on cell proliferation and irradiation-induced apoptosis in LUAD cell lines. RESULTS: PSMB7 was significantly upregulated in LUAD and was associated with advanced pathological T and N stages and overall clinical stage. ROC analysis indicated that PSMB7 showed potential discriminatory ability between LUAD and normal lung tissues. High PSMB7 expression independently predicted unfavorable outcomes across multiple prognostic endpoints. Nomogram evaluation using calibration, C-index, and DCA provided complementary evidence for prognostic performance. PSMB7 hypomethylation was associated with poorer survival. PSMB7 expression was positively correlated with DNA mismatch repair genes, RNA modification regulators, and malignant tumor phenotypes. GSEA showed significant enrichment of oncogenic, cell-cycle, metabolic, DNA-repair, and stress-response pathways. In addition, PSMB7 expression was strongly associated with immune scores, immune-cell infiltration, and the expression of immune modulators, MHC molecules, chemokines, and chemokine receptors in LUAD. In vitro, PSMB7 knockdown suppressed cell proliferation and enhanced irradiation-induced apoptosis, whereas PSMB7 overexpression promoted proliferation and reduced apoptosis after irradiation. CONCLUSION: PSMB7 is a candidate independent prognostic biomarker in LUAD and is associated with malignant progression, immune microenvironment features, and cellular responses to irradiation consistent with a potential role in radioresistance. These findings support PSMB7 as a potential therapeutic target in LUAD.

papers.title_zh: PPP1R14B通过上调ARPC1A促进肺腺癌发生与紫杉醇耐药（公共队列+细胞与小鼠模型机制研究）
papers.title_en: PPP1R14B Promotes Lung Adenocarcinoma Tumorigenesis and Paclitaxel Resistance by Increasing ARPC1A Expression.
papers.authors: Yang Y, You W, Wang X, Shang B, Jiang S
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Jinan Central Hospital, Shandong University, Jinan, Shandong, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: PPP1R14B直接结合ARPC1A并提高其表达，从而促进肺腺癌肿瘤发生与紫杉醇耐药。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未给出任何具体数值、样本量或统计量，效应强度无法评估；紫杉醇耐药仅以细胞增殖/凋亡等体外替代指标定义，未见IC50、耐药株模型或体内耐药验证；沉默与过表达分别只在A549、H1650单株细胞完成，缺乏同株双向验证与多模型重复；“直接结合”仅依据co-IP，未提供结构域定位或纯化蛋白直接结合证据；TCGA预后分析未说明多因素校正与最佳截断值设定，存在选择性报告风险。
papers.abstract_en: To investigate the biological functions of PPP1R14B in lung adenocarcinoma and further elucidate its underlying regulatory mechanisms. The Cancer Genome Atlas clinical cohorts, single-cell sequencing, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blot were performed to assess the expression and prognostic value of PPP1R14B in lung adenocarcinoma. Then, PPP1R14B-silenced A549 cells and PPP1R14B-overexpressing H1650 cells were constructed. Colony formation, CCK-8, EdU assay, flow cytometry, scratch, and Transwell chamber assays were utilized to evaluate cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration, invasion, and paclitaxel (PTX) resistance. To elucidate the molecular mechanism of PPP1R14B, transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) and co-immunoprecipitation assays were conducted. Additionally, a xenograft tumor mouse model was established to explore the in vivo role of PPP1R14B. PPP1R14B exhibited high expression in lung adenocarcinoma and correlated with an unfavorable prognosis. Silencing of PPP1R14B markedly suppressed the proliferation, migration, and invasion of A549 cells, while concurrently promoting apoptosis and sensitizing cells to PTX. Nevertheless, overexpression of PPP1R14B in H1650 cells displayed an opposite trend. PPP1R14B directly interacted with ARPC1A and promoted its expression. Overexpression of ARPC1A reversed the inhibitory effects of PPP1R14B silencing on the malignant biological behaviors of A549 cells. In vivo, silencing of PPP1R14B repressed tumor growth, as evidenced by smaller tumor volume, lower tumor weight, fewer Ki67-positive cells, and more TUNEL-positive cells. PPP1R14B directly binds ARPC1A and increases its expression to facilitate lung adenocarcinoma tumorigenesis and PTX resistance.

papers.authors: Li J, He R, He J, Ye J, Xie Y, Yuan B
papers.affiliation_highlight: Center of Geriatric Medicine, Affiliated Hospital of Guangdong Medical University, Zhanjiang, Guangdong, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: 结果支持如下模型：甜橙素通过抑制Nrf2/ARE依赖性抗氧化防御，至少部分地促进NSCLC细胞氧化应激介导的凋亡。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未给出任何剂量、IC50、凋亡比例、ROS倍数或P值/CI，全部为定性描述，无法判断效应量与统计可靠性；对正常BEAS-2B仅以“comparatively modest”定性表述，缺乏选择性/治疗窗的量化证据；无动物体内或类器官验证，作者由细胞系结果外推至NSCLC治疗潜能，属超出数据的推论；未说明重复次数与统计学方法。
papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells frequently depend on Nrf2/ARE-driven antioxidant programs to maintain redox balance and evade apoptosis. This study investigated whether sinensetin, a naturally occurring polymethoxylated flavone, reduces NSCLC cell survival by interfering with this cytoprotective pathway. A549 and H1299 NSCLC cells and normal BEAS-2B bronchial epithelial cells were exposed to sinensetin. Cell viability was measured by MTT assay, apoptosis was quantified by Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry, and pathway- and apoptosis-related proteins were analyzed by western blotting. Nrf2 distribution was evaluated by nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation, ARE-dependent transcription was assessed using a dual-luciferase reporter system, and Nrf2 was silenced by shRNA. Intracellular ROS was measured by DCFH-DA, antioxidant rescue was assessed with N-acetyl-l-cysteine (NAC), Nrf2/ARE-related proteins were examined in BEAS-2B cells, and Nrf2 overexpression was used as a rescue approach in A549 cells. Sinensetin inhibited NSCLC cell growth, increased apoptosis, reduced total and nuclear Nrf2, decreased ARE reporter activity, and downregulated HO-1 and NQO1. Sinensetin also increased intracellular ROS, whereas NAC partially reduced ROS accumulation, restored cell viability, and decreased apoptosis. BEAS-2B cells showed comparatively modest Nrf2/ARE pathway changes. Nrf2 overexpression partially restored HO-1 and NQO1, reduced apoptotic signaling, and attenuated sinensetin-induced loss of viability and apoptosis. These results support a model in which sinensetin promotes oxidative stress-mediated apoptosis in NSCLC cells, at least in part, through suppression of Nrf2/ARE-dependent antioxidant defense.

papers.authors: Lu S, Girard N, Yang JC, Shepherd FA, Dong X, Arulananda S, Metro G, Hayashi H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Oncology, Shanghai Chest Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, School of Medicine, Shanghai.
papers.authors_conclusion: 在奥希替尼治疗期间进展、伴MET过表达或MET扩增或两者兼有的EGFR突变局部晚期或转移性NSCLC患者中，奥希替尼-赛沃替尼较铂类-培美曲塞显著延长无进展生存和总生存（由阿斯利康资助；SAFFRON，NCT05261399）
papers.ai_note: 开放标签设计，PFS依赖盲法独立中心评估以部分抵消偏倚，但症状性毒性（外周水肿49%）可能影响治疗中止与后续治疗；OS为最终分析且阳性，摘要未交代交叉用药、后续治疗分布及多重性检验策略对OS解释的影响；人群经严格生物标志物限定（IHC 3+≥90%或FISH ≥10拷贝），筛查1746例仅随机338例，结论外推至其他MET定义（如低水平扩增、蛋白中等表达）需谨慎；对照组为化疗，未设奥希替尼+安慰剂臂，故不能区分赛沃替尼的增量贡献；摘要未报告客观缓解率、缓解持续时间及PFS2等次要终点。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy. METHODS: In this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety. RESULTS: Of the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; P<0.001), as well as significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.91; P = 0.01; final analysis). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of 12-month progression-free survival was 36% in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and 10% in the platinum-pemetrexed group, and the estimate of 12-month overall survival was 70% and 53%, respectively. The most frequently reported adverse events that occurred during treatment in the osimertinib-savolitinib group were peripheral edema (in 49% of the patients), anemia (in 26%), and diarrhea (in 26%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group. CONCLUSIONS: Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).
