papers.ai_note: 摘要未报告任何样本量、效应量、置信区间或P值，全部疗效表述为定性描述（改善临床评分与生存、减轻损伤、保留吞噬与NK/NKT细胞毒性与T细胞记忆、感染模型中维持病原控制），无法评估效应大小与统计稳健性；单细胞发现的NAD+轴塌陷与纳米药物疗效之间的因果链在摘要中未给出靶向验证细节；'不重新诱发GVHD'仅在两种感染挑战模型中验证，外推需谨慎；小鼠GVHD模型向人移植后闭塞性细支气管炎的转化不确定性未讨论。
papers.abstract_en: Chronic lung graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains difficult to treat, and broad immunosuppression increases infection risk. Single-cell profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage from bronchiolitis obliterans lesions revealed collapse of an epithelial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) metabolic axis with pathogenic immune-epithelial remodeling, nominating NAD+ restoration as an entry point. Because free NAD+ is poorly cell-permeable and rapidly consumed, we engineered CaNAD+-PGB-LiP (CNAPL), a high-payload NAD+ nanomedicine enabling direct intracellular replenishment. In murine allo-HSCT GVHD, CNAPL improved clinical scores and survival, reduced vascular and epithelial injury, and curtailed hyperinflammation and effector overactivation across GVHD target organs. Unlike immunosuppression, CNAPL preserved phagocytosis, NK/NKT cell (natural killer/natural killer T cell) cytotoxicity, and T cell memory. In posttransplant influenza or Klebsiella infection, CNAPL maintained pathogen control without rekindling GVHD, decoupling inflammation control from infection susceptibility. This metabolism-centered, host-directed strategy restores immune-tissue homeostasis and provides a practical translational path for durable lung GVHD control with preserved antimicrobial defense.

papers.authors_conclusion: 需要进一步工作来描述自我采样加强监测的方法，以优化社区参与和方案依从性、尽可能生成接近实时的数据并降低成本。

papers.abstract_en: Background Self-swab enhanced surveillance of respiratory pathogens is an emerging public health tool that could expand the reach of existing surveillance, providing real-time monitoring of circulating pathogens in the community. Methods We conducted a literature search using terms covering self-swabbing, respiratory infection, and surveillance. For inclusion, publications had to describe a study on the use of serial unsupervised self-swabbing for the purpose of tracking the frequency of respiratory infections in the general population. Results We found 42 publications originating from 27 unique studies on self-swab enhanced surveillance for respiratory infection. Twenty-six studies (96%) were conducted in a high-income setting. Eleven studies (41%) included children under the age of 12 years. Most studies involved a central laboratory conducting polymerase chain reaction testing on returned self-swabs which permitted testing for a wide range of pathogens. Among studies reporting the number of invitees, <20% of invited individuals typically agreed to join. In studies requiring regular symptom reporting, adherence was commonly >75%. Adherence rates for self-swab return were more variable (between 42-96%). Eight studies (30%) explored rapid antigen testing which appears to reduce the time taken between symptom onset and test result notification but limits the number of pathogens that can be evaluated compared with polymerase chain reaction testing. Based on our findings we present a list of suggestions to guide future implementation and investigation. Conclusions Further work is needed to characterise self-swab enhanced surveillance approaches that optimise community participation and protocol adherence, generate as close to real-time data as possible, and minimise costs.

papers.abstract_en: Pleural and thoracic air-leak complications after hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are clinically important but underrepresented in broad post-transplant pulmonary reviews. Direct evidence is concentrated in adult allogeneic HCT. In a cohort of 618 adults, clinically significant pleural effusion had a 1-year cumulative incidence of 9.9% (95% confidence interval, 7.7-12.5%). A separate computed tomography-based cohort of 178 first allogeneic HCT recipients reported a day-100 cumulative incidence of 41.0%; these estimates are not directly comparable because the populations, ascertainment methods, endpoints, and follow-up differed. In 50 HCT recipients undergoing thoracentesis, a specific diagnosis was established in 26%, with 5 pneumothoraces and 0 hemothoraces. Thoracic air-leak syndrome is uncommon but carries poor outcomes in reported adult and pediatric series. This focused narrative review distinguishes direct HCT evidence from data extrapolated from hematologic malignancy, general pleural practice, critical care, interventional radiology, and cellular therapy. We organize evaluation by urgency, transplant phase, and radiographic pattern; define chronic graft-versus-host disease serositis as a diagnosis of exclusion; summarize chylothorax and pleural infection management; and provide procedure-specific safety considerations for thoracentesis, small-bore drainage, indwelling pleural catheters, intrapleural enzyme therapy, and pleural biopsy. No prospective HCT-specific trials validate these procedural pathways. Clinicians should therefore use ultrasound or image guidance; apply procedure-specific rather than uniform hemostatic thresholds; and integrate infection risk, platelet trajectory, anticoagulant exposure, oxygenation, operator setting, and expected benefit. The two clinical frameworks presented are proposed and non-validated.

papers.title_zh: Pathway-level secretome modulation in bronchial epithelial spheroids following indoor dust exposure.
papers.title_en: Pathway-level secretome modulation in bronchial epithelial spheroids following indoor dust exposure.
papers.authors: Celis T, De Ryck E, Hoet PHM, Ghosh M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Environment and Health, Department of Public Health and Primary Care, KU Leuven, 3000, Louvain, Belgium.
papers.abstract_en: As humans spend most of their time indoors, they are continuously exposed to an array of indoor air pollutants. While exposure to individual indoor air pollutants may often occur at low levels, cumulative exposure to indoor air pollutants contributes substantially to the human exposome. Chronic inhalation of indoor air pollutants has been associated with multiple respiratory diseases, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and respiratory infections. In this study, the cellular effects of an acute indoor dust exposure using a three-dimensional airway epithelial model were investigated. Bronchial epithelial cells (16HBE14o-) were cultured as spheroids and exposed to reference indoor dust (SRM 2585; 0-200 µg/mL) for 24 h. Metabolic activity, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, inflammatory cytokine secretion, and secretome profiles were assessed. Indoor dust exposure did not induce morphological alterations or significant reductions in metabolic activity. Instead, a concentration-dependent increase in intracellular ROS was observed. Cytokine analysis revealed selective cytokine modulation, while untargeted proteomics identified limited changes in individual protein abundance. Instead, pathway-level analyses revealed enrichment of epithelial differentiation-related pathways. Overall, these findings suggest that a 24 h indoor dust exposure may elicit subtle cellular responses rather than overt cytotoxicity or inflammatory activation. This study highlights the applicability of integrating functional, immunological, and proteomics-based approaches with 3D airway models to investigate cellular responses to complex environmental particle mixtures. However, direct extrapolation to human exposure scenarios is limited by uncertainties regarding effective cellular dose, particle localization and environmental representativeness. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory, hypothesis-generating observations.

papers.title_en: Hydrophobic remodeling of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD large loop attenuates ACE2 engagement and viral fitness.
papers.authors: Wang A, Guo H, Yang H, Chen H, Imojara A, Ju B, Zhang Z, Yan R et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Biochemistry, Key University Laboratory of Metabolism and Health of Guangdong, SUSTech Homeostatic Medicin…

papers.ai_note: ①“viral fitness 减弱”的依据在摘要中仅为 JN.4 相对 JN.1 传播规模有限的观察性描述，未给出适应度测定的定量结果，属相关性推断；②3.5 倍亲和力下降未报告重复次数、误差范围或统计检验，无法判断效应稳健性；③主要结论建立在体外重组蛋白与模拟体系，向真实感染与流行病学适应性外推存在跨度；④摘要突出“功能受限/结构框架保守”的正面机制叙事，未讨论 A475V 是否伴随其他补偿性突变，信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: The SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariant JN.4 harbors a unique A475V substitution within the receptor binding domain (RBD) but exhibits limited expansion compared to its parallel descendant JN.1. Here, we investigate how hydrophobic remodeling within RBD large loop (residues 475-490) modulates receptor engagement and spike function. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals that A475V induces local remodeling of the receptor-binding motif (RBM) and alters the RBD-ACE2 interaction geometry. Local refinement revealed that the bulky valine substitution disrupts the local interaction network surrounding residue 475, resulting in a 3.5-fold reduction in ACE2-binding affinity compared with BA.2.86. In contrast to the L455S substitution in JN.1, which primarily alters the receptor-binding interface, A475V within the flexible large loop influences both local loop conformation and global spike conformational properties. Systematic mutagenesis identifies A475 and F486 as functionally constrained hydrophobic residues that preserve the structural framework of ACE2 engagement despite extensive sequence variation within the surrounding loop. Together with molecular dynamics simulations and functional assays, our findings establish the RBD 475-490 large loop as a structurally plastic yet functionally constrained element that balances receptor recognition, conformational stability, and antigenic diversification. These results provide a mechanistic framework for understanding region-specific evolutionary constraints that shape SARS-CoV-2 RBD adaptation.

papers.title_en: An Oral Antiviral Combination Against Severe COVID-19 Enabled by the Synergistic Mechanisms of Action of Auranofin and Remdesivir.
papers.authors: Khatun O, Narayan R, Nagaraj SK, Shiraz R, Kaliappan A, Kaur S, Singh A, Shanmugam Selvaraj S et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Emerging Viral Pathogens Laboratory, Infosys Wing, Centre for Infectious Disease Research, Indian Institute of Science, …

papers.ai_note: 摘要仅作定性描述，未给出样本量、效应量、统计检验、随机化/盲法及对照设置细节；药物协同与体内优效需独立重复验证；临床前结果外推至临床为时过早；研究非胸部肿瘤，与胸外科临床决策关联弱。
papers.abstract_en: Auranofin, an FDA-approved oral anti-rheumatic drug, was previously shown by our group to restrict Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) replication and pathology in preclinical models. Here, we systematically characterized its mechanism of action (MOA) through biochemical drug-protein interactions, cell-based mechanistic assays, and preclinical efficacy studies. Auranofin directly binds and inhibits SARS-CoV-2 MPro while simultaneously targeting multiple stages of the viral life cycle, disrupting endosomal trafficking, suppressing Spike S1/S2 proteolytic processing, impairing syncytia formation, and attenuating NF-κB-driven proinflammatory signaling. In cell culture, Auranofin demonstrated robust synergy with Remdesivir but competed with the MPro inhibitor Nirmatrelvir, informing rational combination design. In mice infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant, the oral combination of Auranofin and the Remdesivir prodrug GS-621763 outperformed monotherapy, markedly reducing viral replication, inflammatory cytokine responses, and lung pathology, and improving clinical outcomes. These findings establish a multi-target antiviral MOA of Auranofin and provide a mechanistic rationale for an all-oral antiviral combination regimen against COVID-19.

papers.abstract_en: AbstractHuman adenoviruses (HAdVs) are common respiratory pathogens that cause severe, life-threatening infections in immunocompromised individuals and children. Despite their medical importance, no clinically approved antiviral drugs exist. Here, we showed that 4H30, a 4-branched human defensin peptide, exhibited broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple HAdV subtypes in A549 and Calu-3 cells with negligible cytotoxicity and a high barrier to viral resistance in A549 cells. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that 4H30 exhibited a unique dual mechanism of action: direct virucidal activity through capsid disruption and endosomal trapping by impairing protein VI-mediated membrane penetration. Notably, 4H30 remained effective against HAdV-3 in human respiratory organoids and against HAdV-2 and HAdV-5 in an immunosuppressed hamster model, significantly reducing viral replication and disease-associated pathology. These findings demonstrate that 4H30 can inhibit multiple HAdVs through a novel mechanism, offering a new therapeutic avenue against HAdV infections.

papers.abstract_en: Legionella pneumophila is the causative agent of Legionnaires' disease, an accidental and severe form of pneumonia. The replication of L. pneumophila within alveolar macrophages requires the Dot/Icm type IV secretion system that translocates more than 330 bacterial effector proteins into the infected host cell. Many Dot/Icm effectors possess eukaryotic-like domains and manipulate host processes by functional mimicry. However, only a minority of effectors have been fully characterized. Redundancy among effector protein activities and host targets has complicated functional characterization of individual effector proteins. To explore the collective impact of Dot/Icm effectors on host cell processes, we created a library of 14 L. pneumophila genomic mutant strains lacking effector-rich regions (a total of 85 effector genes deleted) and used the multi-deletion mutants to interrogate host-pathogen interactions. While none of the mutants exhibited a defect in intracellular replication in THP-1 macrophages, several were attenuated in amoebae, including a mutant lacking a predicted amino acid transporter. In THP-1 cells, we observed that wild-type L. pneumophila 130b triggered a strong inflammatory and cellular stress transcriptional response in macrophages, whereas six mutants displayed reduced interferon signalling and one mutant displayed a marked decrease in the global expression of host heat shock response (HSR) genes. Through the creation of further sub-deletions, we found that the Dot/Icm effector kinase LegK4 was responsible for induction of the host HSR via the canonical transcription factor heat shock factor 1 (HSF1). Infection of THP-1 macrophages deficient in HSF1 revealed a potential role for the host HSR in the early stages of L. pneumophila infection. Together, these results reinforce the utility of multi-gene deletions to identify Dot/Icm effector phenotypes and the importance of the host HSR to L. pneumophila infection.

papers.title_en: Worldwide emergence of SARS-CoV-2 NB.1.8.1 sublineage with spike 420N and 478 T dual substitution.
papers.authors: Tsoi HW, Chan WM, Chu AW, Yip CY, Zhang X, Ip JD, Luo Y, Chu H et al.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: After a year of quiescence, SARS-CoV-2 activity increased rapidly in Hong Kong since June 2026. We sought to characterize the genomic profile of SARS-CoV-2 driving this COVID-19 surge in Hong Kong and to examine the global dissemination of the identified circulating lineages. METHODS: We performed SARS-CoV-2 whole-genome sequencing on archived respiratory specimens collected at Queen Mary Hospital, Hong Kong, between January 2025 and July 2026. Viral lineages were assigned via Nextclade. Global SARS-CoV-2 metadata downloaded from GISAID as of July 2026 were analyzed to track global evolutionary trends. RESULTS: Among 615 successfully sequenced strains, the XDV descendant NB.1.8.1 was the predominant lineage. Between April and July 2026, NB.1.8.1 descendants accounted for 95.6% (108/113) of sequenced strains, dominated by PQ.16.1.1 (81.5%). Spike substitutions 420N and 478 T emerged rapidly. While 478 T increased gradually throughout 2025, 420N emerged in April 2026 and reached 98.0% by June-July 2026. Strains harboring 420N-478 T dual substitution arose independently across distinct NB.1.8.1 lineages, accounting for 94.4% (102/108) of NB.1.8.1 descendants in Hong Kong during this period. Globally, the prevalence of NB.1.8.1 strains with 420N-478 T dual substitution increased from <1% before April 2026 to 50.7% by mid-July 2026, with the highest prevalence observed in Southeast Asia and Australia. CONCLUSIONS: The 2026 COVID-19 surge in Hong Kong was driven by NB.1.8.1 descendants harboring spike 420N and 478 T substitutions. The rapid worldwide expansion of these dual-substitution lineages highlights their competitive growth advantage and underscores the need for continued global genomic surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary fibrosis is a common and often fatal outcome of fibrosing interstitial lung diseases, characterized by progressive extracellular matrix deposition, destruction of alveolar architecture and irreversible loss of respiratory function. Although fibroblast activation and epithelial dysfunction are central to disease pathogenesis, fibrosis cannot be adequately explained by mesenchymal dysregulation alone. Rather, it represents a failure of multicellular repair regulation, in which immune cells, fibroblasts and epithelial populations reciprocally reshape cellular states, tissue niches and disease trajectories. Early innate immune responses amplify epithelial injury while simultaneously initiating provisional repair; however, when injury persists, these transient programmes fail to resolve and become stabilized into chronic profibrotic circuits involving monocyte-derived macrophages, dysfunctional T cells, inflammatory fibroblasts and matrix-producing myofibroblasts. Recent single-cell, spatial transcriptomic and lineage-tracing studies have revealed discrete cellular states, including SPP1⁺ scar-associated macrophages, inflammatory fibroblasts, CTHRC1⁺ myofibroblasts and tertiary-lymphoid-structure-associated stromal cells, that assemble multicellular, stage-specific and microanatomically restricted fibrotic niches. Collectively, these findings support a model in which soluble mediators, extracellular matrix mechanics, metabolic rewiring and immune-regulatory signalling cooperate to establish self-reinforcing stromal-immune circuits. In this Review, we synthesize current evidence for bidirectional immune-fibroblast crosstalk in pulmonary fibrosis, focusing on macrophage and T cell programmes, fibroblast-mediated immune regulation, spatiotemporal niche remodelling, mechanistic signalling networks, experimental models and therapeutic opportunities. We propose that progressive fibrosis reflects the spatiotemporal locking of pathological epithelial-immune-stromal circuits, a framework that may explain the limited efficacy of broad anti-inflammatory therapies in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and guide the development of more precise, stage-specific and combinatorial antifibrotic strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a threat to human health. Although receptor specificity, polymerase adaptation, and airway tropism have been studied extensively, it remains unresolved how they combine to shape tropism in airway epithelia. Here, we show that avian IAVs infect ciliated and secretory cells but preferentially bind to ciliated cells because of higher apical α2,3-linked sialic acid levels. As replication levels are comparable between cell types, this translates into overall preference for ciliated cells. Human IAVs also preferentially bind to ciliated cells despite comparable α2,6-linked sialic acid abundance. Instead, they show higher viral RNA and protein levels in secretory cells, linked to their compatibility with human ANP32 proteins and modestly higher ANP32A/B expression in this cell type, resulting in equal infection levels across cell types. Our findings redefine IAV tropism in the human airway as a stage-resolved process shaped by the interplay between apical glycans, viral binding, polymerase cofactor compatibility, and cell-type-specific replication capacity, moving beyond receptor-centric models.

papers.abstract_en: Robotic systems for computed tomography (CT)-guided needle insertion have been developed to address the limitations of conventional manual needle insertion. Thus far, various robotic systems have been clinically implemented, and accumulating evidence has suggested their clinical utility. The evidence has evolved beyond initial feasibility and early clinical experience to include larger observational and comparative studies. These studies have demonstrated high success rates of robot-assisted needle insertion in various CT-guided interventions, including thermal ablation, biopsy, and preoperative localization. Furthermore, an increasing number of comparative studies have demonstrated the advantages of robot-assisted procedures over conventional manual procedures. These advantages include improved needle insertion accuracy and reduced radiation doses to patients and/or physicians. Although most currently available robotic systems are needle-guiding robots designed to align a needle guide with a predetermined insertion trajectory, we have developed a CT-guided needle insertion robot capable of robotic needle advancement via remote control. Clinical studies have demonstrated the feasibility of robotic needle insertion using this system, as well as needle placement accuracy comparable to that of manual procedures, while eliminating radiation exposure to physicians. The integration of artificial intelligence and the implementation of telerobotic interventions are expected to contribute significantly to the further advancement of robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion. This narrative review summarizes the current clinical implementations and available evidence for robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion, including our system, and discusses future perspectives in this field.

papers.authors: Li Q, Yang J, Chen X, Zhao P, Luo Z, Wang Z, Yang R, Zhou M et al.

papers.abstract_en: Developing effective nanomedicines for pulmonary metastasis remains challenging because of systemic clearance and local stromal barriers. Guided by single-cell transcriptomic profiling, we characterized a compartmentalized immunosuppressive network involving PGE2 and provide a biological rationale for coordinated EP2/EP4 antagonism. We therefore engineered an inhalable biomimetic platform (PD-1@E2/4 Exo) comprising PD-1-displaying exosomes co-loaded with EP2 and EP4 antagonists. Compared with intravenous administration, nebulized delivery increased pulmonary exposure of the engineered vesicles. Within the pulmonary tumor setting, surface PD-1 is intended to interfere with PD-1/PD-L1 signaling, while the co-delivered antagonists target the EP2/EP4 immunosuppressive axis. Treatment was associated with macrophage reprogramming, increased oxidative stress, and enhanced ICD-related responses in tumor cells. In the experimental breast-cancer lung-colonization model, the inhaled formulation reduced established pulmonary tumor burden and was accompanied by systemic immune-memory responses. These findings provide a preclinical study for integrating local pulmonary delivery with coordinated metabolic and immune modulation in breast cancer lung disease.

papers.title_en: The Proteasomal Switch as a Kinetic Battleground for Influenza A Virus Pathogenesis.
papers.authors: Soni S, Anang V, Kumar P, Tizazu AM, Arega EG, Nho RS, Mora AL, Rojas M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Internal Medicine, Division of Pulmonary, Critical Care and Sleep Medicine, Davis Heart and Lung Institute…
papers.authors_conclusion: 免疫蛋白酶体既是宿主防御效应器，也是病毒颠覆的靶点；提出IAV蛋白选择性干扰蛋白酶体亚基以稳定促病毒因子的工作模型，并将iP与UPS/ERAD/自噬共同视为蛋白稳态缓冲；提出时间依赖的双相蛋白酶体调控框架，认为晚期β5i抑制有临床前支持，早期激活仍属理论概念。
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，无系统检索策略、纳入排除标准、偏倚风险评价或定量合并；所提工作模型与双相框架属假说生成，晚期β5i抑制的“临床前支持”未在摘要给出具体数据；将机制推演延伸至急性肺损伤与inflammaging，证据层级有限。
papers.abstract_en: AbstractInfluenza A virus (IAV) infection initiates a high-stakes competition for proteostatic control. While the host reconfigures its degradative machinery for defense, the virus simultaneously hijacks host proteostatic and degradative pathways to facilitate replication and evade immunity. Central to this conflict is the proteasomal switch, a process in which constitutive proteasome subunits (β1, β2, β5) are replaced by their inducible counterparts (β1i, β2i, β5i) to form the immunoproteasome (iP). Although iP is classically recognized for optimizing MHC class I antigen presentation, emerging evidence reveals more nuanced roles in IAV infections. This review synthesizes current knowledge on iP as an effector of host defense and target for viral subversion. We synthesize emerging evidence and propose working models detailing how IAV proteins may selectively interfere with proteasomal subunits to stabilize pro-viral factors. Furthermore, we examine the hypothesis that the iP functions alongside broader ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD), and autophagic pathways as a proteostatic buffer to mitigate proteotoxic and oxidative stress in the infected epithelium. By evaluating how age-related proteostatic decay and viral subversion could impair cellular clearance machinery, we provide a conceptual framework for understanding how proteasomal dysregulation contributes to acute lung injury and the chronic inflammatory state termed as inflammaging. Finally, we propose a hypothesis-generating, biphasic framework for timing-dependent proteasomal modulation, contrasting preclinically supported late-stage β5i inhibition against the theoretical concept of early-stage activation to highlight translational hurdles in severe influenza.

papers.abstract_en: Mitigating on-target off-tumor toxicity remains a central challenge for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy for solid tumors. We developed a hypoxia-inducible CAR-T-cell product targeting carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) that restricts CAR activation to hypoxic tumor niches via oxygen-dependent expression control. In this first-in-human, phase I trial enrolling heavily pretreated patients with relapsed stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), a single infusion of the investigational product achieved an objective response rate of 47% and a disease control rate of 87%, with a manageable safety profile. Exploratory analyses showed that clinical outcomes were associated with baseline factors. Deep single-cell profiling indicated that the clinical response was associated with the expansion of hypoxia-adapted, tumor-reactive-like CD8+ T cells alongside coordinated functional maturation of natural killer (NK) cells. Collectively, these data provide clinical proof-of-concept for hypoxia-inducible CAR design and inform the rational development of strategies leveraging tumor microenvironmental features in solid tumor cellular immunotherapy.

papers.title_zh: Final Analysis of the Neotorch Study: Perioperative Toripalimab in Combination with Chemotherapy for Patients with Stage Ⅱ/Ⅲ Resectable Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.title_en: Final Analysis of the Neotorch Study: Perioperative Toripalimab in Combination with Chemotherapy for Patients with Stage Ⅱ/Ⅲ Resectable Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Li ZM, Wu L, Wang WX, Sun LH, Zhang P, Fang WT, Zheng Y, Chen QX et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Oncology, Shanghai Chest Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine; Shanghai; Chi…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Interim analysis of the Neotorch study demonstrated significant benefit in event-free survival (EFS) and major pathological response (MPR) rate for perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable Stage Ⅲ non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here, we report the final analysis results of the overall Stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ patients from this study. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients with treatment-naïve resectable Stage II, or Stage IIIA, IIIB (N2) NSCLC, were randomized to receive toripalimab or placebo plus chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment (3 cycles), adjuvant treatment (1 cycle), and toripalimab or placebo monotherapy as maintenance treatment (up to 13 cycles). The primary endpoints of this study were EFS assessed by investigators and MPR evaluated by blinded independent pathologic review (BIPR) in Stage Ⅲ patients, as well as the overall Stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ patients. RESULTS: A total of 501 patients in China were randomized (toripalimab arm: N=250, placebo arm: N=251). The baseline characteristics were generally balanced between the 2 arms. At the final analysis (median follow-up of 48.2 months), the investigator-assessed EFS was significantly improved in the toripalimab arm with stratified hazard ratio (HR) of 0.52 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.39, 0.68; stratified P <0.0001), and the median EFS in the toripalimab arm was not reached, while 20.2 months in the placebo arm. The inter-arm difference of MPR rate was statistically significant and clinically meaningful (47% vs 9%, P<0.0001). The OS prolongation was also statistically significant in the toripalimab arm (HR 0.66; 95% CI: 0.49, 0.89, P=0.0072), with median survival not reached in either arm. The safety profile was consistent with the interim analysis, with no new safety signals identified. CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy demonstrated durable and significant benefits on EFS, MPR, and OS in resectable Stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ NSCLC patients, with a manageable safety profile.

papers.title_zh: Extended follow-up of tarlatamab in patients with small-cell lung cancer after platinum-based chemotherapy in the randomized phase 3 DeLLphi-304 study.
papers.title_en: Extended follow-up of tarlatamab in patients with small-cell lung cancer after platinum-based chemotherapy in the randomized phase 3 DeLLphi-304 study.
papers.authors: Rudin CM, Ahn MJ, Schuler M, Blackhall FH, Mountzios G, Yoshida T, Sun L, Cho BC et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York, NY, USA.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In the DeLLphi-304 trial, at a median follow-up of <12 months, tarlatamab significantly improved overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and patient-reported outcomes (PROs), and demonstrated a favorable safety profile versus chemotherapy. We report efficacy and safety outcomes after extended follow-up in patients with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this phase 3, open-label trial, patients with SCLC whose disease had progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy were randomized (1:1) to receive either tarlatamab or chemotherapy (topotecan, lurbinectedin, or amrubicin) until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or death. The primary endpoint was OS. Secondary endpoints included investigator-assessed PFS, objective response, disease control, duration of response per RECIST v1.1, PROs, and safety. RESULTS: As of data cutoff (18 February 2026), median OS was 13.6 and 8.4 months with tarlatamab and chemotherapy, respectively (median follow-up, 23.3 and 22.8 months). Median PFS was 4.2 and 3.2 months, respectively (median follow-up, 22.2 and 21.9 months). Kaplan-Meier estimated OS rates at 12/24 months were 55.9%/30.3% with tarlatamab versus 39.0%/14.9% with chemotherapy; corresponding PFS rates at 12/24 months were 20.6%/14.2% versus 5.9%/2.3%. Objective response rate was 35.4% with tarlatamab, including six confirmed complete responses versus 20.4% with chemotherapy; at data cutoff, ongoing responses were observed in 31.1% (28/90) versus 3.8% (2/52) of responders, respectively. Sustained disease control for ≥52 weeks was observed in 24.4% versus 4.3%. Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 3.2% versus 6.6%; grade ≥3 events decreased over time, with no serious TRAEs with onset ≥12 months. CRS and ICANS occurred early in treatment and were predominantly low grade. CONCLUSIONS: With extended follow-up, tarlatamab continues to demonstrate sustained and durable clinical benefit and a favorable long-term tolerability profile versus chemotherapy, in patients with SCLC after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, supporting its use as the standard of care in this setting.

papers.title_zh: Izalontamab brengitecan versus platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PANKU-Lung01): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.
papers.title_en: Izalontamab brengitecan versus platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PANKU-Lung01): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.
papers.authors: Hong S, Zhou T, Hou X, Meng X, Hu Z, Zheng W, Cui J, Luo Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Oncology, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, State Key Laboratory of Oncology in South China, G…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class bispecific antibody-drug conjugate targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) and has shown antitumour activity in EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We compared iza-bren with platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial (PANKU-Lung01) conducted at 73 sites in China, eligible participants had EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, disease progression after third-generation EGFR TKIs, and had received no previous chemotherapy for advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle) or pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for four to six cycles, with pemetrexed maintenance permitted in participants without progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). The primary analysis included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of study treatment (modified intention-to-treat population). We report the prespecified final progression-free survival and interim overall survival analyses. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06382116. FINDINGS: Between May 22, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, we screened 654 participants. After 222 (34%) were excluded, 432 (66%) participants were randomly assigned to iza-bren (n=217 [50%]) or chemotherapy (n=215 [50%]); 422 (98%) received study treatment (216 [51%] in the iza-bren group and 206 [49%] in the chemotherapy group) and comprised the modified intention-to-treat population. At the data cutoff (July 15, 2026; median follow-up for progression-free survival 14·6 months [95% CI 12·9-16·7] in the iza-bren group vs 15·2 months [11·2-18·2] in the chemotherapy group), median BICR-assessed progression-free survival was 11·1 months (9·2-12·7) with iza-bren versus 5·7 months (5·5-5·9) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0·40 [95% CI 0·31-0·51]; one-sided p<0·0001). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse occurred in 170 (79%) of 216 participants in the iza-bren group and 128 (62%) of 206 in the chemotherapy group (predominantly haematological); treatment-related adverse events led to permanent discontinuation of at least one study-treatment component in four (2%) participants in each group and treatment-related deaths occurred in one participant in each group. Treatment-related interstitial lung disease occurred in two (1%) participants in the iza-bren group and none in the chemotherapy group. INTERPRETATION: In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population. FUNDING: Baili-Bio (Chengdu) Pharmaceutical.

papers.title_zh: Ruzaltatug rezetecan versus chemotherapy for EGFR-mutated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer progressing after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (HERON-Lung01): interim analysis of a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.
papers.title_en: Ruzaltatug rezetecan versus chemotherapy for EGFR-mutated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer progressing after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (HERON-Lung01): interim analysis of a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.
papers.authors: Xu CR, Zhang Y, Lin G, Wang H, Wang Q, Huang D, Yu Y, Zhou J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Guangdong Lung Cancer Institute, Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital and Guangdong Academy of Medical Sciences, South…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ruzaltatug rezetecan is a novel HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has shown promising antitumour activity and manageable safety in pretreated EGFR-.mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a phase 1 trial. We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of ruzaltatug rezetecan with chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC that had progressed after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. METHODS: HERON-Lung01 is a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial conducted at 62 sites in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harbouring an EGFR activating mutation (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation), and had progressed during or after EGFR-TKI therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan 8·0 mg/kg or chemotherapy comprising pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 plus carboplatin (area under the curve 5) or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 for four cycles, followed by maintenance pemetrexed. All treatments were administered intravenously on day 1 of each 3-week cycle. Block randomisation was stratified by presence of brain metastases, EGFR mutation subtype, and use of a first-line third-generation EGFR-TKI. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), in the intention-to-treat population. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06671379). Recruitment is complete, with the trial ongoing. FINDINGS: Between Nov 29, 2024, and Jan 29, 2026, 498 patients were randomly assigned to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan (n=250) or chemotherapy (n=248). The median age was 60·0 years (IQR 54·0-68·0); 276 (55%) patients were female and 222 (45%) male. At the prespecified interim PFS analysis, median follow-up was 7·7 months (95% CI 7·1-8·3). BICR-assessed PFS was significantly longer with ruzaltatug rezetecan than with chemotherapy (median 8·3 months vs 5·4 months; hazard ratio 0·47 [95% CI 0·36-0·60]; one-sided p<0·0001). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 101 (41%) of 248 patients receiving ruzaltatug rezetecan and 93 (39%) of 239 patients receiving chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (64 [26%] of 248 patients vs 46 [19%] of 239 patients), decreased white blood cell count (29 [12%] vs 29 [12%]), and anaemia (15 [6%] vs 26 [11%]). TRAEs led to treatment discontinuation in three (1%) patients in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group and three (1%) in the chemotherapy group. One death (unknown cause) in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group was considered by the investigator to be possibly treatment related. INTERPRETATION: Ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged PFS compared with chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in EGFR-TKI-resistant, EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC. These data support ruzaltatug rezetecan as a potential treatment option in this setting. FUNDING: Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

papers.title_zh: Efzofitimod versus placebo in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis (EFZO-FIT): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
papers.title_en: Efzofitimod versus placebo in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis (EFZO-FIT): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
papers.authors: Culver DA, Bonella F, Gupta R, Spagnolo P, Veltkamp M, Cameli P, Restrepo CI, Frye BC et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Integrated Hospital Care Institute, Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland, OH,…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Oral corticosteroids are currently standard-of-care therapy for pulmonary sarcoidosis, but they are associated with substantial toxicity and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The EFZO-FIT trial aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of efzofitimod, a novel immunomodulatory fusion protein targeting the neuropilin 2 receptor, as a steroid-sparing agent in pulmonary sarcoidosis. METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, adults aged 18-75 years with pulmonary sarcoidosis requiring treatment were enrolled at 85 study centres across nine countries (Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Spain, UK, and USA). Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 using stratified block randomisation to receive monthly intravenous infusions of efzofitimod 3 mg/kg, efzofitimod 5 mg/kg, or placebo over a 48-week treatment period, including a 12-week oral corticosteroid taper targeting 0 mg per day (starting on day 15). Oral corticosteroid dose could be adjusted upwards in the event of worsening sarcoidosis. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in mean daily oral corticosteroid dose at week 48. Outcome and safety analyses were done in participants who received at least one dose of the study drug and had at least one post-baseline efficacy assessment. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05415137) and is complete. FINDINGS: Between Sept 22, 2022, and Aug 14, 2025, 331 patients were screened for inclusion. 63 were excluded and 268 participants were randomly assigned to receive placebo (n=91), efzofitimod 3 mg/kg (n=89), or efzofitimod 5 mg/kg (n=88). Four patients were excluded after random assignment (one in the placebo group and three in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group). 264 patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and had at least one post-baseline assessment were included in the outcome analysis and safety population (90 in the placebo group, 86 in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and 88 in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group). Among the 264 participants, the mean age was 53·8 years (SD 10·6); 114 (43%) of 264 patients were female and 150 (57%) were male. 168 (64%) identified as White. Mean steroid dose was 10·7 mg per day (SD 4·4) at baseline and 2·9 mg per day (4·5) at week 48. No difference was seen in the magnitude of oral corticosteroid taper between the active and placebo dose groups; the placebo-adjusted change from baseline was 0·02 mg per day in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (95% CI -1·49 to 1·52, p=0·98) and -0·73 mg per day in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group (-2·21 to 0·75, p=0·33). The percentage of participants with serious treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between groups. Malaise was more common in the placebo group (five [6%] of 90 patients vs zero in both efzofitimod groups). TEAEs that were more common in the efzofitimod groups included headache (17 [19%] of 88 patients in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group, 11 [13%] of 86 patients in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and four [4%] of 90 patients in the placebo group), sinusitis (nine [10%], six [7%], and two [2%] patients, respectively), wheezing (seven [8%], two [2%], and zero patients, respectively), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) increased (five [6%], one [1%], and zero patients, respectively). Most adverse events were grade 1 or 2. Two participants died, both in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (one respiratory failure and one incarceration of a pre-existing inguinal hernia). Neither event was considered to be causally related to the treatment. INTERPRETATION: Efzofitimod was well tolerated but did not result in lower steroid doses at week 48 compared with placebo. The results from steroid tapering indicate that oral corticosteroid doses can be more aggressively reduced in many patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis. FUNDING: aTyr and Kyorin.

papers.title_zh: Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial.
papers.title_en: Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial.
papers.authors: Reck M, Nadal E, Gay CM, Girard N, Filippi AR, Martin LW, Petersen C, Cairns DA et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Lung Clinic Großhansdorf, Airway Research Center North, German Center for Lung Research, Großhansdorf, Germany.
papers.abstract_en: The phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE study is investigating perioperative durvalumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy (AEGEAN regimen) in resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer and chemoradiotherapy (CRT) followed by consolidation durvalumab (PACIFIC regimen) in patients who become unresectable after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy guided by multidisciplinary team assessments during the neoadjuvant period. The primary endpoint was the overall resection rate (descriptive with no formal hypothesis testing). Secondary endpoints included event-free survival, progression-free survival, pathological complete response rate (resectable patients cohort), circulating tumor DNA clearance between baseline and presurgery/pre-CRT and safety. Overall, 142 patients received neoadjuvant treatment; 64.8% and 35.2% were deemed resectable and borderline resectable at baseline, respectively. The overall resection rate (95% confidence interval) was 74.6% (66.7‒81.6) in a population that included more than one-third of patients with borderline resectable disease. R0 resection rate was 96.2% (90.6‒99.0) in those who underwent surgery. Overall, 131 (92.3%) patients had surgery (n = 106) or CRT (n = 25) after neoadjuvant treatment, and 117 (82.4%) patients received adjuvant (n = 94) or consolidation (n = 23) durvalumab. During adjuvant or consolidation durvalumab, maximum grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 7.4% of resected patients and 17.4% of CRT-treated patients, with 8.5% and 13.0% discontinuing treatment due to adverse events. This multidisciplinary team-guided approach was feasible and enabled delivery of curative-intent treatment (surgery or CRT), followed by durvalumab in most patients, and demonstrated encouraging preliminary efficacy with a manageable adjuvant or consolidation safety profile that was consistent with prior studies. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05925530 .

papers.title_zh: Clinical Phenotypes and Prognostic Heterogeneity of Mild-to-Moderate Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Prospective Community-Based Cohort Study.
papers.title_en: Clinical Phenotypes and Prognostic Heterogeneity of Mild-to-Moderate Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Prospective Community-Based Cohort Study.
papers.authors: Wu F, Wan Q, Zhou K, Wu X, Tang G, Huang S, Xia T, Wu F et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: State Key Laboratory of Respiratory Disease & National Clinical Research Center for Respiratory Diseases & National Cent…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The clinical phenotypes, prognosis, and heterogeneity of mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have not been systematically evaluated. RESEARCH QUESTION: Do different clinical phenotypes of mild-to-moderate COPD have different prognoses? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We analysed the baseline and 3-year follow-up data of participants with mild-to-moderate COPD from a prospective community-based cohort study. Mild-to-moderate COPD was defined as a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) / forced vital capacity ratio of < 0.70 and FEV1 ≥ 50% of the predicted value. The clinical phenotypes included respiratory symptoms, exacerbation history, emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling. Respiratory health outcomes included exacerbations and lung function decline over the 3-year follow-up. RESULTS: Overall, 806 participants with mild-to-moderate COPD were included, of whom 712 (88%) completed the 3-year follow-up. Participants with mild-to-moderate COPD had more severe emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling; increased exacerbation risk; and faster annual FEV1 decline than those with preserved spirometry. The severity of airflow obstruction, respiratory symptoms, emphysema, and air trapping, as well as the eosinophilic phenotype, had low overlap in mild-to-moderate COPD. There was significant individual variation in the annual FEV1 decline rate and exacerbation incidence among participants with mild-to-moderate COPD. Emphysema and air trapping were associated with faster FEV1 decline and higher exacerbation risk. Respiratory symptoms and exacerbations in the previous year were associated with a higher acute exacerbation risk but not with faster lung function decline. INTERPRETATION: Mild-to-moderate COPD exhibited distinct clinical phenotypes with significant prognostic heterogeneity. Accurate phenotype identification is essential for targeted intervention, clinical precision management, and prognostic improvement.

papers.title_zh: Histopathology-Based Spatial Profiling of Immune and Molecular Features Predicts Cancer Risk in Barrett's Esophagus Patients.
papers.title_en: Histopathology-Based Spatial Profiling of Immune and Molecular Features Predicts Cancer Risk in Barrett's Esophagus Patients.
papers.authors: Ercan C, Pan X, Paulson TG, Stachler MD, Göknur Akarca F, Grady WM, Maley CC, Yuan Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: University Hospital of Lausanne Lausanne, VD Switzerland.
papers.abstract_en: Barrett's esophagus (BE) patients require improved cancer risk stratification to identify high-risk individuals while reducing over-treatment in low-risk populations. BE evolution towards adenocarcinoma is likely driven by a combination of genomic and microenvironmental factors, suggesting the potential of predictive models that integrate both. Here, we developed BEACON (Barrett's Esophagus DNA content Abnormality and immune ecology for Cancer Outcome), a spatially aware framework integrating deep learning-based prediction of DNA content and immune architecture from routine histopathology. First, DACOR, a multi-instance learning model that predicts DNA content from histopathology, was trained using 777 BE biopsies with flow cytometry-based DNA content data scanned at two institutions, and it demonstrated strong performance across both validation and test datasets for DNA content abnormality prediction. Patients classified as DNA content abnormal by DACOR demonstrated increased cancer progression. Complementary models for cell classification and tissue segmentation enabled spatial immune ecology metric computations. Abnormal regions exhibited increased lymphoplasmacytic inflammation versus normal regions. Among patients with DNA content abnormality, cancer progressors exhibited increased plasma cell clustering adjacent to abnormal epithelium compared to non-progressors. Finally, a logistic regression model was developed that integrated molecular, immune ecological, and epithelial morphology features for cancer risk stratification. The integrated risk classification model stratified DNA content abnormal patients into high- and low-risk groups that corresponded with progression and patient survival. Overall, BEACON spatially integrates molecular abnormality with immune ecology to stratify BE patients by cancer progression risk using routine pathology images.

papers.title_zh: Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex strain discordance among people with tuberculosis and a history of household contact: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.title_en: Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex strain discordance among people with tuberculosis and a history of household contact: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Yates TA, Chipinduro M, Aldridge RW, Khozoee B, Winter JR, Tanser F, Abubakar I, Kranzer K et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Institute of Health Informatics, University College London, London, UK; Institute of Infection, Immunity and Transplanta…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis disease clusters within households, but the proportion of disease among household contacts that results from recent within-household transmission remains unclear. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex strain discordance among pairs of individuals with tuberculosis and a history of household contact, and the proportion of all tuberculosis disease attributable to recent household transmission. METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we included empirical studies or systematic reviews published in English from Jan 1, 1985, to Jan 26, 2024, that described at least ten pairs of individuals with a history of household contact, in which both people had active tuberculosis and their isolates were strain-typed using RFLP, mycobacterial interspersed repetitive unit-variable-number tandem repeat, or whole-genome sequencing. We excluded studies that only collected data on residence for isolates of the same strain and studies that used preselection for both index and secondary cases. Searches of MEDLINE, Embase, Global Health, Web of Science, and POPLINE databases were updated on Jan 26, 2024. Titles and abstracts and then full texts were screened, and data were extracted independently, by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Summary data were extracted from published reports; when necessary, we contacted study authors, some of whom reanalysed data. The main outcome was the prevalence of strain discordance among pairs of individuals with tuberculosis and a history of household contact. Our main analyses excluded studies using 12-loci or 15-loci mycobacterial interspersed repetitive unit-variable-number tandem repeat and studies performed during tuberculosis outbreaks, as these were considered to be at high risk of bias. We used an inverse variance heterogeneity model applying a double-arcsine transformation to stabilise variance. The proportion of total variability due to between-study heterogeneity was estimated using I2. We estimated the proportion of all tuberculosis attributable to recent household transmission as the product of strain concordance and the proportion of all cases in the community with a history of household exposure to a putative index case, which we derived from external data. Sensitivity analyses assessed robustness to the choice of model and to varying assumptions about household size when estimating the attributable fraction. Our PROSPERO registration number was CRD42024504096. FINDINGS: The updated searches identified an additional 3735 unique records. Thirty studies from 18 countries met the inclusion criteria. Four studies were omitted from the meta-analysis because they were at high risk of bias. The remaining 26 studies comprised 1544 index-secondary patient pairs. A high proportion of total variability was due to between-study heterogeneity (I2 90·3, 95% CI 69·0-95·3%). The overall pooled estimate of the prevalence of strain discordance was 0·47 (95% CI 0·32-0·62). Pooled estimates differed by tuberculosis incidence: 0·30 (0·25-0·34) in low-incidence settings, 0·25 (0·15-0·36) in moderate-incidence settings, and 0·59 (0·41-0·76) in high-incidence settings (p=0·003). The median proportion of tuberculosis disease attributable to recent household transmission was 10·8% (range 1·4-21·1%). INTERPRETATION: Strain discordance is common, particularly in high-incidence settings. These findings suggest that recent household transmission makes a small contribution to the overall burden of tuberculosis disease. In this study, the number of household pairs and geographical diversity of the studies were strengths. Between-study heterogeneity limited precision. Our estimates of attributable fraction relied on external data. Strain discordance does not necessarily imply discordance in drug susceptibility. These results should motivate a greater focus on social protection and interrupting community transmission. FUNDING: None.

papers.authors_conclusion: MD2可能是PH中线粒体氧化应激的上游调控因子；抑制MD2通过激活AMPK/PPARγ轴、抑制NOX4介导的线粒体氧化应激来减轻肺动脉高压；靶向MD2可能是PH的新型治疗策略。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未报告任何样本量、效应量或统计值，疗效证据均为动物模型的替代终点（血流动力学、血管重构、右心室肥厚），无临床硬终点；“膜蛋白MD2抑制→胞内AMPK激活”的分子连接机制仅以“mechanistic studies demonstrated”带过，缺直接证据描述；人源证据仅为表达上调，未涉及遗传变异或功能验证；药物抑制的特异性与脱靶（TLR4通路免疫效应）及长期安全性未提及。信息不足处已如实标注。
papers.abstract_en: AIMS: Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a severe vascular disorder, is closely associated with chronic inflammatory states and oxidative stress. Myeloid differentiation protein 2 (MD2), a key co-receptor of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), is well established in mediating various inflammation-driven pathologies. However, its role in pulmonary hypertension and its potential involvement in oxidative stress regulation remain unclear. METHODS AND RESULTS: MD2 expression was upregulated in both PH patients and murine PH models. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of MD2 improved hemodynamic parameters, attenuated pulmonary vascular remodeling, and reduced right ventricular hypertrophy. MD2 inhibition significantly reduced mitochondrial oxidative stress in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that suppression of the membrane protein MD2 activated intracellular AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, leading to enhanced peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) activity. PPARγ, in turn, suppressed nuclear transcription of NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4), resulting in a marked reduction in mitochondrial oxidative stress. CONCLUSION: This study indicates that MD2 may act as an upstream regulator of mitochondrial oxidative stress in PH. Inhibition of MD2 attenuates pulmonary hypertension through activation of the AMPK/PPARγ axis, which suppresses NOX4 mediated mitochondrial oxidative stress. Targeting MD2 may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for PH.

papers.title_en: Faecalibacterium prausnitzii in the gut protects against acute lung injury in influenza through butyrate educated reparative CD4+T cells.
papers.authors: Mao Z, Wang L, Zhuo C, Huang M, Ni J, Liu C, Chen W, Bao J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Laboratory Medicine, the First Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, Hangzhou, Chin…
papers.authors_conclusion: 丁酸来源于肠道共生 Faecalibacterium prausnitzii，在流感感染期间通过调节 CD4+T 细胞内在脂质代谢维持肺组织稳态；Faecalibacterium prausnitzii 补充作为严重流感相关肺损伤的创新治疗策略具有转化潜力。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未报告人类与动物样本量、对照设置、效应量及统计值；人类部分主要为菌群丰度与疾病严重度的相关性观察，因果推断主要依赖小鼠模型；机制链条涉及多组学与敲除验证，但摘要缺少关键节点的定量与独立验证信息；将益生菌补充直接外推为临床治疗策略需临床试验支持。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Uncontrolled pneumonia induced by influenza virus infection results in severe lung pathology. Timely and proper tissue self-repair is critical to improve survival. This study aimed to identify probiotic strains that confer protection against acute lung injury induced by influenza virus infection and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Significant structural alterations in the gut microbiota were observed in influenza patients, characterized by a marked depletion in Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, whose abundance was negatively correlated with disease severity. In a murine model of influenza infection, oral administration of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and its culture supernatant markedly alleviated lung injury. Targeted metabolomic analysis identified butyrate as the principal metabolite produced by Faecalibacterium prausnitzii that mediates lung tissue protection. Single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed that butyrate promotes the differentiation of pulmonary CD4⁺T cells into a reparative phenotype with enhanced interleukin-22 (IL-22) production. Mechanistically, butyrate facilitates IL-22 secretion through monounsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis via a histone-acetylation-dependent NR4A1-SCD1 axis. Accumulated monounsaturated fatty acids further enhance mitochondrial activities, which are essential for robust IL-22 production. Utilizing an IL-22 knockout mouse model, we confirmed the indispensable protective role of IL-22 in this gut-lung axis during influenza infection. CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that butyrate, derived from intestinal commensal Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, plays a crucial role in maintaining pulmonary tissue homeostasis during influenza infection by modulating intrinsic lipid metabolism in CD4+T cells. This study underscores the promising translational potential of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii supplementation as an innovative therapeutic strategy for severe influenza-associated lung injury. Video Abstract.

papers.title_zh: PPE1 被鉴定为电压门控外膜孔蛋白，介导结核分枝杆菌金属载体分泌与异烟肼摄取，ppe1 突变与临床异烟肼耐药相关
papers.title_en: A voltage-gated porin PPE1 regulates secretion and drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.authors: Yadav M, C A NF, Mandal D, Shukla J, Sarkar B, Kumar Mahtha S, Chandramouli A, Prasad A et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Immunometabolism Laboratory, BRIC-National Institute of Immunology, New Delhi 110067, India.
papers.authors_conclusion: PPE1 是分枝杆菌膜通透性的关键决定因素，协调金属载体分泌与抗生素内流；本研究揭示了决定 Mtb 生理、毒力与药物敏感性的既往未被认识的机制，并提供潜在治疗干预靶点。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未给出任何效应量或统计值（GWAS 无 OR/CI/P，表型实验无倍数变化或 P 值），无法评估关联强度；GWAS 为相关性证据，人体因果未验证；'关键决定因素'的表述主要基于单一基因敲除的体外与小鼠表型；结果为选择性摘要式呈现，缺乏主要/次要终点框架（基础研究本无此设计）。与胸部肿瘤临床问题无直接衔接。
papers.abstract_en: Drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) remains a formidable clinical hurdle, compounded by the fact that the pathways by which antibiotics penetrate its multilayered cell envelope remain incompletely mapped. We identify PPE1 as a voltage-gated outer-membrane porin that mediates the secretion of kupyaphores while also facilitating the uptake of the frontline anti-tubercular drug isoniazid (INH). Genome-wide association analysis of 38,038 clinical isolates links ppe1 mutations with INH resistance, highlighting its clinical relevance. Consistent with this, the Mtb Δppe1 mutant shows increased tolerance to INH, accompanied by markedly reduced intracellular accumulation of INH compared with the wild-type strain. The Δppe1 strain exhibits attenuated infection, impaired growth, and reduced virulence in a murine infection model. Electron microscopy, molecular modeling, and single-channel electrophysiology reveal that PPE1 assembles into an unusual pentameric α-helical channel, distinct from classical β-barrel bacterial porins. Together, our findings identify PPE1 as a key determinant of mycobacterial membrane permeability that coordinates metallophore secretion and also antibiotic influx. This work uncovers a previously unrecognized mechanism governing Mtb physiology, virulence, and drug susceptibility, providing a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

papers.authors: Wang J, Feng Y, Shen Y, Gan X, Zhou S, Ye H, Sun X, Meng Q et al.

papers.authors_conclusion: 巨噬细胞YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB信号轴是肺动脉高压炎症与血管重构的关键决定因素，可作为该病的潜在生物标志物与治疗靶点。
papers.ai_note: 摘要通篇为定性表述，未给出任何效应量、组间差异幅度或统计学数值，无法评估效应大小与可重复性；人体部分仅为表达相关性描述，未说明样本量、对照组织与是否校正混杂；三种模型数据被合并概述为“有效减轻”，未区分各模型结果是否一致；缺氧上调Ythdc1并直接结合稳定Tigar mRNA的“直接结合”证据（如RIP/CLIP）在摘要中未呈现；机制链条（TIGAR非酶活性经152-161段结合TAK1激活NF-κB）与表型间的因果充分性需依赖敲除/回补实验细节，摘要信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Immune dysregulation is a pivotal driver of pulmonary hypertension (PH) pathogenesis, yet therapeutic targeting of inflammation has yielded limited clinical success. Although cytosolic RNA-binding proteins are known to regulate immune responses in PH, the specific role of the nuclear m⁶A reader YTHDC1 remains undefined. OBJECTIVES: To elucidate the function of macrophage YTHDC1 in orchestrating inflammatory vascular remodeling during PH. METHODS: Expression profiles of YTHDC1 and TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator (TIGAR) were evaluated in human and rodent PH specimens. The mechanistic and therapeutic roles of this axis were assessed using myeloid-specific knockout mice and pharmacological inhibitors (YL-5092, 5Z-7-oxozeaenol) across hypoxia-, SU5416/hypoxia-, and monocrotaline-induced PH models. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: In patients with idiopathic or connective tissue disease-associated PAH, YTHDC1 and TIGAR expression levels were elevated in pulmonary and circulating macrophages, correlating with disease severity. In murine models, myeloid-specific deletion of Ythdc1 or Tigar conferred profound protection against hypoxia- and SU5416/hypoxia-induced PH. Mechanistically, hypoxia upregulated Ythdc1, which directly bound and stabilized Tigar mRNA. The subsequent accumulation of Tigar protein operated non-enzymatically via a specific domain (residues 152-161) to interact with Tak1, thereby activating the NF-κB cascade, augmenting pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and driving pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell proliferation. Pharmacological inhibition of YTHDC1 (YL-5092) or disruption of the TIGAR-TAK1 interaction (5Z-7-oxozeaenol) effectively attenuated vascular inflammation and mitigated PH progression in diverse rodent models. CONCLUSIONS: The macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB signaling axis acts as a critical determinant of inflammation and vascular remodeling in PH, representing a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for this disease.

papers.title_zh: Heterogeneous contributions of APOBEC3 deaminases to substitution and indel mutagenesis in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.title_en: Heterogeneous contributions of APOBEC3 deaminases to substitution and indel mutagenesis in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Striepen J, Culibrk L, Dananberg A, Rozowsky JS, Petljak M, Maciejowski J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Molecular Biology Program, Sloan Kettering Institute, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York, NY 10065, USA.
papers.abstract_en: APOBEC3 cytosine deaminases are major sources of cancer mutations. In lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), APOBEC3 activity drives tumor evolution and therapy resistance, nominating these enzymes as therapeutic targets. Although APOBEC3A drives most APOBEC3-associated mutational signature burden across cancers, the relative contributions of individual paralogs in LUAD remain unclear. Here, we define the roles of endogenously misregulated APOBEC3 deaminases using CRISPR-Cas9 knockouts and whole-genome sequencing of 197 long-term propagated single-cell clones. APOBEC3 mutagenesis falls into three patterns, driven predominantly by APOBEC3A, by both APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B, or minimal despite detectable enzyme expression. Commonly used surrogate measures, including mRNA and protein levels and in vitro deaminase activity, do not predict these contributions. We also provide the first causal evidence that endogenous APOBEC3A generates the indel signature InD9a, linking it to uracil excision following cytosine deamination. These heterogeneous contributions highlight the need for biomarkers that resolve individual APOBEC3 activities to guide therapeutic targeting.

papers.title_zh: Short-time deep-inspiratory breath-hold pulmonary perfusion SPECT/CT in interstitial pneumonia: a vascular dimension that stratifies risk independently of the GAP score.
papers.title_en: Short-time deep-inspiratory breath-hold pulmonary perfusion SPECT/CT in interstitial pneumonia: a vascular dimension that stratifies risk independently of the GAP score.
papers.authors: Fukushima Y, Yodogawa K, Nakaoka Y, Honda Y, Harashina S, Asano K, Hayashi H, Kumita S et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiology, Nippon Medical School, 1-1-5 Sendagi, Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo, 113-8603, Japan.
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Risk in interstitial pneumonia (IP) is assessed routinely by the Gender-Age-Physiology (GAP) score from pulmonary function and the tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) on echocardiography. This study evaluated whether the percent perfusion defect (%PPD) on short-time deep-inspiratory breath-hold (STDIBH) pulmonary perfusion SPECT/CT carries prognostic information that neither captures. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ninety-one consecutive patients with IP who underwent STDIBH perfusion SPECT/CT between 2012 and 2023 were analyzed retrospectively. The primary endpoint was a composite major adverse event (MAE) of all-cause death, acute exacerbation of IP, respiratory-failure hospitalization, and initiation of home oxygen therapy. Association was assessed by Cox regression and discrimination by censoring-weighted time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. RESULTS: MAE occurred in 66 of 91 patients (72.5%) over a median follow-up of 45.9 months. %PPD was associated with MAE after adjustment for the GAP score and antifibrotic therapy (adjusted hazard ratio 1.2304 per 10 percentage points, 95% CI 1.0568-1.4325; P = 0.008), and, in exploratory analyses, for TRPG and the GAP score together (1.2058, 1.0314-1.4096; P = 0.019). It showed no significant correlation with TRPG (Spearman r = 0.164; P = 0.140). Time-dependent discrimination did not differ significantly between %PPD and the GAP score at 6, 12, and 24 months, and adding %PPD to the GAP score changed the Harrell C-index from 0.692 to 0.719 (difference 0.027, 95% CI - 0.009 to 0.107). %PPD was obtained in all 91 patients and the GAP score in 68 (74.7%). CONCLUSION: In IP, %PPD measures a dimension of risk that the GAP score does not capture, and exploratory analyses suggest that echocardiography does not capture it either. %PPD is obtainable when the GAP score is not. Its discrimination did not differ significantly from that of the GAP score, and adding it to the GAP score did not significantly improve discrimination.

papers.title_zh: PRDM16在肺成纤维细胞中通过NuRD介导的表观遗传重塑抑制肺纤维化
papers.title_en: PRDM16 attenuates pulmonary fibrosis through NuRD-mediated epigenetic remodeling in lung fibroblasts.
papers.authors: Wang J, Li J, Shang B, Feng X, Wang W, Han L, Zhong C, Liu X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: State Key Laboratory of Medicinal Chemical Biology, Tianjin Key Laboratory of Protein Science, and College of Life Scien…
papers.authors_conclusion: PRDM16在肺纤维化过程中维持表观基因组稳态具有关键作用，并提示其作为IPF有前景治疗靶点的潜力。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未报告样本量、效应量和统计值；“治疗靶点”主要由表达关联、敲除/过表达表型及体外机制外推，缺少临床前给药、安全性和临床验证信息；PRDM16ΔPR-ZF1片段与全长PRDM16的生物学等效性及生理相关性信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, progressive, and fatal fibrotic lung disease with a poor prognosis. While epigenetic regulation is increasingly recognized as a key driver of fibrogenesis, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unclear. In this study, we identify PR domain-containing protein 16 (PRDM16) as a critical epigenetic repressor of profibrotic gene transcription. PRDM16 expression is significantly downregulated in lungs of IPF patients, in TGF-β1-activated fibroblasts, and in bleomycin (BLM)-induced mouse models. Functional analyses demonstrate that fibroblast-specific Prdm16 deletion promotes the progression of pulmonary fibrosis following BLM treatment. In contrast, overexpression of full-length PRDM16 or its truncated variant (PRDM16ΔPR-ZF1) attenuates the fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, thereby mitigating BLM-induced fibrotic phenotypes. Mechanistically, PRDM16 binds to the promoters of TGF-β target genes and recruits the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex to remove H3K27ac, resulting in silencing of profibrotic transcriptional programs. Collectively, our findings reveal a pivotal role for PRDM16 in maintaining epigenomic homeostasis during pulmonary fibrosis and underscore its potential as a promising therapeutic target for IPF.

papers.title_zh: SIRPγ在结核性胸腔积液中通过代谢-表观遗传重编程促进CD8⁺ T细胞耗竭
papers.title_en: SIRPγ promotes CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion via metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming in tuberculous pleural effusion.
papers.authors: Yang Y, Xue Q, Wang S, Peng W, Ye L, Yang B, Wang Z, Xiang X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Sci…
papers.authors_conclusion: SIRPγ是TPE中CD8⁺ T细胞耗竭的调节因子，并可能作为TPE诊断的预测生物标志物。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未给出样本量、效应量、P值或诊断准确性指标；将机制相关性与“诊断预测生物标志物”相连缺乏诊断研究数据支撑；TPE与非TPE对照的构成及混杂控制不明；因果性机制表述需谨慎。
papers.abstract_en: Previous studies have shown that signal regulatory protein γ (SIRPγ) is an important regulatory factor for T cell function. However, its expression and biological role in tuberculous pleural effusion (TPE) remain unknown. In this study, we find that the level of SIRPγ is significantly upregulated in TPE compared to non-TPE. Furthermore, we demonstrate SIRPγ involvement in TPE pathogenesis through the induction of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, SIRPγ interacts with CD47 to activate the phosphatidylinositol 3/kinase-protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) pathway, leading to the upregulation of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) and the enhancement of serine metabolism. Serine, in turn, facilitates S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-dependent trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) epigenetic modification at the NFATC2 locus. This modification, in coordination with TCR-induced calcium signaling, promotes NFATC2 activation, ultimately driving the expression of exhaustion-associated transcription factors and immunosuppressive receptors. Together, our findings identify SIRPγ as a regulator of CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion in TPE and suggest its potential as a predictive biomarker for TPE diagnosis.

papers.title_en: Sputum microplastic concentrations and their association with underweight in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: first human evidence combined with integrated network toxicology analysis.
papers.authors: Liu S, Lin D, Yang X, Zhu W, Zheng H, Yang Z, Dong R, Lin Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Clinical Nutrition, the First Affiliated Hospital of Xiamen University, School of Medicine, Xiamen Univers…

papers.ai_note: 横断面设计不能推断时序与因果，暴露与结局同时测量；样本量仅40例、低体重事件12例，报告OR 4.324/4.497却未给出95%CI，估计极不稳定，且“非线性”关联的函数形式与切点未描述；低体重判定标准、微塑料定量单位与检测限未在摘要中给出；中介分析在如此样本量下效能不足，结果只能视为假设；网络毒理学属计算预测，不构成机制证据，摘要中“炎症与脂肪细胞分化通路”不应被读作实证发现；摘要未预设或标注主要终点，主要结论建立在多个探索性分析之上；未报告多重比较校正（除富集分析外）与混杂因素清单
papers.abstract_en: Weight loss is a prevalent symptom in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Nevertheless, the role of microplastics (MPs) in this process remains poorly understood, and the underlying mechanisms are still unknown. We measured 13 MPs types by pyrolysis-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry in sputum from 40 COPD patients. Body composition was assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis. A hypothesis-generating network toxicology analysis explored the potential molecular mechanisms linking MPs exposure to alterations of body composition in COPD. Of the 40 participants, 12 (30.0%) were classified as underweight. Disease stage, nutritional status, and inflammatory indicators did not differ significantly between the two groups. Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) was detected in 97.5% of samples and showed the highest median concentration. PVC and total MPs showed non-linear positive associations with the odds of underweight in COPD, with fully adjusted odds ratios of 4.324 and 4.497. Sensitivity analyses also acquired the similar results. Higher PVC and total MPs were associated with reduced fat mass (P < 0.05), and linear regression models adjusted for all covariables showed similar negative associations. Exploratory mediation analysis showed that after adjustment for fat mass, the negative association between PVC exposure and body mass index (BMI) was no longer observed, suggesting that this association may be explained by reduced fat mass. Using the low-molecular-weight constituents of PVC and its additives (vinyl chloride monomer and phthalates) as the exposure sources, hypothesis-generating network toxicology analysis identified 84 targets shared with COPD and weight loss, enriched in inflammatory and adipocyte-differentiation signaling (adjusted P = 8.4 × 10⁻15 and 2.1 × 10⁻10). In conclusion, sputum MPs exposure was associated with higher odds of underweight and with lower fat mass in COPD patients. Chemicals-driven inflammatory signaling and impaired adipocyte differentiation may be involved in MPs-associated weight loss in COPD, which needs to be verified by experimental evidences.

papers.title_zh: KEYNOTE-867: A Phase III, Randomized, Double-Blind Study of Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy With Pembrolizumab for Unresected Stage I or II Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.title_en: KEYNOTE-867: A Phase III, Randomized, Double-Blind Study of Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy With Pembrolizumab for Unresected Stage I or II Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Jabbour SK, Sótér S, Eaton M, Gálffy G, Kowalski D, Hata A, Valdivia A, Frost N et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiation Oncology, Rutgers Cancer Institute, Rutgers University, New Brunswick, NJ.
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is standard of care for inoperable stage I or II non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). KEYNOTE-867 (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03924869) evaluated the addition of pembrolizumab to SBRT in participants diagnosed with stage I or II NSCLC that was inoperable or in participants who refused surgery. METHODS: Adults with untreated, stage I or II (T1 to limited T3, N0, M0) NSCLC (AJCC 8th edition) that was inoperable, or adults who refused surgery, were randomly assigned 1:1 to thoracic SBRT to primary tumors for ≤2 weeks concomitantly with pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo once every 3 weeks for ≤17 cycles. The primary end point was event-free survival (EFS) by blinded independent central review. RESULTS: A total of 448 participants were randomly assigned to SBRT plus pembrolizumab (n = 227) or SBRT plus placebo (n = 221). The median time from random assignment to the data cutoff date (June 11, 2024) for the prespecified first interim analysis was 20.6 (range, 1.3-56.8) months. The median EFS (95% CI) was 31.2 (22.5 to 39.1) months and 28.3 (19.8 to 33.1) months for the pembrolizumab and placebo arms, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.69 to 1.24]; P = .2932). Among participants who received ≥1 dose of study treatment, grade 3-5 treatment-related adverse events (AEs) occurred in 46/226 (20.4%) participants in the pembrolizumab arm and 8/218 (3.7%) participants in the placebo arm. There were five treatment-related deaths all of which occurred in the pembrolizumab arm (2.2%). CONCLUSION: The addition of pembrolizumab to SBRT did not improve EFS and was associated with a higher incidence of treatment-related AEs compared with SBRT alone in participants with inoperable stage I or II NSCLC. Based on the benefit-risk profile, the KEYNOTE-867 trial was prematurely stopped, and all study treatment was discontinued.

papers.study_type: 系统评价（非荟萃分析）· 对I–IV期融合阳性NSCLC靶向治疗试验的方案、发表文献与注册平台更新进行安全性报告质量评估
