papers.title_zh: 融合阳性NSCLC靶向治疗试验中静脉血栓栓塞安全性报告的系统评价：事件判定与方案层面条款高度异质、报告零散
papers.title_en: Venous Thromboembolism Reporting in Fusion-Positive NSCLC Treated with Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Systematic Review of Safety Reporting and Protocol-Level Provisions in Phase I-IV Clinical Trials.
papers.authors: Citarella F, Fiorenti M, Fragale C, Sini C, Passiglia F, Cortellini A, Bronte G
papers.affiliation_highlight: Thoracic Department, Division of Thoracic Medical Oncology, Istituto Nazionale Tumori "Fondazione G.
papers.authors_conclusion: 在融合阳性NSCLC试验中，事件判定与报告方式的异质性——而非血栓栓塞事件的真实稀缺——是现有证据的主要局限；提高安全性报告标准化并整合注册平台与发表数据，可改善未来研究的完整性、可比性与可解释性
papers.ai_note: 本研究未汇总VTE发生率，无法区分“报告不足”与“事件本身少见”，作者“异质性而非真实稀缺”的结论属推断而非本研究实测；仅描述报告条目的计数，未按试验规模/暴露人时加权，亦未评估各来源间一致性（如kappa）；“>40%”“近60%”为文字性比例，无置信区间与统计检验；检索策略、筛选流程、偏倚评估工具及是否预设方案（PROSPERO）在摘要中均信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant complication in patients with fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the completeness and consistency of thromboembolic safety reporting in clinical trials of tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC. Protocols, publications, and online trial registry updates were systematically reviewed to assess thromboembolic event ascertainment, reporting practices, protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions, and VTE-related eligibility criteria. RESULTS: A total of 108 reporting sources from 61 study entries (58 unique trials) were reviewed. Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis were the predominant reported events. VTE-related information was highly fragmented across reporting sources: 14 study entries reported events exclusively through full-text publications, 19 exclusively through online trial updates, and 15 through both sources. Study protocols rarely prespecified thromboembolic events as dedicated safety outcomes, more commonly addressing them in eligibility criteria, anticoagulant therapy provisions, or differential diagnosis guidance. More than 40% of study entries lacked protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions and nearly 60% lacked VTE-related eligibility restrictions. Marked heterogeneity was observed in event definitions, reporting practices, safety ascertainment, and observation periods. CONCLUSIONS: In fusion-positive NSCLC trials, heterogeneity in event ascertainment and reporting, rather than a true scarcity of thromboembolic events, represents a major limitation of the available evidence. Greater standardization of safety reporting and integration of trial registry and publication data may improve the completeness, comparability, and interpretability of future studies.

papers.title_zh: Exercise Training During Neoadjuvant Treatment for Gastroesophageal Cancer and Tumor Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.title_en: Exercise Training During Neoadjuvant Treatment for Gastroesophageal Cancer and Tumor Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.authors: Simonsen C, de Heer P, Thomsen SN, Krabek R, Thorsen-Streit S, Printz Lyngbæk MP, Sundberg A, Hjort ASK et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Centre for Physical Activity Research, Copenhagen University Hospital, Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen, Denmark.
papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Physical deterioration and disease progression during neoadjuvant treatment can preclude tumor surgery in patients with gastroesophageal cancer. Whether preoperative exercise training can increase the probability of undergoing tumor surgery remains unknown. OBJECTIVE: To compare exercise training with usual care on the likelihood of not undergoing tumor surgery with curative intent after neoadjuvant treatment for gastroesophageal cancer. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: PRESET-RCT was a single-blinded, parallel-group, 2-arm, superiority randomized clinical trial. Patients with gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma scheduled to undergo treatment with curative intent, including neoadjuvant treatment, and with no contraindication to exercise training were eligible. Participants were enrolled at University Hospital Copenhagen, Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen, Denmark, from August 16, 2018, to September 23, 2022, with final follow-up on October 22, 2024. Data analysis was performed from March 2023 to May 2025. INTERVENTION: The participants were randomized 1:1 to preoperative exercise training from diagnosis until tumor surgery or control. The intervention consisted of twice-weekly concurrent aerobic exercise and resistance training. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was not undergoing tumor surgery with curative intent. The secondary outcomes were treatment tolerance and overall survival. RESULTS: In total, 207 participants (73.7%) were randomized and 202 were included in the modified intention-to-treat analyses (mean [SD] age, 65.3 [8.5] years; 161 [78.9%] male; 170 [83.3%] with gastroesophageal junction cancer), with 101 randomized to each group. In the exercise group, 10 (9.9%) did not undergo tumor surgery with curative intent compared with 8 (7.9%) in the control group (odds ratio, 1.28; 95% CI, 0.48-3.38; P = .62). There were no between-group differences in permanent discontinuation of neoadjuvant treatment (odds ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.38-1.72) or postoperative complications (odds ratio, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.61-2.20). The overall survival rates at 3 years for the exercise and control group were 51.0% and 65.0%, respectively (hazard ratio, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.02-2.45). CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, preoperative exercise training did not increase the likelihood of undergoing tumor surgery for patients with gastroesophageal cancer. The findings do not support the use of exercise training during neoadjuvant treatment to improve surgical outcomes, and further research is needed to determine its effects on long-term outcomes. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03490565.

papers.title_zh: Effectiveness of the mRNA-1345 Vaccine Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus in US Veterans.
papers.title_en: Effectiveness of the mRNA-1345 Vaccine Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus in US Veterans.
papers.authors: Bui DP, Yan L, Li Y, Rajeevan N, Vergun R, Sriskantharajah V, Hynes DM, Berry K et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Veterans Affairs (VA) Portland Health Care System, Portland, Oregon.
papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: In clinical trials, the messenger RNA (mRNA)-1345 vaccine provided protection against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) illness. Data on mRNA-1345 effectiveness in broader patient populations are needed. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effectiveness of mRNA-1345 vaccination during a single respiratory illness season. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used a target trial emulation framework to assess veterans 50 years and older receiving care in the Veterans Health Administration. Eligible vaccine recipients were matched with up to 4 unvaccinated individuals in 4 monthly, nested, sequential trials from October 1, 2025, to January 31, 2026. Outcomes were ascertained through May 31, 2026, or 24 weeks. EXPOSURE: A single dose of mRNA-1345 RSV vaccine vs no RSV vaccination. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was any positive RSV test result from day 14 after the matched index date. Secondary outcomes included RSV-associated emergency department (ED) or urgent care (UC) encounters and RSV-associated hospitalizations. Vaccine effectiveness was estimated as 100 × (1 - risk ratio). A sensitivity analysis comparing veterans who received same-day mRNA-1345 and influenza vaccination to influenza vaccination alone (active comparator arm) was performed to explore potential bias from differences in health care-seeking behavior and outcome ascertainment between comparator groups. RESULTS: A total of 74 926 vaccinated veterans were matched to 286 425 unique control individuals, weighted to represent 74 926 individuals, for a total of 149 852 study participants (median [IQR] age, 73.0 [63.3-78.6] years; 136 756 [91.3%] male). During a median (IQR) follow-up of 160 (130-168) days, estimated vaccine effectiveness was 60.3% (95% CI, 49.0%-70.4%) against any documented infection, 60.2% (95% CI, 47.2%-71.5%) against RSV-associated ED or UC encounters, and 81.8% (95% CI, 58.1%-99.9%) against RSV-associated hospitalizations. Estimated effectiveness against documented infections decreased with increasing age, from 82.9% (95% CI, 64.0%-96.7%) in the 50- to 59-year age group to 28.6% (95% CI, -12.0% to 60.4%) in the 80-year or older age group. With an active comparator arm, estimated effectiveness was 67.1% (95% CI, 48.9%-82.6%) against documented RSV infections, 69.5% (95% CI, 49.7%-85.4%) against RSV-associated ED and UC encounters, and 86.9% (95% CI, 56.5%-100.0%) against RSV-associated hospitalizations. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study using a target trial emulation of mRNA-1345 vaccine effectiveness during 24 weeks, vaccination was associated with protection against RSV illness and associated health care use in adults 50 years and older. Comparative effectiveness studies are needed to determine the relative benefits of available RSV vaccine products.

papers.title_zh: Effect of telemonitoring on adherence to inhalation therapy and pulmonary exacerbations in people with cystic fibrosis (conneCT CF): a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
papers.title_en: Effect of telemonitoring on adherence to inhalation therapy and pulmonary exacerbations in people with cystic fibrosis (conneCT CF): a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
papers.authors: Thee S, Stahl M, Sutharsan S, Fischer R, Ballmann M, Straßburg S, Lauer F, Weitzel J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pediatric Respiratory Medicine, Immunology and Critical Care Medicine, Division of Cystic Fibrosis, Charit…
papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Recurrent pulmonary exacerbations contribute substantially to lung function decline in people with cystic fibrosis (CF). Inhalation therapies are a cornerstone of standard of care, yet adherence to inhalation therapies is variable and data on the relationship between adherence and pulmonary exacerbations remain limited. OBJECTIVES: To assess the impact of multimodal telemonitoring and coaching on adherence and pulmonary exacerbations in people with CF. METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter, unblinded, randomized, controlled trial people with CF aged ≥12 years were randomized (1:1) to either standard of care or an intervention involving continuous objective home monitoring of inhalation adherence, weekly home spirometry, a self-management app, professional telephone coaching, and optional video conferencing over 18 months. The primary endpoint was time to first pulmonary exacerbation. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: 296 participants were included with a mean age of 31.3 (SD 10.8) years, 54.1% females, mean FEV1% predicted of 70.2% (SD 24.7), 52.7% chronically infected with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and 85.1% on triple CFTR modulator therapy. Baseline adherence was higher in the intervention group (58.1%) than in the control group (44.0%) and remained higher throughout the study (last 6 months: 49.2% vs. 32.6%). Time to first exacerbation did not differ between groups. However, across all participants, a 10% increase in adherence correlated with a 9% reduction in pulmonary exacerbation risk. Participants with FEV1<40% had a 2.4-fold higher risk of exacerbations. CONCLUSION: Multimodal telemedicine improved inhalation therapy adherence. The association between higher adherence and reduced exacerbations highlights the ongoing importance of inhalation therapy in CF, even with widespread CFTR modulator use. Clinical trial registered with German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00024642).

papers.title_en: EZH2 lactylation: a key epigenetic regulator and potential therapeutic target for sepsis-associated lung injury.
papers.authors: Liu J, Zhao Y, Zhang X, Guo Y, Yu D, Song X, Wang Q, Tian J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Critical Care Medicine, the Second Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University, Harbin 150086, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: EZH2乳酸化通过CITED2/NF-κB轴加重SALI，提示该表观遗传修饰是有前景的治疗靶点，为开发位点特异性抑制剂治疗SALI开辟了新的药理学途径。
papers.ai_note: 标题与结论直接使用“关键表观调控因子”“有前景的治疗靶点”等表述，强于摘要所提供的证据层级。临床部分仅为血清乳酸与炎症指标、肺损伤严重程度的相关性观察，不能支持因果关系，亦无EZH2乳酸化的人体直接检测数据；核心机制结论完全来自小鼠与内皮细胞模型，向ICU人群外推需谨慎。摘要缺乏任何效应量、置信区间与P值，无法判断相关强度及干预效应大小。未报告以死亡、无机械通气天数等患者重要结局为终点的数据。全身性抑制乳酸生成或EZH2乳酸化的可及性与安全性未讨论。
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Sepsis-associated lung injury (SALI) is a lethal infection-induced complication with high mortality and limited targeted therapies. Dysregulated lactate metabolism is closely linked to SALI, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to investigate the role and molecular mechanism of EZH2 (Enhancer of zeste homolog 2) lactylation in SALI development, thereby uncovering a novel exploitable therapeutic target. METHODS: A total of 209 ICU patients were enrolled and divided into the SALI group (n = 104) and non-SALI group (n = 105) to detect serum lactate levels. Cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) mouse models and endothelial cell-specific Ezh2 knockout (Ezh2ECKO) mouse models were established. Combined with lactate and lactate dehydrogenase inhibitor intervention, multi-omics analysis, ChIP, qPCR, immunofluorescence and other techniques were used in the study. RESULTS: Serum lactate levels were significantly elevated in patients with SALI and model mice, and lung tissue lactate levels were elevated in model mice. Lactate levels were positively associated with inflammatory markers and lung injury severity. EZH2 underwent site-specific lactylation at lysine 30 and 406 (EZH2 K30/K406la) in SALI, which was enhanced with disease progression. Inhibiting lactate production or EZH2 lactylation improved pulmonary function, reduced inflammatory infiltration and pathological lung tissue damage. EZH2 K30/K406la downregulated CITED2 (CBP-p300 interacting transactivator with Glu/Asp-rich carboxy-terminal domain 2) expression by reducing its occupancy at the CITED2 promoter and altering CITED2 promoter activity, relieving the inhibition of the NF-κB (Nuclear Factor-kappa B) pathway and exacerbating inflammatory responses and endothelial dysfunction. CONCLUSION: EZH2 lactylation aggravates SALI via the CITED2/NF-κB axis, highlighting this epigenetic modification as a promising therapeutic target that opens a new pharmacological avenue for developing site-specific inhibitors to combat SALI.

papers.title_zh: Noninvasive Detection and Subtyping of Esophageal Cancer by Circulating Cell-Free mtDNA Fragmentomics: A Multi-Center Validation Study.
papers.title_en: Noninvasive Detection and Subtyping of Esophageal Cancer by Circulating Cell-Free mtDNA Fragmentomics: A Multi-Center Validation Study.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Yang W, Li Y, Wang S, Li X, Peng F, Dang M, Zhang H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: State Key Laboratory of Holistic Integrative Management of Gastrointestinal Cancers and Department of Physiology and Pat…
papers.abstract_en: Esophageal cancer (EC) is highly lethal due to late diagnosis, and accurate non-invasive tools for early detection and subtyping remain lacking. Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) fragmentomics offers a promising biomarker source. In this large multi-center study enrolling 1,260 participants spanning healthy control (HC), benign esophageal diseases (BED), precancerous lesions and EC patients, we developed two machine learning models based on plasma ccf-mtDNA fragmentomic profiles: an EC detection (ED) model and a pathological subtyping prediction (PSP) model. The ED model achieved an AUC of 0.9706 (EC vs. non-EC) in the training cohort, with high performance in internal (0.9762), external (0.9748), and Chinese minority (0.9668, Uyghur and Kazakh) validation cohorts. At the optimal cut-off, it yielded 92.16% sensitivity for stage I EC in the combined validation cohort and correctly identified 93.10% of early EC cases missed by preoperative biopsy. It also discriminated high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia from non-EC with an AUC of 0.9597. The PSP model distinguished ESCC from EAC with 89.71% accuracy, improving to 90.74% after integrating key clinical parameters. In summary, ccf-mtDNA fragmentomics provides a robust, non-invasive platform for early EC detection, precancerous risk stratification, and histological subtyping, demonstrating strong potential to transform clinical management.

papers.title_zh: Sintilimab plus R-CHOP versus DA-EPOCH-R as first-line therapy for primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma: a real-world comparative cohort study.
papers.title_en: Sintilimab plus R-CHOP versus DA-EPOCH-R as first-line therapy for primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma: a real-world comparative cohort study.
papers.authors: Liu Z, Ren J, Jiang K, Guan H, Zhao X
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Lymphoma, the Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University, Qingdao, China.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma (PMBCL) is a highly curable lymphoma in which first-line therapy must balance durable disease control with acute and late treatment toxicity. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 98 patients with newly diagnosed PMBCL who received sintilimab plus R-CHOP (group 1, n = 42) or DA-EPOCH-R (group 2, n = 56). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), and secondary endpoints included complete metabolic response (CMR) and safety. Propensity-score matching (PSM) and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for baseline imbalances. Molecular profiling was performed in 75 diagnostic samples to characterize immune-escape features, including 9p24.1 alterations and PD-L1/PD-L2 expression. RESULTS: Sintilimab plus R-CHOP produced numerically comparable response and PFS outcomes to DA-EPOCH-R, although equivalence or non-inferiority cannot be inferred from this retrospective, event-limited cohort. CMR rates were 85.7% versus 83.9% before matching (Fisher P = 1.000) and 83.3% versus 80.6% after PSM (P = 1.000; 36 pairs). Estimated 24-, 36-, and 60-month PFS rates were 81.0% versus 83.9% before matching (HR 1.19, 95% CI 0.46-3.09; log-rank P = 0.716), 83.3% versus 80.6% after matching (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.28-2.51; P = 0.759), and 83.9% versus 84.6% after IPTW (HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.39-2.76; robust P = 0.942), respectively. These estimates were based on 17 PFS events in the full cohort and 13 events after matching. Grade 3-4 neutropenia was less frequent with sintilimab plus R-CHOP before matching (38.1% versus 66.1%; P = 0.008) and remained lower after matching (30.6% versus 61.1%; P = 0.017). In 75 profiled diagnostic samples, group-level molecular data confirmed the expected immune-escape architecture of PMBCL and showed broadly similar distributions of 9p24.1 alterations and PD-L1/PD-L2 expression between treatment groups. CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort, sintilimab plus R-CHOP produced overlapping response and PFS estimates relative to DA-EPOCH-R, together with less grade 3-4 neutropenia. The study cannot establish equivalence, non-inferiority, treatment replacement, or radiotherapy omission. These findings support the biological rationale for integrating PD-1 blockade into frontline chemoimmunotherapy and highlight the need for prospective studies to define its role within PET-adapted and immune-driven treatment strategies for PMBCL.

papers.title_zh: Lactate-Induced PPP1R1B Upregulation Drives Resistance to Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy in NSCLC via IRF3 Dephosphorylation.
papers.title_en: Lactate-Induced PPP1R1B Upregulation Drives Resistance to Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy in NSCLC via IRF3 Dephosphorylation.
papers.authors: Jiang Z, Yuan J, Li G, Wang X, Zhao J, Li M, Zhang Y, Liu M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: State Key Laboratory of Molecular Oncology, National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer/Cancer H…
papers.abstract_en: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has improved clinical outcomes in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve durable responses, and the mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified protein phosphatase 1 regulatory inhibitor subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a metabolic driver of immunotherapy resistance in NSCLC through RNA sequencing of tumors with differential responses to neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy. PPP1R1B was significantly upregulated in non-responders and correlated with poor prognosis in NSCLC patients. Mechanistically, PPP1R1B directly interacted with IRF3 through the Arg29 residue and promoted dephosphorylation of IRF3 at Ser396, thereby suppressing IRF3 activation and downstream interferon-β (IFN-β) signaling. PPP1R1B-mediated inhibition of IFN-β signaling reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and impaired antitumor immunity, ultimately conferring resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in vivo. Blockade of IFN-β signaling abrogated the antitumor effects induced by PPP1R1B depletion, supporting an immune-dependent mechanism. Notably, tumors resistant to neoadjuvant immunotherapy exhibited impaired oxidative phosphorylation and excessive lactate accumulation. Lactate induced PPP1R1B expression through NF-κB-dependent transcriptional activation, linking metabolic reprogramming to innate immune suppression. Collectively, our findings identify a lactate/NF-κB/PPP1R1B/IRF3 signaling axis that drives immune evasion and resistance to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in NSCLC, and nominate PPP1R1B as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming anti-PD-1 resistance.

papers.title_zh: Evaluation of Andes virus vaccine-derived human antibody for protection in Syrian hamsters: a passive transfer study using phase 1 trial sera.
papers.title_en: Evaluation of Andes virus vaccine-derived human antibody for protection in Syrian hamsters: a passive transfer study using phase 1 trial sera.
papers.authors: Hooper JW, Lesko S, Principe L, Josleyn M, Kwilas S, Norris S, Tomashek KM, Paulsen G et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Virology Division, United States Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases, Fort Detrick, MD, USA.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Andes virus (ANDV) causes severe hantavirus pulmonary syndrome and is uniquely capable of person-to-person transmission, with no licenced vaccines or therapeutics available. A Phase 1 trial (NCT03682107) demonstrated that an ANDV DNA vaccine targeting Gn/Gc envelope proteins elicits neutralising antibodies in humans. We evaluated whether these human antibodies protect against lethal disease in an animal model. METHODS: Day 197 sera from vaccinated human subjects were pooled, purified, and passively transferred to female Syrian hamsters one day prior to lethal ANDV challenge across two independent experiments. Controls included normal human IgG, PBS (negative controls), and SAB-400 (positive control). Neutralising antibody levels were quantified using pseudovirion neutralisation assays (PsVNA) and plaque reduction neutralisation tests (PRNT) to determine exploratory cutoff titres predicting survival. FINDINGS: Human antibodies from DNA-vaccinated subjects-unlike normal IgG-conferred significant protection against lethal ANDV challenge in both experiments. The exploratory cutoff titres predicting protection were determined to be 31-184 for PsVNA50 and 20-80 for PRNT50, depending on the analysis population and model parameters. INTERPRETATION: Vaccine-induced human antibodies are sufficient to protect against lethal ANDV infection in an established animal model. If confirmed, these results indicate that neutralising antibody titres could serve as a surrogate endpoint and correlate of protection for future hantavirus Gn/Gc-targeted vaccines. FUNDING: Defense Health Program and the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

papers.title_zh: Vitamin E Nanoemulsion Loaded Exosomes Attenuates Bleomycin-Induced Pulmonary Fibrosis by Inhibiting NLRP3-Mediated Pyroptosis and Fibrotic Signaling.
papers.title_en: Vitamin E Nanoemulsion Loaded Exosomes Attenuates Bleomycin-Induced Pulmonary Fibrosis by Inhibiting NLRP3-Mediated Pyroptosis and Fibrotic Signaling.
papers.authors: Elgohary R, Abdel-Hameed R, S Ahmed A, A Taha D, S Kishta M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Narcotics, Ergogenics and Poisons Department, Medical Research and Clinical Studies Institute, National Research Centre,…
papers.abstract_en: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of nano-formulated vitamin E combined with mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-derived exosomes in bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis. AD-MSCs were isolated, expanded, and characterized by spindle morphology with high CD105/CD73 and low CD34/CD45 expression. Exosomes isolated from these cells displayed typical spherical morphology (131 nm), high CD81/CD63/CD9 expression, and low CD14. Skin fibrosis was induced in rats by subcutaneous administration of bleomycin. Animals subsequently received free vitamin E, nano-formulated vitamin E, or exosomes loaded with nano-formulated vitamin E. The antifibrotic efficacy of these treatments was assessed using biochemical, molecular, histopathological, and immunohistochemical analyses. Vitamin E nanoemulsion (mean of 48 nm, PDI 0.221, zeta -27.6 mV) was successfully loaded into the exosomes (EE 86.3%, LE 19.8%), yielding stable vesicles (137 nm) with excellent cytocompatibility. The formulation markedly attenuated bleomycin-induced fibrotic injury by restoring redox balance, reduction of TNF-α and TGF-β1 and attenuated extracellular matrix remodeling by decreasing collagen I, α-SMA, MMP-2, and TIMP-1. Moreover, inhibition of the NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD pathway and IL-1β indicated suppression of pyroptosis. VEGFR2 expression was also reduced, accompanied by marked improvement in histopathological alterations. The combination therapy exerted pronounced anti-fibrotic effects through coordinated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-pyroptotic, anti-ECM-remodeling, and anti-angiogenic mechanisms.

papers.title_zh: Pleuroparenchymal abnormalities in cancer patients undergoing CTPA for suspected pulmonary embolism.
papers.title_en: Pleuroparenchymal abnormalities in cancer patients undergoing CTPA for suspected pulmonary embolism.
papers.authors: Allahham MF, Mustafa H, Faroun J, Amro AM, Allahham FM, Shrateh ON, Murphy D
papers.affiliation_highlight: Faculty of Medicine, Al-Quds University, Jerusalem, Palestine.
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To characterize pleuroparenchymal abnormalities identified on computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) in cancer patients investigated for suspected pulmonary embolism (PE) and to compare imaging findings between patients with and without confirmed PE. METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included 113 consecutive cancer patients who underwent CTPA for suspected acute PE between January 2022 and January 2026. Radiology reports and electronic medical records were reviewed for demographic data, malignancy type and stage, PE-related imaging characteristics, and pleural and pulmonary parenchymal abnormalities. Imaging findings were compared between PE-positive and PE-negative groups. An exploratory multivariable model with a restricted set of imaging predictors was constructed to limit overfitting, with correction for multiple comparisons and bootstrap-based internal validation. Exploratory subgroup analyses by malignancy type and disease burden were also performed. RESULTS: PE was confirmed in 32 patients (28.3%). The median age was 59 years (IQR, 51-65), and 42.5% were female. The highest PE prevalence was observed in gastrointestinal, gynecologic, and thoracic malignancies. At nominal testing, infarct-like wedge-shaped opacity was more frequent in PE-positive patients (12.5% vs. 1.2%; OR, 11.43; p = 0.022), whereas ground-glass opacity (15.6% vs. 35.8%; OR, 0.33; p = 0.041) and interstitial/septal change (3.1% vs. 25.9%; OR, 0.09; p = 0.007) were less frequent. None remained statistically significant after false-discovery-rate correction (q = 0.133, 0.166, and 0.082, respectively). The parsimonious model had an apparent AUROC of 0.707 and an optimism-adjusted AUROC of 0.699, with acceptable grouped calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.522). No exploratory cancer-subgroup comparison met q < 0.05. CONCLUSIONS: Pleuroparenchymal abnormalities are highly prevalent in cancer patients undergoing CTPA for suspected PE; however, most findings are nonspecific. Infarct-like wedge-shaped opacity generated the strongest exploratory PE-associated signal, but no individual imaging comparison survived multiplicity correction and model estimates remained imprecise. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title_zh: A CD68-expressing tissue-homing subset in peripheral CD8+ T cells predicts response to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer.
papers.title_en: A CD68-expressing tissue-homing subset in peripheral CD8+ T cells predicts response to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Huang J, Sun Z, Pei Y, Xu J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Laboratory Medicine, Infectious Diseases and Pathogen Biology Center, The First Hospital of Jilin Universi…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: T-cell function is regulated by immunometabolism, and lysosomes are signaling hubs. CD68 (LAMP4), traditionally regarded as a monocyte/macrophage marker, has been largely neglected in T cell biology. We aimed to assess the link between CD68 expression in T cells and anti-PD-1 response in lung cancer, and its potential as an early dynamic biomarker in peripheral blood CD8+ T cells. METHODS: We analyzed transcriptomic (GSE126044, GSE135222, GSE166449) and single-cell (GSE207422) data from anti-PD-1-treated lung cancer cohorts to identify lysosome related pathways and key genes, validated with peripheral blood CD8+ T cell data (GSE111414). Prospectively, we enrolled lung cancer patients receiving anti-PD-1 therapy, collecting peripheral blood at baseline and week 3. Flow cytometry measured CD68 in CD8+ T cells and subsets, assessing association with response, progression-free survival (PFS), and functional markers (granzyme B, perforin, Ki-67, CD69, IFN-γ, IL-1β). RESULTS: Responders showed enrichment of lysosome pathways and upregulation of 8 lysosome related genes including CD68, positively correlated with monocyte and T cell infiltration. Single-cell data linked CD68 expression in T cell to favorable response. After one cycle, the proportion of CD8+CD68+ T cells was lower in non-responders (P<0.05), with AUC 0.803 (P=0.044) and cutoff 1.015%, stratifying PFS (P=0.0225). CD68 was highest in naïve T cells at baseline, but decreased across subsets after treatment in non-responders (all P<0.01). Functionally, compared with CD8+CD68- T cells, CD8+CD68+ T cells exhibited lower expression of granzyme B and perforin but higher expression of Ki-67, CD69, IFN-γ, and IL-1β (all P<0.001), suggesting a CD8+ T cell state characterized by lower cytotoxicity and enhanced proliferative and cytokine producing capacities, accompanied by a tissue residency associated phenotype. CONCLUSION: CD8+CD68+ T cells exhibit lower cytotoxicity but greater proliferative and cytokine producing capacities, together with a tissue residency associated phenotype, suggesting a precursor-like state. Low CD68 expression in tumor-infiltrating T cells and the post-treatment reduction of CD68 expression in peripheral blood CD8+ T cells are associated with resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer. These findings suggest that CD8+CD68+ T cells may serve as a potential early dynamic immune biomarker for monitoring and assessing response to anti-PD-1 therapy in lung cancer.

papers.authors: Wagner J, Rajan D, Field SF, Betteridge E, Bellis K, Knoll M, Ng D, Teixeira D et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Wellcome Sanger Institute, Wellcome Genome Campus, Hinxton, Cambridge, CB10 1SA, UK.
papers.authors_conclusion: 杂交捕获富集为呼吸道病毒基因组测序提供了有效且可扩展的途径；成本降低与自动化可在不损害性能的前提下实施，支持其用于常规基因组监测与公共卫生应急准备。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未给出各流程的样本量、检出率、基因组覆盖度或完整性等定量指标，也未做统计学比较，“大致可比”“高效”等均为定性表述；以“约100拷贝仍可检出reads”作为灵敏度证据，但reads检出并不等于完整基因组回收，摘要未区分两者；合成对照难以代表真实临床基质的宿主核酸与病原载量分布；仅覆盖5种病毒，外推至其他呼吸道病原（含新发病原）需谨慎；未报告失败样本或假阴性情况。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sequencing respiratory virus genomes is essential for public health surveillance and research. Although shotgun metagenomics is pathogen agnostic, its sensitivity is limited by abundant off-target host nucleic acids. Hybridization bait capture overcomes this limitation by selectively enriching viral sequences prior to sequencing. METHODS: We evaluated three respiratory viral bait capture workflows (veSEQ, RVI-seq, and Illumina) to compare their performance and assess their suitability for scalable respiratory virus sequencing. Synthetic RNA controls and clinical samples containing SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, human parainfluenza virus, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were analysed. RESULTS: All three workflows demonstrated high efficiency, reproducibility and broadly comparable performance across respiratory viruses. Complete viral genomes were consistently recovered from samples containing 10,000 viral copies, while viral reads remained detectable at substantially lower viral loads, including approximately 100 copies. Workflow optimisation reduced reagent costs and enabled laboratory automation without compromising sequencing sensitivity. CONCLUSION: Hybridization bait capture provides an effective and scalable approach for respiratory virus genome sequencing. Cost reductions and automation can be implemented without compromising performance, supporting its use in routine genomic surveillance and public health preparedness.

papers.authors: Guasch-Vallés M, Ribes-Santolaria M, Eritja N, Scholtus A, Bech-Serra JJ, Torre-Gómez C, Pedraza N, Ferrezuelo F et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department de Ciències Mèdiques Bàsiques, Facultat de Medicina, Universitat de Lleida, Av.
papers.authors_conclusion: Scin 在转移过程中起重要作用，可能作为肿瘤侵袭性与转移潜能的候选生物标志物。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未给出任何样本量、效应值与统计量（仅用 significant/remarkably 等定性词），无法评估效应大小与把握度；功能证据仅来自小鼠模型与细胞系敲低，属相关性＋单一基因干预，不能确立因果与临床可用性；人体验证全部来自子宫内膜癌（TIF、组织芯片、血浆），与标题所指的肺结节场景并不对应，向胸部肿瘤的外推缺乏直接数据；敲低后 DTC 下降被描述为“程度较轻”，提示该表型可能为继发效应；血浆为回顾性设计，存在样本采集时相与混杂控制不明的问题；组织芯片配对分析未说明转移灶与原发灶数量及配对完整性。信息不足：未披露统计方法、多重比较校正与验证队列规模。
papers.abstract_en: The tumor microenvironment is a critical factor in understanding cancer progression and metastasis. In this context, isolating tumor interstitial fluid (TIF) is a powerful tool for detecting cancer biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In our study, we conducted a proteomic analysis of TIFs from metastatic lung nodules using a murine model. The TIFs from these lungs were enriched with actin-binding proteins, among other molecules. Notably, we identified Scinderin (Scin), an actin-binding protein secreted by tumor cells. Knockdown of Scin resulted in a significant decrease in the number and size of lung nodules, as well as a reduction, albeit to a lesser extent, in disseminated tumor cells (DTCs). Furthermore, silencing Scin inhibited cell and tumor growth in different cancer cell lines. In human tumors, Scin was detected in the tumor interstitial fluid (TIF) of endometrial cancer patients. Scin was expressed abundantly in serous endometrial carcinomas and in the secretory endometrium. Remarkably, a paired analysis using an endometrial cancer tissue-array revealed increased Scin expression in metastatic samples compared to their corresponding primary tumors. In addition, a retrospective study revealed that levels of Scin in plasma were significantly elevated in patients who developed metastases. These findings suggest that Scin plays a significant role in the metastatic process and may serve as a promising biomarker for tumor aggressiveness and metastatic potential.

papers.title_zh: Human nasal organoids sustain reproducible airway epithelial differentiation and influenza virus-host innate immune interaction.
papers.title_en: Human nasal organoids sustain reproducible airway epithelial differentiation and influenza virus-host innate immune interaction.
papers.authors: Jin S, Kim S, Kim M, Cha H, Chung S, Kim HJ
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Seoul National University Hospital, Seoul, Republic of Korea.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The cultures of human nasal epithelial cells (NECs) are good surrogate models for studying immune responses. Three-dimensional (3D) organoids have emerged as an alternative for nasal epithelium, serving as robust platforms for modeling respiratory viral infections. We aimed to generate human NEC organoids and to determine their cellular characteristics as an in vitro model for air-liquid interface (ALI) culture and influenza A virus (IAV) infection. METHODS: Primary human nasal mucosal tissues were obtained from healthy donors undergoing nasal surgery, and nasal epithelial cell (NEC) organoids were established using Matrigel-based three-dimensional culture. Differentiated NEC organoids and air-liquid interface (ALI) cultures were characterized by histology, immunostaining, electron microscopy, and quantitative real-time PCR, followed by influenza A virus (A/WS/33, H1N1) infection assays. In addition, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed to analyze cellular heterogeneity and differentiation trajectories of NEC organoids. RESULTS: We successfully developed human NEC organoids with using a Matrigel-based 3D culture system that recapitulates the structural characteristics and cellular composition of the human nasal epithelium. Histological results, real-time PCR, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) revealed that the organoids consisted of seven different cell types and displayed a difference in the composition between the cells. The organoids displayed a much higher rate of basal progenitor cells whereas ciliated cells were less dominant. Unlike ALI cultures in which passage (P) 2 was the limit, the organoids exhibited successful and subsequent passages up to P5. Our data determined that NEC organoids are an adequate in vitro model for IAV infection and showed a sharp induction of mRNA levels for interferons (IFNs) and IFN-stimulated genes following IAV infection. CONCLUSIONS: This study's results demonstrate that human NEC organoids serve as a robust in vitro model, successfully recapitulating the biological characteristics of nasal epithelium, and could be an adequate tool for exploring distinct IFN-related innate immune responses following influenza infection.

papers.title_zh: Fluoxetine attenuates asthma symptoms in a murine model through modulation of innate and adaptive immune components, and regulation of RORγt signalling axis in a pathogenic Th17 cell population.
papers.title_en: Fluoxetine attenuates asthma symptoms in a murine model through modulation of innate and adaptive immune components, and regulation of RORγt signalling axis in a pathogenic Th17 cell population.
papers.authors: Pramanik A, Sarkar D, Mondal P, Saha J, Mahanti K, Mahato M, Majumdar S, Pramanik A et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Academic Building II, Immunobiology and Translational Medicine Laboratory, Department of Zoology, Sidho Kanho Birsha Uni…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Asthma is a heterogeneous chronic inflammatory airway disease, characterised by dysregulated interactions between innate and adaptive immune cells. Although Th2-mediated inflammation predominates, persistent Th17-associated immune responses contribute to chronic airway inflammation implicated in the corticosteroid-insensitive disease state. Fluoxetine, a SSRI with immunomodulatory properties, was investigated to determine its effects on inflammation and Th17 response in experimental allergic airway disease. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Immunomodulatory effects of fluoxetine evaluated in exploratory in vitro assays. In vivo studies were performed in an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced murine model of allergic asthma using oral fluoxetine at clinically relevant doses. Airway pathology, immunophenotypes, cytokine production, gene and protein expression were evaluated by histology, flow cytometry, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), confocal microscopy and ex vivo functional assays. Public transcriptomic datasets were integrated with target enrichment analyses, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations used to explore potential molecular interactions. KEY RESULTS: Fluoxetine reduced the inflammatory response in activated macrophages without noticeable cytotoxicity. In an allergic asthma model, fluoxetine attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, eosinophilia, IgE production and pulmonary macrophage activation, whilst reducing the accumulation of the phenotypically granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor like cell population along with diminished T-cell activation and reduced Th17 responses, reduced IL-17 production together with decreased expression and nuclear localisation of RORγt. Ex vivo studies confirmed inhibition of RORγt expression and IL-17 production in Th17 cells. Transcriptomic integration identified significant enrichment of Th17-associated inflammatory pathways, whereas molecular docking and molecular dynamics analyses supported RORγt as a plausible molecular target. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Fluoxetine attenuates experimental allergic airway inflammation through coordinated modulation of innate and adaptive immune responses, with suppression of the RORγt-IL-17 signalling axis emerging as a key mechanistic feature. These findings expand the immunopharmacological profile of fluoxetine and provide an experimental rationale for further investigating its therapeutic potential in Th17-associated airway inflammatory diseases and in experimental models that more closely recapitulate corticosteroid-resistant asthma.

papers.title_zh: 计算筛选发现非核苷RdRp变构抑制剂BAY-850，临床前研究显示其广谱抗冠状病毒活性
papers.title_en: Identification and characterization of a non-nucleotide RdRp allosteric inhibitor with pan-coronavirus protection.
papers.authors: Guo Q, Yang X, Zhao Z, Cai JP, Wei L, Tang K, Chan WM, Chu AW et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: State Key Laboratory of Emerging Infectious Diseases, Carol Yu Centre for Infection, Department of Microbiology, Li Ka S…
papers.authors_conclusion: These findings validate a novel allosteric site in RdRp and support BAY-850 as a start-point for broad-spectrum anti-coronavirus development.
papers.ai_note: 摘要仅报告定性结果，未给出体外EC50、动物病毒载量降幅、样本量及统计学检验；治疗给药“显著降低”病毒载量缺乏数值支持；“广谱/pan-coronavirus”结论基于多种变异株和其他人类冠状病毒的概括性表述，具体病毒谱与效应强度信息不足；属于临床前研究，不能外推临床疗效。
papers.abstract_en: The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is a conserved and compelling target for pan-coronavirus antiviral development. To date, all US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved RdRp inhibitors are nucleotide inhibitors (NIs), which are prone to drug resistance and show limited clinical efficacy. Developing alternative non-nucleotide inhibitors (NNIs) with high target specificity, structural diversity, and metabolic stability could yield more effective antivirals. Here, we identify an allosteric RdRp NNI, BAY-850, via computational screening. BAY-850 exhibits potent, broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants and other human coronaviruses. Mechanistic studies show that BAY-850 binds directly to a previously unrecognized allosteric site on nsp12, thereby fine-tuning the catalytic motif F loop out-conformation the orthosteric site. Importantly, therapeutic administration of BAY-850 significantly reduces viral loads in the nasal turbinates and lungs of SARS-CoV-2-infected K18-hACE2 mice. These findings validate a novel allosteric site in RdRp and support BAY-850 as a start-point for broad-spectrum anti-coronavirus development.

papers.study_type: 方法学研究 · 体外诊断检测方法开发与解析性能验证（非临床样本对照研究）
papers.title_zh: 基于人工智能辅助抗体筛选与抗体-核酸偶联信号放大的SARS-CoV-2受体结合域超敏检测方法（ANCLISA）建立与体外分析性能验证
papers.title_en: Ultra-sensitive detection of receptor binding domain of SARS-CoV-2 based on artificial intelligence assisted antibody selection and antibody‒nucleic acid conjugation signal amplification.
papers.authors: Liu J, Chen W, Li X, Luo Y, Li Q, Zhao W, He Q, Zeng S et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: College of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou 310058, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: 该创新方法在实现SARS-CoV-2精准超敏检测方面迈出重要一步，有望提升当前全球抗疫中的诊断能力
papers.ai_note: 摘要仅报告缓冲体系/纯化抗原条件下的解析性能（线性范围、LOD），未提供临床样本验证、与 RT-qPCR 或抗原快检的头对头比较，也未说明 LOD 所在基质与复孔/重复次数，超敏宣称的外部有效性信息不足；标题与正文强调“Delta 变异株”检测，但方法靶向的是保守性未知的 RBD 蛋白，变异株特异性归属不清；AI 仅用于抗体亲和力预测筛选，与“AI 诊断”不同层级，勿混淆；无主要/次要终点概念，属分析性能指标，不存在终点替代问题。
papers.abstract_en: The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 has led to a global pandemic, causing unprecedented disruption to health systems and economies worldwide, calling for an urgent imperative for precise and sensitive diagnostic method. To address this, a novel detection method, termed antibody‒nucleic acid conjugate linked immunosorbent assay (ANCLISA), was designed for the ultra-sensitive detection of the receptor binding domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2, which play a pivotal role in the diagnosis of COVID-19. Leveraging the Alphafold 2 model for simulating antibody‒antigen complexes and the ΔΔG predictor model for forecasting the binding free energy of antigen‒antibody complex, we successfully identified the high-affinity antibody TB1. Through the utilization of succinimidyl 4-[N-maleimidomethyl] cyclohexane-1-carboxylate (SMCC) for antibody‒nucleic acid conjugation and the integration of the hybridization chain reaction (HCR) for signal amplification within the system, we have established an ultra-sensitive approach for the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant detection. The proposed immunoassay provided exhibited a linear detection range spanning 11 fg/mL to 11 ng/mL, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.48 fg/mL. Our innovative approach represents a significant stride in enabling precise and ultra-sensitive detection of SARS-CoV-2, thereby holding promise for enhancing diagnostic capabilities in the ongoing global battle against the pandemic.

papers.title_zh: 人CD46人源化小鼠模型显示HAdV-7肺部感染伴随干扰素相关肺免疫重塑
papers.title_en: Human CD46 humanized mice reveal interferon associated pulmonary immune remodeling during human adenovirus type 7 lung infection.
papers.authors: Yang Z, Meng Z, Wan M, Lu Y, Rao L, Qu H, Wei J, Liao J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory Medicine, Children's Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, Chongqing, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: HAdV-7感染hCD46人源化小鼠与干扰素富集的肺部炎症环境、显著的炎性髓系重塑及淋巴系转录状态改变相关；该易感小鼠模型为研究HAdV-7相关肺病及抗病毒、免疫调节与疫苗策略的临床前评价提供了有用的实验工具。
papers.ai_note: 全文为定性描述，未报告任何样本量、效应量、置信区间或P值，无法判断差异幅度与统计稳健性；单细胞与PBMC结果属相关性“投影”，不能证明人体系统性免疫程序与小鼠肺程序同源；人源化程度、CD46表达组织分布、病毒接种量与时间点、野生型对照数量等关键方法学信息在摘要中缺失，信息不足；结论使用“associated with”口径，但模型“易感”与“可用于疫苗/免疫调节评价”的推论超出所展示数据。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Human adenovirus type 7(HAdV-7) is a major cause of severe pediatric pneumonia, but the mechanisms linking viral infection to pulmonary immune remodeling and lung pathology remain incompletely understood. Progress has been limited by the lack of physiologically relevant animal models that recapitulate human susceptibility. METHODS: We generated human CD46 (hCD46) humanized mice and evaluated pulmonary viral burden, recoverable infectious virus, and lung pathology after HAdV-7 infection. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on lung tissues from wild type and hCD46 humanized mice under control and infected conditions to characterize cellular composition, transcriptional states, and intercellular communication. Human PBMC bulk transcriptomes from pediatric HAdV infection were further analyzed to assess the systemic relevance of mouse lung derived immune programs. RESULTS: hCD46 humanized mice showed increased pulmonary viral burden, recoverable infectious virions, and more severe lung pathology after HAdV-7 infection. Single-cell profiling revealed depletion of resident alveolar macrophages, pronounced expansion of inflammatory macrophage subsets, and remodeling of lymphoid transcriptional states in infected hCD46 lungs. These changes were accompanied by prominent type I/II interferon and interferon associated chemokine programs. B cells and CD4+ and CD8+ T cells showed prominent interferon stimulated genes (ISGs) associated transcriptional states, together with alterations in selected effector- and memory-associated programs and computationally inferred trajectories. Projection of mouse lung derived signatures onto transcriptomes of human peripheral blood mononuclear cell showed that selected interferon associated myeloid and lymphoid programs were also detectable systemically in pediatric HAdV infection. CONCLUSIONS: HAdV-7 infection in hCD46 humanized mice was associated with an interferon enriched pulmonary inflammatory environment, prominent inflammatory myeloid remodeling, and altered lymphoid transcriptional states. This susceptible mouse model provides a useful experimental tool for studying HAdV-7 associated lung disease and for preclinical evaluation of antiviral, immunomodulatory, and vaccine strategies.

papers.title_en: Targeting Neutrophil Hitchhiking for Drug Delivery to Block CCL5-CCR1 and Effectively Alleviate Acute Lung Injury.
papers.authors: Huang QY, Kang ZY, Yu MJ, Yan XQ, Tian BP
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Critical Care Medicine, The Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, Hangzhou, …
papers.authors_conclusion: 研究揭示ALI/ARDS中巨噬细胞分泌CCL5激活中性粒细胞CCR1、经Giα2依赖途径抑制cAMP从而驱动中性粒细胞肺内趋化的关键细胞通讯轴；药理性抑制CCR1（BX471）可阻断该通路并减轻ALI进展；所开发的衰老中性粒细胞导向纳米递送系统可在骨髓内靶向释药、从源头抑制中性粒细胞外逸至肺，在降低给药剂量与频次的同时显著缓解ALI，并具备对细胞与组织无毒的安全优势，为炎症性肺损伤的靶向干预提供新型细胞导向治疗策略。
papers.ai_note: 摘要通篇为定性表述（“显著减轻”“无毒”“优越安全性”），未给出任何效应量、剂量-效应关系、样本量、对照分组与统计学结果，无法判断效应大小与可重复性；机制链条（CCL5-CCR1-Giα2-cAMP）虽完整，但递送策略依赖“CXCR4high衰老中性粒细胞”这一特定细胞状态，向人体、不同病因ALI及不同病程阶段的转化边界未讨论；未与现有ALI治疗（如小潮气量通气、激素等支持治疗）或已有CCR1/趋化因子通路抑制剂进行头对头比较，疗效定位不明；安全性仅以“对细胞与组织无毒”概括，缺少体内毒性、免疫抑制风险评估数据（CCR1阻断可能影响宿主抗感染能力，对ARDS这一感染高发人群尤为关键）；未见预注册或主要终点预设信息，信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: Acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome (ALI/ARDS) is a severe respiratory condition characterized by acute, diffuse inflammatory damage to the lungs, posing a significant threat to human health. Although neutrophils and macrophages are known to play critical roles in ALI/ARDS pathogenesis, the precise cellular pathways governing their interaction remain poorly defined, and targeted therapeutics modulating these pathways are currently lacking. Here, we show that macrophages secrete CCL5 to activate CCR1 on neutrophils, thereby driving neutrophil chemotaxis toward the lungs in ALI. Mechanistically, this signaling axis operates primarily through Giα2-dependent suppression of intracellular cAMP levels. Pharmacological inhibition of CCR1 with BX471 blocks this pathway and attenuates ALI progression. Furthermore, we developed a nanoparticle-based delivery system encapsulating BX471 that exploits the intrinsic bone marrow-homing property of CXCR4high senescent neutrophils. This neutrophil‑guided strategy enables targeted drug release within the bone marrow, effectively inhibiting neutrophil egress to the lungs at the source. This approach not only significantly alleviates ALI by reducing drug dosage and administration frequency but also offers the superior safety advantage of being non-toxic to cells and tissues. Together, our findings reveal a key cellular communication axis in ALI/ARDS and present a novel, cell‑guided therapeutic strategy for targeted intervention in inflammatory lung injury.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Institute of Quantitative Biomedicine, Rutgers-The State University of New Jersey, New Brunswick, USA.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Asthma is a heterogeneous disease with well-documented sex differences in prevalence. However, the sex-specific and pubertal effects of inhaled corticosteroids on endogenous steroid metabolites and their relationship with asthma-related clinical outcomes remain poorly understood. METHODS: Targeted serum profiling of the steroid biosynthesis pathway was generated by Precion Inc. (NC, USA). Sixteen metabolites from the steroid biosynthesis pathway were quantified at baseline and end-of-trial in children with asthma from the Childhood Asthma Management Program (CAMP; n = 1,041; metabolomics analytic subset n = 664), aged 5-12 years. Linear mixed models and generalized linear models were used to evaluate sex-specific longitudinal and endpoint responses of steroid metabolites and clinical outcomes with inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) use, adjusting for age, sex, race, height, and body mass index. RESULTS: ICS use in males was associated with significantly lower cortisol and cortisone levels at Year 4 (end of trial). In females, cortisol and cortisone showed more stable trajectories with ICS use, which resulted in a non-significant reduction at year 4. Males receiving ICS showed suggestive positive longitudinal associations for 17α-hydroxyprogesterone, estrone, and testosterone, while females showed a suggestive positive trajectory for androstenedione. ICS exposure modified the associations between metabolites and clinical outcomes (FEV1, FVC, eosinophils, and airway hyperresponsiveness) in a pathway- and sex-specific manner. Overall, ICS attenuated longitudinal associations between endogenous steroids and clinical outcomes, particularly in females, while selected relationships from the androgen-lung function associations were preserved at the end of the trial. CONCLUSION: We identify sex-specific differences in ICS-associated metabolite profiles and clinical outcomes, supporting the need for further investigation into sex-informed approaches to corticosteroid use in pediatric asthma. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov: NCT00000575; registered 1999-10-27.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Outcomes following curative-intent resection of synchronous primary lung cancer (SPLC) remain incompletely defined. We compared recurrence and survival in SPLC versus solitary primary tumors among patients with clinical stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of Veterans undergoing curative-intent resection for clinical stage I NSCLC in the Veterans Health Administration (2006-2020). SPLC was defined as two distinct clinical stage I NSCLC tumors diagnosed within six weeks, with curative-intent treatment of both tumors within one year. Propensity score matching (PSM) (1:1) was used to compare patients with SPLC to those with solitary tumors. The primary outcome was cumulative incidence of recurrence (CIR); secondary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). Additional analyses examined the role of adjuvant treatment and drivers of recurrence in SPLC patients. RESULTS: Of 12,606 Veterans with resected clinical stage I NSCLC, 337 (2.7%) had SPLC. SPLC presented with larger tumors and more advanced pathologic stage. Histology was discordant between the two tumors in 44.2% of SPLC cases. In the propensity-matched cohort (281 pairs), SPLC was associated with higher CIR (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.10-2.07), worse DFS (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.03-1.50), and worse OS (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.01-1.45). Within SPLC, wedge resection of both tumors was independently associated with recurrence. CONCLUSIONS: After adjustment, SPLC was associated with higher recurrence and worse survival than solitary tumors, supporting recognition of SPLC as a higher-risk phenotype within clinical stage I NSCLC.

papers.title_zh: Benmelstobart With or Without Anlotinib After Chemoradiotherapy for Unresectable Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: The R-ALPS Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.title_en: Benmelstobart With or Without Anlotinib After Chemoradiotherapy for Unresectable Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: The R-ALPS Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.authors: Ji Y, Li Q, Chen L, Pang Q, Jiang O, Chen Y, Wang J, Ge H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Zhejiang Cancer Hospital, Hangzhou Institute of Medicine, Chinese Academy of Science, Hangzhou, China.
papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Consolidation immunotherapy improves outcomes after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Disease progression remains common, and more effective consolidation strategies are needed. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of benmelstobart with or without anlotinib as consolidation therapy after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III NSCLC. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter double-blind phase 3 randomized clinical trial took place at 42 centers in China from 2020 to 2023 among patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after concurrent or sequential chemoradiotherapy. In stage 1, patients were randomized 1:1:1 to 2 active regimens or placebo; in stage 2, additional patients were randomized 1:1 between the active regimens to power their direct comparison. Data cutoffs were November 30, 2023, for stage 1 and July 8, 2024, for the pooled analysis. Data analysis was performed from January 17 to March 23, 2025. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to receive benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart plus anlotinib placebo, or their matching placebos. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary end point was independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS). RESULTS: Of 553 participants (median [IQR] age, 62 [56-67] years; 495 male individuals [89.5%]), 390 were randomized in stage 1 and 163 in stage 2. In stage 1, median PFS was 15.1 months (95% CI, 9.4-21.7) with benmelstobart plus anlotinib, 9.7 months (95% CI, 6.0-34.4) with benmelstobart alone, and 4.2 months (95% CI, 3.2-6.8) with placebo. The hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.49 (95% CI, 0.36-0.66; P < .001) for benmelstobart plus anlotinib vs placebo and 0.53 (95% CI, 0.39-0.72; P < .001) for benmelstobart vs placebo. In the pooled stage 1 and 2 analysis, median PFS was 17.4 (95% CI, 12.5-24.8) months with benmelstobart plus anlotinib and 11.2 (95% CI, 7.0-20.7) months with benmelstobart alone (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.63-1.08; P = .12). Grade 3 to 5 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 48.8%, 29.4%, and 19.7% in the benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart alone, and placebo groups, respectively; grade 5 events occurred in 7.2%, 1.4%, and 1.5%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This randomized clinical trial found that benmelstobart with or without anlotinib significantly improved PFS compared with placebo. Adding anlotinib did not significantly improve PFS compared with benmelstobart alone and increased severe and fatal treatment-related adverse events. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04325763.

papers.abstract_en: We examined whether the impact on quality of life (QOL) of early palliative care delivered via video versus in-person visits varied across patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Between 6/2018 and 5/2023, 1250 patients with advanced NSCLC enrolled in a randomized trial comparing early palliative care delivered via video or in-person visits at 22 cancer centers. Using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Lung scale, we examined whether the effect of palliative care delivery modality on patient-reported QOL at 24 weeks post-enrollment varied by baseline sociodemographic and other factors. Black patients, Hispanic/Latino patients, and those with incomes <$50,000 reported better QOL in the video visit group versus the in-person group. However, Asian patients in the video visit group reported worse QOL than the in-person group. Early palliative care delivered via video may provide greater QOL benefits for Black and Hispanic/Latino patients with advanced NSCLC and those with lower incomes. Trial Registration: NCT03375489.

papers.title_zh: DLL3靶向治疗在小细胞肺癌中的演进：T细胞衔接器、抗体偶联药物与CAR-T及生物标志物应用综述
papers.title_en: The evolving landscape of DLL3-directed Therapeutics in small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Tieu VT, Arter ZL, Nagasaka M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Internal Medicine, University of California Irvine School of Medicine, 101 The City Drive South, Orange, C…
papers.ai_note: 摘要未说明文献检索策略、纳入排除标准及证据分级，属叙述性综述，选择偏倚与强调偏倚无法评估；Rova-T III期未显示生存获益被作为背景，叙述重心转向新一代DLL3策略，需警惕对早期/机制性证据的乐观强调；无原始疗效数据。
papers.abstract_en: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) remains one of the most lethal thoracic malignancies, characterized by rapid progression, early metastasis, and limited durable responses to conventional therapy. Delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3), a Notch pathway inhibitory ligand aberrantly overexpressed on the surface of approximately 70-85% of SCLC tumor cells but largely absent from normal adult tissue, has emerged as a compelling and therapeutically actionable target. Early efforts to exploit DLL3 through the antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) rovalpituzumab tesirine (Rova-T) yielded important mechanistic insights despite failing to demonstrate survival benefit in phase III trials and have since catalyzed a new generation of more refined DLL3-directed strategies. This review critically examines the evolving portfolio of DLL3-targeted therapies across three principal modalities: T-cell engagers, ADCs, and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies. In parallel, we examine emerging non-DLL3 therapeutic strategies reshaping the broader SCLC landscape. We additionally discuss the translational science underpinning DLL3 as a biomarker, including the emerging roles of circulating tumor cell-based liquid biopsy and DLL3-directed immunoPET-CT imaging in patient selection and treatment monitoring.

papers.title_en: A Robust Bio-Supportive Hydrogel Patch for Full-Thickness Repair of Gastroesophageal Defects.
papers.authors: Song X, Shuai Z, Sun W, Chen L, Shen Y, Hu J, Ma Y, Luo J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, Shanghai Key Lab of Tissue Engineering, Shanghai 9th People's Hospital…
papers.authors_conclusion: RBS贴片在胃穿孔、食管穿孔及气管食管瘘模型中实现显著愈合，黏膜、黏膜下及肌层完整再生，疗效与安全性在比格犬模型中进一步验证，具有临床转化潜力，可作为胃食管缺损的通用生物支持技术及动态生理环境下组织修复的有前景平台。
papers.ai_note: 摘要通篇为定性表述（remarkable healing、intact regeneration），未给出任何愈合率、闭合压力、渗漏率、组织学评分等定量数据；未报告各组样本量、对照设置、随访时长与统计方法；'疗效与安全性在比格犬中进一步验证'缺乏安全性指标的具体内容；多物种结果被合并陈述，无法判断各模型的效应一致性；由动物模型直接推导'临床转化潜力'属外推表述。信息不足，无法评估偏倚风险。
papers.abstract_en: Surgical repair of gastroesophageal (GE) defects is a formidable clinical challenge, plagued by high leakage, fistula recurrence and life-threatening complications due to gastric acid exposure and persistent mechanical stress. To address this unmet need, we developed a robust bio-supportive (RBS) hydrogel patch for immediate fluid-tight closure and full-thickness tissue regeneration. Fabricated from highly crystalline polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogel, the RBS patch has a double-disc architecture, inherent porous network and weakly bound water. The double-disc design ensures effective sealing and deformation resistance; high crystallinity confers adequate mechanical strength and long-term acid/enzyme resistance. Moreover, its porous microstructure and weakly bound water synergistically promote cellular adhesion, migration and tissue infiltration for functional repair. In rat and rabbit models, the RBS patch achieved remarkable healing of gastric perforations (GP), esophageal perforations (EP) and tracheoesophageal fistulas (TEF), with intact mucosal, submucosal and muscular layers regeneration. Its efficacy and safety were further validated in beagle dog models, highlighting clinical translation potential. This RBS patch serves as a versatile bio-supportive technology for GE defects and a promising platform for tissue repair in dynamic physiological environments.

papers.title_zh: Subspecialty ILD Clinic Care is Associated with More Guideline-Concordant Evaluation and Improved Outcomes Compared to Other Ambulatory Settings: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.title_en: Subspecialty ILD Clinic Care is Associated with More Guideline-Concordant Evaluation and Improved Outcomes Compared to Other Ambulatory Settings: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.authors: Farrand E, Mills H, Radhakrishnan L, Ieong M, Lee A, Gologorskaya O, Butte A
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medicine, University of California San Francisco, San Francisco, CA.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Subspecialty interstitial lung disease (ILD) clinics are associated with improved outcomes, yet access remains uneven. Even within tertiary health systems, patients with ILD are managed across diverse ambulatory settings, with unclear implications for care and outcomes. RESEARCH QUESTION: Within a single academic health system, do patient characteristics, care delivery, and outcomes differ between individuals with ILD managed in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus other ambulatory settings? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with ILD at a large academic medical center. Identified patients were stratified by care in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus non-specialty setting. Demographic, diagnostic testing, treatment, health care utilization, and survival data were extracted from the electronic health record. Diagnostic and treatment measures were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Hospitalization, emergency department visit, and death were analyzed as time-to-event outcomes. RESULTS: Among 6,637 patients with ILD, 4,371 (66%) were seen in the subspecialty ILD clinic. The 2,266 patients (34%) managed in non-specialty settings were more likely to identify as Black or Latinx, reside in more socioeconomically deprived neighborhoods, and have an unspecified ILD diagnosis (all p < 0.001). In the peri-diagnostic period, ILD clinic care was associated with higher adjusted odds of chest CT imaging (OR 2.51, 2.07-3.05) and antifibrotic therapy (OR 1.54, 1.32-1.80), and lower odds of lung biopsy (OR 0.47, 0.32-0.68). ILD clinic care was associated with a lower adjusted hazards of all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.46, 0.42-0.51), emergency department visit (HR 0.68, 0.59-0.78), and death (HR 0.57, 0.45-0.72). P-value <0.001 for all. INTERPRETATION: Within a single health system, subspecialty ILD clinic care was associated with more guideline-concordant care and improved outcomes. Differences in access to subspecialty expertise may contribute to inequities in care delivery, underscoring the need for scalable strategies, referral optimization, telemedicine, and clinical decision support, to extend ILD expertise and improve outcomes.

papers.title_zh: Azithromycin Exposure and Incident Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Isolation in Bronchiectasis and COPD: A Nationwide Nested Case-Control Study.
papers.title_en: Azithromycin Exposure and Incident Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Isolation in Bronchiectasis and COPD: A Nationwide Nested Case-Control Study.
papers.authors: Torsheim IL, Wedervang EB, Vognsen AK, Lillebaek T, Fløe A, Dahl VN, Stæhr Jensen JU, Sivapalan P et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Section of Respiratory Medicine, Department of Medicine, Herlev and Gentofte Hospital, University of Copenhagen, Copenha…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Azithromycin reduces exacerbations in chronic airway disease, but whether it alters the risk of nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) isolation is unresolved. RESEARCH QUESTION: Is azithromycin exposure in the preceding year associated with incident respiratory NTM isolation in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis and in COPD? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Two nationwide register-based nested case-control analyses in Denmark. Case patients had a first positive respiratory culture for NTM; controls, alive and free of prior NTM isolation on the index date, were matched 1:20 on age, sex, and comorbidity index. The prespecified exposure was at least 3,000 mg of azithromycin with at least two prescriptions redeemed in the preceding 12 months, with a 3-month lag. Conditional logistic regression was adjusted for inhaled and oral corticosteroids. Exploratory analyses examined an active comparator at matched thresholds, recency, and outcome stringency. RESULTS: The analyses comprised 173 cases and 3,409 controls (bronchiectasis) and 365 and 7,300 (COPD). Under the prespecified definition, azithromycin was not associated with incident NTM isolation (bronchiectasis: OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 0.79-2.18; COPD: 1.29; 0.78-2.13). In COPD, the OR was 1.61 (1.14-2.28) for one or more prescriptions and 1.29 (0.78-2.13) for two or more. The COPD association was concentrated within 90 days of the index date (2.55; 1.73-3.76) and attenuated with microbiological stringency (definite isolates: 0.77; 0.27-2.20). Non-macrolide antibacterials were more strongly associated than azithromycin at every matched threshold in bronchiectasis (one or more prescriptions: 1.90 [1.36-2.65] vs 1.15 [0.75-1.75]), and at the two higher thresholds in COPD (two or more: 1.48 [1.17-1.86] vs 1.24 [0.75-2.05]). INTERPRETATION: Azithromycin was not associated with NTM isolation under the prespecified definition. Associations under broader definitions were not dose-dependent and clustered close to the index date, more consistent with indication-driven testing than a drug effect, although in COPD an association with any exposure persisted after accounting for other antibacterials.

papers.title_zh: DNA methylation-based immune profiling reveals distinct subtypes in esophageal adenocarcinoma.
papers.title_en: DNA methylation-based immune profiling reveals distinct subtypes in esophageal adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Pinto R, Sjurgard IV, Hauge T, Brandt-Winge S, Pharo H, Kumar T, Øvrebø KK
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Molecular Oncology, Institute for Cancer Research, Oslo University Hospital, the Norwegian Radium Hospital…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Only a subset of patients with esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) achieve complete or partial histopathological response to immunotherapy, highlighting the need for better understanding of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Despite efforts to characterize the EAC TME at the molecular level, its epigenetic landscape remains understudied. METHODS: We combined bulk DNA methylation data from a large Norwegian multicenter EAC cohort (n = 232) with immune gene annotations to identify immune-related CpG sites differentially methylated between tumor and normal tissue. Hierarchical consensus clustering of EAC samples based on these sites was performed, and the identified subtypes were characterized according to their immune cell type composition, association with clinical features and potential prognostic relevance. RESULTS: We identified four immune subtypes (IS1-IS4) with distinct DNA methylation patterns and tumor-infiltrating immune cell composition. The highest DNA methylation levels at immune-related CpG sites were found in IS3, which showed the lowest relative fractions of CD8+ T cells and the highest fractions of regulatory T cells (Tregs), consistent with an immunosuppressed phenotype. Conversely, IS1, with the lowest DNA methylation levels at immune-related CpG sites, displayed the highest relative fractions of CD8+ T cells and the lowest fractions of Tregs, aligning with an "inflamed" immune profile. These findings were validated in an independent multicenter cohort (n = 285). No significant differences in 5-year overall survival were observed across immune subtypes, possibly reflecting the influence of variable response to neoadjuvant treatment. CONCLUSION: The identified immune subtypes offer new insights into the epigenetic landscape of the EAC TME and reveal differences in its cellular composition.

papers.title_zh: Endoscopic Classification of Fundoplication Integrity Predicts Pathologic Reflux: Development and Prospective Validation.
papers.title_en: Endoscopic Classification of Fundoplication Integrity Predicts Pathologic Reflux: Development and Prospective Validation.
papers.authors: Siboni S, De Maron R, Lovece A, Milito P, Riva CG, Bernardi D, Sozzi M, Asti E et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of General and Emergency Surgery, Esophageal and Reflux Center, IRCCS Policlinico San Donato, University of Mil…
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: We aimed to validate individual endoscopic parameters against clinical and functional testing and to build a simple classification of fundoplication integrity. SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: Endoscopy is the main tool to assess the gastroesophageal valve after antireflux surgery (ARS), but existing classifications are complex and have never been validated against objective pathophysiologic data. METHODS: This was a single-center, two-phase cohort study of adults undergoing endoscopy, high-resolution manometry (HRM), and reflux monitoring after ARS. Retroflexed videoclips were reviewed blinded to functional results. In the development cohort (2018-2024), endoscopic parameters were tested against pathologic GERD (Lyon 2.0 criteria); those correlating with reflux were included in the classification and the population was stratified according to the number of impaired mechanisms (0-3). In the second phase, the classification was validated prospectively (2024-2026). RESULTS: Of 122 patients, 73 formed the development and 49 the validation cohort. Three parameters were associated with pathologic GERD: intrathoracic valve, disrupted valve, and visible hiatus. Clinical, manometric, and reflux metrics worsened stepwise with the number of impaired mechanisms, and pathologic GERD rose from 11.8% to 37.5% to 85.7%. The new classification discriminated pathologic GERD with an area under the curve of 0.860 in the development and 0.870 in the validation cohort (0.869 overall). CONCLUSIONS: A simple endoscopic classification based on valve location, disruption, and hiatal opening reliably identifies fundoplication failure and correlates with symptoms, manometric features, and reflux burden.

papers.title_zh: Traumatic Emergency Thoracotomy for Resuscitation in Shock (TETRiS): a national service evaluation of resuscitative thoracotomy practice outside the operating theatre.
papers.title_en: Traumatic Emergency Thoracotomy for Resuscitation in Shock (TETRiS): a national service evaluation of resuscitative thoracotomy practice outside the operating theatre.
papers.authors: Ramage L, Tucker H, Marsden ME, Wohlgemut JM, Naeem S, Christian M, Davenport R, Perkins ZB et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Barts Health NHS Trust, London, UK; Essex & Herts Air Ambulance.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Resuscitative thoracotomy (RT) is performed in patients with traumatic cardiac arrest or peri-arrest to treat potentially reversible causes of circulatory collapse. Optimal patient selection and timing remain uncertain, and existing evidence is largely retrospective, often excluding prehospital deaths. This prospective service evaluation examined contemporary RT practice and outcomes across a national major trauma system, including prehospital and emergency department settings. METHODS: Prospective 12-month observational study across 20 UK Helicopter Emergency Medical Services and 26 Major Trauma Centre Emergency Departments, using the PHOTON, TERN, and NaTRIC research networks. RESULTS: A total of 116 patients underwent RT, of which 82 (70.7%) were performed prehospital. Median age was 30 years, 97 patients (83.6%) were male, and 81 (69.8%) sustained penetrating injury. Suspected cardiac tamponade was the most common indication for RT (72/116 [62.1%]), although operative findings demonstrated exsanguinating haemorrhage in 82 patients (70.7%). Overall, 50 patients (43.1%) achieved return of spontaneous circulation and eight (6.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Survival was strongly associated with pathophysiological cause, duration of arrest, and physiological state at the time of intervention, with substantially better outcomes observed in patients with cardiac tamponade than exsanguination. Patients undergoing emergency department RT demonstrated shorter arrest durations, more favourable physiology, and higher survival than those undergoing prehospital RT. There were no survivors beyond 10 minutes of traumatic cardiac arrest. CONCLUSION: In this prospective national evaluation of RT practice, outcomes were strongly associated with the pathophysiological cause and duration of arrest, and the residual physiology present at the time of intervention. The most favourable outcomes were observed in patients with cardiac tamponade and those undergoing RT before irreversible physiological deterioration.

papers.title_en: Columnar-lined esophagus measuring less than 1 cm as a risk factor for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in Japanese men.
papers.authors: Watanabe K, Fukuda S, Kubota D, Yamamichi N, Takahashi Y, Watanabe Y, Adachi K, Ishimura N et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Gastroenterology, Akita University Graduate School of Medicine, 1-1-1 Hondo, Akita, Akita, 010-8543, Japan…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Several case series have noted an association between Barrett's esophagus (BE) and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study to examine the association between baseline BE status, particularly ultra-short-segment BE (USSBE; BE <1 cm), and subsequent ESCC development, focusing on the presence or absence of extensive gastric atrophy (GA). METHODS: Consecutive male participants who underwent endoscopy at 17 health check-up institutes in Japan between 2013 and 2017 and had follow-up endoscopy by December 2022 were enrolled. Baseline endoscopic images were reviewed to assess GA and BE status. The primary outcome was ESCC development during follow-up. The association between BE status and ESCC was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and Cox regression. RESULTS: Among 20,402 male subjects, 7161 (35.1%) had USSBE. During 116,483.1 person-years of follow-up, 73 cases of ESCC developed. The incidence of ESCC was highest among individuals with USSBE (0.0946%/year). Multivariable analysis revealed that USSBE was independently associated with ESCC (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.82, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-3.24). In exploratory subgroup analyses, USSBE was independently associated with ESCC (adjusted HR 2.40, 95% CI 1.13-5.13) among individuals with extensive GA, while no significant association was observed among those without (adjusted HR 1.34, 95% CI 0.64-2.81; p for interaction = 0.369). CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to demonstrate a significant association between USSBE and ESCC. USSBE may help identify individuals at increased risk of ESCC. Exploratory subgroup findings according to GA status require further validation.

papers.authors: Wang CY, Lim BS, Huang YT
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Pulmonary Medicine, Department of Internal Medicine, Cardinal Tien Hospital and School of Medicine, College …
