papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, and an increasing proportion of cases occur in lifetime nonsmokers, particularly East Asian women. Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in outdoor air pollution is classified as a Group 1 carcinogen and increasingly seen as an important modifiable exposure associated with lung cancer in nonsmokers. This narrative review summarizes epidemiologic and toxicological evidence linking environmental and microenvironmental PM2.5 exposures to lung cancer in nonsmokers, defined as individuals who have smoked fewer than 100 cigarettes in their lifetime. Global cohort and meta-analytic data, including dose-response findings and studies from Asian populations, are reviewed. Biological pathways linking PM2.5 to lung carcinogenesis are then examined, including oxidative stress, pulmonary inflammation, and particle-triggered cytokine and growth-factor signaling. Particular emphasis is placed on macrophage-derived interleukin-1β (IL-1β) signaling, which promotes epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant lung adenocarcinoma. High-exposure microenvironments such as religious incense burning, residential cooking and solid-fuel use, urban transit systems (subway, bus, motorbike, and professional driving), and selected occupational settings (career and wildland firefighters, construction trades, informal e-waste recycling) are identified. These settings might contribute significantly to daily PM2.5 exposure in some individuals. Finally, future research priorities, including incorporation of cumulative PM2.5 exposure into lung cancer risk prediction models and development of cost-effective strategies for lung cancer screening in nonsmokers with high PM2.5 exposure, are presented.

papers.title_zh: Effects of perioperative esketamine infusion on chronic pain after video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind clinical trial.
papers.title_en: Effects of perioperative esketamine infusion on chronic pain after video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind clinical trial.
papers.authors: Wang QY, Zhang JY, Gu JQ, Li B, Gao YT, Guo F, Qi Y, Li Q et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Anaesthesiology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University, Suzhou, Jiangsu, China; Institute of…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic postsurgical pain after thoracoscopic surgery remains common. We investigated whether perioperative low-dose esketamine infusion would reduce chronic pain after video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection. METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised controlled trial, 914 adults were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either esketamine or normal saline. Esketamine was administered as a 0.1 mg kg-1 bolus at induction, followed by continuous intraoperative infusion (0.1 mg kg-1 h-1) and postoperative infusion (0.015 mg kg-1 h-1) for 48 h. The primary outcome was chronic pain at 3 months, defined as persistent pain with a numeric rating scale score ≥1 during coughing in the surgical region. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, supplemental analgesics use, recovery of bowel function, in-hospital adverse events, and esketamine-related side-effects. RESULTS: We analysed 873 patients (median age, 55 yr; 63% female). The incidence of 3 month chronic pain was lower in the esketamine group than in the control group (14.7% vs 21.2%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.62; 95% confidence interval, 0.43-0.90; P=0.013). A reduction was also observed when using a post hoc outcome definition of a numeric rating scale pain score ≥3 during coughing at 3 months (adjusted odds ratio, 0.39; 95% confidence interval, 0.19-0.84; P=0.015). Esketamine also reduced overall pain scores at rest and during coughing within the first 48 h, and decreased supplemental analgesic requirements within 48 h and 3 months. CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative low-dose esketamine infusion significantly reduced 3 month chronic pain after thoracoscopic lung resection without increasing adverse effects. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR2000040012. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was registered on the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Identifier: ChiCTR2000040012; principal investigator: Fu-hai Ji; dated November 18, 2020; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=62319).

papers.title_zh: Antibody 3CF5 neutralizes historical and emerging H5Nx influenza viruses by targeting a conserved non-receptor-binding hemagglutinin epitope.
papers.title_en: Antibody 3CF5 neutralizes historical and emerging H5Nx influenza viruses by targeting a conserved non-receptor-binding hemagglutinin epitope.
papers.authors: Liang H, Niu C, Cheng Y, Liew KY, Qu L, Zheng Z, Yang W, Wang Q et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: State Key Laboratory of Respiratory Disease, Guangzhou Institute of Respiratory Health, The First Affiliated Hospital of…
papers.abstract_en: Avian influenza viruses of the H5Nx subtype pose persistent pandemic threats. Here, we immunized rhesus macaques with an H5N6 vaccine and obtained 30 H5-reactive monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). Three IgG mAbs, 3CF5, 3BG3, and 3BE7, demonstrated potent neutralizing activity against multiple H5Nx viruses and conferred protection in a lethal mouse challenge model. Notably, 3CF5 exhibited broad neutralization against H5Nx viruses spanning 1997-2024, including contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 strains associated with an ongoing outbreak in dairy cattle. Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) analysis revealed that 3CF5 targets a conserved non-receptor-binding epitope on the hemagglutinin (HA) head, spanning the vestigial esterase domain and an adjacent lateral surface. 3CF5 mediates neutralization primarily through inhibiting membrane fusion and also possesses antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. Furthermore, isotype conversion of 3CF5-IgG to mucosal secretory IgA1 (sIgA1) enhanced neutralization potency against H5N1 viruses up to 128-fold, highlighting the advantage of sIgA1 as a nasally administered prophylactic agent.

papers.title_zh: Free-breathing Pulmonary Relaxometry at 0.55T.
papers.title_en: Free-breathing Pulmonary Relaxometry at 0.55T.
papers.authors: Panos P, Bieri O, Pradella M, Hostettler KE, Bauman G
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Basel, Allschwil, Switzerland; Department of Radiology, Division of …
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility of an integrated, free-breathing workflow for automated 2D pulmonary relaxometry (T1, T2) at 0.55T. METHODS: A 2D inversion recovery balanced steady-state free precession (IR-bSSFP) sequence was adapted to achieve high-temporal sampling of its transient phase at 0.55T. IR-bSSFP relaxometry was validated in manganese-doped phantoms using reference methods and tested in eight healthy volunteers as well as one patient. A fully automated pipeline was developed, featuring multi-contrast registration for motion correction and deep learning-based lung segmentation to enable voxel-wise nonlinear fitting for T1 and T2 map generation. RESULTS: Phantom results were in agreement with reference scans. The proposed free-breathing framework effectively mitigated respiratory motion, yielding quantitative maps in close agreement with breath-hold references. Average healthy lung parenchyma relaxation times were T1 = (920 ± 40)ms and T2 = (90 ± 8)ms. In a patient case, the method successfully distinguished a solid lung mass from surrounding parenchyma, with the lesion showing elevated T1 (950 vs 800ms in the surrounding parenchyma). CONCLUSIONS: Simultaneous free-breathing T1 and T2 mapping of the lung is feasible at 0.55T using a fully automated pipeline. By eliminating breath-holds and external gating, this approach may improve patient compliance, demonstrating technical feasibility in a clinical setting and offering potential for future clinical evaluation.

papers.title_zh: Comparative evaluation of metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing for pathogen detection in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from patients with lower respiratory tract infections: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.title_en: Comparative evaluation of metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing for pathogen detection in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from patients with lower respiratory tract infections: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Zhao R, Na H, Miao W, Liu L, Zhang J, Miao Y, Zhao Y, Li X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, Chifeng Municipal Hospital, Chifeng, Inner Mongolia, China.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Rapid and precise pathogen identification is crucial for managing lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs). While metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) and targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) are emerging as valuable diagnostic tools, large-scale studies directly evaluating their real-world impact on antimicrobial stewardship remain scarce. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study encompassing 941 patients with suspected LRTIs who underwent bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) sequencing. Patients were evaluated in either an mNGS cohort (n = 479; DNA-only sequencing) or a tNGS cohort (n = 462; DNA and RNA sequencing). Diagnostic performance, pathogen spectrum, and clinical utility were compared against a composite final clinical diagnosis, which served as the reference standard. RESULTS: Both sequencing platforms demonstrated diagnostic efficacy superior to traditional laboratory tests. In the tNGS cohort, polymicrobial infections were highly prevalent (93.5%). Furthermore, tNGS demonstrated high sensitivity for fastidious pathogens, identifying 54 cases of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (a cohort in which routine smears missed 77.8% of cases) and effectively detecting Pneumocystis jirovecii. The overall diagnostic sensitivity was 90.6% (95% CI: 87.5-93.1%) for mNGS and 73.4% (95% CI:69.2%-77.3%) for tNGS. Guided by tNGS results, clinicians escalated antimicrobial therapy in 22.6% of positive cases. The clinical improvement rate following this targeted escalation was 66.2%, comparable to the 66.7% improvement rate observed in patients receiving appropriate initial empirical therapy (P = 0.946). CONCLUSION: Both tNGS and mNGS offer substantial diagnostic value for LRTIs, with tNGS showing particular utility in identifying fastidious and low-titer pathogens. Sequencing-guided diagnostics frequently informed antimicrobial adjustments and were associated with favorable clinical progress; however, future prospective paired-testing studies are required to isolate the direct impact of sequencing on patient survival outcomes.

papers.title_zh: Machine learning-based risk prediction for invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in non-neutropenic intensive care unit patients, with an exploratory analysis of pathogen-related risk factors.
papers.title_en: Machine learning-based risk prediction for invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in non-neutropenic intensive care unit patients, with an exploratory analysis of pathogen-related risk factors.
papers.authors: Bai J, Feng T, Liu B, Wang J, Wang Z, Liu F, Zhu J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Critical Care Medicine, General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University, Yinchuan, China.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) is increasingly recognized in non-neutropenic patients, but validated bedside risk stratification tools remain scarce. We developed a machine learning model to predict IPA and tested whether corticosteroid effect depends on bacterial co-pathogen. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolled 837 non-neutropenic adults hospitalized with pulmonary infections across three tertiary hospitals in China between December 2020 and December 2025. The discovery cohort was split into training and internal validation sets. Four classifiers were compared, with Random Forest selected for optimal performance. The final model was externally validated in an independent cohort. Feature importance was assessed using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis. Corticosteroid-bacteria interactions were examined using subgroup analyses and propensity score matching, with the synergy index S calculated to quantify biological interaction. A simplified bedside score was derived from the top-ranking predictors. RESULTS: The Random Forest model achieved external validation AUC of 0.865. Six predictors consistently dominated across all assessments: Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation, hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 <200 mmHg), diabetes mellitus, organ failure (Sequential Organ Failure Assessment, SOFA >5), lymphopenia (lymphocyte count <0.8×109/L), and ICU (intensive care unit) admission. Corticosteroid exposure did not rank among the top six predictors. However, its association with IPA diverged sharply by bacterial context: OR below 1 with P. aeruginosa (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.214-1.283) but OR above 1 with other Gram-negative bacilli (OR 2.17, 95% CI 0.722-6.535); P for interaction = 0.131; a directional pattern that persisted after propensity matching. The six-variable score derived from these predictors showed AUCs of 0.869 (training), 0.774 (internal validation), and 0.719 (external validation). CONCLUSIONS: IPA risk in non-neutropenic ICU patients is shaped more by bacterial co-pathogen context than by corticosteroid exposure alone. The divergent corticosteroid effects across bacterial species challenge the conventional assumption of a uniform steroid-associated risk. The externally validated six-variable score offers a practical, software-free tool to support pathogen-informed, individualized risk stratification and clinical decision-making in the ICU.

papers.title_en: Phagocytosis of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid- and RNA-containing immune complexes drives inflammatory cytokine production and endothelial dysfunction.
papers.authors: Gach JS, Kim D, Vu K, Marshall M, Cachay C, Rangwala AA, Kerster G, Tifrea D et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medicine, Division of Infectious Diseases, University of California, Irvine School of Medicine, Irvine, Ca…
papers.authors_conclusion: 含RNA的免疫复合物可能在重型COVID-19发病机制中起作用；由于致病病毒均编码核酸结合蛋白并可诱导抗体反应，核酸免疫复合物的炎症性清除也可能加重其他病毒感染。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未给出样本量、效应值、置信区间或校正信息；临床部分仅为抗N IgG:IgM比值与结局的相关性，不能证明因果；体外与微器官结果不能直接外推至体内清除过程；“其他病毒感染”属于机制外推。
papers.abstract_en: The aberrant inflammation that characterizes severe COVID-19 is incompletely understood. Given the persistence of SARS-Cov-2 RNA and nucleocapsid protein (N) and the presence of anti-N antibody during the course of severe infection, we investigated the role of RNA-containing immune complexes (ICs) in driving inflammation. We found that ICs consisting of SARS-CoV-2 RNA, N, and anti-N IgG1 are internalized by primary human monocytes and stimulate inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in a manner dependent on Fcγ receptors and partially dependent on toll-like receptor-8. In addition, the inflammatory response induced in monocytes by RNA-containing ICs caused endothelial dysfunction in vascularized micro-organs. Using nasopharyngeal samples from SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals, SARS-CoV-2 RNA and N were captured by anti-N monoclonal antibody in the absence of lysing reagents, indicating that SARS-CoV-2 RNA and N complexes are present outside of virions and cells. Finally, we found that during an early wave of COVID-19, higher anti-N IgG:IgM ratios were associated with more severe clinical outcomes, consistent with a role for inflammatory, IgG-mediated phagocytic clearance of nucleic acid-containing ICs in SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis, perhaps mitigated by non-inflammatory, IgM-mediated clearance. We conclude that RNA-containing ICs may play a role in the pathogenesis of severe COVID-19. Since all pathogenic viruses encode nucleic acid-binding proteins, such as N, and these proteins often elicit an antibody response, inflammatory clearance of nucleic acid-containing ICs may also contribute to disease severity in other viral infections.

papers.title_zh: Pulmonary Toxicity of Particulate-Phase Combustion Byproducts from Lithium-Ion Battery Fires.
papers.title_en: Pulmonary Toxicity of Particulate-Phase Combustion Byproducts from Lithium-Ion Battery Fires.
papers.authors: Nored A, Horn GP, Kesler RM, Barowy A, Schraiber A, Gaudet B, Mayer AC, Fent KW et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Center for Public Health and Environmental Assessment, United States Environmental Protection Agency, Research Triangle …
papers.abstract_en: The frequency of lithium-ion battery (LIB) fires is increasing globally, creating new challenges for firefighters and growing public safety concerns from smoke and intense heat. However, the health effects from exposure to LIB fires are not well understood. We collected soot and smoke particulate matter (PM) from LIB thermal runaway events (10 and 2 fire tests for soot and PM samples, respectively), filtered them to remove non-inhalable particles (>10 μm), analyzed for chemical composition and assessed for lung toxicity and pulmonary function in mice at 4 h and 24 h post exposure to 100 μg of the sample. Chemical and biological results were analyzed using a computational approach to identify hazardous chemical components that were potentially responsible for toxicity outcomes. Computational findings were further compared to those produced by other sources of air pollution. The soot sample contained more carbon species than the smoke PM sample (37% vs. 18%), whereas anions were higher in the PM sample (12% vs. 6%), and concentrations of inorganic elements were similar (23% vs. 28%). Fluoride particulate was found to account for up to 5% of the mass of each sample. Only soot significantly increased ventilatory timing and peak expiratory flow in mice and decreased relaxation time, while both samples caused significant increases in inflammatory responses. Soot and PM exhibited similar lung inflammatory outcomes relative to those caused by previously reported combustion-related air pollution sources. Computational analysis indicated that fluoride, Al, Fe, Ni, and Li from both samples were significantly associated with the lung toxicity responses (p < 0.05). The findings indicate that LIB fire soot and PM that contain hazardous metals and fluoride elicit pulmonary toxicity responses comparable to other sources of air pollution, increasing the need for awareness of potential strategies to mitigate public health impacts.

papers.title_zh: Associations of multiple ambient air pollutants and sleep apnea, sleep architecture and nocturnal oxygenation in adult patients with or without obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
papers.title_en: Associations of multiple ambient air pollutants and sleep apnea, sleep architecture and nocturnal oxygenation in adult patients with or without obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
papers.authors: Wang XY, Wang S, Tan X, Wu Y, Tang Y, Zhong S, Huang G, Fang J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Public Health and Preventive Medicine, School of Medicine, Jinan University, Guangzhou 510632, China.
papers.abstract_en: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects an estimated 936 million adults worldwide, yet how environmental exposures relate to sleep architecture and nocturnal oxygenation remains unclear. We conducted a retrospective polysomnography-based study of 4049 adults in Shenzhen, China, to examine the relationships of ambient air pollutants, PM2.5 inorganic components, and meteorological factors with OSA severity, sleep architecture, and nocturnal oxygenation. Lag 0-180 days was selected post hoc as the main reporting window. Within this window, PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, and diurnal temperature range (DTR) were all linked to greater OSA severity. Multiple pollutants were associated with lighter sleep; for example, PM2.5 and PM10 were associated with 1.71%TST and 1.32%TST increases in N1 sleep and 1.51%TST and 1.32%TST decreases in N3 sleep, respectively. O3 and DTR showed the clearest adverse relationships with nocturnal oxygenation and sleep continuity. Non-linear analyses showed increasing exposure-response associations for PM2.5, SO2, and DTR, but a U-shaped association for O3. Interaction and mixture analyses further indicated meteorological modification and more consistent mixture relationships with altered sleep architecture than with categorical OSA severity. These findings highlight the importance of broader polysomnographic dimensions, cumulative exposure windows, and co-exposure patterns in future research.

papers.title_zh: T cell Cyp27b1 promotes granzyme B expression and antiviral host defense in a mouse model of H1N1 influenza A virus infection.
papers.title_en: T cell Cyp27b1 promotes granzyme B expression and antiviral host defense in a mouse model of H1N1 influenza A virus infection.
papers.authors: Froelich NE, Tang M, Hanna NJ, Sutton TC, Meyer MB, Cantorna MT
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Veterinary and Biomedical Sciences, The Pennsylvania State University, University Park, PA, United States.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Immune cells express vitamin D receptors (VDR) and the CYP27B1 enzyme needed to produce the VDR ligand, 1,25(OH)2D; suggesting that perhaps the vitamin D response is regulated locally at the site of infection. Here, we examined the role of immune cell-derived 1,25(OH)2D in host resistance to influenza infection. METHODS: Mice were infected with mouse-adapted H1N1 influenza A virus, to determine the role of CYP27B1 on host resistance to influenza infection. The mouse strains infected include; wild type (WT) littermates, whole-body Cyp27b1 knockout (Cyp27b1 KO) mice, mice lacking renal 1,25(OH)2D production (double intronic (DI)KO), mice with T cell-specific deletion of Cyp27b1 (T-Cyp27b1 KO), and mice with T cell-specific deletion of Vdr (T-Vdr KO). RESULTS: Whole body Cyp27b1 KO mice developed severe influenza A virus disease, including infection induced mortality, compared to WT littermates. Oral treatments of the Cyp27b1 KO mice with 1,25(OH)2D failed to completely protect the Cyp27b1 KO mice from influenza A virus disease. Mice without renal 1,25(OH)2D had similar influenza disease as WT littermates. Influenza infection of T cell-specific Cyp27b1 KO resulted in increased respiratory distress and lethargy compared to WT littermates. WT and DIKO mice had more CD8+ T cells expressing higher amounts of granzyme B+ (GrzB) and disruptions in PD-1 than either whole-body Cyp27b1 KO or T-Cyp27b1 KO mice. DISCUSSION: The work suggests that renal 1,25(OH)2D is not required for host resistance to this influenza A virus infection. The work further demonstrates that immune cells and in particular T cells may produce 1,25(OH)2D to locally support CD8+ T cell responses to influenza A virus infection. Defining the mechanisms that regulate local 1,25(OH)2D production in T cells or other immune cell types is needed.

papers.title_zh: Sex steroids differentially modulate SARS-CoV-2-induced inflammatory responses in endothelial and immune cells.
papers.title_en: Sex steroids differentially modulate SARS-CoV-2-induced inflammatory responses in endothelial and immune cells.
papers.authors: Bižić-Radulović S, Subotički T, Kovačević A, Živković E, Popović O, Mitrović-Ajtić O, Diklić M, Jovanović S et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Molecular Oncology, Clinic of Hematology, University Clinical Center of Serbia, Belgrade, Serbia.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Sex-related differences in coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity suggest an important role for sex steroids in regulating immune and endothelial responses to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). METHODS: Receptor expression, inflammatory signaling, and monocyte transendothelial migration were assessed by RT-PCR, immunoblotting, and Boyden chamber assay, respectively. HULEC-5a and primary human immune cells were exposed to in vitro-amplified SARS-CoV-2. Samples were collected between June 2020 and April 2022, with sample sizes based on primary sample availability and independent experiments. RESULTS: SARS-CoV-2 differentially regulates estrogen receptor gene expression, decreasing it in endothelial cells (p<0.05) while increasing it in immune cells (p<0.01). SARS-CoV-2 generally activated inflammatory signaling pathways, including NFκB, STAT3, and p38 MAPK, in THP-1 monocytic cells (up to 1.9-fold). The NFκB response was augmented by the androgen receptor agonist dihydrotestosterone (DHT, 44.6%) and attenuated by the androgen receptor antagonist flutamide (44.1%). In endothelial cells, DHT twice reduced SARS-CoV-2 activation of the p38 MAPK signaling pathway. β-estradiol inhibited (2.2-fold), whereas DHT stimulated (4.9-fold) NFκB signaling pathway in neutrophils isolated from patients with COVID-19. SARS-CoV-2 activation of inflammatory signaling pathways deteriorates over time in monocytes from patients with COVID-19 (p<0.05). Furthermore, DHT significantly increased trans-endothelial migration of monocytes (p<0.001) and detachment of SARS-CoV-2 exposed endothelial cells (p<0.01), suggesting a potential role for androgen-responsive pathways in endothelial dysfunction and immune cell trafficking. DISCUSSION: These findings elucidate the molecular mechanisms driving male-biased COVID-19 severity and underscore the potential of targeting androgen-responsive pathways as a therapeutic strategy to mitigate severe viral inflammation and endothelial dysfunction.

papers.title_zh: Clinical utility of circulating tumor cell PD-L1 expression for predicting immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in esophageal cancer.
papers.title_en: Clinical utility of circulating tumor cell PD-L1 expression for predicting immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in esophageal cancer.
papers.authors: Li J, Li Y, Chen L, Yang Z, Lu Y, Tang D, Qin Y
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Oncology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, longhu zhonghuan road, No.1, Zhengzhou, H…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in esophageal cancer, yet reliable biomarkers remain lacking. Tissue PD-L1 testing is limited by intratumoral heterogeneity and invasiveness, whereas circulating tumor cells (CTCs) offer a non-invasive alternative. This study evaluated CTC PD-L1 expression as a predictive and prognostic biomarker in patients with advanced esophageal cancer receiving chemo-immunotherapy. METHODS: A total of 93 patients with stage III-IV esophageal cancer were enrolled. The primary biomarker analysis was restricted to 59 patients who received chemo-immunotherapy, while 34 patients treated with chemotherapy alone were analyzed separately. Baseline CTCs were isolated and PD-L1 expression assessed, alongside tissue PD-L1 (tPD-L1) by immunohistochemistry. Associations with objective response rate (ORR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using ROC curves and univariate and multivariable Cox regression. RESULTS: CTC positivity correlated significantly with advanced stage, metastasis (p = 0.0411), and larger tumor size (p = 0.0454). In the chemo-immunotherapy cohort, CTC PD-L1 positivity was associated with a higher ORR (75.0% vs. 29.6%, p < 0.001) and showed moderate predictive ability (AUC = 0.7049, p = 0.0037). CTC PD-L1 positivity was significantly associated with OS (HR = 0.254, p = 0.002), but not significantly with PFS in univariate analysis (HR = 0.546, p = 0.042; Kaplan-Meier p = 0.061). Conversely, tPD-L1 status was not significantly associated with PFS or OS (both p > 0.05). In multivariable analysis adjusting for age, sex, histological subtype, stage, metastasis, and treatment modality, CTC PD-L1 remained an independent prognostic factor for PFS (HR = 0.488, p = 0.039) and OS (HR = 0.244, p = 0.002). CONCLUSIONS: Baseline CTC PD-L1 expression was associated with favorable response and OS in patients receiving chemo-immunotherapy, and may complement tissue testing. These exploratory findings require prospective validation in larger cohorts before clinical use.

papers.authors: Yan M, Liu Y, Deng M, Pi D, Zhu J, Yu Q, Huang C, Ran Q et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pediatrics & Neonatology, Daping Hospital, Army Medical University, Chongqing 400042, China.

papers.abstract_en: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) undergo functional reprogramming that critically regulates lung inflammation. Although mitophagy is essential for mitochondrial quality control, its role in macrophage functional reprogramming during acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains unclear. Here, we identify the nuclear receptor Nr1h4 (FXR) as a transcriptional regulator of mitophagy in AMs. FXR activation transcriptionally upregulates serine palmitoyltransferase long chain base subunit 2 (Sptlc2), thereby enhancing mitophagy and promoting an anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotype under inflammatory conditions. The FXR/Sptlc2 axis reduces oxidative stress and inflammatory mediator production while increasing anti-inflammatory markers. Conversely, FXR deficiency impairs mitophagy, exacerbates pulmonary inflammation, and aggravates lung injury in vivo. These findings establish the FXR/Sptlc2 axis as a regulator of mitochondrial quality control and macrophage functional reprogramming and identify it as a potential therapeutic target in ARDS.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Health Sciences and Technology, GAIHST, Gachon University, Incheon 21999, Republic of Korea.
papers.authors_conclusion: SD-2102抑制PDK1/Akt信号并对肺癌细胞表现出优先的抗癌活性，支持其作为抗癌药物进一步开发。

papers.abstract_en: The phosphoinositide-dependent kinase-1 (PDK1)-Akt signaling pathway plays a central role in regulating diverse cellular processes, including cell growth, survival, and metabolism. Dysregulation of this pathway is frequently observed in malignancies and is associated with tumor progression and resistance to therapy. Despite the recognized therapeutic potential of PDK1, potent and selective inhibitors remain limited. In this study, we developed and characterized a novel PDK1 inhibitor, SD-2102, and evaluated its anticancer effects in vitro and in vivo. A novel small-molecule compound, SD-2102, was synthesized and screened for PDK1 inhibitory activity. Binding affinity and interaction sites were examined using biochemical assays to identify the targeted domain. Functional assays, including cell proliferation, cell cycle analysis, and apoptosis detection, were performed in cancer cell lines. The in vivo efficacy of SD-2102 was assessed using a xenograft model. SD-2102 was predicted to interact with the pleckstrin homology domain of PDK1 and reduced PDK1 plasma membrane translocation. This inhibition led to decreased phosphorylation and activation of Akt. In vitro, SD-2102 suppressed cancer cell proliferation by inducing G1 phase arrest and promoting apoptosis. Importantly, SD-2102 induced minimal apoptosis in BEAS-2B non-tumorigenic human bronchial epithelial cells, supporting a preferential apoptotic effect toward lung cancer cells. In vivo, treatment with SD-2102 significantly reduced tumor growth in the xenograft model, consistent with the cellular findings. Together, these findings suggest that SD-2102 suppresses PDK1/Akt signaling while exhibiting preferential anticancer activity in lung cancer cells, supporting its further development as an anticancer agent.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Precision Medicine, University of Campania Luigi Vanvitelli, Naples, Italy.
papers.authors_conclusion: 通过剖析MYC致癌活性在不同分子亚型间的差异，本综述旨在提示可改善特定患者人群临床结局的靶向干预新机会；并强调在 distinct MYC-driven subtypes 内靶向分子脆弱性。

papers.abstract_en: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is one of the most aggressive and rapidly progressing forms of lung cancer, characterized by its high proliferative rate and strong tendency to metastasize. Although SCLC initially responds well to platinum-based chemotherapy, resistance typically develops quickly, leaving few effective options and resulting in poor overall survival. Immunotherapies, including PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors have been introduced in clinical settings and other drugs, such as antibody-drug conjugates, are being actively studied, but their efficacy has so far been limited. Despite a shared genetic foundation, most notably the near-universal loss of tumor suppressor genes TP53 and RB1, alongside frequent over-activation of the MYC family of oncogenes (MYC, MYCN, MYCL), SCLC exhibits remarkable diversity at the molecular level. Historically, classification of SCLC was based on the presence or absence of neuroendocrine features. However, recent advances have shifted the paradigm toward a transcription factor-driven framework that defines molecular subtypes. One of the key areas of current investigation is understanding the multifaceted role of oncogenic activation of MYC family members in SCLC biology. Given its prominent involvement in driving certain subtypes of the disease, it represents a critical axis of vulnerability that may be exploited for therapeutic use. By dissecting how MYC oncogenic activity varies across molecular subtypes, this review aims to highlight novel opportunities for targeted interventions that could improve clinical outcomes for specific patient populations. This review explores the underlying mechanisms that drive SCLC initiation and progression, focusing on tumor heterogeneity, immune landscape, and especially the role of oncogenic MYC in promoting metastasis and therapeutic resistance. We further explore how recent insights into these processes are shaping emerging treatment strategies, with an emphasis on targeting molecular vulnerabilities within distinct MYC-driven subtypes.

papers.authors: Abuduxukuer Z, Zhu L, Li D, Zhu G, Zeng Y, Chen Y, Mo Y, Cai H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Allergy, Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, 200032, China.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dysregulated epithelial alarmin release is a key driver of chronic airway inflammation in asthma. Interleukin-33 (IL-33), released from activated airway epithelial cells, amplifies type 2 immune responses, yet the upstream mechanisms that link epithelial stress to IL-33 secretion remain incompletely defined. We investigated whether circGDI2 contributed to epithelial IL-33 release and allergic airway inflammation. METHODS: circGDI2 expression was examined in IL-13-stimulated BEAS-2B cells. Its functional role was evaluated in a house dust mite (HDM)-induced murine asthma model using adeno-associated virus-mediated circGDI2 knockdown, miR-103a-3p agomir, and NLRP3 siRNA. Molecular interactions were assessed by dual-luciferase reporter assays, RNA pull-down, and fluorescence in situ hybridization. NLRP3 inflammasome activation was monitored by cleaved caspase-1 p20, mature IL-1β, and IL-18 secretion, along with LDH release. RESULTS: circGDI2 was upregulated in IL-13-stimulated BEAS-2B cells. circGDI2 silencing alleviated airway inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and remodeling, and reduced type 2 immune responses in HDM-exposed mice. Mechanistically, circGDI2 sponged miR-103a-3p to derepress NLRP3 and promoted epithelial IL-33 release, accompanied by increased cleaved caspase-1 p20 and mature IL-1β and IL-18 secretion together with only a limited and NLRP3-dependent increase in LDH release. Consistent with this, miR-103a-3p restoration, NLRP3 knockdown, or MCC950 treatment each attenuated airway inflammation and IL-33 release, confirming the circGDI2/miR-103a-3p/NLRP3 axis. CONCLUSIONS: circGDI2 promotes allergic airway inflammation by enhancing epithelial IL-33 release through the miR-103a-3p/NLRP3 pathway. These findings support circGDI2 as an upstream regulator of inflammatory responses in experimental asthma.

papers.title_en: HSPA12B modulates lung injury and neutrophil-related inflammatory responses in LPS-induced acute lung injury: a potential link to the PKC-PAD4 pathway.
papers.authors: Wu W, Lin Y, Bian Y, Lin D, Wei Y, Zhang X, Liu J, Zeng H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: The Department of Anesthesiology, Fuzhou First General Hospital Affiliated with Fujian Medical University, Fuzhou, Fujia…
papers.authors_conclusion: HSPA12B在LPS诱导的ALI中与PKC-PAD4级联及中性粒细胞介导的肺损伤存在功能联系；HSPA12B是进一步机制研究的潜在上游调控节点，为未来ALI/ARDS中HSPA12B靶向研究提供基础。
papers.ai_note: 摘要自述PKC-PAD4联系为提出而非直接证实，且缺乏同工酶特异性与活性水平证据；过表达/敲低结果以伴随性描述为主，未报告样本量、对照设置、统计值或盲法，因果推断受限；研究为临床前ALI模型，无肿瘤或胸科肿瘤临床数据。
papers.abstract_en: Acute lung injury (ALI) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are life-threatening conditions with high mortality. Excessive neutrophil activation and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-related responses, together with pulmonary endothelial barrier impairment, are critical pathological features. Heat shock protein A12B (HSPA12B) has endothelial-protective and anti-inflammatory functions, but its relationship with the PKC-PAD4 pathway and neutrophil-associated lung injury remains unclear. In this study, we combined bioinformatics analysis with an LPS-induced ALI mouse model to examine whether HSPA12B expression is associated with PKC-PAD4 pathway activation and neutrophil-related lung injury. HSPA12B overexpression was associated with reduced pathological lung damage, lower levels of inflammatory cytokines and oxidative stress markers, as well as decreased lung-tissue levels of PKC, PAD4 and neutrophil-associated markers (CitH3, MPO, NE). Conversely, HSPA12B knockdown was accompanied by elevated protein levels of PKC, aggravated lung injury, and further upregulation of these markers; transcriptomic analysis of lungs from HSPA12B-knockdown mice revealed enrichment of the neutrophil extracellular trap formation pathway. These findings indicate that HSPA12B is functionally linked to the PKC-PAD4 cascade and neutrophil-mediated lung injury in LPS-induced ALI. Of note, the PKC-PAD4 link is proposed rather than directly demonstrated, and that isoform-specific and activity-level evidence is still lacking. This study identifies HSPA12B as a potential upstream regulatory node for further mechanistic investigation, providing a basis for future HSPA12B-targeted studies in ALI/ARDS.

papers.abstract_en: Right ventricular (RV) failure is the major cause of mortality in pulmonary hypertension (PH). Adaptive angiogenesis and RV endothelial cell (RVEC) function are major modifiers of RV adaptation in PH, but the underlying mechanisms and their regulators remain incompletely understood. RV adaptation in PH is sexually dimorphic, and 17β-estradiol (E2) exerts protective effects on RV cardiomyocytes. Whether E2 modifies angiogenesis and RVEC function in RV failure remains unknown. We hypothesized that E2 and estrogen receptor α (ERα) promote RV angiogenesis and RVEC homeostasis in PH and aimed to identify underlying mechanisms. We assessed E2's angiogenic effects using cultured human cardiac microvascular endothelial cells (hCMVECs), RVECs from PH patients with RV failure, and RVECs from sugen/hypoxia (SuHx) and monocrotaline rat models. In vivo, we evaluated RV capillary density in PH rats treated with E2 or ERα-selective agonist. Apelin signaling was evaluated via apelin receptor (APLNR) blockade and knockdown studies. E2 preserved angiogenesis in male hCMVECs and RV capillary density in male and female SuHx-PH rats. E2 reversed angiogenic alterations in RVECs from SuHx-PH rats via APLNR signaling. In RVECs from RV failure patients, E2 stimulated vascular network formation. In rat and human PH-RVECs, ERα was necessary and sufficient to mediate E2-induced angiogenesis. Activation of ERα with ERα-specific agonist restored RV capillary density in vivo. ERα-mediated angiogenesis required apelin signaling. These data indicate that E2 promotes RV angiogenesis via ERα and apelin signaling and identify a novel ERα-apelin axis in RVECs as a potential therapeutic target to restore RV vascular integrity in PH.

papers.authors: Martin-Loeches I, Povoa P, Robba C, Bandera A, Guglielmi A, Citerio G
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Intensive Care Medicine, Multidisciplinary Intensive Care Research Organization (MICRO), St James' Hospita…

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is frequent after traumatic brain injury (TBI), but its biological meaning and outcome impact remain incompletely defined. Traditional models emphasise mechanical ventilation, aspiration, colonisation, endotracheal tube biofilm, and hospital pathogens. These mechanisms remain essential, but they do not fully explain the early clustering, heterogeneous susceptibility, changing bacteriology, and variable mortality effect observed after TBI. MAIN TEXT: Severe brain injury creates an early vulnerable host state through impaired consciousness and airway protection, neuroimmune dysregulation, autonomic and endocrine activation, altered pulmonary immune surveillance, and, in many patients, extracranial trauma, shock, transfusion, or thoracic injury. These processes interact with ventilation, antibiotic pressure, and rapid respiratory microbiome disruption. Early VAP may reflect abrupt loss of control after injury and intubation, whereas late VAP may reflect persistent or secondary failure driven by biofilm maturation, antibiotic selection, multidrug-resistant pathogens, and intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired immune dysfunction. Clinically, VAP consistently prolongs ventilation, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and resource use, while its independent effect on mortality is phenotype- and context-dependent. CONCLUSIONS: This model proposes a timing-sensitive ecological framework in which established mechanisms may converge early and with particular clinical intensity after severe TBI, creating a vulnerable host-microbe state that may lower the threshold for clinically apparent infection. Future studies should distinguish isolated TBI from polytrauma, compare TBI with other acute brain injuries and non-neurological ventilated populations, and incorporate dynamic immune, microbial, and trajectory-based outcomes. HIGHLIGHTS: VAP after TBI should be viewed as a timing-sensitive interaction between ventilator exposure and early host vulnerability, not as a distinct disease entity or as a pneumonia pathway unique to traumatic brain injury. The TBI-focused contribution lies in the early convergence of otherwise non-unique mechanisms: impaired airway control, aspiration risk, neuroimmune-endocrine activation, treatment exposure, dysbiosis, and extracranial injury burden, rather than in any single TBI-specific mechanism. Isolated TBI and TBI with polytrauma are biologically different phenotypes and should be separated in future studies. Early and late VAP may represent different phases of loss of pulmonary host-microbe containment; this distinction is probabilistic rather than TBI-specific in itself and requires validation in TBI-stratified cohorts. Mortality remains clinically relevant but context-dependent; VAP more consistently modifies recovery trajectory, ventilator dependence, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and possibly neurological recovery.

papers.abstract_en: Although SerpinE3, an extracellular serine protease inhibitor, has been documented in several studies, its biological function remains largely undefined. In a screen for interactors of TMPRSS11E-a protease known to exacerbate inflammation and lung injury during infection-we identified a novel interaction with SerpinE3. Initially, we assessed the inhibitory effect of SerpinE3 on TMPRSS11E activity using synthetic fluorescent substrates PAR1 and PAR2 peptides. We further characterized SerpinE3 expression patterns in mouse cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) models of inflammation and in patients with pneumonia. Subsequently, the anti-inflammatory effects of SerpinE3 were investigated in both in vitro and in vivo inflammatory models. Finally, we examined the regulatory mechanisms governing SerpinE3 expression via promoter activity assays and electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSA). Our results demonstrate that SerpinE3 directly inhibits TMPRSS11E activity. SerpinE3 expression was significantly upregulated in alveolar and liver macrophages under inflammatory conditions. Administration of recombinant SerpinE3 protein markedly alleviated inflammation and acute lung injury in the mouse CLP model. Conversely, SerpinE3 knockout mice exhibited aggravated lung injury, a phenotype that was rescued by recombinant protein administration. Notably, aged SerpinE3 knockout mice displayed a spontaneous accumulation of inflammatory cells in the lungs. Mechanistically, we identified a functional NF-κB response element within the proximal promoter of SerpinE3. In conclusion, we identify SerpinE3 as an infection-inducible, macrophage-derived regulator that attenuates inflammatory lung injury, likely through the inhibition of TMPRSS11E. This study elucidates a critical anti-inflammatory role for SerpinE3 and paves the way for developing SerpinE3-based therapies for inflammatory acute lung injury.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To access whether a structured, facility-level quality improvement (QI) approach using an adapted tuberculosis (TB) Building and Strengthening Infection Control Strategies (TB BASICS) methodology could improve TB infection prevention and control (IPC) practices in outpatient TB clinics in Vietnam. METHODS: From October 2022 to September 2023, 11 health care facilities in Ho Chi Minh City implemented QI interventions with local experts' mentorship. A context- adapted assessment evaluated 103 indicators across four IPC domains. Baseline and final assessments were conducted before and after six months of QI implementation, with progress measured by percent change in average scores. RESULTS: All IPC domains improved across all facilities. Environmental controls showed the largest improvement (89.6%), followed by respiratory protection (62.4%), IPC core components (57.7%), and administrative controls (31.0%). Low-cost ventilation measures contributed to ≥12 air changes per hour in 20 of 34 (58.8%) targeted areas. Improvements were also observed in IPC guidelines, compliance monitoring, respiratory protection policies, fit testing; although gaps in patient fast-tracking, separation practices, and respirator availability remained. CONCLUSIONS: A structured, mentor- supported, tailored QI initiative was associated with improved TB IPC practices and provides a scalable framework for strengthening TB IPC in health care settings vulnerable to TB and other airborne threats.

papers.ai_note: 摘要仅以“significantly”表述抑制效应，未给出任何效应量、浓度、P值或置信区间，无法判断效应大小与剂量关系；结论完全建立在单一细胞系、单一刺激（TNF-α）模型上，缺乏原代细胞或体内验证；TAK1依赖性为通路层面的间接推断，摘要未说明是否采用TAK1过表达/敲低或抑制剂进行因果验证；未见细胞毒性对照说明，不能排除6-HR的非特异抑制；与胸部肿瘤临床决策距离远，属基础机制探索。
papers.abstract_en: In this study, we aimed to investigate whether 6-hydroxyrubiadin (6-HR), a compound derived from the root of Rubia akane Nakai, exerts a regulatory effect on the gene expression of MUC5AC mucin under conditions mimicking pulmonary inflammation in human airway epithelial cells. Confluent NCI-H292 cells were pretreated with 6-HR for 30 min, followed by stimulation with tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α for 24 h. MUC5AC mRNA expression and glycoprotein production were measured using reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), respectively. Further, we examined the effect of 6-HR on TNF-α-induced activation of the nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathways via immunoblot analysis. The results were as follows: (1) 6-HR significantly reduced both the production of MUC5AC glycoprotein and MUC5AC mRNA expression in NCI-H292 cells. (2) 6-HR inhibited TNF-α-induced NF-κB activation through a transforming growth factor-β-activated kinase 1 (TAK1)-dependent mechanism. (3) 6-HR also inhibited TAK1-dependent MAPK signaling pathways activated by TNF-α, resulting in the downregulation of MUC5AC mucin production in NCI-H292 cells. These findings suggest that 6-HR regulates the gene expression of MUC5AC mucin by directly acting on airway epithelial cells through modulation of the MAPK and NF-κB signaling pathways.

papers.title_en: Factors associated with acceptance of preventive treatment among older adults with latent tuberculosis infection in Huzhou, Zhejiang province: a cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Yang Z, Zu Z, Sun X, Chen X, Wang W, Zheng P, Wen D, Ren F et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of HIV/TB Control and Prevention, Huzhou Center for Disease Control and Prevention, Huzhou, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: 湖州≥60岁LTBI老年人TPT接受率相对较高；接受度与家庭结构、经济状况和健康状况独立相关；家庭人口数较小（≤3人）、年家庭收入较低（≤150,000元）及存在基础疾病者接受TPT的可能性更高；应针对大家庭、经济条件较好及无基础疾病的老年人制定针对性干预策略以提高TPT总体覆盖
papers.ai_note: 横断面设计无法确定暴露与接受TPT的时序和因果方向，文中'独立相关'只能作关联解读；69.35%的接受率被表述为'相对较高'，但缺少可比参照或预设阈值；仅报告'是否接受'，未报告治疗启动后完成率、不良事件与拒绝原因，也未说明筛查受邀人群的应答比例，存在选择偏倚可能；多因素模型变量筛选过程、共线性与多重比较未见交代；结论中针对特定人群的干预建议属外推性推论，摘要未提供干预效果数据
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the acceptance of Tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) and the factors associated with treatment acceptance among individuals aged ≥60 years that screened positive for latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) in Huzhou city, Zhejiang Province of China, and to provide scientific evidence for TPT implementation in this population. METHODS: Older adults aged ≥60 years with LTBI were recruited through community-based health examinations and screening of close contacts of active tuberculosis patients. Univariate and multivariate Logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with TPT acceptance. RESULTS: Of the 620 participants enrolled, 430 (69.35%) accepted TPT. Among the participants, 354 (57.09%) were male, 192 (30.96%) were aged over 70 years, 593 (95.65%) were married, 499 (80.48%) resided in rural areas, 577 (93.06%) had an education level of junior high school or below, 135 (21.77%) smoked daily or occasionally, and 152 (24.52%) consumed alcohol occasionally or at least twice weekly. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis revealed that participants with a household size of ≤3 persons (aOR: 1.88; 95% CI: 1.15-3.07), an annual household income of ≤150, 000 CNY (aOR: 2.24; 95% CI: 1.33-3.77), and a history of underlying diseases (aOR: 1.86; 95% CI: 1.16-2.99) were more likely to accept TPT. CONCLUSION: The TPT acceptance rate among older adults aged ≥60 years with LTBI in Huzhou was relatively high. Acceptance was independently associated with household structure, economic status, and health status. Smaller household size (≤3 persons), lower annual household income (≤150, 000 CNY), and the presence of underlying diseases were independently associated with TPT acceptance in this population. Targeted intervention strategies should be developed for older adults from larger households, those with better economic conditions, and those without underlying diseases to improve overall TPT coverage.

papers.ai_note: 本文为叙述性综述，摘要未交代文献检索策略、纳入排除标准与证据分级方法，却使用“批判性评价当前证据”的表述，评价强度与方法透明度不匹配；虽声称区分“直接来自结核模型的证据”与“由其他疾病外推的证据”，但摘要中无任何可核验的量化结果或证据表格线索；所提“循证分层”“严谨试验设计”属倡议性主张，非本研究产出；主题为结核病免疫调节，与胸部肿瘤外科诊疗决策关联有限。信息不足，无法评估偏倚风险。
papers.abstract_en: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global public health challenge, with treatment complicated by drug resistance, adverse effects, and suboptimal host immune responses. Whilst conventional anti-TB drugs are effective bactericidally, their immunomodulatory effects may, in certain contexts, contribute to immune imbalance and affect treatment outcomes. Host-directed therapy (HDT), which aims to modulate the host immune response to enhance pathogen control and limit immunopathology, has emerged as a promising adjunctive strategy. This narrative review critically evaluates the current evidence for HDT in TB, focusing on immunosenescence, trained immunity, cytokine and lipid mediator networks, immunometabolic reprogramming, neuroendocrine regulation, and repurposed drugs including metformin and statins. Importantly, we distinguish between evidence derived directly from TB models (in vitro, animal, and clinical studies) and evidence extrapolated from other diseases, highlighting knowledge gaps and areas requiring further investigation. We propose that future progress depends on evidence-based stratification of HDT candidates, rigorous clinical trial design, and a personalised approach that accounts for patient comorbidities and immune status. This review aims to provide a balanced framework for advancing HDT from bench to bedside in TB therapy.

papers.title_zh: Pragmatic trial of a self-directed intervention for weight loss in obstructive sleep apnea (POWER).
papers.title_en: Pragmatic trial of a self-directed intervention for weight loss in obstructive sleep apnea (POWER).
papers.authors: Donovan LM, McDowell JA, Maskey P, Josey K, Bais AF, Plumley R, Dashtestani K, Leonhard AG et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Seattle-Denver Center of Innovation for Veteran-Centered and Value-Driven Care, Veterans Affairs Puget Sound Health Care…
papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Self-directed lifestyle interventions may improve access to weight loss care in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but effectiveness in routine practice is unknown. OBJECTIVE: Test whether a proactively delivered self-directed lifestyle intervention improves weight and sleep-related quality of life versus usual care. METHODS: POWER enrolled patients with OSA and body mass index of 30-45 kg/m2, recruited from Veteran Affairs (VA) sites nationwide, and randomized participants to a self-directed intervention based on the Diabetes Prevention Program with video-based sessions, readings, and regular coaching reminders or usual care. Co-primary outcomes were change in Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire (FOSQ) and clinical weight in kilograms (kg) from baseline to 12 months post-randomization. Given two primary outcomes, we defined significance at p = 0.025. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: This trial randomized 696 participants. Mean age was 56.2 years (SD 12.2), with 19.7% identifying as female. Clinical weights at 12 months were available for 81.9% of intervention and 83.6% of control participants. Unadjusted weight declined 2.1 kg (SD 6.8) in intervention and 0.9 kg (SD 5.9) in control (adjusted between-group difference: -1.1 kg, 95%CI -2.0, -0.1; p = 0.037). FOSQ measures were available at 12 months for 78.2% of intervention and 90.5% of control participants. From baseline to 12 months, unadjusted FOSQ improved 1.4 (SD 2.7) points in intervention and 0.9 (SD 2.9) points in control (adjusted between-group difference: 0.6 points, 95%CI 0.2, 1.0; p = 0.001). CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Among participants with OSA and obesity, a self-directed lifestyle intervention did not improve weight loss and led to improvements in sleep-related quality of life that are of limited clinical importance. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT05104450, registered 10/19/2021.

papers.title_en: Clinician-guided digital CBT-I improves sleep quality and apnea severity in patients with co-morbid insomnia and OSA: A Double-Blind, Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.authors: Shi Y, Feng X, Chen Z, Guan S, Zhang Y, Lei F, Zhang X, Jiang Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Sleep Medicine Center, Mental Health Center, National Center for Mental Disorders, Sleep Research Laboratory, West China…
papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the accepted first-line treatment for insomnia, but its scalability and safety in patients with co-morbid insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea (COMISA) remain unclear. Clinician-guided digital CBT-I (D-CBT-I) is a potential treatment option that may address these limitations in COMISA. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of clinician-guided D-CBT-I versus sleep hygiene education (SHE) in patients with COMISA. METHODS: This randomized trial (n = 88) compared clinician-guided D-CBT-I (6 weekly online sessions: sleep restriction, sleep hygiene, stimulus control, cognitive restructuring, relapse prevention) with SHE alone. Blinded outcome assessments were conducted at baseline, posttreatment (6 weeks), and 3-month follow-up. Primary outcomes were Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scores at posttreatment and 3-month follow-up. Secondary outcomes included daytime sleepiness, sleep parameters, OSA severity, neurocognitive function, and adverse events. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: At 3-month follow-up, intention-to-treat analysis showed significantly greater improvements with D-CBT-I versus SHE on ISI (-9.5 vs. -4.0 points; d = -1.18, P = 0.001) and PSQI (-4.9 vs. -1.8 points; d = -0.87, P = 0.001); D-CBT-I also reduced subjective sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale; -3.4 vs. -1.0 points; d = -0.68, P < 0.001). At posttreatment, D-CBT-I reduced the apnea-hypopnea index (attended in-laboratory polysomnography; -6.0 vs. +2.0 events/h; d = -0.64, P = 0.019). Although transient increases in ESS occurred at weeks 2-4, no functional impairment or sleepiness-related adverse events were reported. Additional benefits were observed in metacognition and executive function. CONCLUSION: Clinician-guided D-CBT-I improved insomnia and OSA severity, and enhanced cognitive function in COMISA patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry; NO.: ChiCTR2500099854; URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=267457.

papers.authors: Liu Z, Wu Q, Lin H, Yang D, Tang C, Lu X, Zhao Y, Chen J et al.

papers.ai_note: 摘要仅报告发现队列C指数，未给出独立验证队列的C指数、风险比或95%CI/ P值，验证性能仅有定性表述；未与TNM分期或现有病理预后模型做头对头比较；'超越传统组织学分级'缺乏量化证据；HCC与LUAD合并建模未分层报告各自性能；'8个生物标志物'的筛选过程、多重检验校正及过拟合控制信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: The clinical adoption of deep learning in pathology is largely hindered by the "black box" nature of current models, which often obscure the biological basis of prognosis. Here, we introduce MorphX, an interpretable framework that predicts patient survival by explicitly decoding multi-scale morphological patterns from whole-slide images. Unlike conventional methods relying on latent features, MorphX fuses macro-scale tissue texture with micro-scale nuclear metrics to attribute risk to interpretable biological phenotypes. In a multi-center study spanning 1,067 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), MorphX achieves concordance indices of 0.775-0.799 in discovery cohorts. Crucially, we derive eight distinct morphology-based biomarkers-driven by texture heterogeneity in necrotic regions, lymphocyte density, and nuclear shape-that demonstrate reproducible survival associations across independent cohorts, offering a granular resolution of tumor aggressiveness that transcends traditional histological grading. By translating opaque computational predictions into validated biological insights, MorphX supports trustworthy, transparent, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven precision oncology.

papers.title_en: Chlorhexidine within a standardized oral-care bundle for the prevention of ventilator-associated pneumonia: a pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover trial in six medical intensive care units.
papers.authors: Anushapreethi S, Chhotray P, Samal S, Panda S, Patnaik R, Mishra SB
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Critical Care Medicine, Institute of Medical Sciences and SUM Hospital, Siksha 'O' Anusandhan (Deemed to b…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chlorhexidine (CHX) has been a long-standing component of oral-care bundles for preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), but recent evidence has questioned its benefit in non-cardiac-surgery ICU. We evaluated whether adding 0.12% CHX to standardized oral-care bundle provides incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover (AB/BA) trial in six adult medical ICUs of a single tertiary-care academic hospital in Bhubaneswar, India. ICUs were randomized as three ICUs of two Period of 9 months with the multicomponent oral-care bundle without chlorhexidine and three with the same bundle plus 0.12% chlorhexidine with a 1-month wash-in and re-training interval. Consecutive adults ventilated for ≥ 48 h were included. The primary outcome was VAP incidence density (Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) > 6) as per 1,000 ventilator-days. Secondary outcomes were 28-day all-cause mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, 28- day ventilator-free days, Beck Oral Assessment Scale (BOAS) and Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT) scores. The primary model was a population-averaged Poisson generalized estimating equation (GEE) and adjustment for treatment, period, sequence, age, sex, APACHE II, and SOFA. RESULTS: A total of 1,035 patients (637 No CHX, 398 CHX) accrued 10,024 ventilator-days (5,918 vs. 4,106). Groups were well balanced at baseline (mean age ≈ 55 years; APACHE II ≈ 19.6; SOFA ≈ 13.4). VAP occurred in 100/5,918 ventilator-days (16.9 per 1,000) vs. 77/4,106 (18.8 per 1,000) (No CHX vs. CHX). The adjusted Poisson incidence rate ratio was 1.08 (95% CI 0.84-1.38; p = 0.56). 28-day mortality was 28.7% vs. 26.4% (no CHX vs. CHX) (adjusted OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65-1.15; p = 0.33). ICU length of stay was longer in the CHX arm (adjusted mean difference + 0.89 days, 95% CI + 0.19 to + 1.58; p = 0.013). BOAS and CPOT scores did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, adding 0.12% chlorhexidine to a standardized oral-care bundle did not reduce VAP incidence density or 28-day mortality and was associated with a modest increase in ICU length of stay. Routine CHX use provided no clear incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU population. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Regisrty- India (CTRI) identifier [CTRI/2024/02/062201], registered [01 February 2024].

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Depemokimab is the first ultra-long-acting biologic, with enhanced interleukin-5 binding affinity, high potency, and extended half-life, enabling twice-yearly dosing. The double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3a SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 studies demonstrated depemokimab efficacy and safety over 52 weeks in patients with asthma with type 2 inflammation and an eosinophilic phenotype. Here, we present long-term safety and efficacy outcomes over the 52-week, phase 3a open-label extension (OLE) of SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 (AGILE) alongside an integrated post-hoc analysis of the 104-week SWIFT and AGILE period. METHODS: In SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2, patients (aged ≥12 years) with asthma with type 2 inflammation, an eosinophilic phenotype (≥150 cells/μL at screening or ≥300 cells/μL during the previous 12 months), and a history of at least two exacerbations in the previous 12 months despite receiving medium-dose or high-dose inhaled corticosteroids were randomly assigned (2:1) to subcutaneous depemokimab 100 mg or placebo every 26 weeks in addition to standard of care for 52 weeks. Patients who completed SWIFT-1 or SWIFT-2 could join the single-arm, 52-week AGILE OLE study, conducted at 156 centres across 14 countries. Patients continued depemokimab (depemokimab-depemokimab group) or switched to depemokimab from placebo (placebo-depemokimab group). The primary endpoints for the 52-week AGILE OLE period were the incidence of adverse events and serious adverse events, and immunogenicity as measured by the presence of anti-drug antibodies and neutralising antibodies. Secondary efficacy outcomes, including exacerbation rate, St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score, Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 (ACQ-5) score, and pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), were also assessed. Additional post-hoc analyses were carried out to assess safety and efficacy over the 104-week integrated SWIFT and AGILE analysis period. AGILE OLE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05243680. The SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04719832 and NCT04718103. FINDINGS: Between March 1, 2022, and May 19, 2025, 629 patients were included in the AGILE OLE study (419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group). During the 52-week AGILE OLE period, adverse events occurred in 297 (71%) of 419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 146 (70%) of 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group; serious adverse events were infrequent (37 [9%] of 419 in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 19 [9%] of 210 in the placebo-depemokimab group), with no treatment-related or fatal serious adverse events reported. In the depemokimab-depemokimab group, the reduced annualised exacerbation rate was sustained over 2 years (0·51 [95% CI 0·43-0·61] in the 52-week SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 period and 0·56 [0·47-0·66] in the AGILE OLE). Improvements in SGRQ total score, ACQ-5 score, and FEV1 were maintained over 2 years. In the placebo-depemokimab group, improvements in clinical outcomes were observed after the switch to depemokimab during the AGILE OLE. INTERPRETATION: Twice-yearly depemokimab was well tolerated and demonstrated sustained efficacy over the 2-year SWIFT and AGILE period, supporting its long-term therapeutic benefit and safety profile. FUNDING: GSK.

papers.authors: Hafez A, Youssef A, Nour M, Farina JM, Awad K, Pietri MP, Scalia IG, Abdelfattah F et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Cardiovascular Medicine, Mayo Clinic, Phoenix, AZ.
papers.abstract_en: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve outcomes across several cardiometabolic conditions, but their role in World Health Organization group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study of adults with group 1 PAH. Patients prescribed SGLT2i were compared with patients without exposure. Propensity-score matching was performed 1:2 using age, sex, baseline REVEAL Lite 2 risk category, diabetes mellitus, and statin use. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events. Associations were evaluated using fixed-exposure and start-stop time-varying Cox models. The matched cohort included 366 patients: 122 (33%) receiving SGLT2i and 244 (67%) controls. Most patients were classified as high risk by REVEAL Lite 2 (106 SGLT2i recipients (87%) and 215 controls (88%), respectively). In the fixed-exposure analysis, SGLT2i use was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.53; 95% CI, 0.31-0.91; P=.018), without a significant difference in major adverse cardiovascular events (HR, 1.23; 95% CI, 0.93-1.63; P=.14). In the time-varying analysis, SGLT2i exposure was not significantly associated with mortality (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.26-2.11; P=.57). The apparent survival association was attenuated after accounting for treatment timing, demonstrating the sensitivity of observational PAH estimates to exposure classification and supporting prospective randomized trials.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer associated with cystic airspaces (LCCA) is an increasingly recognised yet under-characterised presentation of non-small cell lung cancer, accounting for approximately 1-4% of cases. Despite growing awareness driven by thin-section computed tomography and lung cancer screening, LCCA remains absent from major international guidelines and classifications, including those of the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer, and the World Health Organization. This narrative review synthesises the available evidence to define LCCA as a distinct clinico-radiological entity and to inform future guideline development. LCCA presents heterogeneously, with thin- or thick walled cysts, unilocular or multiloculated morphology, and variable solid components, frequently mimicking benign cysts, bullae, or emphysema. Such ambiguity contributes to diagnostic delay; in the NELSON screening trial, LCCA accounted for 22.7% of missed or delayed diagnoses. Several radiological classifications, notably that of Mascalchi, aid description and risk stratification. Conventional staging is problematic, as measurement of the solid component alone may underestimate true tumour extent, while fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography carries a high false-negative rate. Tissue sampling is similarly complicated by low diagnostic yield and false negative results, underscoring the importance of multidisciplinary team discussion. The natural history follows a stepwise progression from thin-walled cyst to wall thickening, mural nodularity, and invasive disease, with prognosis determined principally by stage, although mural nodularity and increasing solid components confer higher recurrence risk. Treatment broadly mirrors that of solid lung tumours; current guidance advocates targeting the whole cystic lesion for radical therapy rather than the solid component alone, with systemic anticancer therapy appropriate in advanced or multifocal disease. Much current practice is extrapolated from part-solid tumours; consensus on Powered by Editorial Manager® and ProduXion Manager® from Aries Systems Corporation terminology, classification, and staging, supported by prospective registry data, is required to optimise outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Rapid pathogen identification is critical for timely antibiotic therapy in patients with pneumonia, yet current methods remain too slow or complex for routine clinical use. Here, we describe a localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR)-based biosensor platform that detects Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria directly in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) without nucleic acid extraction or amplification. Gold nano-islands (AuNIs) functionalized with antibodies against lipoteichoic acid (LTA) or lipopolysaccharide (LPS) enabled selective bacterial capture. The sensor achieved a refractive index resolution of 8.52 × 10-8 RIU with good reusability and dynamic range. Detection limits reached the concentration of 0.027 μM for purified LTA and 0.208 endotoxin units (EU) for LPS. When tested with Escherichia coli in artificial samples, the LPS sensor showed a reproducibility standard deviation (RSD) of 3.14%, detecting bacterial growth significantly earlier than conventional OD600 measurement. In 33 clinical BALF samples, sensor results correlated strongly with standard diagnostics (Pearson r = 0.963) and distinguished infected from noninfected cases using cutoff values of 0.060 rad (Gram-positive) and 0.083 rad (Gram-negative). The platform detects polymyxin B susceptibility 8 h earlier than conventional OD600 measurements, and a proof-of-concept sandwich immunoassay enables species-level discrimination between E. coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae. With excellent reproducibility (RSD = 3.14%), reusability over six cycles (84.21% ± 2.03% signal retention), and four-week storage stability (98.63% ± 5.42%), this LSPR platform offers a practical, rapid approach for frontline bacterial screening and accelerated antibiotic stewardship in pneumonia.

papers.title_zh: 18F-BMS-986192 PET to Predict Durable Response to Nivolumab in NSCLC: A Novel Approach Beyond PD-L1 Immunohistochemistry.
papers.title_en: 18F-BMS-986192 PET to Predict Durable Response to Nivolumab in NSCLC: A Novel Approach Beyond PD-L1 Immunohistochemistry.
papers.authors: Borm FJ, Smit J, Gerards NR, Wiegers SE, van der Noort V, Wang Y, Cohen D, Monkhorst K et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Oncology, Antoni van Leeuwenhoek Hospital-Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam, The Netherland…
papers.abstract_en: Programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunohistochemistry, the current standard biomarker for predicting response to programmed death protein 1/PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors in non-small cell lung cancer, has moderate predictive value among others because of tumor heterogeneity and limited biopsy representation, whereas PD-L1 PET/CT using 18F-BMS-986192 enables noninvasive, whole-tumor assessment of PD-L1 expression and heterogeneity, potentially improving prediction of response to immunotherapy. Methods: In this prospective multicenter biomarker exploration study, patients with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer eligible for nivolumab-based therapies underwent baseline 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT, 18F-FDG PET/CT, and tumor biopsy for PD-L1 immunohistochemistry before treatment initiation. The primary endpoint was durable clinical benefit, defined as progression-free survival (PFS) of 9 mo or greater, with secondary analyses assessing associations among tracer uptake, PD-L1 expression, survival outcomes, and PET-based radiomic features. Results: Of 91 enrolled patients, 77 were included in the final analysis of 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT. Although PD-L1 immunohistochemistry did not differ between patients with PFS of less than 9 mo versus 9 mo or greater, PD-L1 PET uptake in lung lesions was significantly higher in patients with PFS of at least 9 mo (P = 0.01). Using an optimal mean SUVpeak cutoff of 2.4, PD-L1 PET demonstrated a high negative predictive value (94%) for durable clinical benefit, with significant associations for both PFS and overall survival, particularly in patients receiving first-line treatment. Tracer uptake showed no correlation with 18F-FDG uptake. Conclusion: 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT revealed interpatient PD-L1 variability. Low uptake in lung lesions predicted poor outcomes with high negative predictive value. 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT demonstrated stronger negative predictive value than did baseline PD-L1 immunohistochemistry in this cohort. These findings require prospective validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Relapsed/refractory (R/R) lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a clinical challenge with limited therapies and poor prognosis. CAR‑NK cell therapy has shown promise in solid tumors, but its efficacy is limited by both the availability of effective targets and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. CD73 (NT5E), highly expressed across solid tumors, catalyzes adenosine production to drive immunosuppression, representing both a specific CAR‑NK target and a key leverage point to overcome tumor immune evasion. However, its systematic evaluation as a therapeutically actionable target for CAR‑NK cell therapy in R/R LUAD remains unexplored. METHODS: We first characterized CD73 expression through integrative analysis of public datasets, primary and relapsed clinical LUAD specimens, and LUAD cell lines derived from primary and metastatic tumors. We then constructed CD73‑CAR‑NK cells and assessed their in vitro cytotoxicity across LUAD cell lines of varying malignancy, as well as their effects on extracellular adenosine and resistance to adenosine‑mediated immunosuppression. Finally, we assessed their antitumor efficacy in a stepwise manner across a tiered panel of in vivo models, including cell line‑derived xenograft (CDX), metastasis, patient‑derived xenograft (PDX), and clinically relevant immune‑humanized PDX models. RESULTS: CD73 expression was elevated in metastasis-derived LUAD cell lines and R/R LUAD specimens. Accordingly, CD73-CAR-NK92 cells exhibited potent cytotoxicity against CD73-high LUAD cells, accompanied by an activated effector phenotype, reduced extracellular adenosine, partial resistance to adenosine-mediated suppression, and limited activity toward normal bronchial epithelial cells. Notably, this enhanced function was consistently observed across multiple NK cell sources including peripheral blood-derived NK (PBNK), umbilical cord blood‑derived NK (UBNK), and iPSC-derived NK (iNK). In vivo, CD73‑CAR‑NK92 cells significantly suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, with enhanced tumor‑site enrichment, prolonged retention, and elevated intratumoral levels of TNF‑α and IFN‑γ. Importantly, in an immune‑humanized PDX mouse model, CD73‑CAR‑NK92 cells significantly reduced the growth of R/R patient‑derived xenografts, accompanied by immune remodeling, without marked systemic inflammation during the observation period. CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide preclinical evidence that CD73-CAR-NK cells exhibit potent antitumor efficacy for R/R LUAD through their dual functions of eliminating CD73-high tumor cells and resisting adenosine-mediated immunosuppressive signaling, supporting their therapeutic potential.

papers.title_zh: Muco-obstructive lung disease exhibits distinct hypoxic and inflammatory airway epithelial gene pathways.
papers.title_en: Muco-obstructive lung disease exhibits distinct hypoxic and inflammatory airway epithelial gene pathways.
papers.authors: Mikami Y, Burns E, Dang H, van Heusden C, Caldwell RA, Reidel B, Furusho M, Murano H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Marsico Lung Institute, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Chapel Hill, NC, , USA.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Intraluminal obstruction produces chronic airway epithelial hypoxia. We investigated how chronic airway epithelial hypoxia and inflammatory stimuli interact in human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cultures and resected human bronchiectatic lungs to produce an airway epithelial environment characteristic of muco-obstructive disease. MATERIALS AND METHODS: HBE cultures were exposed to normoxia or hypoxia (1% O2) for 5 days, followed by administration of supernatants from cystic fibrosis (CF) lung-derived mucopurulent material (SMM) or PBS for 24 h. A reverse order protocol with SMM followed by hypoxia was also performed. Bulk RNA-sequencing and functional (Na+ transport) studies were performed. HIF1A and EPAS1-mediated transcriptional responses were characterised in CRISPR knockdown HBE cells. RNA in situ hybridisation studies of excised bronchiectatic lungs and bioinformatic analyses of published datasets tested for relevance of in vitro findings to in vivo conditions. RESULTS: Hypoxia and SMM regulated largely separate airway epithelial transcriptional programmes regardless of treatment order. PTGS2 (COX-2), CCL20, MUC5B, and CXCL8 (IL-8) represented a small number of genes upregulated by both hypoxia and SMM. HIF1A knockdown and EPAS1 knockdown produced distinct, often opposing, effects on hypoxia-responsive pathways. HIF1A dominated upregulation of glycolytic pathway signalling. EPAS1 regulated genes that increase mucus concentration under hypoxia (e.g., SCNN1G). An EPAS1 inhibitor blocked hypoxia-induced upregulation of Na+ transport. CONCLUSION: Chronic hypoxia and inflammation regulated distinct genes/pathways that combine to produce a complex diseased environment in muco-obstructed airway epithelia. HIF1A and EPAS1 regulated distinct hypoxia-induced transcriptional responses. EPAS1 inhibition may exhibit a favourable therapeutic ratio for treatment of muco-obstructive lung diseases.
