papers.authors: Hoshino M, Harada T, Kitamura H, Ootawa J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory Medicine, Nasu Medical Center, International University of Health and Welfare, Nasushiobara, J…
papers.authors_conclusion: In patients with biologic-controlled severe asthma with allergic rhinitis, the most consistent benefit associated with add-on HDM-SLIT was improvement in rhinitis-related quality of life.
papers.ai_note: ACQ-6、FEV1% predicted、WA/Ao%名义显著但协变量校正后失去统计学意义，提示初次分析存在混杂偏倚；研究未明确指定主要终点，多终点同时报告存在多重比较风险；观察性设计即使经倾向性评分匹配仍可能存在残余混杂；样本量较小（每组43例），且dupilumab限制的敏感性分析进一步缩小人群；哮喘控制相关指标（ACQ-6、肺功能）最终未证实获益，与临床预期的免疫治疗核心获益存在落差
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Whether house dust mite sublingual immunotherapy (HDM-SLIT) provides additional clinical benefits in patients with severe asthma already controlled by biologic therapy remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of add-on HDM-SLIT on rhinitis-related and asthma-related outcomes in patients with biologic-controlled severe asthma and allergic rhinitis. METHODS: In this propensity score-matched real-world study, 86 patients with severe asthma and allergic rhinitis were analyzed after 1:1 matching of patients receiving HDM-SLIT with those receiving biologic therapy or continuing biologic therapy alone (43 patients per group). Changes in Rhinoconjunctivitis Quality of Life Questionnaire (RQLQ), Asthma Quality of Life Questionnaire (AQLQ), Asthma Control Questionnaire (ACQ)-6, lung function, type 2 biomarkers, and airway structural parameters by quantitative computed tomography were evaluated over 12 months. Covariate-adjusted analyses and a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients receiving dupilumab were performed. RESULTS: RQLQ showed greater improvement with HDM-SLIT than with control (standardized mean differences [SMD] 1.545, 95% CI 0.910-2.180; p <0.001), and this finding remained significant in covariate-adjusted and dupilumab-restricted sensitivity analyses. AQLQ also improved with HDM-SLIT (SMD 0.673, 95% CI 0.097-1.250; p = 0.036). ACQ-6, FEV1% predicted, and percentage of airway wall area relative to total area (WA/Ao%) showed nominally greater improvements in the primary analyses (p = 0.023, 0.039, and 0.038, respectively). but these findings were not statistically significant after additional covariate adjustment. CONCLUSION: In patients with biologic-controlled severe asthma with allergic rhinitis, the most consistent benefit associated with add-on HDM-SLIT was improvement in rhinitis-related quality of life.

papers.authors_conclusion: In severe left-right asymmetry, global mechanical power may obscure differences in lung-specific mechanical conditions. ILV may permit individualized ventilation when shared settings impose incompatible requirements, but redistribution or reduction of delivered energy alone does not establish lung protection. Whether appropriately selected ILV settings reduce injurious regional mechanical processes, ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI), or adverse clinical outcomes remains to be determined.
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，作者自述证据仅来源于生理学研究、技术报告与病例经验，未报告任何效应量、CI或P值；无系统检索与偏倚评估流程，框架为提案性质（'proposed physiological framework'），不可当作推荐强度证据。结论表述克制，未过度宣称临床获益。信息不足：无法评估纳入文献的质量与覆盖度。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Mechanical power describes the rate of mechanical energy transfer to the respiratory system but does not directly quantify injurious tissue dissipation. In severe left-right asymmetry, global airway-opening values may conceal major differences in lung-specific mechanics. Uniform settings may overdistend the more compliant lung while inadequately ventilating the affected lung. MAIN TEXT: This physiology-driven narrative review examines independent lung ventilation (ILV) for applying lung-specific ventilatory goals and mechanical constraints in severe left-right asymmetry. ILV may be considered when conventional ventilator optimization is ineffective or poorly tolerated and shared settings impose incompatible requirements. Implementation requires anatomical and circuit separation and may involve double-lumen tubes, bronchial blockers in selected configurations, two ventilators, or differential-ventilation systems. A proposed physiological framework aims to limit excessive tidal expansion and pressure exposure in the more compliant lung while adapting ventilation of the affected lung to recruitability, time-constant abnormalities, or air-leak physiology. Lung-specific estimates of delivered mechanical power may characterize mechanical loading but do not directly measure injurious tissue dissipation. Evidence remains limited, deriving from physiological studies, technical reports, and case-based clinical experience. CONCLUSION: In severe left-right asymmetry, global mechanical power may obscure differences in lung-specific mechanical conditions. ILV may permit individualized ventilation when shared settings impose incompatible requirements, but redistribution or reduction of delivered energy alone does not establish lung protection. Whether appropriately selected ILV settings reduce injurious regional mechanical processes, ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI), or adverse clinical outcomes remains to be determined.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medicine, University of Alabama at Birmingham, Birmingham, AL 35294-0012.

papers.ai_note: 摘要全为定性描述，无任何样本量、效应量、CI或P值，results 无法取数（信息不足）；胞葬抑制与CD47高表达在IPF中的证据来源（患者组织、细胞还是模型）未交代；AMPK激活同时通过降低inflammaging/CD47可用性与重编程巨噬细胞表型两条机制，摘要未说明何者为主要通路或是否有阻断实验验证因果；'药理学破坏胞葬信号可致纤维化'与'恢复胞葬促进消退'互为印证但缺乏剂量与时程信息；从机制到'广泛治疗相关性'的外推跨度大，未涉及疗效与安全性数据。
papers.abstract_en: Efferocytosis is essential for tissue homeostasis and resolution of inflammation, yet its direct contribution to resolve organ fibrosis remains poorly understood. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive age-driven lung disease, we found profound suppression of efferocytosis coupled with robust production and release of extracellular vesicles presenting functional receptor CD47, a canonical "don't eat me" mediator. Restoration of efferocytosis contributes to the natural resolution of fibrosis, which is accelerated by CD47 deficiency or alterations in macrophage metabolic responses. In turn, pharmacologic disruption of efferocytic receptors or signaling results in lung fibrosis development and its persistence. While sustained reduction of efferocytic capacity align with fibrosis persistence in aged mice, AMPK activation promotes fibrosis resolution via reducing inflammaging and CD47 bioavailability, thus restoring clearance of apoptotic fibroblast. Importantly, AMPK activation also reprograms macrophages engaging apoptotic fibroblasts toward a fibrosis pro-resolving phenotype by suppressing TGF-β1 and promoting secretion of pro-regenerative hepatocyte growth factor (HGF). Together, these findings link metabolism and immune efferocytic fitness in lung fibrosis resolution and suggest that an AMPK senomorphic pathway has broad therapeutic relevance for fibrotic diseases.

papers.authors: West JD, Moore C, Gladson S, Shay S, Sevier E, Kobeck E, Cai Y, Agrawal V et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Allergy, Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine, Vanderbilt University, 1161 21st Ave.

The magnitude of hemodynamic improvement combined with substantial diastolic function improvement suggests clinical potential, particularly for PH patients with metabolic comorbidities.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Reactive oxygen species are increased across most pulmonary hypertension (PH) etiologies, resulting in increased reactive lipid dicarbonyls, which form protein adducts and impair mitochondrial function. We hypothesized that reducing reactive lipids would reduce right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) and improve cardiac function by eliminating protein-lipid damage feedback loops. METHODS: We used 2-hydroxybenzylamine (2-HOBA) to scavenge reactive lipids in three complimentary mouse models of PH: AKR-high fat diet (HFD, metabolic stress), LNAME-HFD (cardiometabolic syndrome), and pulmonary artery banding (PAB, load stress). Cardiac function was measured by echocardiography and catheterization. RV energy metabolism was determined by oxygraphy. Mass spectrometry analyzed lipids and ceramides; O-link and RNA-Seq evaluated proteomic and gene expression in lungs, RV, and LV. RESULTS: Reducing reactive lipids with 2-HOBA resulted in a ~ 10% reduction in RVSP, reduced diastolic dysfunction, reduced plasma lipids and ceramides, and normalized RV fatty acid oxidation that was severely impaired in the AKR-HFD and PAB models. Proteomic and RNA changes in the lungs, RV, and LV suggested reduced oxidative damage and inflammatory signaling and altered developmental and actin organization signaling; these changes are plausibly associated with the improved adaptation. Some changes were sex specific, including a 4x higher cardiac fatty acid content in males than females. CONCLUSIONS: Reactive lipid scavenging improves cardiac metabolic and diastolic function and right ventricular systolic pressure through restoration of mitochondrial function and reduced oxidative protein damage. The magnitude of hemodynamic improvement combined with substantial diastolic function improvement suggests clinical potential, particularly for PH patients with metabolic comorbidities.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sex-related differences in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) are well recognized, but their association with dynamic upper airway collapse remains poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: To characterize sex-related clinical profiles in OSA through the integrated assessment of clinical characteristics, sleep study parameters, and drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) findings. METHODS: This retrospective study compared clinical profiles, sleep parameters, collapse patterns, airway reversibility, and treatment recommendations in 767 patients undergoing DISE. RESULTS: Women were older and more frequently reported insomnia and mood disorders, whereas men had higher body mass index, larger tonsils, and higher Mallampati scores. Sleep study differences were also observed: men exhibited longer apneas, higher apnea-to-hypopnea ratios, and more positional OSA. Respiratory event clustering suggestive of REM-related OSA was more frequent in women, although REM sleep was not EEG-confirmed. DISE demonstrated that obstruction was more frequent in men at all assessed levels, including palatal concentric collapse (62.5% vs 40.7%). Complete resolution with jaw thrust was more frequent in women (30.2% vs 18.4%). Mandibular advancement therapy was more commonly recommended for women, whereas surgery was more frequently recommended for men. CONCLUSIONS: Findings in this DISE-selected cohort suggest a predominantly anatomy-driven pattern in men and a potentially more functionally modulated profile in women, supporting the integration of sex-related characteristics into personalized treatment selection.

papers.abstract_en: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by recurrent alveolar epithelial injury, maladaptive repair, fibroblast activation, and extracellular-matrix accumulation. Lactate metabolism is increasingly implicated in communication between stromal and immune cells in fibrotic lung niches through monocarboxylate transporter (MCT)-mediated transport, hydroxycarboxylic acid receptor 1 (HCAR1/GPR81) sensing, extracellular acidification, and lysine lactylation. This narrative review evaluates the evidence for directional lactate-associated fibroblast-macrophage signaling, the limits of proposed reciprocal interactions, and their therapeutic implications. Human IPF observations, experimental pulmonary-fibrosis studies, and indirect evidence from other disease contexts are separated according to disease relevance and causal resolution. The strongest direct mechanistic evidence supports lactate released by activated myofibroblasts as a stimulus for macrophage histone lactylation and profibrotic transcription, whereas reciprocal macrophage-to-fibroblast lactate feedback remains unproven. Among the lactate-associated targets reviewed, fibroblast-associated MCT4 currently has the most developed preclinical evidence package, supported by disease-relevant observations, target perturbation, and antifibrotic activity in experimental models. However, no lactate-directed therapeutic strategy has yet demonstrated clinical efficacy in IPF. HCAR1/GPR81, lactate-production pathways, and lactylation-associated machinery remain mechanistically compelling but are at earlier stages of pharmacological validation. Overall, available evidence is more consistent with lactate functioning as a context-dependent amplifier or maintenance signal than with a demonstrated uniform initiating role in IPF. Lactate-directed interventions may therefore be considered adjunctive strategies alongside established antifibrotic therapy. Further translation will require cell- and disease-stage-specific causal validation, lesion-resolved target engagement, efficacy in established fibrosis, and a therapeutic window that preserves physiological lactate metabolism.

papers.authors: Liu X, Chen Q, Hu Y, Liu Z, Yang Z, Yu J, Li H, Chen R et al.

papers.ai_note: 摘要的体内结果全部为方向性描述（降低RVSP、改善PAT/PET、减轻右心室肥厚与血管壁厚度），未提供任何数值、效应量、CI或P值，亦未说明是否预设主要终点及统计方法，方法学与结果可信度信息不足；仅报告单一剂量单一时长，无剂量-反应；曲前列尼为阳性对照但摘要未给出与他克莫司的比较数据，无法判断疗效位次；组织学终点（α-SMA、Fn1、Col1a1、Ki67）与细胞实验指标多为机制性/替代终点，未见生存或功能学硬终点；从动物模型直接外推至'血管重构突出的IPF-PH患者'存在人群限定松动。信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is frequently complicated by pulmonary hypertension (IPF-PH), a severe condition that worsens symptoms, reduces exercise capacity, and shortens survival. Current anti-fibrotic and PH-targeted therapies show limited efficacy in IPF-PH, and the therapeutic role of tacrolimus in this composite disease remains underexplored. METHODS: A bleomycin-induced IPF-PH rat model was established. Rats were randomized into control, bleomycin model, treprostinil (positive control), and tacrolimus (0.05 mg/kg/day, subcutaneous, 21 days) groups. Right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP), echocardiography, right ventricular and lung histology, immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blot were assessed. In vitro, C166 endothelial cells and primary rat pulmonary arterial endothelial cells were stimulated with bleomycin with or without tacrolimus; MOVAS smooth muscle cells were stimulated with TGF-β1 with or without tacrolimus. Endpoints included cell viability, tube formation, ROS, SOD/GSH, apoptosis, proliferation/migration, and MAPK/PI3K/AKT signaling. RESULTS: Tacrolimus reduced RVSP, improved PAT/PET and right heart function, attenuated right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary fibrosis, and decreased vascular wall thickness and α-SMA expression. It also downregulated fibrosis markers Fn1 and Col1a1. In endothelial cells, tacrolimus restored P-VEGFR2/VEGFR2 and VE-cadherin expression, promoted tube formation, reduced apoptosis (Bax/Bcl-2, cleaved caspase-9/3), and alleviated oxidative stress (ROS, SOD/GSH, Keap1/HO-1). In smooth muscle cells, tacrolimus inhibited TGF-β1-induced proliferation and migration and reduced Ki67 expression. Mechanistically, tacrolimus suppressed MAPK (JNK, ERK, p38) and PI3K/AKT pathway activation in vivo and in vitro. DISCUSSION: Tacrolimus ameliorates bleomycin-induced IPF-PH through vascular remodeling-oriented, multi-target effects, including endothelial protection, suppression of oxidative stress and apoptosis, and inhibition of smooth muscle proliferation, partly via MAPK and PI3K/AKT signaling. These findings support tacrolimus as a potential therapeutic candidate for IPF-PH, especially in patients with prominent vascular remodeling, while highlighting the need for further dose-response, target-specific, immunomodulatory, and delivery optimization studies before clinical translation.

Nocturnal CPAP therapy had been prescribed, delivered through an oronasal mask at a fixed pressure of 11 cm H2O.

papers.abstract_en: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a life-threatening inflammatory lung disorder characterized by excessive neutrophilic inflammation and increased microvascular permeability. We previously demonstrated the involvement of the Gq-coupled P2Y2 purinergic receptor (P2RY2) in ARDS pathogenesis. Here, we investigated the contribution of the related purinergic receptor P2Y6 (P2RY6) and defined its cell-type-specific functions using a preclinical mouse model of ARDS. Wild-type female mice were treated with the selective P2RY6 antagonist MRS2578 through intratracheal administration using prophylactic and therapeutic approaches, followed by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge. The role of P2RY6 was further evaluated in global P2ry6 -deficient mice and conditional knockout models targeting specific cellular compartments. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) samples were analyzed by flow cytometry and multiplex cytokine assays, and lung tissues were assessed by histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Pharmacological inhibition of P2RY6 significantly reduced Ly6G+F4/80⁻ neutrophil accumulation, vascular leakage and pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine production in the ARDS model. Consistently, P2ry6 -deficient mice exhibited reduced Ly6G+F4/80⁻ neutrophil recruitment and attenuated inflammatory responses following LPS challenge. Cell-type-specific deletion revealed that P2RY6 deficiency in Vav-expressing hematopoietic cells and CD11c-expressing cells reproduced the protective phenotype observed in global P2ry6 knockout mice. In contrast, P2RY6 deletion in CD4+ T cells, Scgb1a1-expressing airway epithelial cells or LysM-expressing myeloid cells did not significantly alter ARDS-associated inflammation. Collectively, our findings identify CD11c-expressing P2RY6 + cells as critical regulators of ARDS pathogenesis and highlight P2RY6 as a potential therapeutic target for controlling inflammatory lung injury.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a common and devastating complication of advanced malignancies, particularly lung cancer, with limited therapeutic options and poor prognosis. Immune checkpoint inhibitors and cytokine therapies have shown promise in solid tumors but are constrained by dose-dependent toxicity and limited efficacy in the pleural cavity. Engineered Mycobacterium smegmatis (M. smegmatis) co-expressing a PD-L1 inhibitor and interleukin-15 immunocytokine (Ms-PI15) represents a novel in situ vaccine platform capable of sustained local drug delivery with favorable biosafety profiles. Here, we investigated the therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms of intrapleural Ms-PI15 administration in a murine MPE model. METHODS: A syngeneic MPE mouse model was established by intrapleural inoculation of luciferase-expressing Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC-Luc) cells into C57BL/6 mice. Mice were treated with intrapleural injections of PBS, Ms-vector (empty vector control), or Ms-PI15. Tumor burden was monitored by bioluminescence imaging. Pharmacokinetics and biodistribution of Ms-PI15 were evaluated using DIR fluorescence imaging and bacterial colony enumeration. Flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry were employed to characterize immune cell populations in the tumor microenvironment, spleen, and thoracic draining lymph nodes (TDLNs). Biosafety was assessed by histopathological examination and serum biochemistry. RESULTS: Intrapleural administration of Ms-PI15 significantly suppressed MPE development and pleural tumor growth compared with PBS and Ms-vector controls. DIR fluorescence imaging and CFU enumeration demonstrated that Ms-PI15 accumulated predominantly in the pleural tumor microenvironment and TDLNs, peaking at 72 h post-administration, with minimal dissemination to distant organs. Mechanistically, Ms-PI15 remodeled the immune microenvironment by promoting maturation of CD80+CD86+ myeloid dendritic cells (mDCs), driving M1 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages (increased CD86+, decreased CD206+), and significantly enhancing infiltration of CD8 T cells and NK1.1+ NK cells in the pleural tumor, spleen, and TDLNs. No significant histopathological abnormalities or serum biochemical alterations were observed in major organs following Ms-PI15 treatment, confirming its favorable biosafety profile. CONCLUSION: Intrapleural administration of the engineered M. smegmatis Ms-PI15 effectively inhibits MPE progression by remodeling the pleural immune microenvironment toward an antitumor phenotype, while maintaining excellent biosafety. These findings provide a preclinical foundation for the development of intracavitary bacterial immunotherapy as a novel treatment strategy for malignant pleural effusion.

papers.title_zh: Development and evaluation of inhalable imipenem dry powder for treating pulmonary P. aeruginosa infection.
papers.title_en: Development and evaluation of inhalable imipenem dry powder for treating pulmonary P. aeruginosa infection.
papers.authors: Kommarajula P, Guo Y, Bootle R, Silva L, Patil S, Suman J, Kunda NK
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences, College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences, St.
papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary infections caused by P. aeruginosa (PA) remain a major clinical challenge due to biofilm formation, intrinsic resistance, and limited antibiotic penetration into lung tissues following systemic administration. Imipenem (IPM), a broad-spectrum carbapenem, requires high intravenous doses (500 mg every 6 h with cilastatin) to achieve therapeutic lung levels, leading to frequent dosing and systemic toxicity. Pulmonary delivery via dry powder for inhalation (DPI) offers a targeted alternative. However, formulation development is hindered by the chemical instability, specifically its susceptibility to thermal and hydrolytic degradation in the amorphous state. In this study, a high-dose, chemically stable IPM dry powder for inhalation (IPM-DPI) was developed by co-spray-drying IPM with L-leucine. The optimized 50:50 (w/w) IPM: L-leucine powder exhibited an initial IPM potency of ∼94% and low residual moisture content (<2% w/w). Differential scanning calorimetry and powder X-ray diffraction of IPM-DPI confirmed amorphous IPM and semi-crystalline L-leucine, while Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy suggested intermolecular interactions between IPM and L-leucine. The IPM-DPI demonstrated excellent aerosolization, achieving fine particle fractions of ∼67% (Orbital™ DPI) and ∼53% (RS01® DPI), with a mass median aerodynamic diameter of 2.4-3.2 µm and retained antimicrobial potency (minimum inhibitory concentration of 0.125-0.25 µg/mL). IPM-DPI maintained >95% of its initial IPM potency after 6 months at -20 °C, demonstrating improved stability associated with intermolecular interactions between leucine and IMP, with the semi-crystalline leucine phase forming a matrix around IMP molecules within the particle core. Overall, the developed IPM-DPI enables localized pulmonary delivery of imipenem, potentially eliminating the need for cilastatin and reducing systemic toxicity associated with parenteral therapy.

papers.title_zh: Circulating tumor DNA dynamics and mutational profiles as indicators in neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy for resectable or borderline resectable non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.title_en: Circulating tumor DNA dynamics and mutational profiles as indicators in neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy for resectable or borderline resectable non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Jiang W, Lei S, Liu S, Huo H, Lv Z, Liu C, Xu H, Tian L et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Oncology, National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer/Cancer Hospital, Chi…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy has reshaped the treatment landscape for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet critical gaps remain in real-time monitoring and personalized adaptation. METHODS: In this observational study, patients were evaluated via imaging and multidisciplinary review for subsequent surgery or radiotherapy after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Serial plasma samples for circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics and mutational analyses were collected. The endpoint was event-free survival (EFS). A pognostic mutational signature was developed using the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression. RESULTS: Among the 138 patients, 46.4% and 52.2% underwent surgery and radiotherapy, respectively. Compared to patients with persistently positive ctDNA, the ctDNA non-shedder exhibited a numerically longer EFS (hazard ratio [HR] 0.26, 95% CI: 0.06-1.25, p = 0.062), and the clearance group exhibited a statistically longer EFS (HR 0.33, 95% CI: 0.11-0.97, p = 0.040). Patients with positive ctDNA before surgery/radiotherapy showed a shorter EFS (HR 3.38, 95% CI: 1.26-9.08, p = 0.010), and positive ctDNA was correlated with a numerically shorter EFS (HR 9.72, 95% CI: 0.98-95.96, p = 0.051) in patients assessed as stable disease (SD) of high heterogeneity in the exploratory subgroup analysis. For patients with post-C1 negative ctDNA, no EFS difference was observed between those receiving 3-4 versus 2 cycles of chemoimmunotherapy (HR 1.54, 95% CI: 0.56-4.26, p = 0.41). For patients with post-C1 positive ctDNA, the post-C1 quantity was associated with clearance (AUC = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.55-0.89, p = 0.019). After balancing clinical characteristics, LASSO-Cox regression selected four genes (SLX4, IRF4, TP53, and SOX2) to construct a prognostic signature for EFS. The AUC at 36 months was 0.75, 0.71, 0.74 in the training, validation and full cohort. The high-risk group demonstrated a shorter EFS (p = 0.0002). CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal ctDNA assessment identified high-risk subgroups in neoadjuvant NSCLC, particularly by refining prognosis in heterogeneous SD populations. An exploratory gene-based mutational signature provided potential molecular risk stratification.

papers.title_zh: Intermittent hypoxia-driven gut microbial and metabolic remodeling in obstructive sleep apnea: mechanisms and evidence across target organs.
papers.title_en: Intermittent hypoxia-driven gut microbial and metabolic remodeling in obstructive sleep apnea: mechanisms and evidence across target organs.
papers.authors: Wu M, Chen L, Zhou J, Huang H, Chen X, Wan S, Xie X, Zhou M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, Lishui Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine Affiliated to Zhej…
papers.abstract_en: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) exposes tissues to recurrent intermittent hypoxia (IH) and is associated with multisystem morbidity. Growing evidence implicates the gut microbiota and microbial metabolism in these consequences, but their contribution to target-organ injury remains uncertain. This narrative review examines how IH remodels the intestinal environment and evaluates the evidence linking these changes to systemic injury, distinguishing preclinical experimental findings from human clinical observations. IH can disturb intestinal oxygen homeostasis, impair epithelial barrier function, and alter microbial and host-microbial metabolic pathways involving short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and trimethylamine N-oxide. These changes may influence distant tissues through metabolic signaling and immune activation. Preclinical studies support a functional microbial contribution to selected cardiovascular, metabolic, and neurocognitive phenotypes, but mechanistic resolution and applicability vary with exposure conditions, diet, and host background. Human studies remain predominantly observational and do not establish microbial mediation of OSA-related organ injury. Overall, the gut microbiota is best regarded as a context-dependent contributor and amplifier of IH-related injury, rather than a universal mediator. A focus on microbial function and host-microbial co-metabolism may be more informative than inconsistent taxonomic signatures. Longitudinal studies and targeted interventions are needed to establish clinical relevance and determine whether microbiome-directed approaches can complement established OSA treatment.

papers.title_zh: Computational drug screening for drug-resistant tuberculosis: advances, challenges, and future perspectives.
papers.title_en: Computational drug screening for drug-resistant tuberculosis: advances, challenges, and future perspectives.
papers.authors: Hu S, Li X, Batool Z, Zheng X, Dong J, Zhang C, Yang Y, Shen B et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine and Institutes for Systems Genetics, Frontiers Science Center for D…
papers.abstract_en: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, remains a major global health challenge, further exacerbated by the rapid emergence of drug-resistant strains. Despite continuous efforts, the discovery of novel anti-TB agents has lagged behind the evolution of resistance, largely due to the limitations of conventional experimental pipelines and the growing biological complexity of the pathogen. In recent years, computational drug discovery approaches-including virtual screening, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven modeling, and hybrid computational frameworks-have substantially expanded the chemical space accessible for early-stage anti-TB research. However, their translational success remains limited. This discrepancy reflects a fundamental mismatch between target-centric computational paradigms and the multi-scale biological constraints of Mtb, including permeability barriers, efflux mechanisms, metabolic state heterogeneity, lesion-level pharmacokinetics, and regimen-dependent therapeutic effects. This review critically evaluates current computational strategies for anti-TB drug screening, with particular emphasis on their performance under TB-specific biological and resistance constraints. We further explore computational approaches designed to address drug-resistant Mtb, including resistance-aware compound design, host-directed therapy, and combination regimen modeling. Finally, we explore key limitations in current computational pipelines, including challenges in data quality, biological integration, and regimen-level modeling, and propose a shift toward biologically grounded, regimen-aware, and systems-level frameworks. Bridging the gap between in silico prediction and clinical efficacy will require integrating multi-scale biological realism into computational pipelines, enabling more reliable translation of computational advances into effective anti-TB therapeutics.

papers.title_zh: Host-Age Structure in Influenza A(H3N2) HA Lineage Transitions in South Korea, 2009-2025.
papers.title_en: Host-Age Structure in Influenza A(H3N2) HA Lineage Transitions in South Korea, 2009-2025.
papers.authors: Lee S, Cho S, Demirev AV, Kim H, Shin W, Lee S, Park S, Kang H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Microbiology, Institute for Viral Diseases, Korea University College of Medicine, Seoul, Republic of Korea…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Influenza A(H3N2) has resurged in South Korea despite a shrinking pediatric population and high vaccination coverage. We examined correlates of host-age state transitions on the H3N2 hemagglutinin (HA) genealogy. METHODS: We analyzed 703 South Korean H3N2 HA sequences (2009-2025) in eight host-age states (ages 0-4, 5-9, then 10-year bands to 60 years and older). Discrete-trait analysis and an epoch-structured hierarchical generalized linear model (GLM) were fitted over 1700 HA trees, with epochs split at mid-2020. Within-year age-label permutation provided the sampling control (one for the discrete-trait analysis, 20 for the GLM). RESULTS: Children aged 5-9 years showed the largest net source balance (+11.7 vs. +10.5 under permuted labels), reflecting a lower recipient-side rate (0.39 vs. 1.08) rather than a higher source-side rate (12.11 vs. 11.59). Of 56 routes, 18 were supported (Bayes factor ≥ 10) but only three exceeded the permutation control, two from this group. Observed labels fitted the genealogy 400 log-likelihood units better, with 24% fewer transitions. Source-group population size (posterior inclusion probability, 0.74) and vaccination coverage (0.66) were supported, both with negative coefficients; contact rate was not (0.016). Only population size exceeded the permutation null (0.74 vs. 0.65; p = 0.048). CONCLUSIONS: H3N2 HA lineage transitions in South Korea were age-structured after accounting for sampling, most clearly for children aged 5-9 years. Their net source balance reflects a low recipient-side rate rather than a high source-side rate, and therefore describes lineage position rather than transmission intensity. These findings support age-resolved genomic surveillance for interpreting such patterns.

papers.authors: Liu M, Hu J, Wang D, Liu C, Ma X, Zhu Y, Sun J, Xu S et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Sc…
papers.authors_conclusion: These findings identify FH as a previously unrecognized metabolic regulator with protective effects in airway inflammation and support a role for mitochondrial fission-fusion dynamics in FH-mediated protection of airway epithelial cells.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial structural and functional dysfunction in airway epithelial cells is recognized as a central driver in the progression of severe asthma. However, the current understanding of the mechanisms underlying damage to the mitochondria remains insufficient, and effective therapeutic strategies for its repair are lacking. Fumarate hydratase (FH) is a pivotal metabolic enzyme in the tricarboxylic acid cycle. It exhibits anti-inflammatory and tissue-repairing effects in immune-related diseases, but its contribution to asthma has not been previously reported. METHODS: We examined the role of FH in severe asthma utilizing human transcriptomic datasets and in vitro (airway epithelial cells) and in vivo (mouse) models induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in combination with house dust mites (HDM), in conjunction with FH overexpression and pharmacological inhibition interventions. Mitochondrial function, mitochondrial dynamics, and inflammatory responses were assessed, together with Drp1 overexpression rescue and NRF2 inhibition experiments. RESULTS: Analysis of human severe asthma datasets, together with HDM/LPS-induced cellular and mouse models, consistently revealed reduced FH expression. Restoration of FH expression improved mitochondrial function, suppressed Drp1-associated mitochondrial fission, and reduced airway inflammation, whereas Drp1 overexpression partially reversed the mitochondrial protective effects of FH. FH also reduced Keap1 expression, promoted NRF2 nuclear translocation and HO-1 expression, and NRF2 inhibition attenuated the anti-inflammatory effects of FH. CONCLUSION: These findings identify FH as a previously unrecognized metabolic regulator with protective effects in airway inflammation and support a role for mitochondrial fission-fusion dynamics in FH-mediated protection of airway epithelial cells.

papers.title_en: H3K9 lactylation transcriptionally activates EHMT2 to drive pulmonary arterial hypertension via PPARγ repression.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Liu C, Ma X, Yao Q, Zhou C, Liu H, Tang H, Chen Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Cardiology, Xinqiao Hospital, Army Medical University, Chongqing, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: Collectively, these findings identify a lactate-H3K9la-EHMT2-PPARγ axis linking hypoxia-induced metabolic reprogramming to pulmonary vascular remodeling and PAH progression.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterized by excessive proliferation and migration of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), yet how hypoxia-associated metabolic reprogramming contributes to pulmonary vascular remodeling remains unclear. Here, we show that hypoxia elevates intracellular lactate in PASMCs, promoting HBO1 (lysine acetyltransferase 7/KAT7)-catalyzed H3K9 lactylation (H3K9la) at the EHMT2 promoter and enhancing EHMT2 transcription. Smooth muscle cell-specific Ehmt2 deletion attenuates pulmonary vascular remodeling and right ventricular hypertrophy in SU5416/hypoxia (SuHx) mice and suppresses PASMC proliferation and migration. Conversely, EHMT2 overexpression promotes these phenotypes and mediates lactate-induced PASMC dysfunction. RNA sequencing of pulmonary arteries from Ehmt2-deficient mice identifies PPARγ repression as a downstream mechanism. EHMT2 inhibits PPARγ nuclear translocation, whereas rosiglitazone ameliorates EHMT2-induced PASMC dysfunction. Moreover, administration of lactate exacerbates SuHx-induced PAH in an EHMT2-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings identify a lactate-H3K9la-EHMT2-PPARγ axis linking hypoxia-induced metabolic reprogramming to pulmonary vascular remodeling and PAH progression.

papers.authors: Ding L, Hu R, Ying Y
papers.affiliation_highlight: Intensive Care Unit, Zhejiang Xiaoshan Hospital, Zhejiang, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: 在CAP相关脓毒症患者中，β-内酰胺联合治疗较单药治疗显示出更早达到临床稳定的趋势，尽管差异无统计学意义。本研究填补了脓毒性肺炎管理的重要证据空白，并支持开展以疾病严重程度和生物学特征为导向的个体化抗感染策略的进一步研究。回顾性单中心设计和相对较小的样本量应在解读这些发现时予以考虑

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) complicated by sepsis remains a life-threatening infectious syndrome associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare burden. Although β-lactam-based combination therapy is widely recommended for severe CAP, the optimal empirical antibiotic strategy for septic pneumonia remains uncertain. At the same time, empirical antibiotic selection must balance adequate early treatment against unnecessary broad-spectrum antibiotic use and the risk of antimicrobial resistance. Evidence specifically targeting this high-risk population is limited. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of β-lactam monotherapy and β-lactam-based combination therapy in patients with CAP-associated sepsis. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at Zhejiang Xiaoshan Hospital from January 2021 to January 2025, including adult patients with CAP-associated sepsis who received empirical β-lactam monotherapy or β-lactam-based combination therapy with macrolides or doxycycline within 48 hours of admission. A total of 100 patients were included before propensity score matching, and 80 patients remained after 1:1 matching. The primary outcome was time to clinical stability (TTCS). Secondary outcomes included mortality, length of hospital stay, antibiotic duration, changes in SOFA score, inflammatory biomarkers, clinical cure, and adverse events. TTCS was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression. RESULTS: Median TTCS was 5.0 days with monotherapy and 4.0 days with combination therapy (P = 0.129). Combination therapy also showed favorable trends in hospitalization duration, clinical cure, inflammatory marker reduction, and organ function recovery. After adjustment for admission SOFA score, combination therapy showed a nonsignificant trend toward earlier clinical stability (adjusted HR 1.42, 95% CI 0.88-2.29; P = 0.151). No significant increase in adverse events was observed. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CAP-associated sepsis, β-lactam-based combination therapy showed a trend toward earlier clinical stability than β-lactam monotherapy, although the difference was not statistically significant. This study addresses an important evidence gap in septic pneumonia management and supports further investigation of individualized antimicrobial strategies guided by disease severity and biological characteristics. The retrospective single-center design and relatively small sample size should be considered when interpreting these findings.

papers.abstract_en: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of global mortality, driven by declining lung function and frequent exacerbations. Conventional pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) programs usually last 6-12 weeks, and evidence supporting long-term PR is limited. In addition, the role of negative-pressure ventilation (NPV) in the management of COPD remains unclear.ObjectivesThis study investigated the clinical efficacy of a sequential long-term NPV and PR program in patients with COPD.DesignA retrospective cohort study.MethodsWe analyzed 125 COPD patients treated between 2019 and 2023. The intervention group received 12 months of NPV preceding hospital-based PR with lower-limb exercise twice weekly (NPV-PR), while the comparison group received PR alone. Longitudinal outcomes included pulmonary function tests, 6-min walking distance (6-MWD), COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score, Modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea score, and the number of acute exacerbations.ResultsThe NPV-PR group showed significant within-group improvements in pulmonary function, marked by an increased change in forced vital capacity (ΔFVC%) and a significant reduction in residual volume (ΔRV). Despite a lower baseline 6-MWD, the NPV-PR cohort achieved 12-month walking distances comparable to the PR-alone group. Furthermore, CAT scores declined rapidly by 6 months in the NPV-PR group, suggesting NPV may accelerate symptom relief. Notably, the combined approach sustained long-term rehabilitation benefits, yielding significant reductions in mMRC dyspnea scores and the expected count of acute exacerbations.ConclusionOur findings suggest that integrating long-term NPV with extended PR may represent a novel strategy, potentially optimizing the long-term management and clinical trajectory of patients with symptomatic COPD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bronchial asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease and a major global public health concern. Although numerous studies have reported asthma prevalence, evidence focusing specifically on adult populations in Saudi Arabia remains limited and fragmented. This study aimed to systematically review available evidence and estimate the pooled prevalence of bronchial asthma among adults in Saudi Arabia. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Electronic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar) were searched for studies published between 2010 and 2025. Observational studies reporting asthma prevalence among adults (≥ 18 years) in Saudi Arabia were included. Study selection involved title and abstract screening followed by full-text assessment. Data were extracted using a standardized form, and methodological quality was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. A random-effects meta-analysis with Freeman-Tukey transformation was performed using JASP software. RESULTS: A total of 1,280 records were identified, of which twelve studies met the inclusion criteria. All included studies were cross-sectional and conducted across national and regional settings. The pooled prevalence of bronchial asthma among adults in Saudi Arabia was 12.9% (95% CI: 8.8%-17.6%), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 99.1%, p < 0.001). Prevalence estimates varied widely across studies due to differences in study design, sampling strategies, and asthma definitions. CONCLUSION: Bronchial asthma represents a significant public health burden among adults in Saudi Arabia. The high heterogeneity highlights the need for standardized epidemiological methods and improved surveillance. Strengthening prevention, early diagnosis, and disease management strategies is essential to reduce the burden of asthma and improve population health outcomes.

papers.title_en: Sinomenine prevents monocrotaline-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension by inhibiting osteopontin-mediated PASMC phenotypic switching.
papers.authors: Zeng Z, Chen Z, Liu J, Xu W, Qin Y, Lin X, Wu W, Zhou H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: School of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Biomedical Research Institute, Hunan Medical College, Huaihua 418000, Hunan, China…

papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要全篇无任何样本量、效应量、CI或P值，'significantly attenuated'等表述无数据支撑，无法评估效应大小与统计学严谨性；结论主要依赖RNA-seq通路富集、分子对接与CETSA等间接证据，OPN为'central functional target'的因果链仅由过表达回补实验支持；分子对接属预测性证据，未见结合位点突变验证；动物为MCT单一化学诱导模型，且全部为非人体证据，向PAH患者外推缺乏依据；研究对象为非肿瘤性肺血管疾病，与胸部肿瘤业务关联有限
papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a life-threatening disease driven by progressive pulmonary vascular remodeling, and aberrant phenotypic transition of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) serves as the core pathological driver of disease deterioration. Sinomenine (SIN), a structurally defined isoquinoline alkaloid isolated from Sinomenium acutum (Thunb.) Rehder & E.H.Wilson, exhibits anti-inflammatory, vascular-protective, and anti-remodeling activities. Nevertheless, the exact molecular mechanism by which SIN regulates PASMC dysfunction to prevent PAH remains unclear. In vivo, SIN administration significantly attenuated MCT-induced PAH, right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary vascular remodeling in rats. In vitro, SIN effectively suppressed platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)-triggered proliferation, migration and phenotypic switching of PASMCs. RNA-sequencing coupled with KEGG enrichment analysis further identified the ECM-receptor interaction pathway as the key signaling cascade dysregulated by MCT, with osteopontin (OPN) validated as the central functional target of SIN. OPN overexpression recapitulated the pro-remodeling effects of PDGF-BB in PASMCs, and such abnormal phenotypes were prevented by SIN. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay demonstrated that SIN binds to NF-κB, a transcription factor of OPN, and suppresses PDGF-BB-induced NF-κB activation. This study uncovers a novel mechanism of SIN against PAH and highlights OPN as a critical mediator of its protective effects.

papers.study_type: GBD 2021 全球疾病负担描述性生态学研究 · 1990–2021年趋势分析（EAPC与倍数变化）
papers.title_zh: 1990–2021年全球204个国家和地区耐多药/广泛耐药结核病（含合并HIV）负担与趋势：各耐药类型发病与死亡均上升，HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB死亡增幅最大，高中等SDI地区负担最高
papers.title_en: The burden of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis and its attributable risk factors in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2021.
papers.authors: Wang H, Lv S, Yao P, Cen J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pharmacy, The First Affiliated Hospital of Army Medical University (Third Military Medical University), Ch…
papers.authors_conclusion: Over the past 30 years, a significant increase in the global burden of MDR-TB, XDR-TB, HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB, and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB has been reported, with marked variations in various resistance types across different regions and countries. In particular, the high-middle SDI regions warrant special attention. These findings highlight the need for further research to identify effective intervention strategies tailored to the epidemiological patterns observed in different regions and populations.
papers.ai_note: 疑点1：标题与研究目的声称分析'attributable risk factors'（归因风险因素），但摘要的方法与结果仅报告EAPC与倍数变化，未见任何风险因素模型或归因估计——信息不足，存在题目与内容不符。疑点2：结论称四类耐药结核病负担均'显著上升'，但MDR-TB的ASDR EAPC为1.18(-0.37–2.75)，95%CI跨越0，即趋势无统计学显著性，结论表述与所报数值矛盾。疑点3：MDR-TB的2021年ASIR与ASDR按其自身描述为四类中最高，但叙述重点落在增幅最大的HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB，绝对负担与相对增幅的权重易被混读。疑点4：GBD建模数据为估计值（UI反映不确定性），生态学描述设计无法支持因果或归因推断；'incidence and death ratio ... highest'的具体数值摘要未给出。
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Anti-tuberculosis drug resistance has become a major challenge to global tuberculosis control. This study aims to comprehensively the global burden, trends, and risks for disease deaths of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB), extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB), HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB, and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB from 1990 to 2021. METHODS: Data on the incidence and deaths of MDR-TB, XDR-TB, HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB, and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB were obtained from GBD 2021. The estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) and fold change were calculated to assess the trends of disease burden changes from baseline (1990 for MDR-TB and HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB; 1993 for XDR-TB and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB) to 2021. RESULTS: In 2021, the highest age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR) and age-standardized death rates (ASDR) were observed in MDR-TB globally, with 5.4161 (3.1676-9.3429) and 1.2791 (0.4992-2.5331) per 100,000 population, respectively. A significant increase in the global incidence and death burden of MDR-TB, XDR-TB, HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB, and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB has been reported from baseline to 2021. Especially for HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB, death cases increased 84.89-fold, with an EAPC in ASDR of 10 (6.26-13.86). In contrast, MDR-TB demonstrated a comparatively smaller increase, with death cases rising 5.65-fold and an EAPC in ASDR of 1.18 (-0.37-2.75). Over the past 32 years, the incidence and death ratio of these types of DR-TB in the High-middle SDI region have been the highest. In terms of age patterns, the burden of MDR-TB and XDR-TB has increased most significantly in the 15-49 age group. In contrast, the burden of HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB has notably increased among those aged 5-14. CONCLUSION: Over the past 30 years, a significant increase in the global burden of MDR-TB, XDR-TB, HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB, and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB has been reported, with marked variations in various resistance types across different regions and countries. In particular, the high-middle SDI regions warrant special attention. These findings highlight the need for further research to identify effective intervention strategies tailored to the epidemiological patterns observed in different regions and populations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer exhibits profound clinical, radiological, and biological heterogeneity, which poses significant challenges for early recognition and timely diagnosis in select atypical cases. Among rare manifestations, massive bronchorrhea caused by EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma with radiological findings of a dominant pulmonary nodule and migratory ground-glass opacities (GGOs) remains extremely uncommon. CASE PRESENTATION: A 67-year-old male patient presented with massive bronchorrhea and progressive dyspnea. Serial chest computed tomography (CT) scans revealed bilateral migratory GGOs and a small nodular lesion in the basal segment of the right lower lobe. Empiric antibiotic therapy and subsequent systemic corticosteroid treatment failed to alleviate his respiratory symptoms. Ultimately, markedly elevated sputum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) levels, combined with pathological results from transbronchial biopsy of the right lung nodule, confirmed a diagnosis of EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma. Treatment with osimertinib achieved rapid resolution of bronchorrhea, accompanied by complete regression of the pulmonary nodule and GGOs during clinical follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for lung adenocarcinoma in patients with persistent unexplained bronchorrhea. For patients harboring EGFR-sensitive mutations, EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) remain the first-line treatment, yielding favorable therapeutic effects on bronchorrhea control and improving survival outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Large pedunculated submucosal lesions of the proximal esophagus are uncommon. Their mobility and bulk can obscure the pedicle and restrict safe access for conventional endoscopic resection. We describe a single illustrative case and a rigid endoscopic technique in which a flexible detachable loop is tightened around the lesion, released from its delivery catheter and grasped by its free proximal tail to maintain traction during monopolar resection. A 75-year-old woman with progressive dysphagia had a 15-mm pedunculated lesion in the proximal esophagus. The lesion was excised without a perioperative complication and histology confirmed a submucosal lipoma. Solid food was gradually reintroduced, dysphagia had resolved by 6 months, and there was no clinical evidence of recurrence at 1 year. Snare-assisted suspension may facilitate exposure and manipulation of selected pedunculated benign-appearing esophageal lesions during rigid endoscopy. Further evaluation is required to determine wider applicability and clinical benefit.

papers.abstract_en: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease that affects various tissues of the body. One of these tissues is the lung, in which pleuropulmonary manifestations commonly occur. In these patients, homeostasis is disrupted, characterized by a decrease in Treg and an increase in Th1 and Th2 cells. Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are a cell population characterized by their ability to suppress the T cell response; however, in recent years, the presence of major histocompatibility complex class II (MHC-II) molecules on MDSCs has been reported. Nevertheless, the presence of costimulatory molecules, such as CD80, CD86, and ICOSL, has not been studied yet in MDSCs expressing MHC-II in the context of SLE. In this study, we evaluated the pulmonary microenvironment in SLE mice from an immunological and histological perspective. We observed increased pro-inflammatory cytokines and cellular infiltration in lungs of SLE mice. We also observed MDSC MHC-II cells expressing CD80, CD86, and ICOSL in this tissue, along with alterations of CD4+ T cells subsets, characterized by a decrease in IL-10 frequency in SLE mice. Moreover, we observed that G-MDSCs MHC-II expressing CD80, CD86, or ICOSL correlate positively with phenotypes of CD4+ T cells that produce IL-17 and IFN-γ. For this reason, we suggest that MHC-II+ G-MDSC cells may contribute to an inflammatory environment that triggers tissue damage in the lungs of SLE mice.

He had no wheezing, hemoptysis, chest pain, palpitations, or skin rashes. He did not smoke and reported occasional alcohol intake. One year earlier, he had been diagnosed elsewhere with pleuro-pericardial TB based on an ultrasound showing right-sided pleural effusion, and 2-dimensional echocardiography showed pericardial effusion. Pleural fluid analysis showed a lymphocytic exudative pleural effusion with elevated adenosine deaminase levels (46 IU/mL). The patient received anti-tubercular therapy along with tapering corticosteroids, showing initial clinical improvement. He was employed as a soldier in the army, and his last posting was in northeast India, where he frequently consumed raw crabs pickled in alcohol. There was no other significant environmental history.

papers.title_en: RNA-binding proteins as emerging regulators in interstitial lung diseases.
papers.authors: Mahavadi P, Guenther A
papers.affiliation_highlight: Center for Interstitial and Rare Lung Diseases, Department of Internal Medicine, Justus-Liebig University (JLU), 35392 G…
papers.authors_conclusion: RBP dysregulation may represent a broader post-transcriptional phenomenon across ILD subtypes; RBPs are emerging as post-transcriptional orchestrators of ILD pathogenesis with potential as therapeutic targets
papers.ai_note: 综述性质，无原创临床数据，pico与数值均信息不足；文中引用的FUS相关证据来自他人细胞、离体与3D模型研究，属临床前证据，向人体治疗靶点外推存在距离；对RBP靶向的临床可成药性与安全性未提供系统评价
papers.abstract_en: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are emerging as critical post-transcriptional regulators that control multiple stages of RNA life cycle, thereby linking post-transcriptional programs to cellular function. Increasing evidence implicates dysregulated RBP-RNA interactions in key pathological mechanisms underlying interstitial lung diseases (ILDs), including epithelial injury, fibroblast activation, immune dysregulation and impaired tissue repair. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), cytoplasmic retention of the RBP Fused in Sarcoma (FUS) in patient derived fibroblasts is associated with preferential binding to profibrotic transcripts, while antisense oligonucleotide mediated suppression of FUS attenuates fibrotic signaling and enhances epithelial regenerative programs in cellular, ex vivo and 3D models. Emerging findings across ILD subtypes suggest that RBP dysregulation may represent a broader post-transcriptional phenomenon. Here, we review the principles governing RBP-RNA interactions, approaches for identifying and measuring these interactions and the links between RBPs, aging and lung pathology. We further discuss the emerging role of RBPs as post-transcriptional orchestrators of ILD pathogenesis and consider their potential as therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: RA-ILD is a serious complication of RA. Patients are prone to spontaneous pneumothorax and have a higher risk of lung cancer.Given poor lung function and high risk of pneumothorax recurrence, conventional biopsy is challenging, making diagnosis difficult. CASE PRESENTATION: A 67-year-old male with a history of smoking and well-controlled rheumatoid arthritis presented with chest tightness and pleuritic chest pain. On admission, he was found to have respiratory failure (PaO₂ 58.9mmHg). Chest CT revealed left-sided pneumothorax with interstitial lung disease.Following closed thoracic drainage, the pneumothorax resolved, which was confirmed by follow-up chest X-ray.But the persistence of the patient's chest pain despite resolution of the pneumothorax prompted further investigation.CT pulmonary angiography identified a suspicious mass in the left lower lobe with adjacent rib destruction and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Given the high risk of recurrent pneumothorax from percutaneous biopsy in a patient with recent pneumothorax and pre-existing respiratory failure, a multidisciplinary team recommended Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration(EBUS-TBNA) as a safer alternative. EBUS of enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes (stations 7 and 11L) confirmed poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinoma.The patient subsequently received first-line chemotherapy with pemetrexed, cisplatin, and bevacizumab, after which his condition gradually stabilized. CONCLUSION: Both pneumothorax and interstitial lung disease can mask an occult malignancy, underscoring the need for clinical vigilance. EBUS-TBNA is a safe and effective diagnostic option in such high-risk cases.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: More than one billion people live within 100 km of an active volcano, yet the respiratory hazard of ash resists generalization. Bulk composition modulates eruption parameters, therefore respirability, and determines the availability of crystalline silica and labile metals in basaltic ash. AREAS COVERED: We review the health-pertinent properties of volcanic ash, consistently reported symptoms of acute exposure, and the thin, confounded evidence for chronic disease, where co-exposure to volcanic gases and aerosols impairs attribution. We develop an underexplored possibility: volcanic environments increase the risk of environmentally acquired lung infection via ash fomites carrying viable bacteria, innate defense impairment, including iron-dependent nutritional immunity, and selection for pathogen metal-resistance systems in metal-rich volcanic environments. Nontuberculous mycobacterial lung disease in Hawai'i and an exploratory country-level comparison of epidemiology metrics with volcanism test whether the disease axis is visible in existing data. EXPERT OPINION: Volcanic ash hazards are eruption-specific and crystalline silica and labile metals are joined by a scarcely tested third. That is, environmentally acquired bacterial lung infections are higher in 'volcanic' countries and account for a greater share of respiratory infections; both outcomes are ecological and hypothesis-generating. The infectious disease pathway and health effects of chronic exposure remain the least constrained assessment element.

papers.abstract_en: Asthma is a heterogeneous disease characterized by chronic airway inflammation and airway remodeling. Growing evidence suggests that mitochondrial dysfunction is not only a consequence of inflammatory injury but may also contribute to disease persistence and progression. In asthma, mitochondrial redox balance, energy metabolism, Ca2+ homeostasis, dynamics, biogenesis, and quality control can all become dysregulated. These abnormalities are interconnected and can alter mitochondrial energy supply, structural integrity, and quality maintenance. Mitochondrial damage can increase mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, promote the mislocalization of mitochondrial nucleic acids, alter membrane lipid oxidation and remodeling, and induce the release of mitochondrial proteins and other components. These changes generate diverse mitochondria-derived damage signals that can regulate inflammation-related gene transcription, nucleic acid sensing, and inflammasome activation. More broadly, mitochondrial abnormalities also alter immune cell function, airway epithelial repair, smooth muscle cell accumulation, and extracellular matrix production. Together, these effects may contribute to persistent airway inflammation and airway remodeling. This review summarizes the major forms of mitochondrial dysfunction in asthma. It also examines how these abnormalities generate mitochondria-derived damage signals, engage inflammatory sensing, and alter immune and airway structural cell functions.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Dirozalkib is a highly selective anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) inhibitor with intracranial antitumor activity against crizotinib-resistant mutations. This phase III trial evaluated dirozalkib versus crizotinib in patients with ALK inhibitor-naïve, ALK-positive, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods: In this multicenter, randomized, open-label DIAMOND-2 trial, adult patients with ALK inhibitor-naïve, ALK-positive, advanced NSCLC who either had received no prior systemic therapy or had experienced disease progression or intolerance after one prior chemotherapy regimen were randomly assigned 1:1 to dirozalkib (500 mg once daily) or crizotinib (250 mg twice daily). The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS). Results: Between 2022 January 24 and 2023 April 30, 275 patients were randomly assigned to receive dirozalkib (n = 137) or crizotinib (n = 138). As of 2025 May 31, the median follow-up durations were 32.8 and 31.6 months, respectively. Median investigator-assessed PFS was 29.5 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 20.3 to not reached) months with dirozalkib versus 12.9 (95% CI = 11.1 to 17.6) months with crizotinib (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.47, 95% CI = 0.34 to 0.66; P < 0.001). Blinded-independent-central-review-assessed PFS was also significantly prolonged with dirozalkib (median PFS, 27.5 versus 12.9 months; HR = 0.54, 95% CI = 0.39 to 0.74; P < 0.001). Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were less frequent with dirozalkib than with crizotinib (60.6% versus 72.5%), and TEAEs led to treatment discontinuation in 2.2% and 7.2% of patients, respectively. Conclusions: Dirozalkib significantly improved PFS versus crizotinib, with a manageable safety profile, supporting its use as a first-line therapy for ALK-positive advanced NSCLC. Trial registration: This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov on 2022 January 24 (NCT05204628).

papers.abstract_en: Although EGFR inhibitors are highly effective for treating EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinomas (EGFR+ LUADs), resistance inevitably emerges, with histologic transformation to small cell lung cancer (SCLC) representing a particularly aggressive mechanism. Our prospective trial enrolled patients with EGFR+ LUAD at high risk of transformation (TP53/RB1-deficient) and treated them with first-line osimertinib combined with platinum and etoposide. Despite the addition of SCLC-directed chemotherapy, nearly half of patients (5 of 11) underwent SCLC transformation, with median progression-free survival of 11 months and overall survival of 33 months. Genomic and single-cell transcriptomic profiling of patient samples revealed clinical and subclinical plasticity associated with TP53/RB1 comutations, including histological transformation to SCLC, as well as mesenchymal and squamous histologies. These changes in plasticity were linked to progressive disruption of the RB pathway, leading to altered chromatin accessibility and induction of neuronal differentiation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition transcriptional programs, further intensified by osimertinib treatment. These findings provide insights into the role of plasticity in mediating drug tolerance.

papers.abstract_en: Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based chemoimmunotherapy has become a standard first-line treatment for patients with driver-negative metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the clinical benefit is limited. Radiotherapy has potential antitumor immunomodulatory effects, but the optimal dose and fractionation remain unclear. Methods: This single-arm, multicenter, prospective, phase II trial enrolled patients with stage IV driver-negative NSCLC who received first-line chemoimmunotherapy. During the ICI maintenance phase, patients received hybrid dose-fraction radiotherapy (Hybrid-RT): stereotactic ablative body radiotherapy (SABR) to targetable lesions and low-dose radiotherapy (LDRT) to other sites. Patients restaged to stage III disease after chemoimmunotherapy received short-course hypofractionated radiotherapy to all residual lesions. The primary endpoint was 1-year progression-free survival (PFS) rate. The secondary endpoints included 1-year overall survival (OS) rate, objective response rate, and safety. Parallel preclinical mechanistic studies were performed in a murine model. Results: A total of 83 patients were enrolled from 2022 May 9 to 2023 December 31. The 1-year PFS rate was 54.2% (median PFS 16.1 months; 95% confidence interval [CI] 11.4 to 19.2 months), meeting the primary endpoint. The 1-year OS rate was 83.1% (median OS 29.3 months; 95% CI 21.9 months to not reached), and treatment was well tolerated. Peripheral immune profiling showed posttreatment expansion of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and natural killer (NK) cells associated with promising clinical efficacy. In the murine model, ICI plus Hybrid-RT (IHBRT) induced a division of labor between CD8+ T and NK cells. At LDRT lesions, it facilitated both C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (Cxcr3)-mediated recruitment of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and natural killer group 2 member D-mediated NK cell cytotoxicity. At SABR lesions, Cxcr3-mediated CD8+ T cells played a predominant role, whereas NK cells contributed minimally. Moreover, IHBRT suppressed secreted phosphoprotein 1 positive (Spp1+) macrophages and relieved immunosuppression. Conclusions: Clinically, IHBRT demonstrates promising efficacy and a manageable safety profile in driver-negative metastatic NSCLC. Preclinically, it induces a functional division of labor between CD8+ T and NK cells to activate antitumor immune cytotoxicity, and suppresses Spp1+ macrophages, thereby relieving immunosuppression. Trial registration: This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT05348668). Date of registration: 2022 April 26.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Variable clinical remission rates on biologics may reflect heterogeneity within type 2 (T2) asthma, but such heterogeneity remains largely unexplored. OBJECTIVES: To identify clinically distinct T2 asthma subtypes using multidimensional profiling and hierarchical clustering. METHODS: All T2 participants (n=764) were from the Australasian Severe Asthma Network, identified by elevated eosinophil levels, elevated FeNO, or allergic sensitization. Baseline clinical and inflammatory data were integrated to identify potential clusters in the training set using hierarchical clustering, followed by prospective assessment of exacerbation over 12 months. A random forest classifier was internally cross-validated and applied to a held-out validation set to assess profile consistency. RESULTS: Three subtypes emerged as: Cluster 1 (n=241, 45.0%) represented a female-predominant, well-controlled allergic subtype; Cluster 2 (n=110, 20.6%) constituted older T2 asthma patients with overlapping non-T2 features, including increased sputum neutrophil counts, fixed airflow limitation, and multiple comorbidities, with higher severe exacerbation rates (incidence rate ratios [IRR]=2.54, P=0.025) and emergency visit rates (IRR=5.06, P=0.040); and Cluster 3 (n=184, 34.4%) showed multiple elevated T2 biomarkers, poor symptom control and increased severe exacerbation (IRR=2.49, P=0.007) and hospitalization risk (IRR=3.28, P=0.009). The classifier showed 83.6% agreement with the original cluster assignments (κ=0.738), with post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC, age, and BMI as leading discriminators. CONCLUSIONS: T2 asthma encompasses distinct subtypes with prognostic and therapeutic implications. Our findings support a precision medicine approach for these subtypes: Cluster 3 patients may warrant early assessment for biologic therapy when eligible, while Cluster 2 may benefit from integrated strategies addressing non-T2 traits.

papers.abstract_en: Primary pulmonary NUT carcinoma (PPNC) is an ultra-rare, highly aggressive thoracic malignancy driven by NUTM1 rearrangements, most commonly BRD4:NUTM1. Morphologic overlap with poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, neuroendocrine carcinoma, and carcinoma not otherwise specified frequently delays diagnosis, while rapid progression and limited evidence hinder treatment standardization. This narrative review synthesizes literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science, together with registered trials from ClinicalTrials.gov, through May 2026, covering epidemiology, molecular pathogenesis, diagnosis, locoregional therapy, systemic treatment, and investigational strategies. An exploratory descriptive analysis of 15,938 lung tumor samples from 41 independent cBioPortal datasets identified a canonical NUTM1 structural variant in 1 of 15,938 samples (0.006%), supporting the genomic rarity of PPNC and highlighting potential limitations of DNA-only workflows for clinically relevant rearrangements. PPNC is usually reported in young to middle-aged adults, appears more frequent in men, and commonly presents with nonspecific thoracic symptoms. Molecular data suggest phenotypic and transcriptional convergence with squamous cell carcinoma through BRD-NUT-driven programs centered on MYC and TP63, with context-dependent SOX2 activation. Accurate recognition requires early NUT immunohistochemistry, followed when feasible by RNA-based fusion testing. No standard systemic regimen exists. Platinum-based regimens remain common, whereas retrospective pulmonary-specific data suggest that definitive chemoradiotherapy may be preferable to chemotherapy alone in selected patients. Bromodomain and extraterminal (BET) inhibitor monotherapy shows target engagement but limited durability, supporting rational combinations. Radiotherapy-immunotherapy combinations and PRAME-directed T-cell-engaging therapies remain investigational; the latter have only preclinical support so far. Earlier diagnosis, multimodal definitive treatment, and prioritized basket-trial enrollment are essential to improve outcomes.
