papers.abstract_en: Cisplatin resistance remains a major therapeutic challenge in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Here, we investigated the antitumor effects and underlying mechanisms of Huayu Wan (HYW) in cisplatin-resistant ESCC. HYW markedly inhibited the growth of cisplatin-resistant human KYSE150 and murine mEC25 cells and induced a ferroptotic phenotype characterized by reactive oxygen species accumulation, increased intracellular iron, glutathione depletion, lipid peroxidation, and reduced GPX4 expression. Ferrostatin-1 partially reversed HYW-induced cytotoxicity. HYW also promoted immunogenic cell death-associated changes, including extracellular ATP and HMGB1 release and cell-surface calreticulin exposure. Mechanistically, HYW increased p53 expression and impaired the SLC7A11/GCLC-dependent cystine-glutathione antioxidant system, whereas GCLC overexpression and P53 inhibition partially restored redox homeostasis and cell survival. In parallel, HYW suppressed AKT-mTOR signaling and promoted NCOA4-associated ferritinophagy, as evidenced by increased NCOA4 and LC3-II and decreased FTH expression. Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy and NCOA4 knockdown attenuated iron accumulation and HYW-induced cytotoxicity. In cisplatin-resistant syngeneic tumors, HYW suppressed tumor growth with generally acceptable systemic tolerability, enhanced ferroptosis- and immunogenic stress-associated changes, reduced PD-L1 expression, and increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration. Moreover, HYW combined with anti-PD-1 treatment produced greater antitumor effects than either monotherapy. These findings suggest that HYW promotes ferroptosis through coordinated disruption of glutathione metabolism and NCOA4-associated ferritinophagy while enhancing antitumor immune responses in cisplatin-resistant ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Extracellular adenosine triphosphate contributes to cough hypersensitivity through purinergic signalling, but airway purinergic biomarkers have not been well characterized in chronic cough. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of measuring sputum adenosine triphosphate, adenosine, and CD39L1 and their relationship with cough outcomes. METHODS: In a prospective observational study, 100 adults with chronic cough were classified as chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis (n=45) or refractory chronic cough (n=55) and received guideline-based treatment. Induced sputum was collected before and after treatment. Biomarkers were quantified using bioluminescence and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays and compared with 24-hour cough frequency, cough-specific quality of life, and cough severity. RESULTS: Baseline biomarker concentrations were similar between groups. In refractory chronic cough, lower sputum adenosine triphosphate and higher CD39L1 were associated with worse patient-reported cough outcomes, whereas no associations were observed in chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis. Sputum adenosine triphosphate decreased following treatment in the overall cohort and in chronic cough secondary to asthma or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis, while adenosine and CD39L1 remained unchanged. Changes in biomarkers were not associated with clinical improvement. CONCLUSION: Purinergic biomarkers can be measured in induced sputum. Lower adenosine triphosphate and higher CD39L1 were associated with worse cough outcomes in refractory chronic cough. CLINICAL IMPLICATION: Measurement of airway purinergic biomarkers may help identify neuronal dysfunction and support the development of targeted therapies for refractory chronic cough. GOV ID: NCT04758351 CAPSULE SUMMARY: Sputum purinergic biomarkers can be measured in chronic cough and may identify neuronal dysfunction, supporting their potential as treatable traits and biomarkers for targeted therapies.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Adherence to center-based pulmonary rehabilitation after a COPD-related hospitalization-which improves all outcomes, including survival-is only 3%. Home-based programs have been proposed as a more feasible option, but they are not systematically offered, and patient preference is unknown. OBJECTIVES AND METHODS: This pragmatic randomized trial involving patients with COPD recently hospitalized for a COPD exacerbation, originally aimed to investigate the comparative effect two arms: The choice of a facilitated referral to a center-based outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation program or a home-based program versus a home-based program on adherence to post-hospitalization rehabilitation and disease-specific QoL measured by the Chronic Respiratory Questionnaire. The trial aimed to investigate the patient's preference of home vs center-based rehabilitation in individuals randomized to the choice arm. Daily steps were measured by Actigraph ®.The asynchronous home-based program included weekly health coaching and daily monitoring of daily steps, symptoms, and a 20-minute daily flexibility-balance exercise routine. RESULTS: Of 1,906 patients approached, 294 (15%) were randomized and agreed to the rehabilitation options offered by the study arms (uptake); of those, 56% completed the 12-week intervention (adherence). Of the 145 randomized to the choice arm, only one patient chose center-based PR; therefore, both groups received the same intervention, and results are presented as a one-group (before-after) analysis. Compared with baseline, the home intervention significantly improved (p < 0.01) physical and emotional QoL (Chronic Respiratory Questionnaire) and increased daily steps beyond the minimal clinically important difference. Trajectory models adjusted for age, FEV1%, and mMRC (breathlessness) confirmed sustained improvements in QoL at 6 and 12 months from baseline. CONCLUSIONS: When offered a choice of rehabilitation setting after a COPD-related hospital admission for an exacerbation, home-based rehabilitation is patients' preferred option. Sustained quality-of-life improvements in 1 year may represent an opportunity to regain well-being and/or deliver primary palliative care. Our results may have important implications for clinical practice.

papers.title_zh: Echinacoside inhibits ferroptosis and pyroptosis in ARDS through modulation of the KEAP1/NRF2/P62 signaling pathway.
papers.title_en: Echinacoside inhibits ferroptosis and pyroptosis in ARDS through modulation of the KEAP1/NRF2/P62 signaling pathway.
papers.authors: Su D, Li R, Deng G, Li J, Ren J, Gao Y, Zhang J, Han Z et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Critical Care Medicine, the Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University, Xi'an, China; Departm…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains a life-threatening pulmonary condition with persistently high mortality rates. Echinacoside (ECH) is a natural compound that has shown protective effects in experimental acute lung injury; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects in ARDS remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to explore the potential mechanisms underlying the protective role of ECH in ARDS. METHODS: The protective effect of ECH on ARDS mice was evaluated. Subsequently, network pharmacology combined with RNA-sequencing was employed to identify mechanisms modulated by ECH. Finally, the mechanism of ECH on ARDS was verified in ARDS mice and mouse lung epithelial cells. RESULTS: ECH reduced the level of inflammatory response and alleviated lung injury in ARDS mice. Network pharmacology and RNA sequencing results suggested that its mechanism may be related to regulating inflammatory response, anti-oxidative stress, and inhibiting cell death. Further experiments indicated that ECH inhibited ferroptosis and pyroptosis, possibly through regulation of the KEAP1/NRF2 axis. Molecular dynamics, molecular docking, and protein-small molecule interaction verification demonstrated that ECH binds to the Kelch/DGR domain of KEAP1. CONCLUSIONS: ECH binds to KEAP1 and may interfere with the KEAP1-NRF2 interaction, thereby promoting NRF2 release, which subsequently suppresses cellular pyroptosis and ferroptosis, ultimately reducing inflammation and lung injury. These findings support further investigation of ECH as a potential strategy for ARDS.

papers.abstract_en: Asymptomatic tuberculosis is a major but incompletely defined manifestation of the tuberculosis disease spectrum and an important challenge for active case finding. It is best understood as a symptom-defined and method-dependent phenotype rather than a uniform biological stage. Individuals classified as asymptomatic may have minimal or extensive radiographic abnormalities, low or intermittent bacillary shedding, or clinically inapparent disease that remains stable, regresses, fluctuates, or progresses. Differences in terminology, symptom ascertainment, population risk and diagnostic intensity have therefore led to substantial variation in how asymptomatic or subclinical tuberculosis is recognized and interpreted across studies and programmes. This Review examines current and emerging approaches for diagnosing asymptomatic tuberculosis, with emphasis on the interaction between epidemiological risk, radiological detectability, microbiological confirmation and longitudinal follow-up. Symptom-based screening and passive case finding miss a substantial proportion of bacteriologically or radiographically evident tuberculosis. Conventional sputum-based testing is constrained by difficulty obtaining specimens, paucibacillary disease, intermittent shedding and imperfect sensitivity. Chest radiography and computer-aided detection can expand screening capacity and standardize triage, but they cannot independently establish disease activity or exclude tuberculosis. Computed tomography and positron emission tomography/computed tomography provide more sensitive characterization in selected settings, although their cost, accessibility and limited specificity preclude routine use. Non-sputum pathogen assays and host biomarkers are promising because they may reduce dependence on spontaneous sputum, but most remain insufficiently validated, and their incremental clinical or programmatic value over imaging-based triage and conventional confirmation remains uncertain. The diagnostic challenge of asymptomatic tuberculosis lies not simply in the absence of symptoms, but in the unstable boundary between infection, early disease, radiological abnormality, microbiological detectability and future risk. Clinical and public health practice should therefore move beyond single-test strategies toward staged, risk-stratified diagnostic pathways that integrate symptom ascertainment, exposure risk, imaging, confirmatory microbiology, enhanced specimen collection and longitudinal reassessment. Such pathways should be viewed as flexible clinical-programmatic frameworks for organizing diagnostic uncertainty, guiding multidisciplinary decisions and generating testable hypotheses, rather than as validated treatment algorithms.

papers.title_zh: Mycobacterium abscessus induces immune suppression in cystic fibrosis macrophages.
papers.title_en: Mycobacterium abscessus induces immune suppression in cystic fibrosis macrophages.
papers.authors: Hill PJ, Miller CJ, Rascon R, Clary G, Idosa AW, Gavrilin MA, McCoy KS, Amer AO et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Microbial Infection & Immunity, The Ohio State University, Columbus, OH, United States.
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: People with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) are highly susceptible to chronic lung infections with Mycobacterium abscessus (MAB), a nontuberculous mycobacterium (NTM) that is intrinsically resistant to antibiotics. While macrophage dysfunction is recognized in CF, responses to MAB in primary human macrophages remain poorly defined. METHODS: We investigated the innate immune response to MAB using peripheral blood monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages from pwCF and healthy donors. Macrophages were infected with opsonized smooth (MAS) or rough (MAR) isolates of MAB morphotypes at low multiplicity of infection. After removal of extracellular bacteria, intracellular burden, oxidative burst, NOX2 activation, and cytokine production were assessed at 2- and 24-hours post-infection. RESULTS: MAB uptake was comparable across all groups and non-CF macrophages showed no difference in intracellular MAR or MAS at 24h. In contrast, CF macrophages harbored significantly more intracellular MAR at 24 hours, a phenotype recapitulated by CFTR knockdown in non-CF macrophages. MAB-infected CF macrophages demonstrated a significantly reduced oxidative burst and diminished NOX2 p47phox phosphorylation. Non-CF macrophages treated with CFTR inhibitor mimicked the reduced oxidative burst. CF macrophages also exhibited an altered cytokine response with significantly elevated IL-8 but decreased IL-1β relative to healthy macrophages. Notably, MAR-infected CF macrophages secreted significantly less TNF-α compared with non-CF macrophages and exhibited markedly reduced apoptosis compared with MAR-infected non-CF and MAS-infected CF macrophages. DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate that CF macrophages are intrinsically impaired in their ability to control the virulent rough MAB morphotype, highlighting a potential mechanism for persistent NTM infection in pwCF and underscoring the need for host-directed therapies.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Drug-resistant tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia. This study aimed to characterize the genetic diversity, lineage distribution, and genotypic resistance profiles of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates across the Indonesian archipelago using whole-genome sequencing. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted using 1,281 analyzed MTB isolates derived from the 2017-2018 National Tuberculosis Drug Resistance Survey (DRS TB). Samples were screened via Xpert MTB/RIF and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing using the MGIT 960 system. Genomic DNA was extracted using the CTAB protocol. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) libraries were prepared using the Nextera XT DNA Library Preparation Kit (Illumina, San Diego, CA, USA). Sequencing was performed on an Illumina MiSeq platform using the MiSeq Reagent Kit v3 (600 cycles), generating paired-end reads of 2 × 300 bp. To identify drug resistance-associated mutations and determine strain lineage/sub-lineages, raw sequencing reads were initially processed with Trimmomatic. The filtered reads were subsequently aligned to the Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv reference genome (ATCC 27294;NC_000962.3) using the MTBseq pipeline, which the BWA-MEM algorithm (v0.7.17) for sequence mapping. Variant calling was carried out with Samtools mpileup (v1.6). RESULTS: Four major MTB lineages were identified: Lineage 4 (43.1%) was dominant, followed by Lineage 2 (30.4%) and Lineage 1 (26.3%), while Lineage 3 was rare, with only 0.16% detected. At the sub-lineage level, L2.2.1 (18.5%), L1.2.1 (11.3%), and L4.1.2.1 (9.7%) were the most prevalent. Resistance to first-line drugs was the most frequent, primarily driven by mutations in the katG p.Ser315Thr (7.5%) and rpoB p.Ser450Leu (5%), conferring isoniazid and rifampicin resistance, respectively. Second-line resistance was highest for Fluoroquinolones (2.03%). Notably, four pre-XDR strains (0.31%) were identified and validated across Java-Bali and Sumatera, all harboring critical gyrA mutations and rpoB mutations (p.Asp435Tyr, p.Asn437Asp, p.Ser450Leu, and p.Ser450Trp). CONCLUSION: The study confirms a high prevalence of L2 and L4 in Indonesia. The identification of pre-XDR-TB isolates among the national survey samples highlights an urgent need for expanded molecular surveillance. While newer drugs like Bedaquiline remain effective, the presence of specific gyrA mutations underscores the necessity of integrating WGS into national TB control programs to proactively manage resistance and optimize treatment regimens.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Vagal sensory neurons that innervate the airways signal the detected noxious information to the brain to produce a perceptible sensation called urge-to-cough as well as reflex and behavioural coughing. Understanding the central neural mechanisms in regulating airway sensory processing is important for the development of more effective therapeutic options for conditions such as chronic cough. METHODS: In this pilot study, healthy volunteers (n=14) inhaled nebulised capsaicin at a personalised maximum concentration for induction of a strong level of urge-to-cough without coughing. Magnetoencephalography (MEG) was employed to directly detect regional neural activity changes in the brain accompanying capsaicin-evoked urge-to-cough sensations. RESULTS: The neural activity in delta and high gamma bands increased with an increase in capsaicin-evoked urge-to-cough in multiple higher order brain regions such as the insula, the cerebellum, the thalamus, the putamen and the brainstem areas, including the medullary nuclei where airway-innervating vagal sensory neurons are known to terminate. CONCLUSION: For the first time, we have established the feasibility and utility of MEG for examining the brain control of coughing. We show that the neural activity in delta and high gamma bands in multiple brain regions including medullary nuclei is involved in processing of urge-to-cough, confirming previous findings with functional magnetic resonance imaging.

papers.authors: Yang Y, Yao Z, Zhang Z, Yu M, Yao C, Jia L, Hua F

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Pneumonia is one of the deadliest lower respiratory tract infections worldwide, and rapidly distinguishing bacterial pneumonia, viral pneumonia, and normal chest radiographs is crucial for guiding precise medication and avoiding misdiagnosis. However, the imaging manifestations of bacterial and viral pneumonia on chest X-rays often overlap, and some normal chest X-rays may also show atypical changes. Clinical differentiation relies heavily on the expertise of senior physicians. In primary care or emergency settings where experienced radiologists are scarce, this can readily lead to diagnostic delays and antibiotic misuse, further exacerbating the risk of antimicrobial resistance and severe outcomes. METHODS: To address this challenge, this study proposes a lightweight network named FLIFuse. By adopting a parallel multi-branch architecture, the model thoroughly mines discriminative imaging features, substantially reducing computational overhead while maintaining high classification accuracy. This provides a technical solution that balances accuracy and efficiency for medical image analysis in resource-constrained environments. FLIFuse consists of three heterogeneous branches: an ExtraDW module that enhances local texture details, a Conv2Next module that captures global semantic structures, and an FLI Block that fuses multi-granularity information across different receptive fields to strengthen the response in critical regions. RESULTS: The model occupies only 33.43 M parameters and incurs a computational cost of 6.61 GFLOPs. On the public ChestXRay2017 dataset, FLIFuse achieves a three-class classification accuracy of 91.4% for normal, bacterial pneumonia, and viral pneumonia, outperforming several current state-of-the-art models and attaining extremely low resource consumption while ensuring diagnostic accuracy. In cross-domain tests on an external COVID-19 chest X-ray dataset and the Nerthus endoscopic image dataset, the model also exhibits stable transferability, demonstrating its potential for cross-domain adaptation across different medical imaging tasks. DISCUSSION: These results demonstrate that FLIFuse strikes a favorable balance between diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency, providing an efficient and lightweight model option for computer-aided interpretation of pneumonia imaging, and showing potential for translation into clinical auxiliary diagnosis.

papers.abstract_en: A 27-year-old man with cystic fibrosis, prior liver transplantation for advanced cystic fibrosis related liver disease, tacrolimus immunosuppression, multidrug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, recurrent drug induced liver injury, and intolerance to elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor underwent matched bacteriophage therapy. Intravenous phages were administered at 109 plaque forming units per dose and nebulised phages at 5 × 109 plaque forming units per dose twice daily. Within two days, marked elevations in alanine transaminase, aspartate transaminase, alkaline phosphatase, and gamma glutamyl transferase developed, prompting treatment cessation. Peak alanine transaminase reached 494 U/L and alkaline phosphatase 527 U/L were observed, while bilirubin and coagulation parameters remained normal. Extensive investigation, including magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography and medication review, identified no alternative cause. Rechallenge with nebulised phage therapy alone resulted in recurrent liver enzyme elevation after eight days, again resolving following discontinuation. Temporal correlation was demonstrated between liver function test abnormalities and detection of phage DNA in serum and sputum. No bacteriophage neutralisation, bacterial DNAaemia, development of phage resistance, or significant bacterial genomic change was observed. Despite early cessation, lung function improved over the subsequent six months.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Allergic and type 2 (T2) inflammatory biomarkers are increasingly used to predict outcomes and guide treatment in asthma and COPD. The objective of this cross-sectional study was to determine the prevalence of allergic sensitisation and T2 biomarkers and their clinical associations among patients with diagnoses of asthma and/or COPD in NOVELTY, a large multinational, observational study. METHODS: Participants were enrolled from primary/specialist care, stratified by physician-assigned diagnosis and severity. We assessed fractional exhaled nitric oxide (≥25 ppb), blood eosinophils (≥300 cells·µL-1) and allergen-specific IgE sensitisation (≥0.35 kU·L-1 to any of 11 aeroallergens). Associations between biomarkers and clinical outcomes were examined using descriptive statistics and multivariable regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index and smoking status. RESULTS: Data for all biomarkers were available for 4352 participants (asthma: n=2194; asthma+COPD: n=633; COPD: n=1525). Overall, 63% participants had at least one positive biomarker (asthma: 77%; asthma+COPD: 60%; COPD: 45%); only 8%, 4% and 1% of participants, respectively, were positive for all three biomarkers. Women and current smokers were more likely to be triple-negative. Among participants with asthma, having more positive biomarkers was associated with more severe physician-assessed disease, lower lung function and exacerbations. By contrast, in COPD, having no positive biomarkers was associated with more severe physician-assessed disease and lower lung function. CONCLUSIONS: Allergic and T2 biomarkers are highly prevalent in asthma and asthma+COPD but less frequent in COPD. Their patterns show distinct associations, sometimes with opposite trends, across diagnostic groups, suggesting distinct underlying mechanisms that differ.

papers.authors: Semphere R, Mukoka M, Msosa TC, Twabi HH, MacPherson P, Mushonga R, Nliwasa M, Kumwenda MK et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Chichiri Centre for Health Research and Training, Kamuzu University of Health Sciences, Blantyre, Malawi.

papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要未报告任何效应量、比例或统计检验数值，结论为参与者主观叙述的归纳，样本量仅14人且照护者作为儿童患者的代理，存在代理报告偏倚；作为单一城市地区的质性发现，外推性有限。
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge in Malawi. While diagnostic pathways are well established, less is known about how people experience repeated care-seeking and diagnostic uncertainty before receiving a TB diagnosis. OBJECTIVE: To explore pre-diagnostic TB experiences and care-seeking among adults with TB and caregivers of children with TB in urban Blantyre, Malawi. METHODS: We conducted in-depth interviews with 14 participants in urban Blantyre, Malawi (five male patients, five female patients, and four female caregivers acting as proxies for pediatric TB patients under 11 years). Data were coded deductively and inductively, then analyzed using a framework approach. Social Cognitive Theory informed the interview guide, and Candidacy Theory informed interpretation of access to TB investigation across multiple healthcare encounters. RESULTS: Participants described prolonged, distressing pre-diagnostic journeys, with early symptoms of TB frequently misattributed to malaria or minor respiratory conditions. As symptoms persisted, participants reported repeatedly seeking care, often attending health facilities multiple times before TB testing was initiated. These encounters did not provide immediate diagnostic resolution and represented participant-reported opportunities for earlier TB investigation. Participants' social networks shaped decision-making along the pathway, occasionally reinforcing misattribution but often prompting escalation to formal care. Repeated unresolved encounters imposed substantial economic burden on participants and their families, including loss of income, business disruption, and increased reliance on family support. CONCLUSION: In urban Malawi, participants described TB diagnostic pathways shaped by symptom uncertainty, social and material circumstances, and repeated healthcare encounters without timely diagnostic resolution. The findings highlight the potential value of reassessing persistent or worsening symptoms during repeat encounters. Strengthening such reassessment may support integrated, patient-centered TB care and reduce avoidable socioeconomic burden.

papers.abstract_en: Endobronchial carcinoid tumor rarely causes secondary spontaneous pneumothorax. We report a female in her 30s who reported progressive decline in her overall exercise tolerance with dyspnea on exertion and frequent upper respiratory infections (URIs) for 2 years presented for persistent spontaneous pneumothorax (SP). Initially, she presented to the emergency department (ED) for concerns of cough with mild hemoptysis and congestion for 2 weeks. She was found to have a small left-sided pneumothorax. She was admitted and treated for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Post-hospital follow-up showed a persistent pneumothorax unchanged in size. She was followed for weeks with serial chest X-rays, which later showed an increased size of the pneumothorax. She was admitted, and a chest tube was placed. Later, bronchoscopy was done, which showed near complete occlusion of the left mainstem bronchus by an endobronchial lesion. Pathology results showed a well-differentiated neuroendocrine grade 1 tumor consistent with carcinoid. She was successfully treated with tumor resection and photodynamic therapy (PDT). This case highlighted an unusual presentation of an endobronchial carcinoid tumor that requires further diagnostic workup with appropriate intervention.

papers.authors: Un Nisa MM, Sofi PA, Ahmad PI, Mir R, Bhat TB
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Forest Products and Utilization, Faculty of Forestry, Sher-E-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and…
papers.authors_conclusion: Atisine 和 podophyllotoxin 表现出显著抗肿瘤活性，并显示出与 IL-1R1 和 AR 良好的预测性相互作用，提示其作为双调节剂的潜力，值得进一步实验验证；其有希望的抗肿瘤谱得到强细胞毒性、良好的预测性蛋白-配体相互作用、可接受的药代动力学性质及多靶点网络药理学分析的支持；这些发现为进一步优化和体内验证、开发靶向炎症驱动与雄激素依赖性癌症的新型抗肿瘤药物提供初步基础
papers.ai_note: 核心主张是同时靶向 IL-1R1 与 AR，但摘要中没有任何靶点层面的实测数据（无结合实验、无受体表达/通路活性检测），全部靶点证据仅为对接与网络药理学预测，信息不足；报告的实测终点是细胞毒 IC50，属非特异性指标，podophyllotoxin 本身为已知微管毒物，其强细胞毒不能支持 IL-1R1/AR 双靶点机制；'outperforming doxorubicin' 未给出 doxorubicin 的 IC50 数值，也无统计学检验/CI，属不可核验的比较；results 将体外细胞毒与计算预测并列陈述以支撑双调节剂结论，存在证据层级混同与选择性强调；linoleic acid 活性弱（IC50 >100 µM）仍纳入结论性表述；网络药理学 hub 基因 SRC/EGFR/AKT1 为泛癌通用靶点，特异性有限；作者结论本身已注明 'warrant further experimental validation'，但摘要结论段仍以 'significant anticancer activity' 起头，措辞强于证据强度
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung and prostate cancers remain leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, driven by inflammation-mediated tumour progression and hormone-dependent signalling. IL-1R1 promotes chronic inflammation, metastasis, and tumour survival, while androgen receptor (AR) signalling is a central driver of prostate cancer growth. Simultaneous targeting of inflammatory and androgenic pathways represents a promising strategy to overcome therapeutic resistance. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate natural compounds derived from Aconitum heterophyllum (atisine, linoleic acid) and Podophyllum hexandrum (podophyllotoxin), as modulators of IL-1R1 and AR using integrated experimental and computational approaches. METHODS: Phytochemicals were extracted from tuberous roots of A. heterophyllum and fruits of P. hexandrum using Soxhlet extraction and isolated by TLC and column chromatography. Cytotoxicity and long-term antiproliferative effects were assessed using MTT and colony formation assays in A549 (lung) and LNCaP (prostate) cancer cell lines. Computational analyses included ADMET profiling, molecular docking against IL-1R1 (PDB: 1ITB) and AR (PDB: 2YHD), 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM-GBSA binding free-energy calculations, network pharmacology-based target and pathway enrichment analyses. RESULTS: Podophyllotoxin exhibited potent cytotoxicity with IC50 values of 0.04 µM in both A549 and LNCaP cells, outperforming doxorubicin, while atisine showed moderate activity (IC50: 2.1-2.3 µM). Linoleic acid displayed weak anticancer activity (IC50 >100 µM). Colony formation assays confirmed strong suppression of clonogenic survival by podophyllotoxin and a moderate inhibitory effect by atisine. Docking studies suggested favorable binding affinities (-8.1 to -5.9 kcal/mol), and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable protein-ligand complexes with low RMSD fluctuations. ADMET analysis supported favorable drug-likeness for atisine and podophyllotoxin. Network pharmacology identified 133 intersecting targets, with key hub genes including SRC, EGFR, and AKT1, enriched in PI3K-Akt and cancer-related signaling pathways. CONCLUSION: Atisine and podophyllotoxin exhibited significant anticancer activity and demonstrated favorable predicted interactions with the Interleukin-1 receptor type 1 (IL-1R1) and Androgen Receptor (AR), suggesting their potential as dual modulators that warrant further experimental validation. Their promising anticancer profile was supported by strong cytotoxicity, favorable predicted protein-ligand interactions, acceptable pharmacokinetic properties, and multitarget network pharmacology analyses. These findings provide a preliminary foundation for further optimization and in vivo validation toward the development of novel anticancer therapeutics targeting inflammation-driven and androgen-dependent cancers.

This study provides new insights into the organization of pulmonary immune states and the potential regulatory mechanisms underlying chronic inflammatory regulation in COPD.
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要未报告样本量、统计检验、效应量或置信区间，COPD与健康对照的富集仅作定性描述（selective enrichment），无法判断差异强度与稳健性。WTAP与炎症单核细胞程序的联系来自关联性多组学分析加体外敲低模型，属机制假说而非因果验证；敲低后促炎介质下降与干扰素/抗原提呈程序升高同时出现，作者对'抑制炎症'的解读需谨慎。研究为描述性基础研究，无临床终点，对临床决策的直接外推有限。
papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent pulmonary inflammation and tissue remodeling, yet the cellular states and regulatory mechanisms underlying monocyte functional heterogeneity remain incompletely understood. Here, we generate a high-resolution single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the human respiratory system and identify a diverse monocyte functional landscape in healthy lungs containing a HSPA1B+ inflammatory monocytes state. This population exhibits enhanced inflammatory programs, cytokine and chemokine activity, and shows a distinct position within the inferred transcriptional landscape of the continuous monocyte functional spectrum. Cell-cell communication analysis further reveals that HSPA1B+ inflammatory monocytes function as active communication nodes within a stromal-immune-vascular network, integrating MIF, extracellular matrix, and immune-regulatory signals while mediating CXCL and adhesion-associated interactions with surrounding cellular compartments. Comparative analysis of COPD lung tissues and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid demonstrates selective enrichment of this inflammatory monocyte program in disease-associated environments, whereas peripheral blood monocytes from healthy individuals and COPD patients show limited representation of this state. Integrated transcriptomic and m6A regulator-associated analyses identify WTAP, a core component of the m6A methyltransferase complex, as a factor associated with the inflammatory monocytes program. WTAP silencing in inflammatory monocyte models suppresses pro-inflammatory mediators while enhancing interferon-response and antigen-presentation programs. Collectively, these findings define an inflammatory monocyte state landscape in the human respiratory system and identify a WTAP-associated transcriptional program linked to monocyte inflammatory activation and functional remodeling in COPD. This study provides new insights into the organization of pulmonary immune states and the potential regulatory mechanisms underlying chronic inflammatory regulation in COPD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with severe uncontrolled asthma (SUA) and a T2 eosinophilic phenotype exhibit variable response to biologic therapy (BT). Currently, accurate biomarkers predicting this response are lacking. We aimed to explore whether microRNA (miRNA) and messenger RNA (mRNA) profiles in bronchial biopsies (BB) may help identify patients achieving a complete clinical response after 6 months of BT. AIMS: To explore whether BB miRNA and mRNA profiles may be associated with clinical response to BT in SUA population. METHODS: Thirty-four consecutive SUA patients with a T2 high phenotype were characterized and underwent bronchoscopy with BB before initiating anti-IL-5/5R BT. Clinical response was evaluated 6 months later. Both, miRNA and mRNA were extracted from BB, and their expression profiles were analyzed via microarrays. Gene Ontology and KEGG pathway analyses were performed to understand the biological functions and signaling pathways involved. RESULTS: After BT, 64% showed complete clinical response, 18% patients were non-responders, and 18% obtained a partial response. Comparing non-responders vs. responders showed 35 differentially expressed mRNAs, and 8 miRNAs in BB samples. Integrated analysis of miRNA and mRNA data suggested that three key genes (FOXO1, ZBTB16 and OLFML3) may be involved in asthma pathogenesis. CONCLUSIONS: Expression patterns between responders and non-responders to BT appeared to differ in BB of SUA patients, highlighting the involvement of multiple pathways related to airway inflammation and airway remodeling. Our results provide preliminary evidence suggesting that FOXO1, ZBTB16 and OLFML3 might be involved in the biological response to anti-IL-5/5R therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a life-threatening respiratory condition characterized by uncontrolled pulmonary inflammation and epithelial barrier dysfunction. Zang-Si-Wei Qingfei Mixture (ZSW) is a promising Tibetan herbal formula used clinically to alleviate pulmonary symptoms, yet its pharmacological targets and therapeutic pathways in ALI have not been fully explored. This study aims to identify the bioactive constituents of ZSW and elucidate their protective and therapeutic mechanisms in ALI. METHODS: ZSW's components were identified via liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) previously and network pharmacology. Target affinity was evaluated using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. In vivo, C57BL/6J mice with lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI were used to evaluate the pretreatment and post-treatment effects of ZSW and its core component, Ellagic Acid (EA). In vitro, MLE-12 cells and the PI3K/mTOR dual inhibitor BEZ235 were utilized to investigate the role of PI3K/AKT signaling and NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis. RESULTS: EA was identified as ZSW's core bioactive constituent, demonstrating high binding stability with AKT1, PIK3CA, and PIK3R1. In vivo, ZSW and EA significantly attenuated lung histological damage, edema, and alveolar-capillary hyperpermeability. Both markedly reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-1β) in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Mechanistically, ZSW and EA inhibited PI3K and AKT phosphorylation and were accompanied by decreased NLRP3 inflammasome-associated proteins (decreased NLRP3, ASC, and cleaved Caspase-1) and GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis (decreased GSDMD-N and lactate dehydrogenase release). Notably, the 6-h post-LPS therapeutic model showed that both treatments effectively reversed established lung injury. CONCLUSION: ZSW and EA exert anti-inflammatory and lung-protective effects, accompanied by modulation of PI3K/AKT signaling and suppression of NLRP3 inflammasome-associated pyroptosis. This provides robust scientific evidence for ZSW's clinical application and highlights EA as a promising therapeutic candidate for acute inflammatory lung diseases.

papers.title_zh: 瑞香素（daphnetin）靶向ACE2及多条炎症/氧化通路用于COVID-19与风湿共病的机制综述：提出'一药双护'假说，未提供临床疗效数据

papers.authors: Chen M, Zhang N, Wu Q, Cao Y, Zhang Z, Tang X, Zhao B, Zhu C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: School of Basic Medical Sciences, Wannan Medical University, Wuhu, 241001, China; Anhui Province Key Laboratory of Basic…
papers.authors_conclusion: 作者提出瑞香素代表一种新型的"one agent, dual protection"策略：既通过降低ACE2阻断病毒进入，又缓解加重COVID-19严重程度与风湿病活动度的高炎症和氧化应激状态；鉴于其已确立的安全性、口服活性和低成本，瑞香素是有前景的临床转化候选药物，适用于高风险共病人群。
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，摘要未报告任何临床疗效或安全性数值，所有机制（HIF-1α/JAK2/STAT3、NF-κB、NLRP3、Nrf2/Keap1、Th17/Treg等）为通路层面的推断整合，属假说生成而非验证；'已确立的安全性'来源于既往其他适应症使用，不能外推至COVID-19高危人群的疗效；针对JN.1/KP.3等变异株的活性未见实验数据支持；与胸科肿瘤业务关联极弱。信息不足：摘要无样本量、对照、终点与统计学信息。；数值未经四元组核验
papers.abstract_en: The continuous emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants (e.g., JN.1, KP.3) and the significantly elevated risk of severe COVID-19 in patients with rheumatic autoimmune diseases highlight an urgent unmet clinical need for dual-targeted therapeutics. Daphnetin (7,8-dihydroxycoumarin), a natural coumarin compound with a long history of clinical use in China, prevents SARS-CoV-2 infection by downregulating the viral entry receptor ACE2 through inhibition of HIF-1α and JAK2/STAT3 signaling. This review synthesizes the pleiotropic pharmacological mechanisms of daphnetin, including anti-inflammatory (NF-κB, JAK/STAT, NLRP3), antioxidant (Nrf2/Keap1), immunomodulatory (Th17/Treg balance), and mitochondrial protective pathways. These pathways are critically involved in the pathogenesis of both severe COVID-19 and rheumatic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We propose that daphnetin represents a novel "one agent, dual protection" strategy: it not only blocks viral entry by reducing ACE2 but also mitigates the hyperinflammatory and oxidative stress states that exacerbate both COVID-19 severity and rheumatic disease activity. Given its established safety, oral activity, and low cost, daphnetin is a promising candidate for clinical translation in high-risk comorbid populations. Key unresolved questions and future research directions are also discussed.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Effective therapy remains lacking for patients with advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) whose disease progressed after standard treatment. Izalontamab brengitecan, an epidermal growth factor receptor and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate with a topoisomerase I inhibitor, Ed-04, has shown clinical activity in ESCC in a phase 1b study. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of izalontamab brengitecan compared with chemotherapy in patients with advanced ESCC who progressed after first-line programmed cell death 1 protein (PD-1)/programmed cell death 1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase 3, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted across 80 hospitals in China. Patients with recurrent or metastatic ESCC that had progressed with first-line PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy were enrolled. Between March 19, 2024, and August 1, 2025 (final follow-up, October 17, 2025), a total of 704 patients were screened, and 497 were enrolled and randomized. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either izalontamab brengitecan (n = 249; 2.5 mg/kg on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks) or physician-selected chemotherapy (n = 248; irinotecan, paclitaxel, or docetaxel) every 3 weeks. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The dual primary end points were progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 and overall survival (OS). RESULTS: Of 497 patients who underwent randomization (median age, 61.0 years [range, 34-76]; 448 male patients [90.1%]), 493 received study treatment. At this interim analysis, izalontamab brengitecan demonstrated statistically significant improvement in both PFS and OS. Median PFS by blinded independent central review was 4.17 months (95% CI, 3.61-4.53 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 1.97 months (95% CI, 1.61-2.73 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.40-0.63; log-rank P < .001). Median OS was 9.79 months (95% CI, 7.89-11.01 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 7.20 months (95% CI, 6.18-7.82 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.48-0.82; log-rank P < .001). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 212 of 249 patients (85.1%) with izalontamab brengitecan and 147 of 248 patients (59.3%) with chemotherapy and were predominantly hematologic. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Izalontamab brengitecan significantly improved PFS and OS vs chemotherapy in patients with recurrent or metastatic ESCC whose disease had progressed after first-line treatment. These findings support izalontamab brengitecan as a new second-line treatment for this population in China. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06304974.

papers.abstract_en: Early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is hindered by a lack of noninvasive biomarkers for precancerous lesions. Here, we report a circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation approach for early esophageal neoplasia detection. In prospective community screening, the assay achieved standardized sensitivity of 78% at 79% specificity for the clinically actionable endpoint of high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (HGIN) or ESCC, with stage-specific sensitivities of 76% for HGIN and 86% for ESCC. Genome-wide methylation profiling reveals HGIN as an early epigenetic reprogramming stage. Integrative spatial and single-cell RNA sequencing reveals pronounced remodeling of the endothelial-proximal epithelial cell population, whose methylation signatures are detected in cfDNA. Guided by these findings, we develop an 11-gene cfDNA methylation panel that shows robust discrimination of early-stage ESCC across three retrospective case-control sets and an independent screening-derived case-control set. Together, these results demonstrate that our cfDNA methylation panel has promising utility for early ESCC detection.

papers.abstract_en: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)-a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate-has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)-a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study (n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population (n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59-1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd.

Further work should focus on external validation, implementation in clinical trial analyses, and assessment of applicability across diverse patient populations and health-care settings.
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要未报告任何一轮的应答率、各条目具体同意百分比、专家Kendall's W或kappa等一致性统计，也未给出各成分严重度权重的具体数值，无法评估共识强度与可重复性；研究无外部验证，作者亦自认随访时限与出院后监测未达共识，提示该定义在实际试验终点中的适用边界仍不确定；单一国际专家组构成的代表性（地区、机构层级）信息不足
papers.abstract_en: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are common after surgery and contribute substantially to morbidity, mortality, and health-care burden, and are frequently used as endpoints in clinical studies. However, absence of standardised definitions and heterogeneity in component selection limit comparability across studies and might bias estimates of treatment effects. The Postoperative Pulmonary Complications-Evaluation for Consensus on Standardised Outcomes (PrECiSIOn) study was an international, mixed-method consensus study using a Delphi process to establish a standardised definition of PPCs, determine severity-based ranking of individual components, and define approaches for their assessment. A multidisciplinary panel of experts in PPCs was recruited and candidate PPC components were identified through a focused literature review, structured into domains, and evaluated across iterative Delphi rounds using a seven-point Likert scale, with consensus predefined as ≥75% agreement. Patient and patient care representative perspectives were incorporated through interviews and surveys, and panellists assigned severity weights to components reaching consensus. Input from 44 panellists and five patients and patient representatives informed the prioritisation of clinically meaningful outcomes. Consensus was achieved on a standardised PPC construct comprising components grouped into four domains: symptoms, diagnoses, therapies, and outcomes. Panellists supported the use of routinely collected clinical data and a standardised in-hospital monitoring approach but did not reach consensus on the optimal follow-up period or need for post-discharge surveillance. Severity-based rank ordering enabled hierarchical organisation of PPC components according to their clinical importance, supporting the development of ordinal composite outcomes that account for differences in severity between individual complications. This international consensus-based framework provides a standardised definition of PPCs incorporating severity-based rank ordering, addresses important limitations of existing composite outcomes, and might facilitate more consistent and clinically meaningful evaluation of perioperative interventions. Further work should focus on external validation, implementation in clinical trial analyses, and assessment of applicability across diverse patient populations and health-care settings.

papers.ai_note: 信息不足：基因组队列与RNA测序队列样本量、PD-L1检测平台与阳性阈值、多因素校正变量清单均未报告。方法学疑点：单臂回顾性设计只能得出预后关联，不能证明预测价值（未与FLAURA2/MARIPOSA等联合方案对照），但标题与结论使用determinants/predict口径，存在预后-预测混淆；survROC的ΔAUC属探索性派生指标，6/12个月与very-early终点非预先设定的主要终点；rwPFS为真实世界终点，影像评估时间与间隔不统一易致早期进展检测偏倚；L858R亚组TP53（p=0.2）与TSG结果不一致，亚组间差异未报告交互检验P值。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: With the recent approvals of the FLAURA2 and MARIPOSA regimens in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), identifying clinico-genomic features predictive of suboptimal outcomes with first-line osimertinib monotherapy is critical in guiding upfront treatment selections. METHODS: This is a multicenter retrospective study enrolling patients with advanced NSCLC harboring common EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletions [ex19del], L858R) treated with first-line osimertinib monotherapy across 13 centers (Clinical cohort). Comprehensive baseline genomic data on tumor tissue were available for DFCI and MSKCC (Genomic cohort). The association of clinicogenomic features with real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS) was investigated. Caris Life Science cohort was used for RNA-sequencing analysis. RESULTS: A total of 1488 patients were enrolled in the clinical cohort; at median follow-up of 43.3 months, median rwPFS was 16.3 months (95%CI 15.3-17.4), median overall survival was 36.7 months (95%CI 34.8-39.4). TP53 mutated (TP53MUT) was independently associated with shorter rwPFS compared with TP53 wild-type (TP53WT), specifically in EGFR ex19del (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.68, p<0.001) than in L858R subgroup (aHR 1.18, p=0.2). Using a survROC model for rwPFS, PD-L1 was the variable with greatest impact on risk of progression at 6 (ΔAUC=0.0549) and 12 (ΔAUC=0.0348) months. In the genomic cohort, patients with TSGMUT (RBM10, CREBBP, ATM, RB1, KMT2D, TSC2, PTEN) had shorted rwPFS compared to TSGWT (aHR 1.5, p=0.01), specifically in L858R subgroup (aHR 1.8, p=0.02). Combining TP53 with TSG, pts with TP53MUT plus at least one TSGMUT and pts with TP53WT-TSGMUT had shorter rwPFS compared to TP53WT-TSGWT and TP53MUT-TSGWT. In the genomic cohort, PD-L1 TPS was the strongest predictor of very-early rwPFS (ΔAUC=0.16), followed by TP53-TSG (ΔAUC=0.08). PD-L1 was associated with higher MET mRNA and immunohistochemistry expression and transcriptional program enriched for proliferative, inflammatory, and metabolic signaling pathways. CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter real-world cohort, baseline PD-L1 and TP53 combined with TSG predict very-early progression to first-line osimertinib, with EGFR subtype-specific prognostic impact of genomic co-alterations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-optimal temperatures and extreme temperature events may trigger acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD), but most evidence is admission based, potentially misclassifying exposure timing and obscuring susceptible groups. RESEARCH QUESTION: Are non-optimal temperature and extreme temperature events associated with AECOPD onset, and which patients are most susceptible? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We used the Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Registry (ACURE) data and assigned residential temperature exposure using ERA5-Land, a reanalysis dataset of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Cold spells (CS) were defined as consecutive days below location-specific low-temperature thresholds, and compound cold spells (CCS) as concurrent daytime and nighttime cold spells. Associations with reported symptom onset were estimated using a time-stratified case-crossover design, conditional logistic regression with distributed lag nonlinear models. Subgroup and cytokine analyses assessed susceptibility and inflammation. RESULTS: Among 5,634 patients with AECOPD (mean age, 69.4 ± 9.5 years; 78.8% male), lower temperature was associated with higher odds of AECOPD onset, whereas higher temperature was not. The strongest associations occurred for CS lasting ≥3 days and CCS lasting ≥2 days over lag 0-3 days, with ORs of 1.84 (95% CI, 1.22-2.78) and 4.31 (95% CI, 2.07-8.97), respectively. Nearly half had delayed admission within 14 days. Using admission rather than onset dates attenuated estimates by 88.8% for CS and 84.8% for CCS. Associations were stronger among older adults, men, smokers, patients with severe AECOPD in the past year or previously diagnosed COPD, and those using combination inhaler in the preceding year. CS were also associated with higher TNF-α, IL-6, and CXCL-11 concentrations. INTERPRETATION: Lower temperature and extreme cold events, particularly CCS, were associated with AECOPD onset. Symptom-onset timing may better capture temperature-related associations than admission timing. These findings highlight the need for targeted cold-weather prevention strategies to reduce AECOPD burden. TRIAL REGISTRY: ClinicalTrials.gov; NO.: NCT02657525.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Chemoradiotherapy commonly causes radiation-induced lymphopenia, neutropenia, and anemia, as measured by reductions in absolute lymphocyte count (ALC), absolute neutrophil count (ANC), and hemoglobin level (Hb). We aimed to quantify these hematological toxicities and characterize dose-time-response relationships between temporal changes in peripheral blood biomarkers and radiation exposure to the circulating blood during volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) definitive chemoradiotherapy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS AND MATERIALS: Blood biomarker measurements were collected from 93 NSCLC patients, treated between 2018 and 2024, at pre-, during-, and post-treatment time points. Radiotherapy prescription doses were 60 Gy in 30 fractions, 55 Gy in 20 fractions, or 50 Gy in 25 fractions with concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy. Organs at risks were delineated by the TotalSegmentator software. The blood dose-volume histogram was estimated through simulations of blood dynamics using the HEDOS software and VMAT dose accumulation was calculated with the BeamSplitter algorithm. Dose-time-response relationships were modelled by linear and exponentially decaying curves, from which rates of change were extracted and goodness of fit quantified using the R2- value. RESULTS: Baseline blood biomarker values (median ± interquartile range) were (1.8±0.9) × 109/L for ALC, (5.6±3.0) × 109/L for ANC, and 132±19 g/L for Hb. Prior to treatment, 0%, 0%, and 30% of patients exhibited lymphopenia, neutropenia, and anemia, respectively. During treatment, these proportions increased to 71%, 19%, and 77%. Dose-response analysis revealed rates of change at low doses of radiation: -69%/Gy (ALC), -83%/Gy (ANC), and -3%/Gy (Hb), with model fits showing R² values between 0.78 and 0.96. CONCLUSIONS: Hematological toxicities were frequent in NSCLC patients treated with VMAT chemoradiotherapy. Radiation exposure was associated with changes in circulating lymphocyte counts and hemoglobin, supporting prospective investigation into reducing circulating blood dose during chemoradiation to mitigate hematological toxicity.

papers.authors_conclusion: 接受NSCLC切除患者中MHD患病率在6年内近乎翻倍，且与约20%的并发症增加及校正后5年生存下降相关；这些发现凸显了针对这一不断增长的人群制定靶向围手术期路径与长期支持以缓解不良结局的必要性。
papers.ai_note: 选择性强调与数值可核查性存疑：结论称并发症增加“约20%”、患病率“近乎翻倍”，但摘要结果段未给出围手术期死亡/并发症的任何具体数值或效应量（信息不足），且16.8%→28.0%的相对增幅约67%而非“近乎翻倍”。暴露为非随机、MHD诊断方式（自报/编码/既往史）摘要未说明；仅纳入已接受手术者，存在健康候选人/选择偏倚，结论不可外推至未手术人群。MHD患者反而更多为临床I期且接受亚肺叶切除，却生存更差，提示残余混杂（ frailty、吸烟、社会经济、辅助治疗差异）可能高估生存差异。Medicare链接子集的样本量、人群界定与随访缺失处理摘要未交代，信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: To determine the prevalence of comorbid mental health disorders (MHDs) and association with stage of diagnosis, extent of resection, and post-operative morbidity/mortality in patients undergoing operative intervention for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: Adults undergoing elective resection of stage I-III NSCLC were identified from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Database (July 2018-June 2024) and linked to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to determine long-term survival. Primary outcomes were stage at diagnosis, extent of resection, perioperative morbidity, and 5-year survival. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regressions estimated associations between MHDs on each outcome. Risk-adjusted survival was derived using multivariable frailty Cox proportional hazards regression. RESULTS: Among 103,263 patients, 24.4% (n=25,163) had ≥1 MHD. Prevalence of MHDs increased from 16.8% in 2018 to 28.0% in 2024 (p<0.001). In risk-adjusted analysis, patients with an MHD were more likely to have clinical stage I disease (aOR 1.16, 95% CI 1.11-1.22) and to undergo sublobar resection (aOR 1.09, 95% CI 1.06-1.14). Perioperative mortality, morbidity, and length of stay were all significantly increased in patients with MHDs. In risk-adjusted analysis among Medicare linked patients, 5-year mortality was modestly but significantly greater among patients with MHDs (aHR 1.12, 95% CI 1.05-1.18). CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of MHDs among patients undergoing NSCLC resection nearly doubled over 6 years and was associated with an ∼20% increase in morbidity and a reduction in adjusted 5-year survival. These findings underscore the need for targeted perioperative pathways and longitudinal support to mitigate adverse outcomes in this growing population.

papers.authors: Burgel PR, Lafourcade A, Da Silva J, Durieu I, Macey J, Danner-Boucher I, de Miranda S, Audousset C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Université Paris-Cité, Institut Cochin, CNRS, Inserm, Paris, France; Respiratory Medicine and Cystic Fibrosis National R…
papers.authors_conclusion: These results suggest that approximately a third of adults with cystic fibrosis who are treated with ETI had a persistent decline in ppFEV1. These data emphasise the importance of regular ppFEV1 monitoring and highlight the need to improve current therapeutic strategies to prevent ppFEV1 decline. Proposed strategies could include use of newer CFTR modulators to restore CFTR function more effectively, as well as mucoactive, anti-infective, and anti-inflammatory therapies.
papers.ai_note: 无同期对照，下降速率与历史约1.5%/年的自然史数据属跨研究比较，非直接头对头证据。参考值定义为ETI头3个月内的最高ppFEV1（取峰值作基线），存在回归均值效应，可能使估计的后续下降幅度偏小。阿奇霉素/吸入抗生素的保护性关联来自观察性数据，存在适应证混杂（用药者疾病严重度、依从性、随访强度不同），不能作因果推断。纳入条件要求3个月内至少3次肺功能测量，可能偏向随访规律的患者。仅纳入≥18岁且携带F508del的成人，外推至儿童、非F508del人群受限。摘要同时报告总体年均下降0.70%与31.8%个体下降>1.5%/年，均值与个体异质性并存，引用时需区分。与III期延长期'4年无下降证据'的表述存在张力，摘要未做直接比较检验
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Without cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulators, cystic fibrosis is associated with an accelerated decline in percent predicted FEV1 (ppFEV1) of approximately 1·5% per year. Although treatment with elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor (ETI) initially increases ppFEV1, little is known about its subsequent effect on ppFEV1 decline. Recent analyses of the extension phases of the phase 3 ETI pivotal studies found no evidence of ppFEV1 decline over 4 years in patients aged 12 years and older who were treated with ETI. The objective of this study was to examine the decline in ppFEV1 in a large, real-world cohort of adults with cystic fibrosis. METHODS: Data from adults (aged ≥18 years) with cystic fibrosis and at least one F508del CFTR variant who initiated treatment with ETI between Dec 24, 2019, and Dec 23, 2023, at 31 cystic fibrosis centres included in the French prospective national observational ETI study in adults were analysed over 3 years. Eligible participants were those with at least three measures of ppFEV1 taken within 3 months following ETI initiation and the end of follow-up. The reference ppFEV1 was the highest ppFEV1 reached during the first 3 months of ETI treatment, after which subsequent decline in ppFEV1 was analysed by use of a linear mixed-effects model with random effects to estimate each participant's variation from the population mean. FINDINGS: Data from 2321 adults with cystic fibrosis were included in this analysis. 1262 (54·4%) participants were male and 1059 (45·6%) were female. Median age was 29·2 years (IQR 23·1-36·7) and the pre-ETI initiation ppFEV1 was 59·7% (IQR 39·8-79·1). Within the first 3 months following ETI initiation, ppFEV1 increased by a median of 14·5 percentage points (IQR 7·9-22·7). The subsequent mean decline in ppFEV1 was 0·70% (95% CI 0·57-0·83) per year. Importantly, the decline in ppFEV1 was heterogeneous, with 1583 (68·2%) of 2321 participants showing no or limited decline (less than or equal to 1·5% per year). The remaining 738 (31·8%) participants showed a decline of greater than 1·5% per year, with 342 (46·3%) of these participants having a decline of greater than 3·0% per year. In multivariable analyses, the decline in ppFEV1 was greater in participants with a higher ppFEV1 at 3 months after ETI initiation. Treatment with oral azithromycin at 1 year after ETI initiation was associated with a lower risk of having a decline greater than 1·5% per year (relative risk 0·78 [95% CI 0·68-0·90]; p <0·01), as was treatment with inhaled antibiotics (0·81 [0·70-0·94]; p <0·01). INTERPRETATION: These results suggest that approximately a third of adults with cystic fibrosis who are treated with ETI had a persistent decline in ppFEV1. These data emphasise the importance of regular ppFEV1 monitoring and highlight the need to improve current therapeutic strategies to prevent ppFEV1 decline. Proposed strategies could include use of newer CFTR modulators to restore CFTR function more effectively, as well as mucoactive, anti-infective, and anti-inflammatory therapies. FUNDING: Association Vaincre la Mucoviscidose, Société Française de la Mucoviscidose, and Filière Maladies Rares MUCO-CFTR.

papers.authors: Song XY, Liu ZC, Hu HH, Li Y, Lin L, Yang Y, Li HX, Feng W et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiation Oncology, Shanghai Chest Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Shanghai 20…
papers.authors_conclusion: These findings reveal distinct CD8+ T cell programs associated with response to different neoadjuvant modalities and provide a cellular rationale for optimizing immunotherapy-radiotherapy sequencing.
papers.ai_note: 摘要仅报告细胞亚群层面的关联性富集/减少（如CXCL13+PD-1+与progenitor-like CD8Tex_CXCR4（NICT应答者维持/富集）、CXCL13+减少与PD-1- CD8Teff_NIBAN1克隆扩增（CRT应答者）），未给出样本量、客观缓解率、EFS/OS等临床终点数值，免疫-放疗时序的因果依据主要来自动物模型而非人体疗效数据；关联性细胞表型与临床应答的因果方向及人群普适性信息不足。
papers.abstract_en: The optimal integration of immunotherapy with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in neoadjuvant treatment of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. We integrate paired pre- and post-treatment single-cell RNA sequencing and TCR sequencing data from patients receiving neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT), chemoradiotherapy (NCRT), or immuno-chemoradiotherapy (NICRT) to investigate how these regimens shape intratumoral CD8+ T cell responses. Favorable responses to NICT are associated with maintenance of pre-existing CXCL13+PD-1+ CD8+ T cells and post-treatment enrichment of a progenitor-like CD8Tex_CXCR4 subset. In contrast, CRT responders show reduced CXCL13+ CD8+ T cells and enrichment of clonally expanded, cytotoxic PD-1- CD8Teff_NIBAN1 cells. These divergent programs are validated in public datasets and independent prospective cohorts. In murine models, radiotherapy limits PD-1+ T cell expansion, whereas induction anti-PD-1 treatment followed by radiotherapy improves tumor control. Together, these findings reveal distinct CD8+ T cell programs associated with response to different neoadjuvant modalities and provide a cellular rationale for optimizing immunotherapy-radiotherapy sequencing.

These simple, readily available indicators may help target preventive interventions in high-burden settings; however, associations with incident TB remain uncertain.
papers.ai_note: 主要结局层面存在替代终点问题：摘要强调的是结核感染（传播的替代指标），而更接近临床硬终点的12个月结核发病在空洞范围（aCRR 1.20, 0.56-2.60）与咳嗽时长（aCRR 1.30, 0.85-1.99）两组均无统计学显著关联，CI均跨越1，提示感染阳性并不转化为发病风险差异，发病终点可能效能不足（事件数未报告）。改良Bandim TB评分阴性结果在结论中被淡化。信息不足：未报告各终点事件数、失访率及评分校准情况。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Interrupting TB transmission is a priority in high-burden settings. Identifying highly infectious people with TB may guide targeted interventions. RESEARCH QUESTION: Can readily available clinical characteristics (eg, lung cavitation, cough duration, modified Bandim TB score) indicate the transmission risk in participants with TB? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study in Lima, Peru, enrolling 4,500 index participants. Of the 4,044 people with microbiologically confirmed TB, 3,109 had at least 1 household contact (HHC), yielding 12,767 HHCs. Index participants underwent chest radiograph and TB symptom assessment, from which we derived a modified Bandim TB score. We assessed HHCs for TB infection at baseline and 6 months, and for incident TB disease over 12 months. We analyzed associations between index participant indicators and TB outcomes in HHCs using modified Poisson regression with generalized estimating equations, adjusting for relevant covariates. RESULTS: Among child HHCs, baseline TB infection risk increased with greater cavitary extent (adjusted trend P = .005) and longer cough duration (adjusted trend P = .002), with similar trends at 6 months. Among cavitation categories, multiple-quadrant involvement was associated with the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.10-2.39), but not with incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 0.56-2.60). Among cough duration categories, ≥ 56 days showed the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.18-2.13), but not incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.85-1.99). The modified Bandim TB score was not associated with transmission risk. INTERPRETATION: Our results show that in this large household cohort, cavitary extent on chest radiograph and cough duration in people with TB were associated with increased TB transmission risk and showed dose-response relationships with TB infection. These simple, readily available indicators may help target preventive interventions in high-burden settings; however, associations with incident TB remain uncertain.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a common malignant tumor in China, with a poor five-year survival rate due to the lack of effective early diagnostic methods. This study aimed to identify potential non-invasive biomarkers and clarify their underlying mechanisms. METHODS: We employed an integrative approach combining serum proteomic profiling, bulk RNA sequencing, and single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) analyses. Quantitative proteomics was conducted on 15 serum samples of treatment-naive early-stage ESCC patients and 5 from healthy controls. Differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were cross-referenced with differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from the GSE53624 dataset, and a diagnostic model was developed using LASSO regression. Cross-validation was performed using scRNA-seq data. The enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was utilized to validate FTL in 155 serum samples from two centers. In silico FTL knockouts were conducted using scTenifoldKnk, followed by GO, KEGG, and PPI network analyses. RESULTS: Proteomic profiling identified a total of 129 DEPs. Intersection with GSE53624 DEGs yielded 8 overlapping genes, and a 6-biomarker (TF, CHAD, CSRP1, FCGR3A, RCN1, FTL) diagnostic model was built, with AUC 0.882-1.0 across validation cohorts. scRNA-seq intersection analysis identified FTL as the only overlapping DEG, exhibiting high expression levels in ESCC epithelial cells and macrophages. FTL demonstrated strong standalone diagnostic performance, with AUC values ranging from 0.872 to 0.970 across three GEO datasets. ELISA validation yielded an AUC of 0.75 (95% CI: 0.674-0.816) and 0.838 (95% CI: 0.751-0.905) for early-stage ESCC, surpassing the performance of CEA and SCCA. The combination of FTL with SCCA further enhanced discriminatory efficacy. Mechanistically, FTL was associated with altered immune cell infiltration, characterized by increased resting dendritic cells and M2 macrophages and decreased follicular helper T cells, as well as activation of the ferroptosis pathway. In silico FTL knockouts revealed DEGs enriched in stress and metabolic biological processes, extracellular vesicles (cellular component), transcriptional regulation (molecular function, CHOP-ATF3 complex), IL-17/TNF pathways, and lipid/ROS-related pathways. Protein-protein interaction hubs included FOS, ATF3, NFKBIA, and CXCL8, with FTL linked to NFE2L2, TFRC, and TXNRD1. CONCLUSIONS: FTL represents a credible non-invasive serum diagnostic biomarker for ESCC. Computational analyses suggest it is a candidate molecule requiring further mechanistic and therapeutic investigation.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a disease that is difficult to diagnose because its clinical findings are nonspecific and it carries high mortality when not treated early. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA), the gold standard for diagnosis, cannot be performed in every patient because of contraindications related to contrast medium; Noncontrast computed tomography (NCCT), on the other hand, cannot be used as a reliable tool for exclusion because of its low sensitivity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, the paired images of 716 patients (129 PE-positive, 587 PE-negative) who had undergone both CTPA and NCCT on the same day between 2018 and 2026 were examined. The availability of two scans obtained from the same patient on the same day provided a paired cohort in which clinical and anatomical variables other than the presence of contrast were largely held constant, so that the CTPA scan established with certainty where a thrombus lay in each patient whose noncontrast scan was analyzed. Each scan was converted into a 12-second mediastinal-window video, from which a 40-frame segment centered on the temporal midpoint of the recording was extracted for analysis. For the automatic detection of thrombus, three-dimensional deep learning architectures have been developed: PureStream-3D, BiLSTM-ResNet-3D based on bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), and AttnFocus-3D based on an attention mechanism. The models have been optimized with different training configurations to address class imbalance, and the dataset has been divided at the patient level into 70% training, 20% validation, and 10% independent test sets. RESULTS: In the CTPA test set, the highest discrimination has been achieved by the AttnFocus-3D-1 model (accuracy 0.9306; area under the curve [AUC] 0.98), whereas the most balanced sensitivity-specificity profile has been obtained with the BiLSTM-ResNet-3D-2 variant (sensitivity 0.9138, specificity 0.8571). In the NCCT test set, the AttnFocus-3D-2 architecture has reached an accuracy of 0.9306, an AUC of 0.97, a sensitivity of 0.9655, and a specificity of 0.7857. CONCLUSION: Taken together, these findings indicate that the developed deep learning approaches are strong in confirming the presence or absence of PE and can be considered as a decision-support infrastructure in clinical scenarios with high diagnostic uncertainty.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: First-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab with/without 2 cycles of chemotherapy has been approved for untreated metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in Japan, based on CheckMate 9LA and CheckMate 227, but long-term real-world data in Japanese patients are limited. METHODS: LIGHT-NING is an ongoing, multicenter, observational study, examining nivolumab plus ipilimumab, with/without chemotherapy for patients with stage IV or recurrent NSCLC. We assessed treatment patterns, effectiveness, and safety, using 2.5-year data from November 2020 to June 2024. Exploratory analyses characterized early progressive disease (PD) and associated baseline factors. These analyses were hypothesis-generating in nature. RESULTS: Of 545 patients (median age: 70 years, 18.9% female, 89.9% Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1, median follow-up period 15.1 months), 319 (58.5%) received nivolumab plus ipilimumab with chemotherapy and 226 (41.5%) without chemotherapy. Median overall survival and real-world progression-free survival were 21.7 and 6.8 months, respectively, in patients with chemotherapy, and 18.8 and 6.3 months, respectively, without chemotherapy. Grade 3-5 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 170 (53.3%) and 69 (30.5%) patients, respectively. As an exploratory analysis, early PD in the cohort without chemotherapy was associated with body mass index in squamous cell carcinoma and albumin, lactate dehydrogenase, and lung immune prognostic index in non-squamous cell carcinoma. CONCLUSIONS: This analysis of LIGHT-NING study indicated that safety and effectiveness in Japanese patients were consistent with those observed in CheckMate 9LA and CheckMate 227. No new safety signals were observed, the combination therapy was generally well manageable.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung protective ventilation is crucial for preventing ventilator-induced lung injury in cardiac surgery. The protective role of a low tidal volume (VT) has been established, whereas the added protection afforded by lung recruitment remains uncertain. We investigated whether sigh breaths could provide additional lung protection, when added to protective ventilation with low VT. METHODS: This randomized, assessor-blinded, phase 2 proof-of-concept trial enrolled 192 patients undergoing elective on-pump cardiac surgery from February to August 2024. Patients were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive sigh ventilation (sigh breaths plus protective ventilation with low VT; 96 patients) or conventional ventilation (protective ventilation with low VT; 96 patients). Sigh breaths targeting a plateau pressure of 35 cmH2O (or 40 cmH2O for BMI >35 kg/m2) were delivered once every 6 min. Perioperative respiratory mechanics and gas exchange were monitored. The primary outcome was postoperative oxygenation, a marker of lung injury, as measured by the time-weighted average SpO2/FiO2 ratio during the first postextubation hour. There were 9 predefined secondary outcomes, including the severity of respiratory failure within postextubation day 7. RESULTS: All 192 patients completed the trial (53% male; median age, 64 [55-72] years). Perioperatively, sigh ventilation produced sustained improvements in oxygenation and respiratory system compliance, together with reductions in driving pressure and mechanical power (All P interaction<0.001). After extubation, the mean time-weighted SpO2/FiO2 ratio was higher in the sigh ventilation group (380 ± 86 vs 338 ± 93; mean difference 42.1, 95% CI [16.7 to 67.5]; P=0.001). The severity and occurrence of respiratory failure was reduced in the sigh ventilation group compared with conventional ventilation group (common odds ratio for lower severity 2.2; 95% CI [1.2 to 3.8]; P=0.007). There was no difference in adverse events of interest between groups. CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing on-pump cardiac surgery, adding sigh breaths was safe and resulted in a statistically significant improvement in postoperative oxygenation. Nevertheless, the clinical importance of this finding is uncertain because oxygenation was adequately maintained in both groups. Reduction in driving pressure and mechanical power, together with findings in secondary outcomes, suggest additional lung protection and justify future trials. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06248320); registered on January 30, 2024.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Spark-like T cells constitute a novel functional state of CD8+T cells and have emerged as key drivers of immunotherapy response in preclinical models, yet their clinical relevance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains undefined. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE207422), spatial transcriptomics (GSE271689), bulk RNA expression cohorts (TCGA-NSCLC, GSE37745, GSE41271, and GSE72094), and multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) of a 100-patient cohort treated with anti-PD-1 were integrated to characterize Spark-like T cells and assess their clinical relevance. A 14-gene prognostic signature was constructed via LASSO-Cox regression. RESULTS: Spark-like T cells were significantly enriched in anti-PD-1 responders in the single-cell RNA sequencing cohort. mIHC validation in the 100-patient cohort confirmed that high Spark-like T cell intensity in tumors was independently associated with prolonged overall survival (log-rank test, p < 0.001) and partial response to anti-PD-1 therapy (p = 0.0075). Spatial transcriptomics indicated strong co-localization of Spark-like T cells with M1 macrophages (Spearman r = 0.524, p = 3.4 × 10-42), suggesting their spatial co-enrichment with pro-inflammatory myeloid cells. In silico knockout identified TNF, ENTPD1 (CD39), and IL2 as cooperative regulators of Spark-like T cell effector function. The 14-gene Spark-like T cell-related signature (VDAC1, ITGB1, GALNT2, SEMA7A, UBB, SLC7A5, FURIN, SNX9, PSMB2, CXCL13, TOX, PPM1M, CCND2, and CLNK) robustly predicted overall survival across all four independent cohorts and remained an independent prognostic factor after adjustment for age, sex, and tumor stage. High-risk patients exhibited an immune-excluded, oncogene-driven tumor microenvironment with reduced infiltration of CD8+T cells. CONCLUSIONS: Spark-like T cells are clinically relevant determinants of anti-PD-1 response in NSCLC. mIHC quantification and the 14-gene signature provide promising translational tools for patient stratification and risk assessment.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pulmonology, University Hospital of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland.
papers.authors_conclusion: The RAP/CO-slope is a strong, independent prognostic marker across a spectrum of RV afterload stress. A RAP/CO slope ≥1 mmHg·min⁻¹ was identified as particularly predictive in manifest PH.
